## TLDR

Add an opt-in, account-independent answer-quality benchmark using real Bedrock inference and AgentCore Evaluations.

- Run 12 versioned synthetic CloudOps cases through Strands and the shared production prompt.
- Score Helpfulness, Faithfulness and ground-truth Correctness; keep a deliberately wrong-answer sanity case separate.
- Capture approved content locally. Preserve production metadata-only telemetry. Require explicit profile, Region, model and paid-operation opt-in.
- Commit sanitized responses, spans, evaluator metadata, usage, mappings and reproducible commands.

## User Flow

### Before

1. Deploy and invoke the sample.
2. Inspect metadata-only traces. No repeatable answer-quality benchmark or measured baseline is available.

### After

1. Configure your own AWS profile, supported Region and model.
2. Follow `evaluations/README.md`: `uv sync --directory evaluations --locked`, then `runner.py invoke`, `score` and `report`.
3. Inspect per-case evidence and separate metric summaries. Re-score saved traces without invoking the agent again.

## Relevant issues

Refs #24. The owner approved the fixture-backed baseline and test boundaries. New reference-answer wording remains for maintainer review.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] One specific problem; no evaluation service/dashboard or production content export.
- [x] Relevant local tests pass and evaluation boundary regressions are covered.
- [ ] Required remote CI checks pass — previous tip passed; checks for the updated evidence commit are pending.
- [x] Documentation covers setup, costs, permissions, retention and limitations.
- [x] Evidence identifies revisions, Region, model and hashes without account credentials.

## Proof of implementation

### Before (`fd57ec7`)

No evaluation runner/dataset or measured README quality metrics. Production exports metadata only.

### After (`cbc3c6b`)

The baseline was rerun in the owner's `aiops_demo` account after verifying STS identity against the intended demo account. Capture and scoring used clean commit `bae50fe`; `cbc3c6b` replaces the evidence and documentation. The earlier `prod`-profile run used the wrong account and is superseded, not relabeled. No account IDs or credentials are included in the public artifact.

Real AWS run on 2026-09-18 in `us-east-1`, model `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0`, Strands 1.20.0, temperature 0. All 12 cases were invoked again in the demo account and all 39 judge calls completed there. Earlier clean-checkout installation and replay verification were performed in the other account. The shared production prompt remains unchanged.

| Metric | Returned scale | Completed / expected | Mean | Labels |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Helpfulness | 0–1 | 12 / 12 | 0.9292 | Above And Beyond: 7; Very Helpful: 5 |
| Faithfulness | 0–1 | 12 / 12 | 0.9583 | Completely Yes: 10; Generally Yes: 2 |
| Correctness | 0–1 | 12 / 12 | 0.9167 | Correct: 11; Incorrect: 1 |

Zero execution failures/skips per metric. Wrong-answer sanity case: zero on all metrics, excluded above. No pass threshold or combined score. GetEvaluator's Helpfulness metadata advertises 0–6, while Evaluate returned normalized 0–1 values; both retained without conversion.

Evidence: `evaluations/evidence/baseline-2026-09-18.json` and `.md`. Observed shortcomings include unsupported claims after empty results and a missing inventory scope caveat. The demo baseline replaces the previous account’s evidence. Built-in judges remain nondeterministic.

### Console-visible batch verification (d5ee83d)

The owner requested console visibility. `evaluations/batch.py` now publishes only the approved synthetic traces into an isolated seven-day-retention log group, waits for Logs Insights visibility, and creates separate baseline and sanity jobs in `aiops_demo/us-east-1`. Production telemetry remains metadata-only.

Verified in the console and through GetBatchEvaluation:

- `cloudops_baseline_20260918_verified-e861b35767`: COMPLETED, 12/12 sessions, 36 evaluator results, no failures/ignored sessions. Service summary means: Helpfulness 0.96, Faithfulness 0.96, Correctness 0.92 (API-rounded).
- `cloudops_sanity_20260918_verified-aabfbcd479`: COMPLETED, 1/1 session, three results, all scores zero.
- Full end-to-end command replay also succeeded: jobs `cloudops_baseline_20260918_063523-5623e46c00` and `cloudops_sanity_20260918_063523-d9f9bd86d8`, with all 39 matching result events downloaded.

Four earlier setup jobs failed because batch queries ran before Logs Insights could see uploaded spans. They remain visible for diagnosis. GetLogEvents visibility was insufficient; the runner now waits for completed Logs Insights counts before job creation. No scores from those failed jobs are used.

Batch evidence: `evaluations/evidence/console-batch-2026-09-18.json`, containing job metadata, references and all 39 actual per-session output events. Account IDs in ARNs are replaced with ACCOUNT_ID. Screenshot is cropped only to omit account/user/browser chrome; failed setup jobs remain visible.

![Successful console batch jobs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aws-samples/sample-cloudops-agent-amazon-bedrock-agentcore/feat/agentcore-evaluations/evaluations/evidence/console-batch-completed.png)

The original on-demand workflow still creates no console job. The optional batch path now creates jobs, CloudWatch result events and evaluation metrics; it does not create an online evaluation configuration or alter production Runtime telemetry.

### Local verification

- Evaluation boundary suite: 10 passed; mypy clean for runner.py and batch.py.
- Agent suite: 107 passed, 7 live-configuration skips, 14 live tests deselected; includes metadata-only OTLP export regression.
- CDK: 15 passed; TypeScript build passed.
- Frontend: 41 passed; production build passed with existing bundle-size warning.
- Lambda suites: 20 passed.
- Inventory: 6 deployed-source tests and 2 standalone tests passed.
- Standalone EOL scraper: 70 passed; existing inventory `utcnow` deprecation warnings.
- Verified 39 reference/result mappings, source hashes, report regeneration and sensitive-marker exclusion.

## Type

- New feature
- Documentation
- Test

## Caveats

- Fixture-backed answer quality only. No deployed Gateway/IAM, live inventory, current AWS pricing, Runtime health or persistent Memory validation.
- Live execution now covered two accounts in one Region; the published baseline is the intended demo account. Fixed fixtures and explicit configuration avoid account-specific expected facts, but model access and SCP/Region support remain prerequisites.
- Batch input log groups have seven-day retention; job records and service-managed output logs require explicit retention/cleanup. No shared log groups are deleted by the runner.
- New reference wording awaits maintainer review. Synthetic prices/lifecycle dates are not vendor guidance.
- No deployment, destructive outage testing, Docker/MCP rebuild or live Gateway security tests performed.
- Content allowlists and secret-pattern rejection are defense in depth, not a general customer-data anonymizer. Only committed synthetic fixtures are approved.

## QA runbook

Use `evaluations/README.md` for exact locked install, offline test, invoke, score, replay and report commands. All paid commands require explicit opt-in. Expect 12 baseline results per metric plus one separate sanity result; missing content/references/results must fail. On-demand creates no cloud resources. Batch creates isolated fixture input logs and job records; follow the documented exact-target cleanup. Local raw batch evidence contains account ARNs and stays gitignored.

## Final Attestation

- [x] Evidence provenance, later corrections, skipped checks and visibility limitations are disclosed. Standards and spec were reviewed separately by one reviewer; parallel subagents were unavailable.

body:
Addresses your two camera asks: **make the studio bigger**, and **do the 20 MP stills** (no longer deferred).

- **Bigger studio**: modal widened to `min(98vw, 1680px)` / `94vh`, so both live videos render much larger (~800px wide each vs ~530px).
- **Full-resolution stills**: snapshots now prefer `ImageCapture.takePhoto` — the camera's **full sensor** size (up to ~20 MP on the science ELP), independent of the ≤4K preview — with the date/time + metadata overlay burned in. Falls back to the live-frame grab where unsupported.
- **Recorded per-layer science captures** (`ScienceCaptureClient`) also grab full-resolution via `takePhoto` when available (marks fire at gantry-parked dwell points, so the ~photo latency is fine), falling back to the instant lossless ≤4K frame.

⚠ **One tradeoff to know:** `takePhoto` returns the camera's own encoding (usually JPEG), so the full-res path trades pixel-exactness for resolution; the fallback stays lossless PNG. For dimensional metrology the resolution gain usually wins, but if you'd rather keep the recorded science captures 4K-**lossless**, say so and I'll gate the recorded path back to the frame grab (keeping full-res for the manual studio snapshot).

Browser-only (`getUserMedia`/`ImageCapture` can't run headless) — verify on the machine. Gates: `npm test` (168), `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (0), `npm run build`.

## Qué pasó

El merge del PR #1 disparó **Deploy — Staging** ([run 35303173795](https://github.com/fabri07/carwash-app/actions/runs/35303173795)) y fallaron los dos jobs.

| Job | Error | Causa raíz |
|---|---|---|
| API staging (Railway) | `Deploy failed` a los 7 s, sin log de build | Los `RUN --mount=type=cache` del Dockerfile no llevan `id=s/<service-id>-<ruta>`, que [Railway exige](https://docs.railway.com/guides/dockerfiles). |
| App staging (Vercel) | `No Next.js version detected` | El proyecto tiene Root Directory `.`; `next` está en `frontend/package.json`. |

## Cambios

- `backend/Dockerfile`: sin cache mounts (el service-id cambia entre staging y prod, no hay un `id` que sirva para los dos). `UV_NO_CACHE=1` para no dejar el caché en la capa.
- `ci-backend.yml`: el job de Docker falla si vuelve un `mount=type=cache`. El build pasaba en CI y lo rechazaba Railway.
- `vercel.json` → `frontend/vercel.json`, con comandos relativos a `frontend/`.

## Antes de mergear (paso manual)

En Vercel, **Root Directory = `frontend`** (y Framework = Next.js) en `carwash-app-staging` **y** `carwash-app-prod`. Sin eso el deploy de Vercel vuelve a fallar.

## Verificación

- `vercel build --prod` contra el proyecto de staging: falla hoy con el mismo error del run; con `rootDirectory=frontend` + este `vercel.json` → `Build completed successfully`.
- `docker build --target runtime` local OK, dependencias importan.

author: rogerhyang
body:
### Summary

A dataset binding can override its evaluator's description and output configs; a binding that stores neither inherits them. The GraphQL mutations that create and update an LLM evaluator through a dataset binding also wrote the evaluator's own description and configs onto the binding, and the code evaluator dialogs sent the same values to the evaluator and to its binding, so every UI-created binding looked like a deliberate override and stopped following later edits to its evaluator. This PR makes those bindings inherit: creating an evaluator through a dataset stores nothing on the binding, and saving the dataset evaluator dialog clears the binding's override. Migration `ef09e3bc213f` resets the copies already stored, so existing bindings inherit too, and makes SQL `NULL` the only way a binding inherits. It also makes the database refuse to delete a prompt version tag an LLM evaluator runs through.

### Behavior

| Operation | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createDatasetLlmEvaluator` | Binding stored a copy of the evaluator's description and output configs | Binding stores nothing for either and inherits |
| `updateDatasetLlmEvaluator` (LLM edit dialog) | Rewrote the binding's description and output configs with the evaluator's new values | Writes the new values to the evaluator and sets the binding's description and output configs to `NULL`, so the binding inherits them |
| Code create dialog | Sent the description and output configs to `createCodeEvaluator` and to `createDatasetCodeEvaluator` | Sends them to `createCodeEvaluator` only; the binding stores nothing and inherits |
| Code edit dialog | Sent the description and output configs to `patchCodeEvaluator` and to `updateDatasetCodeEvaluator` | Sends them to `patchCodeEvaluator` and sends `null` for both to `updateDatasetCodeEvaluator`, which clears the binding's override |
| Saving a dialog for a binding that holds a real override | Wrote the displayed values to the evaluator and to the binding | Writes the displayed values to the evaluator and clears the override: the dataset reads the same values right after the save and follows the evaluator afterwards |
| Existing LLM bindings | Hold a copy of their evaluator's settings | Reset to inherit by the migration |
| Existing code bindings | Hold a copy of their evaluator's settings, or an override | Each setting equal to the evaluator's is reset to inherit by the migration; a setting that differs stays |
| An inheriting binding in storage | `output_configs` holds JSON `null` in a `NOT NULL` column | `output_configs` is SQL `NULL`; the column is nullable, as the model already declared |
| A binding whose `output_configs` is `[]` | The experiment runner treats it as inherit, while GraphQL shows an override with no configs | Reset to SQL `NULL` by the migration |
| Reading a binding's description or outputs in GraphQL | Effective values | Unchanged: the resolvers already fall back to the evaluator when the binding holds none |

### Migration

- `ef09e3bc213f` follows `a7f1c3e9d2b4`. It makes `dataset_evaluators.output_configs` nullable, turns JSON `null` into SQL `NULL` for every binding, and sets `output_configs` and `description` to `NULL` on every binding of an LLM evaluator.
- It sets `output_configs` to `NULL` on every binding, of any evaluator kind, that stores an empty JSON array. Nothing produces an empty override on purpose: every evaluator dialog requires at least one output config, and the experiment runner already treats an empty override as inherit, so runs of these bindings do not change. The predicate is `output_configs = '[]'::jsonb` on PostgreSQL and `json_type(...) = 'array' AND json_array_length(...) = 0` on SQLite. Later PRs in this stack refuse `[]` as an override in REST and GraphQL.
- On bindings of code evaluators it sets `description` to `NULL` where it equals `evaluators.description`, and `output_configs` to `NULL` where it equals the evaluator's `code_evaluators.output_configs`, each column on its own. This step runs after the JSON `null` and `[]` resets. It selects the code bindings, parses both JSON values in Python, and updates matching rows by id: the stored text of equal JSON values can differ in key order, spacing, and number formatting, so a text comparison in SQL would miss copies on SQLite.
- Clearing every LLM binding, not only those equal to their evaluator, is safe because no released version let an LLM binding hold a value of its own: each LLM evaluator was created with its single binding, and create and update wrote the same input to both rows. Those values are copies, never overrides a user chose. Deliberate overrides become possible with the REST binding routes later in this stack, which ship in the same release as the migration. Clearing them all also repairs a copy that has already gone stale, which comparing against the evaluator's current settings would miss.
- Code bindings are compared rather than cleared because they can hold deliberate overrides: `updateDatasetCodeEvaluator` accepts values of its own. The code dialogs wrote the same input to the evaluator and to its binding, so a value equal to the evaluator's is a copy, and a value that differs stays as an override.
- With SQL `NULL`, `IS NULL` finds inheriting bindings on both dialects. The binding column type sets `none_as_null`, so new writes store SQL `NULL` as well.
- On SQLite, dropping `NOT NULL` rebuilds the table. The migration connection runs without foreign-key enforcement, so the `experiment_dataset_evaluators` and `experiment_eval_logs` rows that cascade from bindings survive. The migration test seeds both and checks them, along with the table's indexes and constraints, through upgrade and downgrade on SQLite and PostgreSQL. It also seeds a code and a built-in binding that store `[]` and checks that both become SQL `NULL`, and code bindings that equal their evaluator in both columns, in one column, and in neither, including configs whose stored JSON text differs from the evaluator's.
- After the binding steps, it re-creates `fk_llm_evaluators_prompt_version_tag_id_prompt_version_tags` with `ON DELETE RESTRICT` (see Evaluator tags). PostgreSQL drops and re-adds the constraint. SQLite rebuilds `llm_evaluators` under batch mode, without foreign-key enforcement; no table references `llm_evaluators`. The migration test checks the foreign key's `ondelete` on both dialects, and that the table's rows, both indexes, the `kind` CHECK constraint, and its other two foreign keys survive upgrade and downgrade. With enforcement on, a raw delete of a tag an evaluator uses raises `IntegrityError` after the upgrade and nulls the evaluator's `prompt_version_tag_id` after the downgrade. The SQLite DDL snapshot prints the rebuilt table's `kind` CHECK as a table constraint and its timestamp default in parentheses, as it does for other rebuilt tables.
- The downgrade first restores `ON DELETE SET NULL` on the tag foreign key. It then copies each LLM evaluator's current settings back onto its inheriting bindings, stores JSON `null` for the other inheriting bindings, including those that held `[]` and the code bindings reset to inherit, and restores `NOT NULL`. The earlier code reads these as inherit: its resolvers fall back to the evaluator for a `NULL` description and for JSON `null` output configs, and its experiment runner falls back for empty ones. Overrides written after the upgrade are kept.
- Built-in bindings keep their stored values, apart from an empty list: a built-in evaluator can only be customized through its binding.

### Evaluator tags

- The migration makes `llm_evaluators.prompt_version_tag_id` `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, so the database refuses to delete a prompt version tag an LLM evaluator runs through. Without its tag the evaluator would run the prompt's latest version, whatever is saved there next.
- #16260 refuses such a delete first, with a 409 or GraphQL conflict naming the evaluator.
- `PromptVersionTag.llm_evaluators`

author: nimbleaininja
body:
## Problem

Launching intermittently fails with:

> The virtual machine started, but Try Omarchy could not enable safe Mac sleep. Please close and reopen the app. (I/O failure: cannot connect to QMP socket: Connection refused)

Most often on the first launch after installing a build; the guest console log is empty afterwards; reopening usually works. Seen on an M1 Max / macOS 27.

## Cause

`run-qemu-gpu.sh` prints `[qemu-gpu] Ready. QMP: …` as soon as QEMU has created its socket files. QEMU creates those early in `qemu_init`, but only accepts monitor connections from its main loop, which starts when init finishes — and the QMP chardev listens with a backlog of one (`chardev/char-socket.c`, `qio_net_listener_open_sync(…, 1, …)`).

The helper connects on Ready and gives the greeting two seconds. On a slow start (8 GiB guest, VirGL/ANGLE setup, cold caches after an install) init outlasts that. The connection had already been queued by the kernel, and a queued connection stays queued when its client gives up, so the backlog is now full: every later connect returns `ECONNREFUSED` until the main loop runs. The helper reads that as a broken monitor and sends QEMU `SIGTERM` — hence the empty console log.

Reproduced deterministically against the shipped QEMU with a deliberately slow init: one probe that gives up, then every connect refused, then success the instant the main loop came up. Pacing the helper's retries (#228) cannot help — they retry into a full queue — which is why that PR is closed in favour of this one.

## Fix

Make Ready mean what its consumer assumes. A new sourced library, `macos/qemu-monitor-ready.sh`, waits until a connection to the QMP socket receives a greeting, retrying a refused connect or a silent monitor every 100 ms. A probe that gives up may itself occupy the backlog, and the main loop drains it as its first act, so the next probe gets through. It fails if QEMU exits, or after 60 s, so a monitor that never answers still fails startup. The launcher calls it immediately before printing Ready. The helper is unchanged.

## Validation

- `make test` passes.
- `macos/Tests/qemu-monitor-ready.test.sh` drives the function against a stand-in that listens immediately but only accepts after a delay, the way QEMU does: Ready waits for the answer (≥ 1.4 s on a 1.5 s delay), does not hold up a monitor that answers at once, and reports a dead QEMU promptly. It also asserts the launcher consults the monitor before the Ready line.
- The two launcher contract tests stage the new library into their bundle, and their fake QEMU now answers the monitor with a greeting, as QEMU does.
- Verified on the affected machine on the exact trigger condition — first launch after installing the build — with stderr captured: Ready printed, no sleep-control failure, guest booted.

author: dspo
body:
## Why

The plan-mode chip in **dspo/manox-app** gains a pending state. A mid-turn plan-mode toggle is journaled as `plan_mode_request` and only committed at the next turn boundary (`commit_requested_plan_mode`); the projection already exposes that as `plan_mode_pending`. This crate owns the locale resources (`crates/manox-agent/locales/`).

## What

`plan_mode_pending` is **directionless** (`*enabled != committed`), so one term cannot describe both cases — `active=false, pending=true` is a queued switch-on, while `active=true, pending=true` is a queued exit that leaves writes blocked until the boundary. Four keys, enter/exit:

```
plan-chip-pending-enter-label   = Plan mode pending
plan-chip-pending-enter-tooltip = Takes effect next turn. Click to keep it off.
plan-chip-pending-exit-label    = Plan mode · leaving next turn
plan-chip-pending-exit-tooltip  = Writes stay blocked until the next turn. Click to stay in plan mode.
```

plus the zh-CN counterparts, and `locale_key_sets_agree`, which asserts both locales carry the same message set.

## On the parity test

A term added on one side only degrades **invisibly**, and differently per side:

| missing from | renders |
|---|---|
| `en.ftl` | the raw key |
| `zh-CN.ftl` | the **English string** — `init_with` attaches an en fallback bundle whenever the locale is not en |

So for a Chinese reader a dropped translation ships silent English chrome, not something visibly broken. Verified by probe: removing the zh-CN label and reading under `Language::ZhCn` returns `"Plan mode pending"`. `missing_key_returns_key` covers the mechanism but only for a key absent everywhere; nothing caught a key missing on exactly one side.

## Test Plan

- `cargo test -p manox-agent --lib i18n` — 8 passed
- `cargo clippy -p manox-agent --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `locale_key_sets_agree` **mutation-tested**: deleting a key from `zh-CN.ftl` fails with the key named; restored, passes.
- Fallback behaviour verified by probe (table above).

## Assumptions

- Keys read from source text rather than via `fluent-syntax`, which is not a direct dependency. Known limits recorded in the test's doc comment: a folded `key =` is missed, an indented `ident = ` continuation would be miscounted. Neither appears in the current files.
- Consuming PR: **dspo/manox-app#48**. Until this merges and the app bumps its rev, the labels resolve through the en fallback.

author: kumakumapon
body:
## Summary

#10 の Phase 0(BLE 接続 PoC)は既にマージ済みです。本 PR はその続きで、**MiniStack MOD が「PC の要求に答えるだけ」から「機器側で起きたことを自分から報告できる」状態**になります。タッチ、発話の開始/終了、命令の完了、写真。あわせて 2 KiB に収まらない写真・録音を同じ認証済みチャネル上でチャンク転送できるようにしました。

## スコープ(先に明示します)

#10 の「実装範囲」表のうち `hermes-mcp/`、`robot_service.py`、`stackchan_mcp.py`、`event_server.py`、`config.example.yaml`、`docs/stackchan-firmware.md` は **MiniStack リポジトリのファイル**です(issue 冒頭に「ファイルパスは MiniStack リポジトリを基準にしています」とある通り)。本セッションのリポジトリスコープは `kumakumapon/stack-chan` のみのため、PC 側常駐ブリッジと MCP は本 PR に含みません。本 PR は **stack-chan 側を完結させ、PC 側を書くのに必要な契約と検証クライアントを揃える**ところまでです。

## 設計上、記録しておきたい判断

**イベントは monotonic な id を持ち、PC が ack するまで MOD が保持します。** 配送は at-least-once、重複排除は id による PC 側 — これが「完了した命令はちょうど一度だけ通知される」を、応答が落ちた場合でも成立させます。id は**ブートセッション内**で単調なので、再起動すれば PC は古い id をまとめて捨てられます。

**溢れたときは最古を捨て、最新は残します。** 判断が待っているのは最新だからです。そして捨てたことを記録し、`events.since` が `gap: true` として報告します。ここが無いと、古いカーソルで再接続した PC が「二度と送られてこない完了通知」を「まだ完了していない」と読みます。**ack 済み id と drop 済み id は別々に追っています** — 同一視すると、ack でバッファが空になった後に損失が「何も起きていない」に化けます(実装中にこれを作り込んで、テストで潰しました)。

**写真・録音は pull 型のチャンク転送です。** #10 が挙げる「ローカル HTTP の短命アップロード」か「分割ストリーム」のうち後者を選びました。認証されない別チャンネルを新設せずに済み、オフセット指定の読み出しは冪等なので応答落ちのコストが1チャンクで済みます。カメラフレームの `close()` はレジストリが解放時に呼びます — 参照を捨てるだけではハードウェアバッファがセッション中ずっと漏れます。

**長押し停止は `receive('stop', …)` を経由しません。** 要求は重複排除のため request ID を記録しますが、物理ボタンには重複排除すべき ID がありません。1押しごとに記録すると数百回で256件の履歴が埋まり、**PC 自身のコマンドが `session-full` で締め出されます**。実装レビューで見つけて直し、300回の連続ローカル停止後も PC が応答を得られることをテストで固定しました。

**イベント送出は1件ずつ、id 順です。** `session.send` はリトライ付き非同期なので、並行送信は順序を崩します。PC の状態機械はその順序の上に建っています。送信失敗はイベントを元の位置に残す(削除するのは ack だけ)、送信済み未 ack は ack 済みと別管理(でないと毎tick再送し続ける)。この論理は無線なしでテストできるので、MOD から `controller.js` に引き上げて固定しました。

## 誠実に「できない」と書いたもの

- **`speech.say` の割り込みは効きません。** MOD 向けの音声 API は `say`/`sing`/`tts.stream` のみで、再生中の発話を止める手段がありません。`interrupt` は受理しますが結果は `interruptHonoured: false` を返します。効いたふりはしません。
- **`transcript` イベントはありません。** MOD に音声認識はなく、#10 自身のフローも `audio.record → PC STT → Hermes` です。録音は PC が書き起こすためのバイト列として提供します。**これは #10 のイベント一覧からの意図的な逸脱**です。
- **`connection.changed` も持ちません。** 接続したことは `ready` が伝えており、切断したことは伝えようがありません(伝える経路が失われているため)。届かない種別を宣言しても待つ側を誤らせるだけです。

## What Changed

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `controller.js` | `createEventOutbox`(id / ack / replay / gap)、`createEventPump`(順序・リトライ)、`createTransferRegistry`(チャンク・TTL・解放)、`cancel()`、新規リクエスト7種の検証 |
| `mod.js` | イベント送出、タッチ長押し判定と停止、`conversation.listen`、`photo.capture`、`face.set` の色、`config.set` の適用、base64 エンコーダ、ライフサイクルでのハードウェア解放 |
| `web/ministack/` | イベント重複排除・順序整列・ack、`gap` の明示警告、チャンクダウンロードと画像プレビュー、新規操作 UI |
| `README_ja.md` | プロトコル全面更新(エラーコード一覧、履歴を消費する要求/しない要求、イベント規則、転送、タッチ、制限事項) |

## Verification

- [x] `cd firmware && npm run lint` — 729ファイル、info 1件のみ
- [x] `cd firmware && npm test` — **585 pass**(MiniStack MOD 分 49 件を含む。新規テストは `firmware/package.json` の `test:unit` に登録済み)
- [x] `cd firmware && npm run check:legacy-names` / `check:architecture` — 78 pass
- [x] `cd web && npm run test:legacy` 246 pass / `test:react` 125 pass / `typecheck` clean / `build` clean / `check:editor-artifacts` clean

**未検証(実機):** 本 PR で追加した機器側の機能は **CoreS3 実機で一度も動かしていません。** タッチ長押しの判定と停止、録音、撮影、`config.set` の適用、イベントの実送出、実際の GATT フラグメントサイズ下での混在トラフィックは手動確認が必要です。テストで固定されているのはプラットフォーム非依存のロジック(調停、イベント outbox、送出ポンプ、転送レジストリ、ブラウザ側の重複排除とチャンク再構成)だけで、これらはハードウェアの動作を保証しません。Phase 0 で実機確認済みの BLE 接続・表情・首動作・サーボ診断には手を入れていません。

実機確認の手順は `README_ja.md` の「実機試験」節にあります(新機能が未検証である旨も追記済み)。

## Affected Areas

- [x] firmware
- [x] web
- [ ] schematics
- [ ] case
- [ ] docs
- [ ] ci/github-actions

## Breaking Changes

- [x] none
- [ ] yes, described below

既存の Phase 0 プロトコルは互換です。`capabilities.get` に `events` / `transfers` / `touch` が増え、`modVersion` が `0.2.0` になります。

## Related Issues

- #10(Phase 1–2 の機器側。PC 側ブリッジと MCP は MiniStack リポジトリのため未着手)

body:
## What changed

`.y-severity--error` and `.y-severity--warn` shared `color: var(--warn)` /
`background: var(--warn-bg)` and differed only by a 1px border, so on
`/health` the two weights read as the same colour at a glance. `error` now
paints with the correction tokens (`--gold-ink` over
`color-mix(in oklch, var(--gold) 18%, transparent)`, `border-color: --gold`)
and its marker dot is squared (`border-radius: 1px`, the same value
`.ui-status--ready::before` already uses for its heavier state); `warn` is
unchanged and keeps its round dot. Neither token's own value moved, so
`.yomihon mark` (which also uses `--gold`/`--gold-ink`) is untouched and the
two dark entrances (`[data-theme="dark"]` / `prefers-color-scheme`) stay
declaration-for-declaration identical — `darktokens_test.go` needed no
change. No class was added, so the `internal/ui/pages/testdata/render`
health-page goldens are byte-identical.

## How it was checked

Measured against a live `/health` (`.github/e2e/vault`), not computed:
`contrast-contract.mjs` can't be pointed at `/health` directly — its
`requireCoverage` needs fenced-code tokens `/health` has none of, confirmed
by running it there and watching it report `BROKEN … no diff token was on
any measured page`. Reused its own canvas-raster + WCAG-luminance method in a
throwaway script instead: in both themes, error's ink clears 4.5:1 against
its own composited badge wash (light 5.53:1, dark 8.09:1) and against the
page background (light 6.52:1, dark 10.81:1); `contrast-contract.mjs` itself
still passes unmodified, confirming no regression from the token reuse.

`/health` was screenshotted at 1280 and 390, light and dark, both the
unsorted view (warn rows near the top) and `?sort=severity` (error rows at
the top) — inspected directly, not embedded in this PR: no supported `gh`
path uploads a binary into a comment, and hosting them would have meant an
orphan branch, a release, or PNGs committed to the tree, none of which is a
real deliverable of this change. Regenerate them with:

```
go build -o /tmp/yomihon ./cmd/yomihon
YOMIHON_PORT=24193 ./tmp/yomihon serve --root .github/e2e/vault &
# then open http://127.0.0.1:24193/health and /health?sort=severity
# at 1280x900 and 390x844, in both yomihon_theme cookie values
```

The lock lives in `.github/e2e/health-table.mjs`, which already loads
`/health` and reads computed styles there: two new sites assert error's and
warn's computed `color` differ and their marker's computed `::before`
`border-radius` differ, with one mutation apiece.

| mutation | site | result |
|---|---|---|
| `revert-error-ink` (`.y-severity--error{color:var(--warn)}`) | `error-and-warn-paint-different-inks` | caught — `FAIL … both paint oklch(0.47 0.125 70)` |
| `revert-error-marker` (`.y-severity--error::before{border-radius:50%}`) | `error-and-warn-draw-different-markers` | caught — `FAIL … both draw a 50% marker` |
| `restore-table-layout` | `stacked-cells-name-their-column` | still caught (pre-existing) |
| `unpin-the-evidence-column` | `evidence-sits-beside-the-finding` | still caught (pre-existing) |
| `stretch-the-weight-badge` | `the-weight-is-a-badge-not-a-banner` | still caught (pre-existing) |
| `show-the-empty-cells` | `no-label-over-an-empty-cell` | still caught (pre-existing) |
| `widen-the-cells` | `no-sideways-scroll` | still caught (pre-existing) |
| `drop-the-ordering` | `a-heading-reorders-the-rows` | still caught (pre-existing) |

`MUTATE=list` on the file lists all 8 modes; every run above exited 1 with
`MUTATE-RESULT: caught <mode>` on its own line, and the plain (no `MUTATE`)
run passes.

Also run: `go test -race -shuffle=on ./internal/ui/...` (covers the health
goldens and `darktokens_test.go`) — pass; `make css-check` — pass;
`make stylelint-check` — pass; `biome lint` on the changed `.mjs` — pass. No
`.templ` file changed, so the comment-style hook had nothing to run against;
the one issue-number reference it would have caught in `.mjs` (which the
hook does not cover) was caught on self-review instead and fixed in a
follow-up commit.

One caveat worth recording: the marker's squared/round distinction is drawn
with `background: currentcolor`, which a printer that drops background
graphics (a real default in some setups — checked with an actual
`page.pdf({printBackground:false})` render) drops too. The channel that
survives paper regardless is the badge's own `border`, present on `error`
and absent on `warn` — a mechanism this change kept, not one it added. The
CSS comment says so.

body:
> ​<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:start -->Opened on behalf of @daniel-lxs.<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:end --> Follow up by mentioning @roomote-roomote, in [the web UI](https://roomote.roomote.ai/sessions/1c82e6dd-e088-46e7-8587-73720def03d5?utm_source=github-comment&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=snapshot_resume), or in [Telegram](https://t.me/roomote_roomotebot).

## What changed

Abort credential-egress bootstrap admission when the corresponding detached Modal worker exits before claiming its task run. The exit handler now registers its asynchronous classification before aborting admission, waits for classification before returning, and treats cleanup failure as secondary after a restart has been scheduled.

## Why this change was made

Preview telemetry showed a worker launch that remained in-flight for roughly 20 minutes after the detached worker had already exited. Review identified two recovery races: admission could abort before restart classification completed, and cleanup rejection after restart scheduling could re-enter generic spawn failure.

## Impact

Worker recovery no longer waits for the full credential-egress timeout and cannot be terminally failed by cleanup errors after a guarded restart is scheduled. Regression coverage exercises both race conditions. Retry behavior remains bounded by the existing atomic bootstrap restart policy, and Slack message sizing and rate limiting are unchanged.

body:
## Summary
- A file may now contain several `entity`/`architecture` pairs: one top-level design plus the sub-components it structurally instantiates via `label: ComponentName port map (...)`, either positionally or by name.
- A `component ...  end component;` declaration in an architecture's header is parsed and discarded, since the instantiation statement's own syntax already gives everything needed; what the component actually does comes from a real matching entity/architecture elsewhere in the file.
- Flattening happens as a new parse-to-build stage (`flattenVhdl.ts`): the top-level entity is the one no other entity instantiates, and every instance's internal ports/signals are renamed uniquely per instance before being inlined into one flat design - so ten instances of the same component become ten independent copies, not one shared circuit aliased across all of them. This keeps the existing single-namespace builder completely unchanged.
- Also relaxes `inout` ports to be treated as an ordinary `out`, since this simulator has no bidirectional-wire concept, and a design that only drives (never reads back) its own `inout` port - the common case - loses nothing by the substitution.

- [x] `npx tsc -b` passes
- [x] `npx oxlint` passes
- [x] `npx vitest run` - 100/100 tests passing, including new coverage for positional and named port maps, independent per-instance state, `inout`-as-`out`, a missing-component error, arity/mixed-association errors, duplicate instance labels, and both direct and indirect instantiation cycles

body:
## Work order

Round 4 of the brief self-sufficiency loop (`tests/brief/state/rounds.md`).
The quote checks from #1721 read sentence/quote pairs that were a hand-written
fixture; this makes the pipeline produce them.

## Changed

`s8-evidence.ts` turns captions into verbatim runs. No model touches it — a
model that rewrites a caption line while extracting it produces a quote that is
not in the source, which is the exact defect the quote check exists to catch.
Regex and slicing only, so the same captions always yield the same rows and a
re-run spends nothing.

A run is kept when it carries a number, a unit, or a capitalised name.
Everything else is narration, and an evidence table full of narration is a
table nobody reads. Twelve runs per video, two hundred characters each — past
that it is not a quote, it is republishing.

`caption-source.ts` is where the text comes from, and the policy shaped it:
full captions live on the Mac Mini and nowhere else. This fetches, hands over,
and keeps nothing.

**The collector endpoint does not exist.** v2.1 section 2 calls for
`GET /captions/:videoId`; the Mac Mini runs the fetcher as a LaunchAgent
writing to a local file cache with no server in front of it (confirmed over
SSH: `com.insighta.transcript-svc` is the collector, and the only listeners are
unrelated). So this ships the interface and a `noCaptions` null source, and the
ledger records how many videos had no caption rather than pretending they all
did. Guessing at that endpoint's shape would be worse than recording it as
missing.

## Verified

- `npx jest tests/unit/modules/newsletter --ci` — 162 tests, 16 suites, all
  pass. 16 are new.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors.
- `npx tsx scripts/brief-loop/measure.ts` — 20/20, unchanged. This round adds
  material, not checks.
- **The tests found a real defect.** The unit pattern wrapped Korean unit words
  in word-boundary anchors. Those are defined on word characters, and Hangul is
  word characters throughout, so the anchor was never present and the pattern
  never matched inside a Korean number-plus-unit token — every Korean unit was
  being missed. Latin units keep their boundaries; Korean ones match bare.
- Sixteen tests on one property: a run must be findable in its caption,
  character for character. Offsets land on the run; captions without
  punctuation still split; a long run is cut at a word boundary rather than
  through a figure; decomposed Hangul matches composed; two runs agree. The
  source tests assert that "collector is down" and "video has no captions" are
  recorded differently — conflating them would let an outage read as full
  coverage.

## Not verified

- No caption has passed through this in production. With no collector endpoint,
  a real run produces zero evidence rows, and that is what the ledger will say.
- The stage is not in the pipeline sequence yet. It is constructed by
  `makeS8Evidence` and exercised by tests; wiring it into `buildPipeline`
  belongs with the endpoint that feeds it.
- T1 is unchanged at 0. This round builds the material a draft stage will need,
  not the draft stage.

## Spec

`docs/spec/weekly-brief/implementation-v2.1-2026-09-08.md` section 2 (host
split, caption retention) and section 4 W5 (evidence). Section 2's collector
endpoint is the acknowledged gap above.

author: ericpsimon
body:
Implements VISE-226: fleets can now provision hosts without a human copying a vhost_ token per machine.

## What

- **Enrollment tokens** (`enrollment_tokens`, migration 0003): workspace-scoped, reusable secrets with a `venroll_` prefix, stored only as a SHA-256 hash and shown exactly once at mint. Optional `max_uses` (NULL = unlimited), a `uses` counter, and `revoked_at`.
- **Mint / list / revoke** (`POST`/`GET /hosts/enrollment-tokens`, `POST /hosts/enrollment-tokens/{id}/revoke`) sit behind the caller-identity seam like the rest of the fleet routes: scoped to the caller's workspace, 401 without the API token when `VISE_API_TOKEN` is set. Listings never carry secret material.
- **Exchange** (`POST /hosts/exchange`) is deliberately outside the seam — the enrollment secret in the request body *is* the credential. A booting host posts its `venroll_` secret (plus optional `name_prefix`) and receives a fresh `vhost_` token + host identity, shown once, exactly like hand enrollment. The host lands in the token's workspace with `ephemeral = true` and a generated `{prefix}-{random}` name (retried on per-workspace collision). Unknown, revoked and exhausted tokens all get an undifferentiated 401.
- **No race past max_uses**: the check-and-increment is a single `UPDATE ... WHERE revoked_at IS NULL AND (max_uses IS NULL OR uses < max_uses)`, so concurrent exchanges serialize on the row lock; covered by a 12-way concurrent test.
- **Reaper** in vise-server (pattern-matched on the lease sweeper): every 60s, deletes ephemeral hosts not seen for `VISE_EPHEMERAL_HOST_TTL_SECS` (default 3600, documented in `.env.example`; `created_at` counts for hosts that never checked in). Non-ephemeral hosts are never touched. `sessions.host_id` carries no FK, so deletion leaves finished sessions' host id as a historical string; a host still holding a *running* session is spared so the lease sweeper decides that session's fate first — the next pass then reaps the host.
- **CLI**: `vise hosts tokens ls|create|revoke` (with `--max-uses`, `--token-only`) and `vise host enroll --token venroll_... [--name-prefix ...]`, matching the existing once-only token display style.

## Why

Reusable tokens make host provisioning scriptable (cloud-init, autoscaling groups) without handing out the API token, and ephemeral + reaper keeps the fleet list from accumulating dead autoscaled hosts.

## Testing

`just check` green: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (108 tests, 14 new: 11 core-level on exchange/revocation/max_uses-race/reaper, 3 HTTP-level, plus extended auth and migrations tests), sqlx cache and OpenAPI spec regenerated.

Refs: VISE-226

body:
## What

- **`ui/nginx.conf`.** In production Caddy terminates TLS and forwards `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, but nginx overwrote it with its own `$scheme` (http), so the API never learned the public scheme and built redirects as `http://`. A `map` keeps the upstream value when present and falls back to `$scheme` when nothing is in front (dev/test with the port published directly). Pairs with the `ProxyFix` change in `imls-dmt-api`.
- **`AuthService.logout`.** Requested `/api/logout` without the trailing slash; Flask's 308 to `/api/logout/` changed scheme behind the proxy and the browser refused it, leaving the server session alive ("Logout may not have completed on the server: Network Error"). The route is called directly now.

Applied by hand on the `master` checkout and rebuilt. Logout succeeds on both `www.dmtc-prod.org` and `www.dmtc-devel.org`; the built bundle references `/api/logout/`.

body:
## 症状

選択肢の設問に音声で「なし」「特になし」と答えると、AI が **「（黙って待つ）」** とチャットに出し、そのまま読み上げる。

## 原因 — **前回の修正（`eab0988` / PR #245）がこちらの誤りでした**

そのコミットで足した A-2 の一文:

> ユーザーが声で答えただけのターンは、こちらから依頼が届くまで**黙って待つ**。

**これはト書き（行動の描写）です。** モデルは台本の一部と読んで、そのまま発話しました。

## さらに、前提から間違っていました

発注者のご指摘「**そもそも、黙って待っててはダメでしょ？**」が正しく、実装を確認するとそのとおりでした:

```
live-controller.ts:713   sendModelTurn(msg, next.id);   ← silent ガード無し
```

**音声回答でも、必ず次の質問の読み上げを依頼しています**（依頼文は音声・タップで同一・出し分けない＝2026-09-04 の確定事項）。つまり正しい姿は沈黙ではなく **「次の質問を読む」** で、沈黙を指示すると **声で答えたのに何も返ってこない** 状態を作ります。**A-2 は前提から誤りだったので撤回します。**

## 直したこと

- **A-2（沈黙の指示）を削除。** 旧 A-3（進行状況を自分で判断しない）を A-2 に繰り上げ。
  → **前回の実障害（AI が勝手に「これで問診は完了です」と言う）を止めているのはこちら**なので残します
- **E を「何をしないか」ではなく「何を言えばよいか」の形に書き直し**、**音声で答えたときも次の質問の依頼が届く**ことを明記
- 【問診完了時】の補足を 1 文に短縮（説明が長いほど読み上げられる余地が増えるため）

### 直したあとのプロンプト（該当部）

```
A-2. 問診の進み具合を自分で判断しない。「これで完了です」「最後の質問です」…を絶対に発話しない。

E. ユーザーの回答を復唱しない。確認の聞き返し・お礼・相づち・状況説明もしない。
   回答内容は画面に表示されるので、音声で繰り返すと二重になる。
   発話するのは、こちらから届いた依頼文が指示する内容だけ。
   ユーザーが声で答えたときも、こちらから次の質問の依頼が届く。それを読み上げればよい。
```

## 教訓を検査にしました

**プロンプトにト書き（`黙って` / `無言` / `沈黙` / `何も言わ` / `返事をしない`）を書かない**ことを機械で固定しました（`verify:interview-speech` ④）。**書き戻す退行を注入して、名指しで落ちること**を確認済みです。

> 散文で書いた指示は、**書き方しだいでそのまま音声になる**。これは今回学んだことで、検査にしておかないと同じ形で再発します。

## 検証

| | |
|---|---|
| `verify:interview-speech` | 全通過（ト書きを書き戻すと落ちる） |
| `verify:interview-ui` | 63 / 63 |
| `verify:interview-live-transport` | 53 / 53 |
| `astro check` / `astro build` | 0 errors / 成功 |

変更は `src/scripts/chat/live-controller.ts`（プロンプトのみ）と `scripts/verify-interview-speech.mjs` の 2 ファイル。**プログラム側のターン制御は 1 行も足していません。** DB migration なし / Edge Function 変更なし。

## 限界（正直に）

プロンプトは確率的で、モデルが従う保証はありません。**効果は実機でしか分かりません。** 2 回続けてプロンプトで直しているので、これでも再発する場合は、対症的な書き足しを続けるのではなく、3.8 の proactive audio（関連しないと判断したら応答しない）まで含めて段取りどおり別途扱うのが筋だと考えます。

author: x-lightyear
body:
## Summary

- prevent stale consumer progress requests from overwriting newer diagnostic results
- track request ownership per instance/group diagnostic context
- add deterministic regression coverage for overlapping progress requests

## Root cause

`ConsumerPage.loadProgress` allowed overlapping requests for the same diagnostic context to update `progressByGroup` in completion order.

An older request could therefore complete after a newer "Re-diagnose" request and overwrite the newer result.

## Fix

Track the latest progress request generation per existing `cacheKey`.

Only the request that still owns the latest generation is allowed to update progress or surface an error.

## Testing

- added deterministic deferred-Promise regression coverage for stale progress responses
- `ConsumerPageDiagnosticsRace.test.tsx`: 1 passed
- `ConsumerPage.test.tsx`: 32 passed
- frontend lint: 0 errors
- `npm run build`: passed

Fixes #4545

author: vavallee
body:
## Summary

The Authors page scrolled sideways on a phone: the title was clipped on the left and Merge, Add Book, Add Series, Add Author, Refresh all metadata and the view toggle ran off the right edge. The header was a `flex items-center justify-between` row with no wrapping, so the title and a six control toolbar had to share one line. This gives it the layout Books, Series and History already use, and fixes the same shape on Calendar, Discover and the Search Indexers form.

Originally opened on `feature/grouped-nav` so the two previewed together on dev; now rebased onto `main` on top of the #2679 squash. No Go or API changes.

## What changed

| Page | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| Authors | `flex items-center justify-between mb-4`, toolbar `flex-wrap justify-end` | outer row wraps with `gap-3`; toolbar `w-full sm:w-auto justify-start sm:justify-end`, so below `sm` it drops onto its own lines under the title |
| Calendar | same rigid row; month label fixed at `w-36` | same wrapping header; label `w-28 sm:w-36` |
| Discover | same rigid row | same wrapping header; Refresh button `shrink-0` |
| Search Indexers | `flex-1` input with no `min-w-0` | `min-w-0` on the input, `shrink-0 whitespace-nowrap` on the button |

Every button is still present, in the same order, doing the same thing. Nothing was moved into an overflow menu: `MoreMenu` would have meant either changing the desktop layout too or rendering each control twice behind responsive `hidden` classes, which would give the existing page tests two matches per button name.

## Measured, at 320 / 360 / 390 / 430 px

Headless Chromium against a real binary with three seeded authors, comparing `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` to `clientWidth` and listing every element whose right edge crosses the viewport.

Pages checked: Authors, Books, Series, Wanted, Queue, History, Calendar, Discover, Import, Requests, Users, Settings, Search, author detail.

Overflowing before: Calendar at 320 (month controls), Search at 320, 360, 390 and 430 (the form), and Wanted, Queue, History and Requests at 320. Overflowing after: Wanted, Queue, History and Requests at 320 only, all four from the same element, the nav tab strip, which #2679 has since fixed on main (see below).

One honest caveat: Chromium at 390 does not reproduce the Authors overflow, and the "before" screenshot shows the toolbar wrapping into four tidy lines that fit. The reported device is iOS Safari, whose automatic minimum size for a wrapped flex container is known to differ. The structural defect is real either way, the layout here is engine independent because `w-full` gives the toolbar a definite width that no min content rule can exceed, and Authors was the only page header left that could not wrap.

## Deliberately not touched

The 320px overflow on Wanted, Queue, History and Requests came from the `NavTabs` strip, not a page header, and #2679 has since fixed it on main with `max-w-full overflow-x-auto`. Nothing here touches that component.

No `overflow-x: hidden` or `clip` on the app shell. It was asked for as a guard, and I think it is the wrong one here: it does not prevent a regression, it hides one. NavTabs is the example of what it would cost, because a clipped page turns a tab you can reach by scrolling into one you cannot reach at all. The guard in this PR is a test instead.

## The guard

`web/src/pages/pageHeaderWrap.test.ts`. jsdom does no layout, so a rendering test cannot measure an overflow and one that pretended to would assert nothing. What it can hold is the structural rule: it finds every page header row (a `flex` div with `justify-between` immediately followed by an `h1`/`h2` page title) and fails if one cannot wrap. A first assertion pins the number of headers found, so the regexes going stale is a failure rather than a silent pass over an empty list.

## Fail before evidence

With only the three header fixes reverted and the test in place:

```
FAIL  src/pages/pageHeaderWrap.test.ts > page header rows > lets every title-and-toolbar row wrap
AssertionError: expected [ …(3) ] to deeply equal []
+ [
+   "./AuthorsPage.tsx:352 flex items-center justify-between mb-4",
+   "./CalendarPage.tsx:88 flex items-center justify-between mb-6",
+   "./DiscoverPage.tsx:130 flex items-center justify-between mb-6",
+ ]
```

Both tests pass on the branch.

## Security

No auth, settings or user scoped surface is touched, and no handler is added or moved. The diff is Tailwind class lists on four pages plus one test file, so there is nothing for `RequireAdmin`, `owner_user_id` filtering or `trustedProxyMiddleware` to apply to.

## Performance

No new renders, requests or dependencies. One additional test file, 7ms.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Doc-update gate cleared (no documented behaviour changes; changelog.d fragment added)
- [ ] Wiki pages updated if user-facing behaviour changed (no wiki page covers page layout)

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` (93 files, 1071 tests, all pass, rerun after the rebase)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd web && npm run build`
- [x] `npx eslint` on the touched files (0 errors; one pre-existing `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning in AuthorsPage on untouched code)
- [x] `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...`
- [x] Real binary on a fresh data dir with seeded authors, screenshotted at 390px in light and dark

## Summary

Extracted duplicate CSS from individual dashboard pages into a centralized design system (`govbot.css`) and created a shared shell script (`govbot-shell.js`) for common interactions. This eliminates ~1800 lines of duplicated styling code across four pages while establishing a maintainable, cohesive visual identity.

## Key Changes

- **New `docs/src/dashboard/assets/govbot.css`**: Centralized design tokens (civic palette, typography, spacing, shadows) and reusable component styles. Includes dark-mode-first theming with light-mode overrides via `[data-theme="light"]` and OS preference detection.

- **New `docs/src/dashboard/assets/govbot-shell.js`**: Dependency-free shared interactions for all dashboard pages—theme toggle persistence, scroll-to-top button visibility, and optional page-specific hooks. Inlines a pre-paint snippet to avoid theme flash.

- **New `docs/src/dashboard/legislation.html`**: Refactored to use external stylesheet and shell script, removing ~1800 lines of inlined CSS.

- **Updated `docs/src/dashboard/index.html`, `hearings.html`, `elections.html`, `architecture.html`**: Replaced inlined color tokens and component styles with `<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/govbot.css">` and `<script src="assets/govbot-shell.js"></script>`. Removed duplicate `:root` color definitions and media-query blocks.

- **Added `docs/src/dashboard/assets/il-flag.png`**: Asset for elections dashboard.

- **Updated `CLAUDE.md`**: Clarified dashboard architecture and tab bar conventions (Legislation · Hearings · Elections · How Govbot Works, with color accents `.tab-legis`, `.tab-hearings`, `.tab-elections`, `.tab-arch`).

- **Minor updates**: Fixed page titles for consistency ("Govbot — Explore Legislation", "Govbot — Illinois Elections", etc.) and corrected a feed URL in `actions/scrape-elections/main.py`.

## Implementation Details

- **Design tokens** use CSS custom properties with civic palette colors (gold, blue, green, amber, red, purple) and legacy aliases (`--series-1` through `--series-8`) to keep existing chart/table CSS working without per-page edits.
- **Theme system** is dark-first; localStorage key `"govbot-theme"` stores user preference ("dark" | "light" | absent for OS follow).
- **No breaking changes**: All four pages maintain identical visual appearance and functionality; this is a pure refactor for maintainability.

## Purpose

kv_cache_memory_bytes is a planner budget. The final KV-cache allocation is constrained by cache layout and whole-block rounding, so it can be smaller than the configured value even when release works correctly.

1. Fix test_release_kv_cache_memory_preserves_generation to measure the actual mapped allocations tagged kv_cache.
2. Replace the incorrect assumption that kv_cache_memory_bytes must map to at least 99% of the requested budget.

author: derekperkins
body:
Part of the v0.2.0 plan in #49, revising it: the instance-wide `gatekeeper_enforcement` setting goes away instead of becoming `off | on`. This is the second PR from that plan and makes `CALL gatekeeper_enforce()` the only way a connection becomes enforced.

## Why

Having both a per-connection call and an instance-wide setting was two mechanisms for one job. If a host has to wire `gatekeeper_enforce()` into its connection factory for the mixed trusted/untrusted case anyway, the setting adds a second thing to reason about without adding a host that can use it:

- Any instance-wide value must either enforce the host's own connections (no in-process reader for the audit log, no way to change the policy afterwards) or depend on connection-open ordering, which is where #45's `new_connections` failed open.
- A setting is one more thing a trusted connection can be talked into flipping. The per-connection state is not a setting, so `RESET`, `lock_configuration`, and native option writes never touch it.
- The host's connection factory is already part of the sandbox boundary; putting the call there is the one thing every host can do, and the docs now say so.

What is given up: a host that cannot interpose on connection creation (a third-party tool calling `duckdb.connect()` itself) has no way to enforce. That population is narrow and was the one most exposed to the ordering hazard.

## Changes

- `src/enforcement.cpp`: removed the setting and its `SET` callback, the `ExtensionCallback::OnConnectionOpened` hook, the `'all'` sweep and its publish-before-sweep ordering, and the fail-closed parsing of natively written values. The `lock_configuration` posture warning names only `gatekeeper_policy`.
- Audit log: no `enforcement_changed` event; `policy_changed` is the only `*_changed` record.
- Tests: the mode, sweep, race, and setting-validation cases are replaced by per-connection isolation (`test_enforcement_is_per_connection`) and a pin that the setting no longer exists and that `lock_configuration` does not interfere with `gatekeeper_enforce()`. Audit tests record `RESET gatekeeper_policy` instead of the removed event.
- Docs: README (setup table, audit-log record table, the "Enforcing every connection" section removed), `docs/security.md` ("Enforcement semantics" states why there is no instance-wide setting; the internal-connection residual is reframed as opt-in per connection), the community descriptor (duckdb.org-style callouts, no "latch" wording), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`.

## Validation

- `scripts/build.py`: clean; `clang-format --dry-run --Werror`: clean.
- `pytest test`: 1034 passed, 4 skipped, 2 xfailed.
- sqllogictests (`build/release/test/unittest 'test/sql/*'`): 524 assertions in 8 test cases, all passed.
- `scripts/test_sanitized.py` (ASan/UBSan): 1034 passed, 4 skipped, 2 xfailed.
- `scripts/audit_inventory.py`: no drift (953 compiled defaults).
- Linked SQL fuzz smoke (`gatekeeper-fuzz` image, `fuzz_sql.py --seconds 60`): 5238 runs, no findings.

## Follow-up (PR 3, `feat/dry-run`)

`gatekeeper_dry_run` as designed in #49, minus the `off | on` change, which this PR makes moot.

body:
## What does this PR do?

Documentation and CI for the OpenSSF Best Practices badge (bestpractices.dev project 14695), which follows the OSPS Baseline v2026.08.28. Level 1 is already covered by the existing files; this closes the Level 2 criteria that only needed writing and all of Level 3 except the non-author approval (single maintainer):

- **SECURITY.md**: "Response Expectations" (which said we cannot commit to response times) becomes a **Response timeline** with targets, stated as targets for a volunteer project: acknowledgement within 7 days, assessment within 14, fix or mitigation within 90 days of confirmation, and a re-send path if a report goes quiet. For reference, Node.js publishes 5/10 days, Fastify 4 business days and 90 days to disclosure, date-fns 90 days. New sections: **Disclosure** (coordinated disclosure, GitHub Security Advisory with a CVE through GitHub's CNA, credit to the reporter), **Verifying a release** (`npm audit signatures`, the provenance panel on npmjs.com, the SBOM), **Secrets and credentials** (where the two secrets live, who can set them, when they rotate), **Dependency and static-analysis policy** (no high/critical advisory merged or released, allow-list rules, VEX statements, no accepted threshold of SAST findings) and a **Threat model** (assets, actors, entry points, threat/mitigation table). [VM-01.01, VM-04.01, DO-03.01/03.02, BR-07.02, VM-05.01/05.02, VM-06.01, SA-03.02]
- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: an **Architecture** section (layout, `_internals`, the generated datasets, the two utilities that do I/O and the actors around the code), the **Developer Certificate of Origin** sign-off (`git commit -s`) under commit messages, a **Governance** pointer, TruffleHog, the in-package SBOM and `check:vex` in the supply-chain list. [SA-01.01, LE-01.01, GV-03.02]
- **MAINTAINERS.md** (new): current maintainers, roles (contributor, maintainer, automation), how write access is granted (sustained contributions, review by current maintainers, 2FA, least privilege) and removed. [GV-01.01, GV-01.02, GV-04.01]
- **Security workflow**: new `secrets` job running [TruffleHog](https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog) (pinned by commit) over the commits of every pull request and push, and over the whole history on the weekly and manual runs; `.gitignore` excludes `.env` files. Second, tool-independent check next to GitHub's push protection. [BR-07.01]
- **OpenVEX document** (`openvex.json`, new): a `not_affected` statement (`component_not_present`, with impact statement) for each advisory suppressed in the dependency scanners, today the two extract-zip advisories (development-only transitive dependency of the browser test runner, absent from the published package, no patched release). `npm run check:vex` (`scripts/vex.ts`) fails when the VEX statements and the `audit-ci`/OSV-Scanner suppression lists disagree, and the Check workflow runs it before `audit-ci`. [VM-04.02]
- **SBOM inside the package**: the publish job generates `brazilian-utils.cdx.json` with `npm sbom` right before `npm stage publish`, and package.json lists it in `files`, so every version on npm carries its SBOM (the `sbom-<tag>` artifact stays). `vp pack`/publint accepts the entry. [QA-02.02]
- **context7.json** (new): ownership claim for https://context7.com/brazilian-utils/javascript (`url` + public key, read from the default branch) plus the parsing configuration Context7 takes from the same file, following its docs: `$schema`, title, description, `docs` folder only, `docs/pt-br` excluded like Context7's own i18n defaults, the root community files and the generated llms files excluded by name (setting `excludeFiles` drops the defaults), and rules for coding agents.
- **Context7 workflow** (new): POSTs to Context7's refresh endpoint on a push to `main` that touches `docs/`, `README.md` or `context7.json`, as its docs suggest. Needs the `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` secret; until it is set the job logs a notice and exits green.
- **Test robustness** (`src/_internals/test/arbitraries.ts`): the Mutation tests workflow failed on this PR in Stryker's initial dry run, the `subBusinessDays` "should never throw" property timing out at 5 s. `anyBusinessDayAmount` draws garbage from `fc.anything()`, whose doubles include values like `1e308` that pass `Number.isInteger`; each one walks day by day through the whole 1900–2099 range before returning `null` (40–70 ms uninstrumented), and a hundred property runs of instrumented code on four concurrent runners cross the timeout depending on the seed, so the same test passes on `main` and fails here. Integers beyond 1000 are now clamped to ±1000; the mutation score of both utilities stays at 100% (verified locally with `stryker run --mutate` on the two files, and the Mutation tests workflow is green on this PR since).

The commits carry the `Signed-off-by` line the guide asks contributors for. `vp check`, `knip`, `npm run check:vex` and `npm run build` pass; actionlint and zizmor (`--min-severity low`) pass on the workflows.

## Checklist

- [x] My commit/PR title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (e.g. `feat: ...`, `fix: ...`, `docs: ...`).
- [x] I added or updated tests covering this change (`npm test`). — the test-arbitrary change only; no runtime code changed.
- [ ] I updated the documentation if this adds/changes a utility, in **both**: — N/A, no utility touched.
  - [ ] `docs/utilities.md` (English)
  - [ ] `docs/pt-br/utilities.md` (Portuguese)
- [x] `npm run check` passes locally (format, lint, types).
- [ ] I ran `npm run build:llms` if I touched `docs/utilities.md` (the Check workflow fails when `docs/llms.txt` is stale). — N/A, `docs/` untouched.
- [x] This change does not introduce a breaking change, **or** I flagged it clearly below and it was discussed with maintainers beforehand.
- [x] This change does not add any runtime dependency (this library is zero-runtime-dependency by design).

## Additional context

Settings outside this PR that the docs and workflows assume:

- **DCO enforcement**: the guide asks for `Signed-off-by`, but nothing checks it yet. Installing the [DCO app](https://github.com/apps/dco) on the repository makes it a required check (the OSPS criterion says "MUST require"). Dependabot and release-please commits have no sign-off; the app can exempt them, or release-please can be given `signoff` in `release.yml`.
- **Push protection**: Settings → Code security → Secret scanning → Alerts and Push protection on. The TruffleHog job is the complement, not the replacement.
- **`CONTEXT7_API_KEY`**: from the Context7 dashboard, as a repository Actions secret; without it the Context7 workflow is a no-op.
- **MAINTAINERS.md** states that maintainers hold the `Admin` role, that the organization requires 2FA and that npm publishing is trusted-publisher only; all three match the current setup as far as the repository shows, please correct the file if any differs.
- The SBOM-in-package step runs only on the next release (it lives in the `publish` job), so its first real run is the next `chore(main): release` merge.

body:
## Why

#140 adds one `.build.ae` and both desktop legs die in Phase 1:

```
error: source file exceeds maximum token limit (50000 tokens)
aeb-link: FATAL — failed to compile the fan-out orchestrator
```

The orchestrator is a single generated main file and aetherc lexes a main file into a fixed 50,000-token array. Measured with the lexer over this tree's node list under aeb v0.297's generator: **main = 49,412 tokens, #140 = 49,770** (plus the root node). The tree was one node from the wall, and the error names no file because the file is aeb's.

## What

- `AEB_REF` → `9bfd8e88` (aeb main after aether-lang-dev/aeb#15, which emits the per-node bookkeeping once: same 138 nodes, **49,770 → 7,227 tokens**). A SHA until a tag is cut; `install.sh` takes one.
- `AETHER_REF` → `v0.681.0`, forced rather than chosen: every aeb since v0.302 compiles its own `aeb-main` against `bldr`, which imports `std.zip` (0.667), `std.strarr` (0.675) and calls `os.arch()` (0.681), so `make install` of that aeb needs it on PATH. Scanned the 0.646–0.681 notes: additive stdlib, a 4.5× faster type-check, `@c_callback` emitted weak, `-fPIC` on `--emit=lib` objects. No grammar or removed-API change this tree touches.

The matrix on this PR is the verification. If it is red on something the bump exposes, the fallback is a backport branch of aeb v0.297 carrying only the generator fix.

Compiler side: aether-lang-dev/aether#2059 asks for the main-file cap to be heap-allocated like the module one.

author: 99yash
body:
## Where this change sits

`@alfred/assistant` owns inbound receipt ingestion. Every verified inbound delivery becomes one `event_receipts` row and, in the same transaction, one `documents` row that the corpus sweep later embeds. `receipt-document.ts` writes that document; `inbound-receive.ts` (live webhook path) and `receipt-corpus-backfill.ts` (recovery sweep) are its two callers.

## Why this change is needed

`writeReceiptDocument` used to take an arbitrary `kind: string` and a separate `timezone: IanaTimezone`, both prepared by the caller. Today both callers are correct, but nothing in the type system stops a future replay caller from passing a qualified event type or another user's zone, which would silently change the document description and the cap-day assignment.

## What this change does

- Adds a branded `prepareReceiptProjection(facts)` to `receipt-document.ts`. It owns the kind precedence `rawKind ?? parseEventTypeName(provider, eventType) ?? eventType` and the single `resolveTimezone(userId)` call on the receipt path.
- Adds `ReceiptProjection` (opaque: constructed only by `prepareReceiptProjection`, carrying `provider`, `userId`, `kind`, `timezone`) and `ReceiptDocumentIdentity` (`id`, `payload`, `deliveredAt`, `accountId`).
- Changes the writer to `writeReceiptDocument(tx, projection, identity)`. It no longer accepts `kind` or `timezone`; the user is read from the projection, so the writer cannot pair a receipt and a zone from different users.
- Rewrites both callers to prepare the projection before opening their transaction, then pass projection + identity. Deleting `resolveTimezone` from both callers and `parseEventTypeName` from the backfill.
- `projectionKind` stays exported (the ownerless-delivery report still reads it); `parseEventTypeName` stays in contracts (still read by `inbound-deliver.ts`). No schema change, no migration.

Invariant: given any inbound receipt — a persisted `event_receipts` row or the row being inserted in the receive transaction — and any allowed sequence of `prepareReceiptProjection` / `writeReceiptDocument` calls, including a transaction that rolls back or a `resolveTimezone` failure, the `documents` row written for that receipt carries `kind = rawKind ?? parseEventTypeName(provider, eventType) ?? eventType` and an admission window that is the local day in `resolveTimezone(receipt.userId)` at admission time; no call can substitute a different kind or a different user's zone, and a failed projection writes no document (the receipt/document pair stays all-or-nothing).

Vocabulary ledger: before, a call site had to know `resolveTimezone`, the precedence `rawKind ?? parseEventTypeName(provider, eventType) ?? eventType`, `projectionKind`, and `writeReceiptDocument`. After, it knows `prepareReceiptProjection` and `writeReceiptDocument`; the backfill loses `parseEventTypeName`, both callers lose `resolveTimezone`, and the receive path keeps `projectionKind` only for the report, not the writer. Net: −2 domain names and −1 precedence rule at call sites, +1 owner name.

## Preserved behavior

- The kind derivation is unchanged; a typed row still writes the bare type and a raw row still writes its provider kind.
- The cap accounting, advisory lock, `onConflictDoNothing`, and document key are unchanged.
- `resolveTimezone` is now called before the receive transaction opens, so no pooled settings read happens while the transaction connection is held.
- No new tests (repository rule); `pnpm check` and `pnpm check-types` are the compile-time proof. Residual risk: the non-UTC cap day and the raw-vs-typed kind equivalence are not pinned by a committed test; the bounded DB probe could not run because Postgres is down on this machine.

Refs #995

Adds a **4th composer mode — Architecture** — that renders a system diagram showing how real-time telemetry feeds an MCP context broker feeds a human-approved agent loop. It ties the SLO Sandbox and MCP story together and signals principal/lead-level system design.

### Build choices (vs. the Mermaid draft)
- **Hand-built inline HTML/CSS, not Mermaid** — zero dependencies (the site stays a single dependency-free `index.html`), rendered in the site's own clay/cream palette instead of a dark catppuccin theme that would clash.
- **Vertical 3-tier flow** — stacks cleanly on mobile; overflow-audited at the rendered width (`scrollWidth == clientWidth`, no page widening).

### Grounded in the résumé (kept honest for a VP audience)
- **Tier 1 — Observability & Ingestion:** Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, Datadog, CloudWatch → fires on SLO error-budget burn.
- **Tier 2 — MCP Tooling & Context Broker:** `sre-toolkit` MCP server, FastAPI/Python, ServiceNow (incidents/problems/changes); computes burn-rate math and exposes typed tools (`calculate_burn_rate`, `get_cluster_health`, `fetch_p99_latency`).
- **Tier 3 — AI Agent Decision Loop:** Claude API agent loop, RCA automation, human-in-the-loop approval → **Validated** (agent-checked playbook, gated on one-click human approval) or **Escalate** (Slack/ServiceNow summary with the diagnosis).

Deliberately dropped from the original draft to avoid over-claiming: LangGraph, a vector DB, PagerDuty, and *autonomous* K8s remediation. Tier 3 is framed as *propose → human approves*, matching the human-in-the-loop work you actually shipped.

### Notes
- Also adds `flex-wrap` to the now-4-button `.mode-toggle` — the **same** one-line change as the mobile PR (#9), so the two merge cleanly in either order.
- `index.html` only: new CSS block, one toggle button, `setMode` handling, and an `archHtml()`/`showArchitecture()` renderer. Static content, no user input.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Three areas addressed across this PR:

### Bug fixes
- **dtype warning** — Added `dtype: 'q8'` to the `pipeline()` call so transformers.js doesn't warn about guessing the quantization format.
- **Progress bar frozen at 12%** — The CDN serving the embedding model doesn't send `Content-Length` headers. The old callback skipped all progress updates when `total` was null, leaving the bar stuck for minutes. The new callback derives a progress value from bytes received using an asymptotic curve so the bar visibly moves during the download.
- **No feedback while embedding a large document** — `loadDocuments` now emits a `STATUS` message every 5 chunks (`Embedding chunk N of 860…`), making it clear the system is working during long ingests like the full Frankenstein text.

### Status messages
- Added a `STATUS` worker message type (separate from `PROGRESS`) for phase labels like "Downloading embedding model…", "Downloading language model…", and per-chunk ingest progress.
- Wired a new `onStatus` callback through `FlyRAGSearchEngine` to the `index.html` status element.
- WebLLM's own progress text is forwarded as STATUS messages during LLM model download.

### Performance: pre-computed fly hashes
- **Before:** every `ask()` call re-hashed all ~860 chunk texts through the full fly-hash pipeline (build features + hash features for both query and candidate), burning 860 full hash operations per question.
- **After:** chunk fly hashes are computed once at ingest and stored as `Uint32Array` on each chunk. At query time, the query is hashed once into `queryBits`, then each chunk's stored bits are copied into `candidateBits` and `overlapPrecomputed()` is called — reducing per-query work to 1 query hash + 860 cheap (memcopy + popcount) passes.

New WASM exports: `hashCandidateBuffer`, `hashQueryBuffer`, `candidateBitsPtr`, `hashBitWords`, `overlapPrecomputed`. The existing `scoreFromBuffers` export is retained for compatibility. WASM compiles cleanly and a Node.js smoke test confirms `overlapPrecomputed()` produces identical scores to `scoreFromBuffers()`.

| Module | Before | After | Advisory |
|---|---|---|---|
| `otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploggrpc` | v0.20.0 | v0.21.0 | CVE-2026-81871 (MEDIUM, blocking) |
| `otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace` | v1.44.0 | v1.45.0 | CVE-2026-81870 (LOW) |
| `otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc` | v1.44.0 | v1.45.0 | CVE-2026-81870 (LOW) |

Dragged along by the same release train: `otel/log` and `otel/sdk/log` 0.20.0 → 0.21.0, `proto/otlp` 1.10.0 → 1.11.0, `genproto/googleapis/api` to the 2026-08-03 pseudo-version. `otel` core, `sdk`, `metric`, `trace` were already at v1.46.0. All entries are indirect (they reach us through lib-observability); no Lerian module moved.

Verification: `go build`, `go vet`, `go mod verify`, `make test-unit` (6506 tests) green. `make lint` reports the same 9 pre-existing gosec findings before and after.

body:
## Ringkasan

Menyiapkan seluruh kebutuhan UI ADR-015 sebelum melanjutkan fitur Fase 2,
sesuai permintaan eksplisit pemilik — supaya layar-layar berikutnya (T-2.5
dst.) langsung memakai bahasa visual final, bukan menambal belakangan.

Sebelumnya ini terpecah antara **D-2.1** (kanvas desain visual, belum
dikerjakan) dan **T-7.5** (kode, dijadwalkan akhir MVP: "kalau belum
dikerjakan langsung di fase masing-masing"). PR ini mengerjakan bagian
kodenya sekarang sebagai **T-2.12** (tugas baru, dicatat silang di kedua
tempat itu di `TASK_LIST.md`/`UI_UX_DESIGN_TASKS.md`).

## Apa yang berubah

- **`AppColorsExtension.pixelLight`/`pixelDark`** — palet ADR-015 penuh
  (`income`/`expense`/`overBudget`/`background`/`cardBackground`/
  `textPrimary`/`textMuted`), dibangun lewat `copyWith` dari `light`/`dark`
  ADR-0006 lama. Slot lama **tidak berubah** — ada uji regresi eksplisit
  yang menegaskan itu (`"slot asli (isian) TIDAK ikut berubah..."`), jadi
  nilai ADR-015 disimpan sebagai instance BARU, bukan menimpa di tempat.
  Ini menuntaskan keputusan terbuka T-2.2 soal kapan palet penuh diadopsi.
- **`PixelTheme`** (berkas baru) — widget yang membungkus subtree dengan
  `ThemeData` ADR-015 (palet + tiga peran huruf Space Grotesk/Plus Jakarta
  Sans/Space Mono + radius 4px + garis tepi 2px). Dipasang **satu kali** di
  `AppShellPage`. `Theme` bawaan Flutter otomatis diteruskan ke
  `showModalBottomSheet`/`showDialog` lewat `InheritedTheme.capture`
  (dibuktikan lewat tes) — beda dengan `Provider`/`BlocProvider` yang TIDAK
  diteruskan otomatis — jadi lembar CATAT dkk. ikut terbungkus tanpa perlu
  membungkus dirinya sendiri. `AppTheme`/ADR-0006 tetap tema global
  `MaterialApp`; layar lama sama sekali tidak tersentuh/berubah tampilan.
- **`AppHardCard`** (berkas baru) — kartu bergaris tepi 2px + bayangan
  keras offset, empat level elevasi ADR-015 (flat/card/interactive/
  bottomSheet), termasuk animasi "ditekan" untuk level interaktif.
- **`AppSegmentedProgressBar`** (berkas baru) — bilah progres blok 8px
  berjarak 2px, warna mengikuti ambang `income`/`pending`/`overBudget`.
  ⚠ Ambang "70–100%" mengisi celah kecil di teks ADR-015 sendiri (yang
  hanya eksplisit menyebut "70–90%" untuk `pending`) — didokumentasikan di
  komentar kelas, bisa ditinjau ulang.
- **Token baru** `AppRadius.pixelSm`, `AppBorder.pixelThick`,
  `AppElevation.pixelCard`/`pixelInteractive` — anggota BARU di kelas
  token yang sudah ada; nilai ADR-0006 lama (`AppRadius.sm`,
  `AppBorder.thick`, dst.) tidak berubah.
- `AppShellPage` dibungkus `PixelTheme` sekali di root — seluruh 4 tab dan
  lembar CATAT otomatis memakai bahasa visual baru.

## Belum dikerjakan (dicatat eksplisit)

- Kanvas desain visual D-2.1 itu sendiri (mockup di alat desain).
- Retrofit bentuk `AppButton`/`AppChip`/`AppCard` — baru warna dan
  tipografinya yang ikut ADR-015 lewat `PixelTheme` sekarang (karena
  ketiganya membaca `context.appColors`/`Theme.of(context).textTheme`),
  bentuknya (radius/lebar garis tepi) masih ADR-0006 karena ketiganya
  memakai token `AppRadius.smAll`/`AppBorder.thick` langsung, bukan lewat
  tema. Sisa pekerjaan T-7.5.

## Verifikasi

- `flutter analyze` — 0 isu.
- `flutter test` — seluruh tes lulus, termasuk tes baru yang membuktikan
  `PixelTheme` benar-benar berlaku di dalam `showModalBottomSheet` dan
  TIDAK memengaruhi layar di luar `AppShellPage`.
- `git diff --stat origin/main -- lib/features/{cycle,card,investment,grocery,income} lib/shared/goal`
  — kosong, invarian strangler Fase 1–2 terjaga.

## Catatan urutan merge

PR ini dibuat dari `main` (T-2.3), **belum** dari branch T-2.4 (#28, belum
merge) — keduanya sama-sama menyunting `app_shell_page.dart` untuk alasan
berbeda (T-2.4 menambah `ScopeWidget<RecordScope>`/`BlocProvider`, PR ini
menambah pembungkus `PixelTheme`). Siapa pun yang merge lebih dulu, yang
kedua kemungkinan perlu rebase kecil untuk menggabungkan keduanya —
`PixelTheme` sebaiknya jadi pembungkus TERLUAR, dengan `ScopeWidget`/
`BlocProvider`/`EffectListener`/`Builder`/`Scaffold` T-2.4 di dalamnya.

## Selanjutnya

T-2.5 (`features/transaction/`: daftar riwayat) sekarang bisa langsung
memakai `AppHardCard`/`AppSegmentedProgressBar`/palet pixel lewat
`PixelTheme` yang sudah terpasang di `AppShellPage`.
