author: ikaruga777
body:
## Summary

This replaces the parsing backend of `SolidScore::Parser::RubyParser`, moving from the whitequark `parser` and `ast` gems to Prism.

Prism is bundled with Ruby 3.3 and later, and on Ruby 3.2 it is installed from RubyGems, so the supported Ruby range (3.2 and up) and the CI matrix stay unchanged.
The branch has 11 commits, and the test suite stays green at every one of them.

### Two-step migration through the compatibility layer

Rather than rewriting against the native API in one go, the first step swaps in `Prism::Translation::Parser`.
It returns a parser-gem-compatible AST, so [a two-line change](https://github.com/ikaruga777/solid-score/commit/9ccbeeb) moves the backend to Prism without touching any analysis logic.
At that point the AST produced by the parser gem and by Prism's translation layer was identical for all 27 spec fixtures.
Any output difference introduced by later commits can therefore be attributed to the rewritten analysis, not to the parser swap.

- 16a9233 add prism as a runtime dependency
- 9ccbeeb swap only the parse backend, using the translation layer
- b938522 introduce `SolidScore::Parser::SyntaxError` so the runner and the RuboCop helpers no longer rescue the parser gem's exception class

### Native API components, one at a time

The old `RubyParser` held constant-name resolution, class body scanning, and method body analysis in one file.
The new implementation splits those responsibilities into four classes, each added with its own spec.

- 1533e6e `ConstantName` turns `ConstantReadNode` and `ConstantPathNode` back into an `"A::B"` string
- a998585 `MethodAnalyzer` takes a `DefNode` and produces a `MethodInfo` with parameters, instance variables, calls, effective line count, and branch count
- 7c525f7 `ClassBodyScanner` builds a `ClassInfo` while tracking visibility modifiers, `attr_*`, `include`/`extend`, and Rails DSL calls
- 046fb6b `DefinitionCollector` is a `Prism::Visitor` that collects class and module definitions and assigns nested namespaces

`MethodAnalyzer` is the one component that does not inherit from `Prism::Visitor`.
Prism's visitor walks child nodes inside each `visit_*_node` method, so there is no single hook that sees every node.
A plain recursive `walk` ended up shorter ([method_analyzer.rb](https://github.com/ikaruga777/solid-score/blob/e827001/lib/solid_score/parser/method_analyzer.rb)).

### Switch-over and dependency removal

- c99e201 `RubyParser#parse_file` now uses `Prism.parse_file` and `DefinitionCollector`
- c4daf74h drop `parser` and `ast` from the gemspec
- e827001 update the ROADMAP and the plan document
- 6102d91 restore the namespace after an empty-bodied sibling definition; found by running the CLI on this repository, where `RubyParser` lost its namespace after `class SyntaxError < StandardError; end`

## Known differences and follow-ups

The output is not byte-for-byte identical to the old implementation.
Intentional differences and pre-existing issues deferred to separate PRs are listed in the [plan document](https://github.com/ikaruga777/solid-score/blob/e827001/docs/plans/2026-09-18-prism-native-parser.md#L31-L48).

The intentional differences are cases where the old output was an artifact of the parser gem's AST.
A superclass written as `::Foo` is now reported as `"::Foo"` instead of `"(cbase)::Foo"`, and a non-constant superclass such as `Struct.new(:a, :b)` is reported as its source text instead of an AST dump.
Argument forwarding in `def foo(...)` and destructuring in `def foo((a, b))` used to be dropped or to leak an AST node object as the parameter name; they now yield `[:forward_arg, nil]` and `[:mlhs, nil]`.
Safe-navigation calls (`&.`) are recorded as calls, which the old implementation skipped, and a `->` lambda counts as one statement instead of two.
These are pinned by the [edge cases block in ruby_parser_spec](https://github.com/ikaruga777/solid-score/blob/e827001/spec/solid_score/parser/ruby_parser_spec.rb#L270).

The rewrite also surfaced four issues that are independent of the parser backend.
`private def foo` consumes the visibility modifier and drops the method, methods inside `class << self` are ignored, the `type == :block` check in `ocp_analyzer` never matches the `:blockarg` symbol the parser emits, and the keyword check in `dip_analyzer` mixes `:key` and `:keyreq`.
All four keep their old behaviour in this PR.

## Why

The parser gem sometimes lags behind new Ruby syntax, and together with `ast` it added two external dependencies.
Prism is maintained in the Ruby repository itself, so new syntax is supported as soon as the Ruby version that introduces it.
Prism's `parse_file` reports syntax errors through `result.errors` rather than raising, so [RubyParser](https://github.com/ikaruga777/solid-score/blob/e827001/lib/solid_score/parser/ruby_parser.rb) formats the first error with file name, line, and column into a `SyntaxError`.

## Verification

Run the specs and RuboCop on this branch.

```
bundle install
bundle exec rspec
bundle exec rubocop lib/solid_score/parser spec/solid_score/parser
```

RSpec reports 270 examples, 0 failures, and RuboCop reports no offenses in the parser directory and the new specs.

To compare old and new output, run the CLI on `main` and on this branch and diff the JSON.

```
bundle exec exe/solid-score lib --format json > after.json
git switch main && bundle install
bundle exec exe/solid-score lib --format json > before.json
diff before.json after.json
```

The parser classes themselves differ because they were split up in this PR; the other 39 classes score identically.

The same comparison against a Rails application with 1366 Ruby files under `app/` (1946 classes) produced no score difference at all between `main` and this branch, with no syntax error warnings.
Wall-clock time dropped from 4.3s to 2.1s on that input.

author: basilechretien
body:
## Summary

Three data artifacts showed up in Basile's CV. All three come from the sources, and all three reach every user's CV the same way:

| Artifact | Where it came from | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **"ChréTien"** | An ORCID-less OpenAlex author profile (A5062007856) whose display name has a capital after "é" (a title-caser taking "é" for a word break). It arrives through three ORCID-discovered works, which are **carried across syncs verbatim**, so it never healed. | Case repair in `text/personName.ts`, applied at fetch, in `toCslName`, and on every read of a stored CV. |
| **"U\uFFFDda"** (a U+FFFD) | OpenAlex profile name "Kenji U�da"; the paper's byline says "Kenji Uda". | The printed name (`raw_author_name`) replaces a garbled profile name. |
| **Duplicated Cyrillic collaborators on RECOVER** | Crossref *and* OpenAlex list authors 9–13 again as 15–19 (a deposit error); the second Osamu Suzuki carries a Cyrillic profile name ("Осаму Сузукі"). | The printed name replaces a profile name in another script than a Latin byline, and a byline deposited twice is collapsed at fetch time. |

### What changed
- **`src/lib/text/personName.ts`**: `cleanPersonName` does the following:
  - composes decomposed accents (NFC) but keeps CJK compatibility ideographs;
  - decodes UTF-8 that was read as Windows-1252, word by word, only when the result is plausible (ordinary letters of one script);
  - repairs broken title-casing, only on uniformly mangled names;
  - drops a U+FFFD without ever emptying a name;
  - removes invisibles.

  Plain-ASCII names return at once, and the rest is memoised (bounded).
- **`src/lib/text/authorRuns.ts`** finds a byline printed twice. It needs a run of **≥ 3** names, at least two of them different, repeated in order, and a caller can veto a pair. Lists of more than 500 authors are never collapsed.
- **`src/lib/openalex/authorNames.ts`**, wired into both fetchers in `client.ts`:
  - chooses between the printed name and the profile name;
  - collapses a doubled byline, never across two different ORCIDs;
  - keeps the better-identified copy (one of the owner's author ids, then an ORCID) and merges the corresponding flag and affiliations;
  - re-derives first/last.
- **`src/lib/canonical/migrateAuthorNames.ts`**, in `migrateCanonicalDocument`, repairs name **strings** (author, editor, self-name variants) on every read. It never collapses a list. **Frozen snapshots skip it** (`safeParseCanonicalCv(doc, { frozen: true })`), so their content hash and any DOI still describe what they serve.
- **Claim-by-DOI** resolves the owner before fetching, so the owner's copy of a doubled entry is kept and the picked author index stays stable. `resolveAuthorByOrcid` cleans the header name.

### Adversarial review (three parallel reviewers), and what it changed
The first commit was too eager. The reviewers ran probes, including **1,681 live OpenAlex works (~258k authorships)**. Confirmed and fixed in the second commit:
- **Mojibake decode false positives on real names.** "LÍŠKA", "VÍŠEK" and "KRÍŽ" are valid UTF-8 as bytes and decoded to a combining mark; "Strauß–Meyer" decoded to an N'Ko letter. The plausibility check now rejects these.
- **Read-time collapse dropped real co-authors.** Stored names are *profile* names, and profiles collide on large collaborations: 10 distinct ATLAS authors were dropped in the sample. The collapse was also not idempotent and O(n³) on a crafted stored list (16 s). It is **removed**, so reads are ~1 ms now.
- **A run of 2 was too weak.** CMS 10.1016/j.physletb.2024.138633 prints "J. Wang, Z. Wang" twice, for four different people.
- **Accent-folded keys merged "Lü Wei" with "Lu Wei".** Keys now keep accents.
- **Case repair made all-caps names worse** ("GONZáLEZ" → "GONZálEZ") and left "éMile" lowercase. Both fixed.
- **Frozen snapshots were rewritten on read.** The claim flow could lose the owner's copy, non-string payload fields threw, and the owner's header name was not cleaned. All fixed.

On the reviewers' own probes the final code shows:
- no false positive on their real-name lists;
- hostile inputs done in ≤ 1 ms;
- the fetch → read cycle is idempotent on real works.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] New suites: `tests/person-name.test.ts`, `tests/openalex-author-names.test.ts`, `tests/migrate-author-names.test.ts`. The new modules are at 100% lines and branches.
- [x] Updated: `self-highlight-orcid` (the repaired name is highlighted), `cv-claim` (the owner is passed to the fetch), `snapshot-store` (frozen as frozen, live repaired), `resolve-author`.
- [x] Mutation check: 29 mutations (each rule disabled in turn), all 29 caught.
- [x] Full suite with coverage: 382 files, above the gate. See the note below for `repository-copies-pass`.
- [x] `npx knip` exit 0; Prettier clean.
- [x] Live OpenAlex check on Basile's 166 works:
  - 0 bad names;
  - RECOVER has 28 authors (was 33) and no Cyrillic;
  - the others render as "Uda, K." and "Chrétien, B.";
  - the 2,349-author CMS paper is untouched.
- [ ] After deploy: re-sync Basile's CV and confirm RECOVER shows 28 authors. The stored copy only collapses on a sync; its names are repaired as soon as it opens.

**Note:** `tests/repository-copies-pass.test.ts` › "bounds the token exchange…" fails under full-suite load on Windows and passes alone (4/4). It is a pre-existing clock-rounding flake in `defaultLookups`: `Date.now()` can report 19 ms of a 20 ms timer, so `left` is 1. It is unrelated to this change and flagged separately.

body:
## 摘要

修复 v1.8.234 → 31c4d1cc5e 发布审查发现的完整性、SSOT 与线上兼容问题：

- 移除余额进程锁，避免退款持有数据库连接、新预扣持有用户锁时互相等待；保留 PostgreSQL 原子事务与幂等结算。
- Gemini 流量别名改用 registry `_aliases` 指向完整价格 owner，消除标准价与其他价格字段各自维护的漂移。
- Studio 识别 Grok Video 1.5；两处账号测试共用模型排序及图片资格，接入指南支持 Nano 图片别名及 Gemini 协议识别。
- Prod PG overlay 从唯一源生成进 bootstrap，并在首次 systemd 启动加载；同步保留已有 env 覆盖，SSM 非成功结果返回失败。
- 滚动饱和计数使用版本化 Redis key，使 STRING 旧计数与 ZSET 新计数能在升级和回滚期间共存。

审批锚点：[Stage0 release-check remediation](docs/approved/stage0-release-check-remediation.md)。用户已授权修复、提交、推送及创建 PR。

## 风险

- 尚未合并或部署，未修改线上账号、模型映射或运行时价格配置。
- 余额写入恢复数据库行锁竞争，消除连接池与进程锁倒置；未改变账本/schema，无数据迁移。
- 新 Redis key 初始没有旧版软降权历史，短时间内可能重新尝试已有压力的账号；计数自然重建，不改变候选资格。
- 显式执行 PG tuning `--apply` 会 recreate PostgreSQL，可能短暂中断请求。应用镜像发布不会自动执行该维护操作；edge 不加载 prod 调优。
- Gemini 保持目标 owner 的既定标准费率，别名继承完整 owner 字段。线上已有完整 pricing registry 快照继续优先；运行时刷新需走既有 modelops 流程。

## 验证

- 完整 `scripts/preflight.sh`、`make test`（后端单测/lint、前端 lint/typecheck 与关键测试）通过。
- 真实 PostgreSQL 余额/预扣/结算集成测试通过；同一耗尽连接池回归用旧实现反测失败，修复后通过。
- Redis 新旧类型共存、价格别名及前端共享 owner 回归通过；账号测试实际提交图片提示词并渲染预览，指南生成正确 cURL/Python。
- Playwright 真实 Chromium：Grok Video 1.5 可见、可选、显示价格，页签切换后保持；已接入 CI，不调用付费生成接口。
- 前端生产 build、CFN overlay 生成/首次启动与 SSM 失败传播测试通过。

- 1268abeed3 fix(stage0): close release safety and SSOT gaps

author: dspo
body:
## Why

`ClientStore` mirrored 20 of the 21 projection keys the protocol declares. The missing one was `plan_mode_pending`, dropped by the merge match's `_ => {}` fallback — no compile error, no runtime warning, no test.

That key is the **only** channel through which a client can observe an outstanding plan-mode selection. A mid-turn toggle is journaled as `plan_mode_request` and committed at the next turn boundary (`commit_requested_plan_mode`), which emits **no notice in between**. So for the whole window the chip read the old `plan_mode` and a click looked like it had been ignored.

The pair is the wire's `{ active, pending }` view. dsh models the same thing as `PlanProjection { active, pending }` and its controller documents that "client carriers expose the projection's cropped `{ active, pending }` view" — this client was exposing half of it.

## What

- Mirror `plan_mode_pending` onto a `ClientStore` field.
- `render_plan_chip` becomes three-state: hidden when neither active nor pending; unchanged when active; a muted outline while a selection awaits the boundary.
- The pending state is **directional on read**: `plan_mode_pending` is directionless (`enabled != committed`), so `active && pending` means an exit is queued while plan mode still gates writes. The chip labels both directions separately, and in either a click cancels by re-selecting the committed value:

```rust
let target = if pending { active } else { false };
```

  Re-sending a bare `false` (the original implementation) re-requests an already-queued exit: mid-turn nothing changes, off-turn the request commits immediately and leaves plan mode outright. Neither is a cancel.
- The notice is gated on `active`, so cancelling a queued switch-on no longer claims "full write access restored" for access that was never taken away.
- `every_declared_projection_key_is_mirrored`: every declared key must reach a field or be listed as display-only. Mirroring is **observed**, not asserted from a hand-kept list — each key gets a probe in the shape its arm parses, and the store must react.

The guard is the durable half of this change. The bug existed because nothing tied the client's match arms to the protocol's key set; the first version of the guard compared two handwritten lists and could not see a deleted match arm, so it is now probe-based.

## Test Plan

- `cargo test` — 893 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- Guard **mutation-tested**: deleting the `plan_mode_pending` match arm while the key stays declared fails with the key named; the list-comparison version passed that case.

## Dependency — merge order is load-bearing

Needs **dspo/manox#813** for the `plan-chip-pending-{enter,exit}-{label,tooltip}` terms, then `cargo update -p manox-agent` to pick up the new rev. Locale resources live upstream per AGENTS.md.

**Without the bump, the pending chip renders the literal raw key** (`plan-chip-pending-exit-label`) under *both* UI languages, which is worse than today's localized "Plan mode". The currently locked rev `6dc76499` has none of the four keys in either `en.ftl` or `zh-CN.ftl`, so the en fallback cannot help — and under `en` no fallback bundle is attached at all (`init_with` only builds one when the locale is not `en`). Verified by probe at the locked rev:

```
LANG=En   -> "plan-chip-pending-exit-label"
LANG=ZhCn -> "plan-chip-pending-exit-label"
```

So the order is: **#813 → `cargo update -p manox-agent` → this PR.**

## Assumptions

- The pending state is worth showing as a distinct chip variant; the field mirror and guard stand on their own even if the visual treatment changes.
- `DISPLAY_ONLY_PROJECTION_KEYS` is empty — all 21 declared keys reach a field. An entry added later needs a stated reason.
- Verified at the code level only. The visual treatment and the manual mid-turn-toggle check were not exercised in a running GUI. author: parayi82
body:
## Summary

Implementación completa de las 6 fases del roadmap para la torre de control de logística de transporte de carga:

- **Fase 1 — Modelo de datos multi-tenant**: esquema en Supabase/Postgres (tenants, perfiles/roles, clientes, operadores, vehículos, turnos, geocercas con PostGIS, viajes/checkpoints, eventos, atrasos, evidencia, reportes, WhatsApp, auditoría) con Row Level Security en todas las tablas, por tenant y por rol.
- **Fase 2 — Dashboard en tiempo real**: `dashboard.html` con Supabase Realtime, semáforo de cumplimiento verde/amarillo/rojo por viaje según turno vigente.
- **Fase 3 — WhatsApp Business Platform**: Edge Function `whatsapp-webhook` con verificación de firma HMAC, identificación de operador por teléfono, y flujo guiado por lista interactiva (En tránsito / Detención / Reinicio / Evidencia / Ubicación).
- **Fase 4 — Motor de geocercas**: importador de GeoJSON (Google My Maps) con soporte de polígonos y puntos+radio, y validación automática de cada coordenada recibida vía trigger.
- **Fase 5 — Cálculo automático de atrasos**: trigger que, al recibir un evento `REINICIO`, calcula minutos de atraso contra la hora esperada (checkpoint planeado o umbral de protocolo).
- **Fase 6 — Reporte de turno en PDF**: Edge Function `generate-shift-report` que arma el PDF (pdf-lib) con las 6 secciones requeridas, lo sube a Storage y lo envía por WhatsApp a Jefatura/Seguridad Patrimonial, disparado por un barrido de `pg_cron` cada 5 minutos.

## Validación

Todo el trabajo se validó activamente durante el desarrollo (no solo se escribió):
- Las 18 migraciones se aplicaron end-to-end en un Postgres 16 + PostGIS local, con pruebas funcionales de RLS (aislamiento cross-tenant, visibilidad por rol/cliente), del motor de geocercas, del cálculo de atrasos, y de la infraestructura de scheduling (`shifts_due_for_report`, idempotencia del upsert, `pg_cron` real instalado con `shared_preload_libraries`).
- Ambas Edge Functions (Deno) pasan `deno check`/`deno lint` limpio.
- El frontend pasa `tsc --noEmit` y `npm run build` limpio, y se probó en un navegador headless real (Chromium), lo que expuso y permitió corregir un bug donde un fallo de carga del CDN de Leaflet tumbaba toda la página.
- El generador de PDF se probó generando un archivo real con datos ficticios (incluyendo acentos y paginación forzada), lo que expuso y permitió corregir un bug de codificación de caracteres (la fuente estándar no soporta "→" ni otros caracteres fuera de Latin-1).

## Configuración pendiente (no es código)

Documentada en el README: variables de entorno de Meta Cloud API (Fase 3), y los secrets de Supabase Vault (`project_url`, `service_role_key`) que deben crearse una sola vez desde el SQL Editor del proyecto real para que `pg_cron` pueda invocar la Edge Function de reportes (Fase 6).

## Nota sobre la rama base

Este repositorio estaba completamente vacío (sin commits) al iniciar el trabajo. La rama `main` se creó apuntando al primer commit de este trabajo (scaffold inicial del proyecto) para poder abrir este PR; por eso el diff incluye la totalidad del proyecto.

author: spyle23
body:
## Contexte

Deux constats non bloquants laissés par la revue de #809 (PR #1031), écartés à
l'époque parce que les corriger change un contrat.

**La limite de débit par adresse n'était pas atomique.** `requestPasswordReset`
lisait `password_reset_requested_at`, comparait au délai, puis écrivait. Deux
demandes simultanées sur la même adresse lisaient la même valeur, passaient
toutes deux le contrôle et armaient toutes deux : **deux courriers partaient**, et
seul le second jeton valait — l'écriture la plus récente écrasant l'empreinte de
l'autre. C'est la conduite que le premier critère de #809 cherchait à empêcher,
et la même classe de défaut que booking-engine §1 interdit au moteur de
réservation : une vérification applicative là où la base doit trancher.

**L'égalisation du temps de réponse promettait ce qu'elle ne fournissait pas.**
Le commentaire affirmait que la signature jetée rendait les deux chemins
indistinguables au chronomètre. Elle égalisait un HMAC — des microsecondes — et
laissait intacte une allée-retour en base — des millisecondes.

Closes #1034

## Ce qui change

- **Le seuil est replié dans le `where` d'`armPasswordReset`** : l'écriture exige
  une demande précédente nulle ou antérieure au cutoff. Sous `READ COMMITTED`, la
  perdante bloque sur le verrou de ligne, réévalue son `where` contre la version
  que la gagnante vient d'écrire, et rend `count: 0` — le service n'émet rien. La
  limite est désormais **la condition de l'écriture**, pas une comparaison en
  amont.
- La lecture préalable reste, en **raccourci** : elle épargne l'écriture quand le
  refus est déjà certain et permet au journal de nommer la cause. Son en-tête dit
  explicitement qu'elle n'est pas la garantie.
- La borne est **large** (`lte`), pour décider exactement comme
  `isWithinResetCooldown` — qui refuse tant que l'écart est *strictement*
  inférieur au délai. Avec un `lt`, l'instant où l'écart vaut exactement 60 000 ms
  — atteignable, `requested_at` étant un `timestamp(3)` — passait le raccourci
  puis se faisait refuser par la base : un 202 sans courrier, attribué par le
  journal à une demande concurrente. *(Constat de la revue, corrigé dans le même
  diff.)*
- **Égalisation** : le chemin stérile fait désormais la même seconde lecture que
  le chemin passant, sur `PLACEHOLDER_USER_ID`. Ni écriture factice (un vecteur
  de charge sur une route publique) ni délai constant (il change la latence
  annoncée de la route) : les deux pistes que l'issue évoquait sont écartées, et
  le commentaire dit pourquoi.
- **Les commentaires disent maintenant la vérité** : ce que l'égalisation
  garantit (même travail cryptographique, même nombre d'allers-retours en
  lecture) et ce qu'elle ne garantit pas (l'écriture d'un armement réussi reste
  observable ; ce qui la borne est la limite de débit, pas cette constante — dès
  la deuxième sonde, une adresse connue coûte ce que coûte une adresse inconnue).
- `logger.warn` → `logger.log` sur l'échec d'arming : la perdante d'une course
  est désormais le cas **nominal**, pas une anomalie.

## Comment vérifier

1. `npm run verify` — vert de bout en bout (sortie ci-dessous).
2. Contre-épreuve du test de concurrence : retirer le `OR` du `where` d'
   `armPasswordReset`, relancer
   `npx jest --config jest.concurrency.config.js --testPathPattern password-reset` —
   le cas rend **8 événements au lieu d'un**.
3. Recette MCP : `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset` sur une adresse inconnue et
   sur une adresse connue déjà armée répondent en **16 ms** l'une comme l'autre.

## Critères d'acceptation

- [x] Un test de concurrence : deux `requestPasswordReset` simultanées sur la même
      adresse n'émettent qu'**un** événement — `apps/api/test/identity-password-reset.concurrency-spec.ts`,
      8 demandes de front contre un vrai PostgreSQL.
- [x] Le commentaire sur la signature jetée dit exactement ce qu'elle garantit, et
      ce qu'elle ne garantit pas — en-tête de `PLACEHOLDER_USER_ID` et section
      « Le temps de réponse en dit le moins possible — mais pas rien ».

## Un mot sur le test de concurrence

Écrit naïvement, il ne prouvait **rien**. Mesuré : N demandes lancées de front ne
s'entrelacent pas d'elles-mêmes — la gagnante boucle lecture, signature *et*
écriture avant que la deuxième n'ait lu, si bien que les N−1 suivantes sont
arrêtées par le raccourci applicatif et n'atteignent jamais l'écriture. Le cas
passait au vert **avec ou sans** le correctif.

Une barrière retient donc chaque lecture jusqu'à ce qu'elles soient toutes
arrivées. Cela reproduit l'état de production — plusieurs tâches ECS, rien qui
les sérialise — et laisse les N écritures se disputer la ligne. Deux assertions
vérifient que la barrière a bien tenu, pour qu'elle ne puisse pas redevenir
silencieusement inopérante.

## Recette fonctionnelle (MCP)

| Appel | Statut | Verdict | Durée |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset` (adresse connue) | 202 | ✔ | 63 ms |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset` (même adresse, aussitôt) | 202 | ✔ | 16 ms |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset` (adresse inconnue) | 202 | ✔ | 16 ms |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset` (corps invalide) | 400 | ✔ | 16 ms |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset` (slug inconnu) | 404 | ✔ | 15 ms |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset` (6ᵉ en une minute) | 429 | ✔ | 31 ms |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/confirm` (jeton bidon) | 401 | ✔ | 0 ms |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/confirm` (mot de passe court) | 400 | ✔ | 0 ms |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/login` | 200 | ✔ | 94 ms |
| `GET /api/v1/auth/me` (jeton client) | 200 | ✔ | 16 ms |
| `GET /api/v1/auth/me` (sans jeton) | 401 | ✔ | 15 ms |

**11 appels, 0 échec.** Les deux routes figurent bien dans `/api/docs-json`.
Le 202 est uniforme sur les trois cas qui doivent l'être, les refus de validation
rendent `{ code, message, details }`, et l'égalisation se voit à l'œil nu :
16 ms sur l'adresse inconnue, 16 ms sur l'adresse connue déjà armée.

`perimetre` listait les 19 routes du module `identity` (il remonte au contrôleur
du module touché). La recette s'est bornée aux **deux routes que le diff change
réellement** — `auth.service.requestPasswordReset` et `identity.repository.armPasswordReset`
n'en servent pas d'autres — plus `login` et `me` en non-régression du service.
Les 17 restantes sont couvertes par la CI.

## Validation locale

`npm run verify` — code de sortie 0 :

| Cible | Résultat |
|---|---|
| lint | 0 erreur (1 avertissement préexistant sur `prisma-clients.ts`, hors diff) |
| typecheck | ok |
| build | ok |
| test:unit | 134 suites, 2517 tests |
| test:scripts | 18 suites, 503 tests |
| test:integration:api | 27 suites, 615 tests |
| test:isolation | 33 suites, 457 tests |
| test:concurrency | 6 suites, 40 tests — dont la nouvelle |

## Definition of Done

- [x] Tests unitaires et d'intégration passants
- [x] Test d'isolation inter-tenant pour tout endpoint nouveau ou modifié — aucun
      endpoint nouveau ; `identity-tenant.isolation-spec.ts` couvre le module et
      passe. Le scoping n'est pas touché : l'extension fusionne `tenantId` en
      frère du `OR` de tête (`scopedWhere = { ...where, tenantId }`).
- [x] Migration Prisma relue : additive et réversible — **aucune migration**, le
      schéma est inchangé.
- [x] Aucune entité Prisma renvoyée telle quelle par un contrôleur
- [x] Types d'API exposés ajoutés à `packages/shared` — **aucun contrat exposé ne
      change** : même route, même corps, même 202.
- [x] Aucun secret, clé ou donnée personnelle dans le diff ni dans les logs
- [x] Documentation à jour — la doctrine est dans les en-têtes des deux méthodes
      concernées, là où le prochain lecteur la cherchera. Pas d'ADR : aucune
      décision structurante, l'issue tranchait déjà la forme attendue.

## Points d'attention pour la revue

- **Concurrence** — c'est l'objet du ticket. La garantie repose sur la
  réévaluation du `where` sous `READ COMMITTED` après attente sur le verrou de
  ligne. Le test le prouve contr

body:
## What this changes, and why

`acquire` refused on two readings that did not mean what the refusal said.

A clickdoom container being up refused the machine whatever the container
was doing. clickdoom-a's server sat idle for over an hour tonight after its
own work finished and would have refused every other lane for all of it.
The exemption list for the compose service and the acquirer's own was the
tell: a check that needs a growing list of things it does not mean is
measuring the wrong thing, and the list grows with every lane.

The load average refused a lane that had done nothing wrong. It is the
1-minute one and it decays over about a minute, so it reads high exactly
when the previous holder has finished and the next lane wants the lock.
Between them these cost three lanes five waits in one evening, every one of
them on someone else's finished work.

So a container now counts by what it is using, through `docker stats
--no-stream`, and over `MACHINE_LOCK_MAX_CONTAINER_CPU` percent it refuses
at once. Both name exemptions are gone with the list. The load is waited
out instead: `acquire` looks every 5 seconds for up to
`MACHINE_LOCK_SETTLE` seconds and takes the lock the moment it falls. A
container at work is not something waiting fixes, so that refuses during
the wait as well as before it.

### The two numbers

`MACHINE_LOCK_MAX_LOAD` stays at 3. I was asked to raise it to 5 on the
belief that this host idles near 3, measured it instead, and it idles at
0.75: the median of 21 readings 15 seconds apart over five minutes, lock
held, no clickdoom container running, falling monotonically for the first
two minutes and then sitting between 0.50 and 1.05. The readings above 3
that prompted the question were the previous run decaying, which is the
thing the settle now waits out. Raising the threshold to 5 would let a
machine genuinely running four cores of work read as quiet.

`MACHINE_LOCK_SETTLE` is 180 s rather than 90. The handover below is why:
after a full demo run the load read 7.88 and had not come under 3 within
90 s.

## Evidence

Run by hand. Cases three and four came out of a real handover rather than
staged: clickdoom-c released after a full demo run and I took the machine
next.

**A container with nothing asked of it does not refuse.** `clickdoom-d` is
a real ClickHouse, idle:

```
# clickdoom-d is a real ClickHouse with nothing asked of it.

$ ./scripts/machine-lock.sh status
machine-lock: free, .../machine-lock
machine-lock: load 3.07 over 1 minute, containers clickdoom-d 4.45%

$ ./scripts/machine-lock.sh acquire clickdoom-d "a live suite"
machine-lock: waiting up to 180s for the load to fall
machine-lock: taken by clickdoom-d
exit=0
```

**The same container, working, refuses at once and names it.** The query is
`SELECT count() FROM numbers_mt(...)`, and the refusal does not wait,
because waiting does not fix a container at work:

```
# The same container, now running a query.

$ docker stats --no-stream --format "{{.Name}} {{.CPUPerc}}" | grep clickdoom-
clickdoom-d 1799.17%

$ ./scripts/machine-lock.sh acquire clickdoom-c "another lane wants the machine"
machine-lock: the machine is not quiet:
  containers working: clickdoom-d at 1801.68%
  load 6.74 is above MACHINE_LOCK_MAX_LOAD=3
machine-lock: wait, or say why it is safe: scripts/machine-lock.sh acquire --force clickdoom-c '<reason>'
exit=1
```

**The load is waited out, and refused only after the window.** Cut to 20 s
so the refusal arrives while the load is still falling:

```
# The query is stopped and the container is idle again. The load is that
# query decaying out, which is the case the settle exists for.
# MACHINE_LOCK_SETTLE is cut to 20 s so the refusal arrives inside it.

$ docker stats --no-stream --format "{{.Name}} {{.CPUPerc}}" | grep clickdoom-
clickdoom-d 6.17%

$ MACHINE_LOCK_SETTLE=20 ./scripts/machine-lock.sh acquire clickdoom-d "a live suite"
machine-lock: waiting up to 20s for the load to fall
machine-lock: the machine is not quiet:
  load 5.10 is above MACHINE_LOCK_MAX_LOAD=3
  waited 20s (MACHINE_LOCK_SETTLE) for it to fall
machine-lock: wait, or say why it is safe: scripts/machine-lock.sh acquire --force clickdoom-d '<reason>'
exit=1
```

**The same wait on the real default takes the lock when the load falls**,
after 26 s of the 180 s window rather than at the end of it:

```
# The same wait, given the default window instead. The load is still
# falling from the same query, and the lock is taken the moment it is
# under the threshold rather than after the full 180 s.

$ ./scripts/machine-lock.sh acquire clickdoom-d "a live suite"
machine-lock: waiting up to 180s for the load to fall
machine-lock: taken by clickdoom-d
exit=0
# took 26s of the 180 s window

$ ./scripts/machine-lock.sh status
machine-lock: held, .../machine-lock
holder: clickdoom-d
started: 2026-09-18T03:40:23Z
host: Marcuss-MBP.kainth.co.uk
pid: 40171
worktree: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcus-Develop-ClickDOOM/70fcbc8f-e52d-4e3e-abbd-d097ad2d2c9f/scratchpad/lockev
reason: a live suite
machine-lock: load 2.97 over 1 minute, containers clickdoom-d 5.28%
```

The handover that set the 180 s default, before this change was written,
against the version on main at the time:

```
# The machine is idle: no containers, no lane running, lock free.
# This is the refusal the settle wait removes.

$ docker ps --format "{{.Names}}"
(no output: nothing running)

$ ./scripts/machine-lock.sh status
machine-lock: free, /Users/marcus/Develop/ClickDOOM/.git/machine-lock
machine-lock: load 3.18 over 1 minute, containers none

$ ./scripts/machine-lock.sh acquire clickdoom-d "native-smoke on 933d1f7"
machine-lock: the machine is not quiet:
  load 3.18 is above MACHINE_LOCK_MAX_LOAD=3
machine-lock: wait, or say why it is safe: scripts/machine-lock.sh acquire --force clickdoom-d '<reason>'
exit=1
```

That refusal is what a lane meets today on a machine with nothing running.
Two minutes later, with the settle in place, the same call waited and took
the lock.

The idle baseline, 21 readings over five minutes with the lock held:

```

# lock held by clickdoom-d so no lane starts, no clickdoom container running.
# started 02:04:05Z

$ shellcheck scripts/machine-lock.sh

$ ./scripts/check_purity.sh

## Invariants

None. The lock records a wall-clock timestamp, which already carries its
`purity-ok` note, and the wait's own `sleep` carries one of its own. Both
are pacing. Nothing either reads reaches a computation path.

## Spec impact

author: tim-clifford
body:
## What

Adds an opt-in `EsWriteConfig.retry_transport_timeout` (default `False`) that moves whole-request **timeout** retry from `elasticsearch-py`'s transport into the connector, and enriches `bulk_stats` so timeout cost and the round-trip phase split are visible.

When `retry_transport_timeout=True`:
- the write client is built with `retry_on_timeout=False` (so the two retry layers don't stack);
- `_ship_ndjson_chunk` re-sends a timed-out chunk on `ConnectionTimeout` **only** (allow-list; `ConnectionError`/503/reset stay with the transport) up to `transport_max_retries` times with bounded exponential backoff, then falls closed into `errors` exactly as before;
- `request_timeout` is **not** shortened.

`bulk_stats` now records every send's outcome (`ok`/`timeout`/`error`), so failed attempts are visible:
- new fields `timeout_sends`/`timeout_wait_ms`, `error_sends`/`error_wait_ms` (total es.bulk time = `send_busy_ms + timeout_wait_ms + error_wait_ms`);
- new `http_ms_*` (node-level HTTP wall from `resp.meta.duration`), nested `rtt_ms ≥ http_ms ≥ took_ms`: `rtt−http` = client-above-node (decode/GIL), `http−took` = gzip+network, `took` = ES.

## Honest scope note

This is primarily an **observability + gentler-retry** change, **not** a throughput win on its own: the retry granularity, count, and 300s timeout match the transport retry it replaces, and the terminal behavior is unchanged (an exhausted timeout still fails the batch → Spark re-runs it). The value is visibility, backed-off (gentler) retries, a preserved long `request_timeout`, and making a raised `transport_max_retries` viable. Not-fail-the-batch-on-exhausted-timeout remains deliberately out of scope (data-loss/checkpoint tradeoffs).

## Testing

- 399 unit tests (14 new/changed, red-before-green verified).

## Summary

Hardens the Student Portal v1 (PR #36) from a demo prototype into a production-ready gated portal. Converts the chain `LANDING → STUDENT ACCESS → LOGIN → ENTITLEMENT → ACADEMY → MODULE 01 → HLS REAL` into a working access bridge.

## Changes

- **Deploy pipeline**: Add `inject-academy-link.cjs` and `inject-academy-env.cjs` to `deploy.yml` build step — the "Student Access" nav link and runtime config now deploy to production
- **Build-time runtime config** (`scripts/inject-academy-env.cjs`): Generates `public/academy-env.js` from environment variables (`DMF_STREAM_BASE`, `DMF_ACADEMY_DEMO`, Firebase config), replacing hardcoded `localhost:8080`
- **Firebase Auth SDK**: Load firebase-app-compat + firebase-auth-compat v10.12.0 from CDN in both `login.html` and `academy.html`, initialized from `window.__DMF_FIREBASE_CONFIG__` set by `academy-env.js`
- **Entitlement separation**: Replace `hasCourseAccess() { return !!auth }` with Firestore-based check — reads `enrollments/{uid}` document for `status: 'active'`. Auth answers "who are you?", entitlement answers "do you have access?"
- **Module lock enforcement**: Direct URL access to `/academy/module/:id` now checks `getModuleState()` — locked modules redirect to dashboard instead of rendering
- **Demo mode wiring**: `window.__DMF_ACADEMY_DEMO__` injected at build time, read by both login and academy pages alongside existing `?demo=true` fallback
- **CI hardening**: Media file check now finds `.mp4`, `.ts`, `.m3u8` (not just `.m3u8`), excluding `public/uploads/` which contains pre-existing tiny stubs
- **Docs**: Updated `DMF_ACADEMY_V1.md` with new env vars, Firestore setup instructions, and refreshed production gap checklist

## Environment Variables (new)

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `DMF_STREAM_BASE` | HLS stream server base URL (replaces hardcoded localhost) |
| `DMF_ACADEMY_DEMO` | Set `true` for demo mode |
| `DMF_FIREBASE_API_KEY` | Firebase Web API key |
| `DMF_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN` | Firebase Auth domain (defaults to `{projectId}.firebaseapp.com`) |
| `DMF_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` | Firebase project ID (defaults to `vibraaltoai-11f55`) |

## Firestore Setup Required

For entitlement to work in production:
1. Enable Cloud Firestore in Firebase console
2. Create `enrollments` collection
3. Add document with ID = user's Auth UID, containing `{ status: "active" }`
4. Deploy security rules (see `docs/DMF_ACADEMY_V1.md`)

## Test Plan

- [ ] Demo mode: set `DMF_ACADEMY_DEMO=true`, login with any credentials → full access
- [ ] Firebase Auth: set Firebase env vars, create a user → login works
- [ ] Entitlement gate: authenticated user without enrollment doc → sees "Access Required"
- [ ] Entitlement grant: add `enrollments/{uid}` doc with `status: active` → sees dashboard
- [ ] Module lock: navigate to `/academy/module/08` directly → redirected to dashboard
- [ ] CI: verify media check passes (excludes `public/uploads/` stubs)
- [ ] Build: `node scripts/inject-academy-env.cjs` generates correct `academy-env.js`

## Scope

3D pipeline, Manufacturing Master, and all PR25–35 work is untouched.

## Why

- Treat only `BlobNotFoundError` as absence.

- Add behavioral tests for present, not-found, and access-denied outcomes.

- Preview acceptance only.
- No workflow, credentials, environment, database, payment, or Production changes.
- Production checkout remains disabled.
- No stateful acceptance is run by this PR.

## Provider contract
Vercel documents `head()` as the Blob metadata operation and exports `BlobNotFoundError` for a missing object. This avoids CDN/listing ambiguity while preserving exact zero-residue enforcement.

body:
## 概要

分阶段缩小与 QuickJS 的常数因子差距，保持 plain RC + 循环回收模型（无 JIT）。本 PR 已完成 **S0–S2 可信快路**与 **S3 方案 E（构建基线）**；S3 的结构改造（A 8B 值表示 / B quickening / D 数据导向堆）按设计文档另起。

## 关键文档

| 文档 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/reports/performance-plan.md` | S0–S2 计划、实现与度量，以及各引擎的横向设计比较 |
| `docs/reports/performance-architecture.md` | S3 架构设计：8B 值表示 + quickening + 数据导向堆（无 JIT、默认无 unsafe） |

## 我们做了什么

### S0：测量基线

新增 `scripts/benchmark/property_read_probe.py`；S0 证据（`Result`/`Option` 管道、`copy_value`、IC 归属）保留在 `performance-plan.md` §2。结论：主导成本是 `Result`/`Option` 管道 + 堆 binding 借用。

### S1：可信快路

- `Node.strong` 改 `Cell<u32>` + `retain_raw_fast`（快路饱和，通用路径保持报错）。
- 可信访问器 `live_node_fast(_mut)` / `var_ref_fast(_mut)` / `object_fast`，无失败根转换 `take_owned_raw_value_fast`。
- 共享借用快路 `read_owned_cell_fast` / `read_run_cell`（captured）与 `property_ic_read_fast`（数据属性命中）。
- 精简 `try_replace_immediate_var_ref_value`。

| case | pre-S1 ns/op | S1 ns/op | 变化 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| prop_read_int | 222.87 | 185.38 | −16.8% |
| prop_read_obj | 279.78 | 234.58 | −16.2% |
| prop_read_string | 306.63 | 284.84 | −7.1% |

### S2：可信路径收尾

**已落地 S2.2（可信 IC 读）**：`PropertyReadCache::read_location` 改用 `object_fast`/`shape_fast`；新增 `slot_object_release_readiness_fast`。

| case | pre-S1 | S1 | S2 | pre-S1→S2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| prop_read_int | 222.73 | 185.97 | 184.35 | −17.2% |
| prop_read_obj | 281.70 | 236.71 | 220.22 | −21.8% |
| prop_read_string | 300.87 | 280.10 | 280.86 | −6.7% |

**S2.1（快速释放）与 S2.3（非失败 push）已撤销**：与既有契约冲突（`blocked_borrow_and_deferred_release_do_not_commit_or_drain` 固定「任意借用都 defer 释放」；`operand_push_index` 的容量失败是被事务测试覆盖的可恢复路径），需单独立项。

### S3：架构设计 + 方案 E（构建基线）

- 设计定稿于 `docs/reports/performance-architecture.md`。
- `Cargo.toml`：`[profile.release] lto = "fat", codegen-units = 1`。
- 新增 `scripts/benchmark/pgo.py`：instrumented 构建 → 训练 → `llvm-profdata merge` → profile-use 重建，带 build receipt；逐进程唯一 `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE`，训练用 `scaling.py`（22 case×{64,128}）+ v8-v7 全部 suite。

## 性能总结（pre-E HEAD `06386457` → E，同机串行）

| 套件 | 指标 | LTO+CGU=1 | +PGO |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| V8-v7（8 suite） | Score geomean | +9.1% | **+60.0%（×1.60）** |
| `scaling.py`（44 cell） | 整进程 wall geomean | ×0.898 | **×0.696（−30.2%）** |
| 属性读探针（3 case） | ns/op | −5.5% ~ −8.8% | **−26.9% ~ −37.0%** |

相对 pinned QuickJS 仍有结构差距：V8-v7 Score 慢约 **11.9×**（E 前 19.0×），整进程 wall 慢约 **5.7×**（E 前 8.2×），属性读慢 6.5–10.7×。E 只抬高比较基线，收敛留给 A/B/D。

## 验证

- `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets`：全绿（lib 2278、oracle 907、CLI 32 等）。
- `cargo fmt`、`check-source-layout.py`、benchmark 单测（22）：通过；未新增 clippy lint。
- **Test262 全量零回归**：`--full` 得 `total=102037 pass=79982 runnable=80032`，门禁 `complete Test262 vector matches`；仅产出 current-source receipt，未改 `current.conf`（方案 E 的 `Cargo.toml` 变更使 `--check` 如预期报源码过期）。

## 后续

- **A/B/D**：8B 值表示、quickening、数据导向堆，按 `performance-architecture.md` 分阶段推进。
- **S2.1b/S2.3b**：延迟释放与 operand push 的契约改造需独立设计。

author: 0xmhha
body:
## What this is

A second way out of stage 3. `render` draws a page from a diagram source;
`mermaid` writes the same source as text, one fenced Mermaid block per level:

```
diagrammer mermaid out/component.diagram.json -o component.md
```

That is the shape a README, Notion or Obsidian embeds with no build step, and
the shape [diagram-design](https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design)
reads with the Mermaid importer it already has, so a diagram this program proved
can be redrawn in a design of somebody else's choosing. Nothing on their side
had to change; this fits the door they already opened.

`make diagram` writes the Markdown beside every page.

## Why Mermaid

Because the places a diagram is taken to already read it, and none of them would
read anything invented here.

diagram-design was the occasion, and one coincidence is worth recording: its
`faithful` detail ceiling is 24 nodes, and this program's page ceiling
(`expandedMaxBoxes`) is 24. A level here is a diagram there. The two were built
to the same number without knowing about each other.

## The text carries what the page could not

A page is bound by a grid and records a relationship it cannot route. Mermaid
lays itself out and has no reason to leave a line off. So the text carries every
relationship the document proved, and marks the ones the page recorded:

```
component.diagram.json: 5 level(s), 37 proven, 37 carried
  11 of those the page had recorded rather than drawn; the text has room for them
```

The accounting keeps the shape used everywhere else — carried + omitted ==
proven, per level — and the tests hold it on every fixture.

The one omission is a recorded **message** in a sequence diagram. Order is its
meaning and a recorded message has none, so placing it would be inventing an
order. It is named in a comment and counted as omitted. No fixture records one;
a test constructs one so the path is not a rule nobody has seen fire.

## Family by family

| family | grammar | what survives | what is approximated |
|---|---|---|---|
| component | `flowchart TD` | boxes, bands as subgraphs, every dependency incl. recorded | — |
| sequence | `sequenceDiagram` | lifelines in column order, messages in theirs, activations, `alt/opt/loop/par/critical/break` | `strict`, `seq` → `opt` with the kind in the guard and a comment |
| state | `stateDiagram-v2` | composites as blocks, `[*]` pseudostates placed inside the block that owns them, `trigger [guard] / effect` | `junction`, `history` → `<<choice>>` / plain state |
| usecase | `flowchart LR` | actors as stadiums, boundary as subgraph, `---` association, `-.->` include/extend with stereotype | the whole family: Mermaid has no use case grammar, and neither does diagram-design |

## Ids are rewritten, totally and deterministically

107 of the 198 ids in the fixtures carry a dot or a colon (`rel:d.a`,
`level:pkg0`, `bulk.fn01`), and Mermaid reads both as syntax. So every id becomes
an identifier; a keyword such as `end`, which closes a subgraph, gains an
underscore; a collision is resolved in sorted order, with an id that was already
acceptable keeping its own name. A test reads every id back out of every
fixture's text and holds it to `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`.

Labels are made safe the same way: a quote in a node label, a pipe in a link
label, a semicolon after a colon, each neutralised rather than escaped, because
Mermaid's escaping is not something every reader of the text shares.

## Measured against the importer on the other side

Every family of two fixtures — eight documents — written and handed to
diagram-design's own `mermaid_extract.py` with `--diagram all`:

```
order-service/component        OK  flowchart(n=3,e=4)
order-service/sequence         OK  sequenceDiagram(n=4,e=5)
order-service/state            OK  stateDiagram-v2(n=9,e=7)
order-service/usecase          OK  flowchart(n=7,e=5)
diagrammer-layered/component   OK  5 blocks: flowchart ×5, 26 edges on the overview
diagrammer-layered/sequence    OK  sequenceDiagram(n=8,e=23)
diagrammer-layered/state       OK  stateDiagram-v2(n=8,e=10)
diagrammer-layered/usecase     OK  flowchart(n=12,e=10)
```

All eight accepted, re-run on the final code. That is the importer saying yes,
which is the only claim about interoperability worth making. It is not in
`make verify`, because the gate must run with Go and make alone and the
extractor lives in another repository; the run is recorded here instead.

## The guards found each gap

Adding a capability touches the registry, the CLI, the MCP tool list, the
server's `initialize` instructions and the README, and a guard exists for each
seam. Every one of them fired while this was being wired:

- `TestBothSurfacesCoverTheSameCapabilities` — the tool was in the registry and
  not on the server
- `TestEveryRequestFieldHasAFlag` — no flag reached `Out`
- `TestTheServerSaysWhatItIsFor` — the instructions never placed `mermaid`
- `TestTheReadmeListsTheCommandsThatExist` — the README never mentioned it

## Not built

An importer of our own for draw.io or Excalidraw. Nothing this program produces
is improved by passing through a drawing tool, and one text format the
destinations already share is what was asked for.

## Verification

- `make fmt-check`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint`: clean, both builds, 0 issues.
- `go test ./...`: passes under `CGO_ENABLED=0` and `CGO_ENABLED=1`.
- `make verify`: ok, 19 pages, byte-identical across runs.
- `make verify-cgo`: ok.
- 14 new tests in `internal/mermaid`, including the accounting on every fixture,
  bracket balance on every sequence fixture, pseudostate spelling, composite
  blocks, id safety read back from the text, label neutralisation, and
  determinism.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a safe, browser-friendly way to register the Worker webhook with Telegram using the existing `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` without exposing secrets.
- Allow operators to check webhook status from the Worker without returning any secret material from Telegram's response.
- Preserve the existing health check, webhook verification, Sleep Mode, Busy Mode, urgent-message logic, and message-processing flow.

### Description
- Add `GET /telegram/setup` which derives the webhook URL from the current Worker origin plus `/telegram/webhook`, calls Telegram's `setWebhook` via `callTelegramApi`, and returns the success message `AVA Telegram webhook connected successfully.` or a generic error. 
- Add `GET /telegram/webhook-info` which calls Telegram's `getWebhookInfo` and returns an explicit allowlist of non-secret fields (`connected`, `url`, `pending_update_count`, `last_error_date`, `last_error_message`) rather than forwarding Telegram's full response. 
- Implement helper functions `callTelegramApi`, `setupWebhook`, `webhookInfo`, and `configurationError` and reuse existing safe logging and secret-checking patterns; the original webhook verification and message reply flow remain unchanged. 
- Update `README.md` to document the new browser-based setup endpoint and the webhook-info endpoint, and add tests in `test/index.test.js` that mock `fetch` to validate behavior without leaking secrets.

### Testing
- Ran `npm test` and all tests passed (`5` tests). 
- Ran `git diff --check` and there were no problems reported. 
- Tests include mocked `fetch` calls to verify that `setWebhook` is invoked with the derived origin URL and that `webhook-info` returns only safe, non-secret fields.

author: saphemlock
body:
Fixes #12487.

Cherry picking a single file from a commit is unavailable when git detected the file as a copy of another one.

The menu item is gated on `FileViewer.SupportLinePatching`, whose second condition only recognised `GitItemStatus.IsNew`. A copied file is added at its new path just like a new one, but git reports it with its own status, so `IsNew` is false and `IsCopied` is true. The first condition does not apply either, because it requires the file to exist in the working tree, which it does not when viewing a commit that is not checked out.

Use `IsAdded`, which `GitItemStatus` already defines as "new or copied" for exactly this distinction. Git Extensions passes `--find-copies`, so such items do occur.

author: jmcgill-d
body:
**D15.3c.** `getShaderParameter`, `getUniformLocation`, `getError` and twelve others are calls whose return value *is* the answer, asked about work that is still records in the frame being built — the shader whose `COMPILE_STATUS` content wants was given its source three records ago. So the producer sends what it has recorded as a **barrier** (executed, not presented; presenting the half frame would flash it onto the screen) and blocks in a synchronous request naming that barrier's sequence. The host answers once that sequence has been admitted and run.

- **Three operations, not fifteen.** The operation sizes the reply and there are three shapes of answer: a scalar, text, and an active variable's `(size, type, name)`. Which query is in the parameters, and a kind sent under the wrong operation is refused rather than answered in a shape nobody is reading.
- **One params record** — five fields, a length, a zero-padded UTF-8 name — with the frame stream's payload rule, so a name is a byte count and the padding has one encoding.
- **`getError` asks no renderer.** The queue is the host's, filled while it decoded this producer's own records; the barrier still goes first, because an error made by the frame being asked about has to be in the queue before it is read.

**Checked:** four unit tests drive the real `SyncPath` against a stand-in renderer (a location, a location that does not exist and comes back as -1, an active variable's three fields, `getError` draining one per call with no renderer installed at all) plus the wrong-operation refusal; 60 query records emitted by the producer are decoded by the Rust reader with every kind covered and re-encoded byte for byte (`scripts/test-frame-wire-js-encoder.sh`); the op-boundary gate now reports **sync 15/66** answered.

**iOS simulator acceptance:** content compiles, links, asks for the compile and link status, the active-attribute count, the active uniform's name and the uniform's location — then draws with that location. `queries: pixel=[0, 255, 0, 255] attributes=1`, and the deliberate negative `bufferSubData` offset reads back as `INVALID_VALUE` then drains. **34/34 PerformancePlus tests pass in 42 s.**

Errors reuse the same `AdvisorUpstreamError`/outage-classification machinery already in place (duck-typed on `.status`, not provider-specific), so the existing outage banner UI works unchanged for a Gemini failure too.
- **`propose_settings`** (stage 2, Claude) gains `nextEarningsDate`, `earningsOutlook`, `earningsLikelihood` (low/moderate/high), and `earningsLikelihoodReason` — Claude extracts these from the research text in the same forced tool call it already makes, so this adds no new API call.
- New migration `0012_advisor_earnings_outlook.sql` adds the 4 columns to `advisor_suggestion_cache`.
- The AI Suggestion panel renders a new colored earnings-outlook box (same red/amber/green token reuse as the existing fit verdict box) beneath the rationale.
- Dropped now-dead Claude-web-search-loop machinery (`WEB_SEARCH_TOOL`, `SUBMIT_RESEARCH_TOOL`, `AdvisorTimeoutError`, the turn/search-budget loop) since Gemini's grounding tool resolves in a single call rather than needing a manual multi-turn forcing loop.
- No automatic cross-provider fallback: a Gemini outage surfaces as a normal advisor outage, same as a Claude outage does today.

  - The UI renders the new earnings-outlook box (green, "High likelihood of meeting expectations") correctly alongside the existing fit verdict box, rationale, and settings compare table

author: wuhuizuo
body:
## Summary

Previously `devbuild.Create` always overwrote the caller-supplied `createdBy` with the authenticated identity's email whenever an identity was present in the context. This made it impossible for an authenticated caller to attribute a build to another user.

This change only falls back to the authenticated identity when the request does not provide a `createdBy`. An explicit non-blank `createdBy` is now preserved, and a blank/missing value still yields `DevBuildUnauthorizedError`.

## Behavior

- `createdBy` provided and non-blank -> used as-is, even when an identity is present.
- `createdBy` missing/blank and an authenticated identity exists -> identity email is used.
- `createdBy` missing/blank and no identity -> 401 `DevBuildUnauthorizedError`.

## Note

This intentionally removes the anti-spoofing guard introduced in #644 (where the authenticated identity always won over a request-provided `createdBy`). The corresponding assertion in `TestPortalDevBuildIdentityAndCapabilities` has been updated to expect the explicit `createdBy`.

- [x] `go build ./cmd/tibuild ./cmd/tibuild-cli`

author: maherfayad
body:
## What

`STUDIO-FIGMA-FEEL-PLAN.md` §9 items 4, 5 and 6 — the three `verify-01` findings that made `bun run test:e2e` unusable as a gate — plus `meta-14` landmine 3.

1. **`bun run test:e2e` starts the stack by itself on Windows.** Root cause found and fixed at the source, not worked around.
2. **The canvas perf gate has a tracked corpus.** `studio-board-perf.e2e.ts` no longer self-skips; it measures a committed twelve-frame board and **fails** if that board is missing.
3. **A run leaves `git status` clean.** Every spec runs against a throwaway copy of `studio-workspace/`.
4. **`bun run test:e2e` is the documented fourth gate**, in the testing doc and `PROJECT-BRIEF.md`.

## Why

### 1. The stack could not start itself

Playwright's `webServer` spawns the command with all three stdio as pipes, and `scripts/e2e-dev.ts` handed those pipes straight to Vite. Vite then intermittently **bound its port, printed nothing, and answered nothing** — it was blocked inside a write. Playwright's probe connected and hung until the timeout, so a failed run showed the CMS's two startup lines and `Timed out waiting …`, nothing else. By hand in a terminal the same command comes up in 2–5 s, which is why this read as flakiness for seven weeks.

Measured under a real `webServer`, ten boots per configuration, ports asserted free before each:

| Children's stdout/stderr | boots that came up |
|---|---|
| inherited from our pipes | 3 / 10 |
| `'pipe'` + forwarded by us | 3 / 10 |
| `'ignore'` | 6 / 8 |
| **a FILE, tailed by us** | **8 / 10** |

Ruled out on the way, each with a measurement: the two-children spawn race (reproduces with Vite alone), the runner (`node` is no better than `bun`), `stdin` inheritance, and the workspace copy this PR adds. A large part of the noise in earlier attempts was orphaned stacks from killed runs — now reported with the sentence that fixes it instead of a raw `EBUSY`.

So `scripts/lib/stackChild.ts` decides from one fact — do we own a terminal? — and gives each child either the terminal or a log file it cannot block on. `scripts/e2e-dev.ts` then **supervises** Vite's boot: it asks for a page Vite serves itself, tells "still pre-bundling" apart from "stuck" by whether anything is listening yet, and kills and respawns a Vite that never answers, up to three attempts, naming which of three failure shapes it saw. The readiness request is `AbortSignal.timeout`-bounded, without which the probe loop hangs inside its own first await against exactly the failure it exists for.

The readiness URL moves from `/` to `/admin`: `/` is proxied into the CMS's public-site renderer, which on a just-created database takes seconds and depends on state the stack has no opinion about.

`playwright.config.ts` also sets `VITE_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` for whatever ports it chose, so an isolated stack no longer dies on `Forbidden: invalid origin` (`server/auth/security.ts`'s allowlist hardcodes 5173/5174). `E2E_REUSE_SERVER=1` is unchanged and still the fastest way to iterate on one spec.

### 2. The perf gate had no corpus

`studio-board-perf.e2e.ts` measured `studio-workspace/maherfayad-stack-eSIM`, untracked — so on CI and on every machine but one it called `test.skip`, and the S1 budgets in `helpers/canvasPerf.ts` were asserted nowhere that runs.

`studio-workspace/__board-perf-fixture` is twelve near-identical screens, one shared plain stylesheet, and a committed `boards.json` pinning all twelve frames to fixed grid slots. Twelve is the floor, not a preference: `frameMountPool` keeps `max(8, onScreen + 4)` frames mounted, so a board of eight or fewer mounts nothing during a zoom and there is nothing to measure. Its display name deliberately sorts after `__canonical-fixture`'s so it never becomes the workspace's default project.

Three assertions got stricter, none weaker: a missing corpus now **fails** instead of skipping; `BUDGET_ZOOM_MEAN_FRAME_MS` is asserted beside the worst-frame one; and the WS-5.3 poster criterion is no longer hidden behind `if (departed.length > 0)`. The spec also waits long enough for `framePosterQueue` to drain before the poster pan — at 800 ms on a twelve-frame board that criterion was not flaky, it was impossible (0/4), because a frame that leaves the viewport has its pending capture withdrawn.

### 3. A run dirtied the tracked workspace

`auth.setup.ts` stamps `lastOpenedAt`, the shell scaffolder writes `index.html` and `prototype/*` and rewrites `package.json`, and the framework compiler drops a `.studio/framework.json`. All real product behaviour; none of it something a test run may put in front of `git add`.

The stack now copies the tracked tree to `.tmp/e2e-workspace` and exports `STUDIO_WORKSPACE_DIR`, which `projectsRootDir()` already reads per call and which anchors every containment guard in the feature. The four specs that write a fixture project join onto `WORKSPACE_ROOT` from `tests/e2e/helpers/constants.ts` — including `studioFixtureProject.ts`, which wave 2 added with its own `process.cwd()` root.

## User / developer impact

- `bun run test:e2e` is usable as the fourth gate without hand-starting a server, and a stack that cannot start says why instead of expiring as a bare timeout.
- A Playwright run no longer leaves a diff in `studio-workspace/`, so `git add` cannot sweep test writes into a user's project.
- CI's `e2e-budgets` job measures real canvas budgets on every run instead of skipping the spec that owns them. It also stops starting the stack by hand and uses the config's own `webServer` — CI is the only place that proves that path works on Linux.
- `bun run dev` is byte-for-byte unchanged in a terminal, and no longer hangs when its output is redirected.

## Verification

Run on a Windows machine with eleven agents working in parallel; load matters to several of these numbers.

- `bun run build` exit 0 · `bun run lint` exit 0
- `bun test src/__tests__/architecture` **622 pass / 1 fail** — the fail is `ai-driver-isolation`'s whole-tree scan blowing its 20 s budget under load; **6 pass / 0 fail** run alone (`standing-01`'s named artefact)
- full `bun test` **13,630 pass / 2 skip / 12 fail** over 1,241 files in 741 s. Six are `standing-01`'s named set (`claudeCli` 0600, `studio.test.ts` nested page, `parityMatrix`, `studio_compare` ×2, `studio_list_projects`); the other six (`loadStudioPageInLocale`, `prewarmCaptureBrowser`, `captureFramesHeadless` ×4) are all 5 s timeouts and **pass 17/0 when re-run alone**. Zero new reds.
- `devWorkflow.test.ts`'s preflight gate was pinned to the literal `Bun.spawn(cfg.command`; it now follows `dev.ts` to `spawnStackChild(cfg.command`. Same contract, one moved string — called out because it is an assertion change.
- **Budget slice, cold, no hand-started server:** 16 passed / 4 failed in 10.3 min, and `git status --porcelain studio-workspace/` **empty** afterwards. The four: `studio-board-perf`'s pan worst frame 48.3 ms against a budget of 40 (it measured 18.4 / 19.1 / 20.6 ms in three earlier runs on the same tree — a load artefact, and the budget is deliberately not being raised for it); `studio-feel`'s Alt+drag case, red since #152; and two cases in wave 2's `studio-feel-phase0.e2e.ts`, which this PR does not touch.

author: sakthivelmanii
body:
Ensure database removal fully propagates across all gRPC channels and backend endpoints before recreating the database in TestIntegration_DbRemovalIsFatal.

Waiting for post-drop propagation ensures that database removal takes effect across all channels and backends. On the emulator, this wait is bypassed as changes take effect immediately.

Changes:
- Wait for post-drop propagation and at least 20 consecutive Database not found errors at 500ms poll intervals before recreating the database.
- Reset the consecutive NotFound counter if a query succeeds during the drop window, ensuring all channels observe database removal before recreation.
- Verify that a newly created client can query the recreated database first before asserting permanent failure on the original client.
- Assert that the original client's multiplexed session ID remains unchanged across all post-recreation attempts.
- Use an independent context with timeout when dropping the recreated database in defer cleanup so teardown succeeds even if the test context expires.

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
## What this closes

From `~/memcap-work/feature-competitor-map.md`:

> **integriq/outbound-communication-log** - request-tracker, freescout, otobo, plane, glpi, znuny. A case message is forwarded to someone outside the system and recorded on the case.

Implements `openspec/changes/outbound-communication-log`.

## What it does

"Did the ontvangstbevestiging leave the building" is asked weekly, and the answer was in a container log nobody could reach. Now it is a record.

The record is per recipient, because the failure is. Three people on one ontvangstbevestiging can have three outcomes, and a record that averages them cannot answer Awb 3:41 for any of them. Each recipient carries its own status, its own failed step and the reason the transport gave; the message carries the subject, the channel, the body and the ordered steps. A record is written even when the first step fails, since "it never left" is exactly what is being asked.

Delivery and read each have three states rather than two: `reported`, `not reported`, and `unsupported by this channel`. Most transports say nothing after a successful hand-over, and "not failed" is not "delivered": a term that runs from a delivery nobody reported is a term that runs from an assumption. A read is never inferred from a delivery, and a receipt on a channel that cannot report one is refused rather than recorded.

The body is redacted before it is stored, not on read, and is readable only behind `outbound.read-body`, an action distinct from seeing that a message went out: the fact of a letter and its text are different questions with different audiences. Reading a body is itself recorded on the record.

A retry re-dispatches through the CloudEvents delivery pipeline the message went out on, audited with who asked for it and appended as a new attempt to the same record. There is no second retry mechanism, so there is one audit trail and one place for a message to be. A retry that no delivery route picks up is a refusal, not a success.

A forward is its own record, linked from both ends, and the original is left untouched: Awb 2:3 asks for provability, and an edit replaces the evidence with its consequence. An external address with no Nextcloud account is a recipient like any other, and no account is created for one. Last contact stays a query, because writing it onto another app's record would make integriq own a field on a case and would go stale on the next retry.

A declarative page under Operations carries the queue, filterable by status. The body is deliberately not a column: a table cell is not a permission boundary.

## Verification

Build-first phase, per the lane brief: `php -l`, the unit suites of the classes touched, `openspec validate --strict`, and eslint on the changed JS and TS.

- `vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Unit/Outbound tests/Unit/Controller/OutboundLogControllerTest.php tests/Unit/Settings`: 136 tests green
- `npx vitest run tests/vitest/outboundLogManifest.spec.js`: 5 tests green
- `openspec validate outbound-communication-log --strict`: valid
- eslint on the two changed test files: clean

Mutation check: marking a delivery `reported` on hand-over reddened `MessageRecorderTest.php:153`, the "silence is not delivery" assertion itself. Restored.

Three coordination tasks stay open on purpose, all cross-lane conversations rather than code: handing dossiq the case-surface half and the `lastTold` projection, handing dossiq C-communication-40 (a draft is composed on the case surface and is not a send), and telling the cluster 14 lane that an external address is a recipient here and a participant there.

Deferred to the later quality sweep: phpmd, psalm, phpstan, the whole-tree gates, `check:strict`, and the e2e run. Recorded in `~/memcap-work/quality-debt.md`.

author: k35o
body:
## 概要

`InView` で、見えていた子を外しても `onChange(false)` が呼ばれず、`true` のまま残ることがありました。これを直します。#699 の CI の Tests ジョブで落ちた `SomeAfterRemoval` のフレークの原因がこれです。

## 動機

React 19.3 は Fragment の子が外れると、`IntersectionObserver` の `unobserve` だけをペイント後（rAF 2 回）まで遅らせます。その子の「交差していない」という最後の通知を待つためです。ところが負荷が高いと、交差の計算より先にこの `unobserve` が走り、通知が届かないまま終わります。`InView` はこの通知でしか外れた子を「交差中」の Set から消していなかったので、外れた子が残り続け、ほかの子がどれも見えていなくても `true` のままでした。

- 修正前のストーリーを単体で繰り返すと、60 回中 1 回落ちる程度でした。そこで 4 並列で 100 回流し、トレース付きの失敗を 1 回捕まえました。クリックの 1ms 後に React の `unobserve(A)` が走り、`A:false` の entry は届いていません。
- Chromium で、外した子を通知の前に `unobserve` すると、その子の最後の通知は来ないことを実験で確かめました。
- ストーリーの寸法の問題ではありません。A を外すと B は 800–840px に詰まりますが、見えている範囲は 400–560px なので B は入りません。

## 変更

- `IntersectionObserver` を継承して `unobserve` を上書きしました。React が子を外したら、その呼び出しで直接 Set から消して報告します。React が `unobserve` を遅らせても遅らせなくても、同じ結果になります。
  - クラスを effect の中で定義しているのは、モジュール直下で `IntersectionObserver` を継承すると SSR で落ちるためです。
- effect の後始末と `once` で止めるときも、`unobserveUsing` は子ごとに `unobserve` を呼びます。そこで報告しないよう、先に `stopped` を立てます。
- ストーリーを 2 つ足しました。
  - `SomeAfterUnreportedRemoval`: 外れた子への通知を落とす `IntersectionObserver` に差し替え、通知が失われる状況を毎回作ります。修正前は 5 回中 5 回、CI と同じ形（最後の呼び出しが `true`）で落ちます。
  - `ReobservedWhileInView`: 見えている間に `rootMargin` を変えて observer を張り直しても、`false` を挟まないことを確かめます。後始末で `stopped` を立てないと落ちます。
- changeset: `@k8ordo/ui` patch。ドキュメントは「後から外れた子にも追従する」と既に書いているので変えていません。

## レビューで見てほしいところ

- `SomeAfterUnreportedRemoval` は、`beforeEach` でグローバルの `IntersectionObserver` を差し替え、終わったら戻しています。タイミングでは確実に再現できないので、この形にしました。本物のブラウザで確かめる方針からは少し外れます。

## 確認

- in-view のストーリー 8 本を 4 並列で 100 回流し、失敗は 0 でした。ただ修正前も同じ条件で 100 回中 1 回なので、これだけでは強い証拠になりません。直ったことの根拠は、毎回落ちていた `SomeAfterUnreportedRemoval` が通るようになった点です。
- `InView` を使う Conversation のストーリーが通ることを確かめました。
- `vp check` と `pnpm typecheck`（packages/ui）が通ることを確かめました。

body:
## Submission type

- [ ] Mathematical solver information
- [x] Lean proof or formalization author information

## Problem and proposed change

Problem ID(s): JSP-000701

**Current entry:** [JSP-000701 · "How large can an integer-interval subset be if every pairwise product plus one has a nontrivial square factor?"](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/main/problems/catalog-0701-0800.md#JSP-000701) — Mathematical area: Number theory; Date proposed: No later than 1992 (bibliographic evidence); no publication source listed; Current status: **Open**; Lean proof: No.

**Proposed change (this PR):** add one preliminary candidate record at `candidates/observation/jsp-000701-diophantine-quadruple-v1/` and the corresponding regenerated `data/candidates.json` entry. Nothing in `problems/` is modified, no catalog status field is changed, no batch is created, and no award is claimed. The record is `status: under-verification` with `decision: null`, `recipients: []`, all `verification` fields `null`, and `verification/record.yaml` set to `null`.

**Scope of the formalization:** this observation records a complete, machine-checked Lean proof of a constructive existence component of the catalog question: the classical Diophantine quadruple `{1, 3, 8, 120}` is a 4-element set such that every product of two **distinct** elements plus one has a nontrivial square factor. It does not prove any upper bound, does not determine the maximum size asked by the question, does not resolve the catalogued open problem, and makes no award claim. The theorem proved is:

```lean
theorem jsp000701 : ∃ (s : Finset ℕ), s.card = 4 ∧
    ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, a ≠ b → ∃ q : ℕ, 1 < q ∧ q * q ∣ a * b + 1
```

Proof outline: the witness set is `{1, 3, 8, 120}`; `s.card = 4` holds by `decide`. For the pairwise condition, case analysis on the membership of `a` and `b` (16 cases) closes the 4 self-pair cases by the distinctness hypothesis and supplies, for each of the 12 ordered distinct pairs, an explicit square root `q` verified by `decide`. All six unordered pairs are in fact perfect squares: `1*3+1 = 4 = 2^2`, `1*8+1 = 9 = 3^2`, `1*120+1 = 121 = 11^2`, `3*8+1 = 25 = 5^2`, `3*120+1 = 361 = 19^2`, `8*120+1 = 961 = 31^2` (perfect squares imply a nontrivial square factor, so the condition is met with room to spare).

**Reading disclosure:** "pairwise product" is read in the standard way, as applying to **distinct pairs only**. Self-pairs (`a = a`) are **not** in scope: for example `1*1+1 = 2` is squarefree, so under a self-pair reading no set containing `1` could satisfy the property. This scoping is stated in the record's `Statement.lean`/`Proof.lean` header, `citation.md`, and the proof repository README.

**Attribution:** mathematical credit for the catalogued question belongs to the public record of JSP-000701 (posed no later than 1992, bibliographic evidence; no specific publication source). Formalization author: Yaohua-Leo, AI-assisted via ZCode (GLM). No solver, verifier, or recipient attribution is claimed by this PR.

Since the catalog entry lists no publication details, `posed.citation` in `award.yaml` points to the catalog entry itself as the source of record (the record schema requires a non-empty citation string; `citation: null` would not validate).

## Proof source

```json
[
  {
    "repository": "https://github.com/Yaohua-Leo/jsp-000701-lean",
    "branch": "main",
    "commit": "5963644eff77f4b9f2acef85e8ef5e2788ab1378"
  }
]
```

- Theorem/file: `jsp000701` in `JSP000701.lean` at the pinned commit.
- Toolchain: `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0-rc2`, Mathlib `v4.35.0-rc2` (pinned in the repository).
- Local verification at the pinned commit: `lake env lean JSP000701.lean` produces no errors and no warnings, and `#print axioms jsp000701` reports exactly `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — no `sorryAx` or any other axiom. The proof contains no `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide`, or added unproved assumptions.
- **Pinned-scope disclosure:** the pinned proof covers only the existence of the size-4 set `{1, 3, 8, 120}` satisfying the distinct-pair condition stated above (`|S| ≥ 4` is attainable); it does **not** cover any upper bound or the maximum-size question of the original problem, which remains Open. The observation record's `Statement.lean` and `Proof.lean` are byte-identical copies of `JSP000701.lean` at the pinned commit, per the observation record layout; the canonical proof source is the pinned repository.

## Submission checklist

- [ ] I changed only solver attribution, Lean proof information or supporting sources in the relevant catalog. *(Unchecked by intent: this PR changes nothing in `problems/`; it only adds a `candidates/observation/` record and regenerates `data/candidates.json`, following the observation-precedent layout.)*
- [x] I supplied the evidence required for the type of change above. *(Public proof repository, branch and full 40-character commit SHA above; build instructions and axiom audit in the repository README.)*
- [ ] The mathematical result fully solves the original problem. Any submitted Lean proof is complete at the specified commit, with no `sorry`, `admit` or added unproved assumptions in the proof of that result. *(Unchecked by intent: this is a deliberately scoped observation of the existence component `|S| ≥ 4` and does not solve the catalogued open problem. The pinned proof is complete for that stated existence claim, with no `sorry`/`admit`/unproved assumptions, as evidenced by the axiom audit above.)*
- [x] This PR contains no proof source files, archives, binaries or vendored dependencies. *(The only Lean files are the record's `Statement.lean`/`Proof.lean` required by the observation record layout; no archives, binaries or vendored dependencies are included.)*

## Local validation

- [x] `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — 19/22 pass; the 3 failures (`test_published_statement_immutable_and_superseded`, `test_revocation_keeps_original_evidence`, `test_symlinks_and_misplaced_records_rejected`) are the documented Windows-platform failures (symlink privilege and git-attribute behaviour), unrelated to this record

author: saphemlock
body:
Fixes #5334.

The merge dialog offers "Keep a single branch line if possible (fast forward)", but the argument builder only passed `--no-ff` for the opposite choice and nothing at all for this one. Git then falls back to the `merge.ff` configuration, so a repository with `merge.ff=false` creates a merge commit although the user asked for a fast forward.

Verified against git: with `merge.ff=false`, `git merge <branch>` reports "Merge made by the 'ort' strategy", while `git merge --ff <branch>` fast forwards. Also verified that `--ff` combines with `--squash`; `--no-ff --squash` is rejected by git, but the dialog already prevents that combination via `squash.Enabled = !noFastForward.Checked`.

The existing `MergeBranchCmd` cases are updated for the new flag and one case is added for the plain fast-forward merge.

body:
**Area:** Programmatic SEO (the `← NEXT` row in the growth wiki; 1 prior run, 2026-09-11, which built the `/for` cluster).

**Query targeted:** "invoicing app for nutritionists / dietitians in India", "how to collect diet plan fees on WhatsApp", "app to track diet clients' monthly plan payments".

**What shipped:** a fifth `/for` profession page at `/for/nutritionists`.

**Why it earns a page rather than being templated filler.** The wiki's standing rule for this cluster is that a new profession page is only worth building if the buyer's *money* has a different shape, not a different job title — Zumba is a class pack, yoga is a rate card, tuition is a term fee, photography is a booking paid in two parts. Research on live Indian dietitian pricing pages (published consult fees of ₹600–₹900, a ₹2,000 one-off plan PDF, ₹1,998/month plans with daily WhatsApp support, ₹4,999 12-week programmes, and programme tiers priced "get a quote on WhatsApp") turned up a shape none of the four existing pages has, and a stronger one than the wiki predicted:

- **The chat is the clinic.** Every other persona works somewhere else and bills on WhatsApp. A nutritionist delivers the product *in the same thread the invoice goes into* — the plan, the alternate-day weight logs, the 9pm question about a wedding buffet.
- **So there is no withholding lever.** A class pack lapses at the studio door; a diet plan was already sent and the chat support is someone's health. An unpaid month silently becomes a free month, and nothing was ever counting.
- **The money expires instead of going late.** Programme work is prepaid, so an overdue-invoice tool solves a problem this buyer doesn't have. The loss is day 84 of a 90-day programme — the renewal nobody asked for.
- **Confidentiality of the line item**, which no other page on this site has any reason to raise: the invoice PDF gets forwarded to whoever pays, so it should read "Nutrition programme — 3 months", never the diagnosis.

**Honest concessions on the page:** no document library or plan delivery (the PDF is the invoice, not the diet chart), no calendar or appointment booking for the fortnightly review calls (Calendly / Practo named), no inventory for supplements (Vyapar, myBillBook, Zoho Invoice named), no staff for a multi-dietitian clinic, corporate wellness POs pointed at Refrens / Zoho Invoice, and the ₹0 tier called a trial rather than a home because a programme roster replaces itself.

**Also in this PR:** added to `professions.ts` (so the hub and every cross-link pick it up) and to `pages` in `facts.ts` (so `/llms.txt` lists it); `/for` hub updated from four professions to five and nutritionists removed from its "no page yet" list.

`npm ci && npm run build` clean, `npm run check:stubs` passes (15 stubs), `WebPage` + `FAQPage` + `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD validated. Site goes to 16 indexable pages.
