author: erikbahl-afk
body:
Two commits. The first was already here; the second is the fix for the 42.3% run.

## 1. Stop reporting what the uplink test *sent* as what *arrived*

`capacity_test.sh` printed "12 Mbit/s delivered, 0.0% loss" over a link the same run had just measured at 1.64 Mbit/s, and contradicted itself two lines apart. A flooded uplink cannot get iperf3's end-of-test exchange back, so the client falls back to its own counts and `end.sum` reads as *exactly* the offered rate at *exactly* zero loss. It now parses the server's own per-second log, the way `udpload` already did, and labels the fallback as the sender's number when there is no server output.

## 2. The survey load was filling the modem and blaming the garage

Working back from your own run: median round trip 1381 ms against a 32 ms base, over a link carrying about 1.3 Mbit/s, means the modem was holding roughly **1.75 Mbit (219 KB)** of our data. A continuous 3 Mbit/s offer fills that in about **one second** and keeps it full for the rest of the walk — and ping, which is what dead zones are detected from, sits in the same queue. The survey was finding dead zones it had created.

Fill time scales inversely with the overshoot:

| offered | link carries | time to fill | you've walked |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.0M | 1.3M | 1.0 s | ~1 m |
| 1.5M | 1.3M | 8.8 s | ~9 m |
| 0.75M | 0.70M | 35 s | ~35 m |

So the answer is not a gentler rate, it is a burst short enough that the queue cannot build and a gap long enough that it drains.

### The duty cycle

Uplink sends for `uplink_block_s` (**30 → 10 s**) and then stays quiet for `uplink_idle_s` (**new, 20 s**). Seconds inside a burst, and `uplink_settle_s` (**new, 3 s**) after one, are recorded in `samples.uplink_loaded` and **left out of dead-zone detection** — dropped from the percentage rather than counted as good, the same way paused seconds are. The report prints both how long the walk was and how much of it was judged.

Three consequences, handled here rather than left to bite later:

- Excluding seconds leaves a hole, and a hole normally means a pause, which the detector refuses to stitch across. A burst is not a pause, so each surviving sample carries how many loaded seconds ran before it and the gap calculation subtracts them. Otherwise one bad ramp comes back as three zones with three nearly identical clips.
- **"No stream" for uplink** now counts only the seconds the rig was actually sending, and so does the grey shading on the throughput plot. Counting the deliberate silence would report two thirds of every walk as the link having failed badly enough to take the test down with it.
- **Latency and loss** on the detail tab now describe the unloaded seconds and say so. Folding in seconds whose round trip is 1.8 s by construction gives a median nobody ever experienced, printed right under the headline. On a test render it moved mean loss from 28.8% to 5.0% and the median round trip from 67 ms to 58 ms.

### The saturation warning

The report counts seconds that delivered less than `uplink_saturated_below` (0.85) of the offered rate and says plainly that those readings are a **floor, not a measurement** — a full link loses packets because it is full. This matters because bufferbloat saturates: once the buffer is full the latency stops rising, so "slightly short of the offered rate" and "hopelessly short" look identical in the trace. There is no honest way to recover the number that would have been there, so the report says so and points at lowering the rate rather than pretending.

### What this does not fix

The rate itself is still unvalidated. The burst schedule bounds the damage; it does not make 3 Mbit/s the right number. That still wants a measurement of what a robot really sends with every camera an operator would open.

## Check before merging

If the rig's own `config/config.yaml` sets `uplink_block_s`, it will keep that value and pick up a 20-second gap next to it — 30 s of sending per 50 s cycle rather than 10 per 30. Either remove the line so the new default applies, or set `uplink_block_s: 10` there.

Runs from before and after this are not comparable: the headline is now computed over the unloaded part of the walk rather than all of it.

## Testing

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest` — **316 passed** (was 285). New coverage for the duty cycle, the exclusion end to end through the runner, the merge behaviour around bursts, the no-stream counting, the shading, and the saturation calculation. The report was also rendered in a real browser with a synthetic 10-minute walk and checked for script errors and unbalanced markup.

## No server change needed

Nothing under `server/` changed, so "Apply update" on the rig is enough.

body:
The client asked what the point of a control that cannot change anything is. There is not one. Front end only, no migrations.

## What changed

The user menu is now Profile, Guest booking page, Settings, Reload data, Log out. No Language row, no footnote.

Language was disabled by design — the guest booking page carries the nineteen languages and the staff screens are English, which was the decision taken when that work was scoped. But a menu row that ignores every click is bad whatever the reasoning behind it. It was tried silent, which read as broken; then labelled "English", which read as pointless. Both readings were correct.

The footnote went too, as asked. It existed to explain the disabled row, so once the row was gone it was explaining nothing.

CLAUDE.md now says plainly: do not put a control in this menu that cannot do anything. It also records where the switcher goes back if the staff app is ever translated.

## What this does not do

It does not translate the staff app. That is thirty-four screens of hotel and accounting terminology — blind close, closed to arrival, paid-out — and a different decision from the one taken earlier. The nineteen languages still work on the guest booking page, where the reader might not speak English.

author: jmorrison-juniper
body:
## Summary

This change converts the last two root-logger calls in `tests/unit`.

## Why they survived

Pull request #2933 converted `tests/unit` and measured zero remaining calls. That
measurement was true when it ran.

Pull request #2930 merged first and added two new tests, and each one calls
`logging.info`. The rebase in #2933 carried those two calls into its branch, and
no measurement ran after the rebase.

Four agents worked inside `tests/` at the same time, so this race was possible.
The lesson is small and concrete: **re-measure after a rebase, not only before
one.**

## The change

```text
tests/unit/scripts/test_browser_driver_bootstrap.py:140  logging.info -> logger.info
tests/unit/scripts/test_report_stranded_branches.py:324  logging.info -> logger.info
```

Both files already declare `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`, so this edits
the call prefix on two lines and adds nothing.

## Result

| Directory | Outside a handler |
| - | -: |
| `tests/unit` | **0** |
| `tests/contract` | 55 |
| `tests/e2e` | 35 |
| `tests/integration` | 17 |
| `tests/fixtures` | 5 |
| `tests/` root files | 4 |

`tests/unit` held 309 calls before this wave. It now holds none.

## Validation

| Gate | Result |
| - | - |
| `py_compile` | No output |
| `ruff check` | All checks passed |
| `black --check` | 2 files would be left unchanged |
| `pytest` on both files | 47 passed |
| Abstract syntax tree scan of `tests/unit` | 0 calls outside a handler |

Part of issue #2769.

author: facundo-barbera
body:
The solo conversation route from #576 — `/projects/<projectId>/sessions/<sessionId>/solo` and its `/hosts/<hostId>/…` twin — shipped with the masthead still on it. That PR's author flagged it as the one place they used judgement rather than instruction. The ruling came back the other way: the headset's plate is a transcript, a composer, and the tools they need.

## The bar is not rendered

Not emptied, not hidden, not collapsed to nothing. That was the bar #576 set for itself — a collapsed rail was refused precisely because it stayed in the DOM and in the layout — and a masthead that rendered empty would be the same refusal a second time. The tests assert **absence from the tree**, not invisibility.

Gone from the solo route with it: the breadcrumb out to the project canvas, the session title, the inline rename, the session action menu (settle, delete, the rest), the rail's restore trigger and Open-in-Finder. Which also means there is no way out of the route — wanted rather than tolerated, for a conversation a headset is looking at.

## Two controls survive, because each was the last door

I inventoried the bar before deleting it, and two of its controls turned out to have no second mount site anywhere in the app:

- **Notes** (`WorkspaceInspector`) is the only place a note can be *written* — `ProjectNoteEditor` has no other mount site. The composer's `@` menu reads the same notebook and cannot write to it, so dropping this would have left the headset able to quote a note and unable to make one.
- **Run** (`RunHeaderControl`) likewise: setup, start and stop live there or nowhere. Only "Watch output" went, because watching happens in a right panel this route does not have — which #576 had already decided.

Both are rehomed into the conversation column as `SoloTools`: a zero-height flex child (`h-0`) holding an absolutely-positioned pair. The transcript loses no height — the whole reason the route exists — and because the transcript is centred at `max-w-[50rem]`, on the 1100×700 plate the cluster sits in the ~150px gutter rather than over the words.

## Mechanism

Follows the route's existing mechanism rather than adding another: the cockpit's own `solo` prop decides this, not a third test of the pathname. `app-shell.tsx`'s `isSoloRoute` is untouched.

`SessionMasthead` no longer takes a `solo` prop at all. It is only ever rendered off the solo route now, so the three branches inside it that tested `solo` were dead code and are removed.

## Off the solo route, nothing changes

Asserted rather than assumed — the ordinary-route tests check the masthead is present with its title, its action menu and its link back to the canvas, and that Notes and Run are still *inside* the bar rather than duplicated out of it. That pairing is also what keeps the absence assertions from being vacuous: the same selectors that return `null` on the solo route return an element on the ordinary one.

## Checks

`bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint` (0 errors; 9 pre-existing warnings, none in the changed code) and `bun run test` (6,383 pass, 0 fail) all green locally.

Refs #576 — that issue is already closed; this does not reopen or close it.

author: robobun
body:
Stacked on #43151.

### Problem

- #43151 adds 23 instructions to every `process.nextTick` tick in a program that makes no `Bun.ModuleGraph`. A bare loop of 3e6 ticks goes from 732.3 M to 812.4 M instructions (x1.11).
- The cause is the tick loop in `src/js/builtins/ProcessObjectInternals.ts`. It runs `graph !== restoreGraph` before and after each callback. Both operands have an unknown type, so the FTL JIT type-checks both (8 instructions) and branches twice.

### Fix

- Compare each operand with `undefined`. A compare with a constant needs no type check. When a side is a graph, the loop writes the graph slot and a local makes the restore put it back.
- The behavior is the same. When the tick's graph is already current, the loop writes the same value again.
- Instructions per tick over #43151's base (FTL / DFG / baseline): #43151 +23 / +42 / +125, this PR +16 / +35 / +107. The 3e6 loop takes 790.9 M. In FTL code a tick inside a graph costs less than in #43151.
- Verified: the new test in `module-graph-callbacks.test.ts`, all of `test/js/bun/module-graph/`, `process-nexttick.test.js`, `test/js/node/async_hooks/`.

### Background

- `$asyncContext` is a two-field tuple on the global object. Field 0 is the `AsyncLocalStorage` frame. Field 1, new in #43151, is the current `Bun.ModuleGraph` (`undefined`: the host).
- A tick object keeps both from its `process.nextTick()` call. The loop installs them before the callback and restores the earlier values after.
- The new test drains ticks while a graph's context is current between them. No test covered that path: a loop that ignores it passes 321 tests in three module-graph files.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

**The test and the change.** The new test passes with and without this change. The change has no behavior that can fail first. The test is here because a wrong version of this loop passed every existing test. It uses `expect().resolves`, which runs the event loop where it is called, here inside `graph.run()`. That is how a graph's context is current between the ticks. The host's tick is the last one, so a missing restore shows too. Checked on a debug build against two broken loops: with the restore removed the test fails with `after the wait: host`, with the swap removed it fails with `b: ran in a`.

**Method.** The container has no hardware counters, so the counts come from DynamoRIO `inscount` on local release builds, with `BUN_JSC_useConcurrentJIT=0`. "Per tick" is the slope between N = 1e6 and N = 3e6 ticks, so start-up and JIT compile time drop out. Three repetitions agree within 1 instruction per tick. `BUN_JSC_useFTLJIT=0` and `BUN_JSC_useDFGJIT=0` give the DFG and baseline rows. The table comes from one release binary of this branch that holds the base's loop, the loop of #43151 and this PR's loop, and picks one at start-up. Separate release builds of fd8422ce4 and 1715c938c67 give the same numbers for the first two. The bare loop totals match an independent `perf stat -e instructions:u` run of the same script on other hardware (727 M and 807 M).

Instructions per tick, against the base (one binary that holds the three loops, built from this branch):

| script | tier | #43151 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nextTick(f)` | FTL | +22.7 | +16.5 |
| `nextTick(f, a, b)` | FTL | +22.4 | +15.9 |
| `nextTick(f)` inside `als.run()` | FTL | +24.8 | +16.0 |
| `nextTick(f)` | DFG | +42.5 | +34.7 |
| `nextTick(f)` | baseline | +125.4 | +106.6 |
| `nextTick(f)` inside a graph | FTL | +27.8 | +23.5 |
| `nextTick(f, a, b)` inside a graph | FTL | +27.6 | +25.3 |
| `nextTick(f)` inside a graph | DFG | +39.8 | +42.5 |
| `nextTick(f)` inside a graph | baseline | +184.6 | +164.4 |
| host ticks after a graph existed | FTL | +15.0 | +14.4 |

Totals for the bare loop of 3e6 ticks: base 732.3 M, #43151 812.4 M, this PR 790.9 M.

**The size of the loop decides when it reaches the FTL.** The first version of this PR kept `graph !== restoreGraph` inside the new `if`. Its steady state was the same, but its total for 3e6 ticks was 797.8 M: about 7 M more before the steady state. The cause was a later tier-up, not a dearer compile. With the concurrent JIT off, JSC compiles the loop with the FTL after tick 132,000 for 354 bytes of bytecode (base), 429 (#43151) and 438 (this PR), and after tick 146,000 for 442 (the first version). Twelve variants between 354 and 581 bytes show the same step between 438 and 442. Those 14,000 ticks in DFG code cost about 480 instructions more each, 6.7 M in total. Without the inner compare the loop is 438 bytes and tiers up where it did before.

**Where the 23 instructions are (FTL, from the Air listing of `processTicksAndRejections`).** All of it is in this builtin: the base's loop pasted into a build of #43151 measures the same as the base. In the loop: a load of field 1 (3), a load of `tock.graph` (2), two `Check:Other` for the compare (8), the branch (2) and the same branch again after the callback (3 to 4). In `nextTick()`: a load of field 1 (2), a `Check:Other` that the JIT adds so that it can skip the write barrier (4), the store (1) and one more structure write (1). This PR removes the two checks and the second branch. In a program with no graph the FTL proves that the local is `false` and drops the restore branch.

**What is left, and what else was measured.** About 16 instructions per tick remain: the fourth property of the tick object, one load of field 1 in `nextTick()` and one in the loop. Other shapes, same method, FTL `nextTick(f)`:

- Unconditional writes of field 1 in place of the compare: +25.7. Worse than #43151.
- `(graph !== undefined || restoreGraph !== undefined) && graph !== restoreGraph` as one expression: +11 with the change to `nextTick()` below, but +140 in baseline code, which is worse than #43151. The `if` form in this PR is better in every tier.
- The same two compares with `undefined` again after the callback, and no local: +17.6, and +22.6 inside `als.run()`.
- `graph: undefined` in the literal and a conditional write after it: 3 fewer in FTL, 6 more in baseline code, 3 to 26 more for a tick inside a graph. Not included.
- The graph as an own property only on ticks that were queued inside a graph, read with `$getByIdDirect`: +17.8. The DFG does not fold the miss.
- The slow path in a separate function: same cost for the host, +117 for a tick inside a graph.
- A marker callback on ticks that were queued inside a graph, so that other ticks have the three properties of the base: +9.6 (DFG +18, baseline +55), and +56 for a tick inside a graph.
- A wrapper callback that enters the graph itself, so that the loop is the base's: +3.8 (DFG +9, baseline +29), and +161 for a tick inside a graph.

The last two change what a tick object looks like, and they move cost to ticks inside a graph. This PR does neither.

**Debug build.** On the debug build in this container `module-graph.test.ts` and `module-graph-io.test.ts` have tests that reach the 5 s timeout (no assertion fails). The machine had a load average of 75 to 150. `executables and CodeBlocks are shared across graphs` does the same on a debug build of #43151 without this change. On the release build of this branch all 2370 tests of the suites above pass.

author: finnformica
body:
A note's page and a focused block's page draw the same walk of the graph. This narrows that walk **in place** rather than sending you to a list of results: the rows that match stay, the rows above them stay as dimmed context so you can see where each match lives, and the branches holding nothing you asked for go.

It is drawn by the same `BlockNoteEditor`, from the note's own doc, so the markers, typography, folds and keys are the note page's by construction — `fixedRoots` (which flattens headings, widens root surfaces and makes note rows roomy in the results list) never comes into it. A list of unticked boxes is one pick from the header, and ticking one still ticks it in the note.

**Sort** and **Filter** sit beside the **⋯** menu at the top right. Both live in the URL (`?filter=type:todo&sort=text:desc`), so a narrowed view is a link and the back button takes the narrowing off.

## One vocabulary, one engine

The filter is a query, run by `searchBlocks` scoped to the note (`src/utils/view-narrowing.ts`). There is no second implementation of the query language: every qualifier works in a note's filter on the day it works in the search box — `type:` on the block, `in:` on its ancestry, `has:` / `no:` / `date:` / a property on the containing note, `-` to exclude, comma lists to OR, free text fuzzy-matched over the block's own text.

A note-level qualifier behaves honestly rather than being ignored: inside one note it holds for every row or for none, so `area:work` shows the whole note or nothing — which is what the same query means in a search.

The menus read their keys and values from the query box's own picker vocabulary (`STATIC_QUALIFIER_OPTIONS`, `dateQualifierOptions`, `sortQualifierOptions`), so the Filter menu branches on every qualifier the language has and cannot offer a different set. A key added to the query language appears in the menu with it.

Sorting is the search's own comparator (`compareBlockHits`), which gains `text` and `type` so both halves of the app share one list of sort keys — `sort:text` and `sort:type` now work in search too. A sort reorders each parent's children and leaves the nesting alone.

## A pin that remembers its view

A pinned block can carry a `filter` and a `sort` in its props, turning a pin from a place into a view — "the open to-dos under this heading" rather than "this heading". The sidebar opens it with them.

The save is always deliberate: while the view differs from what the pin saved, the button that moved carries a dot and the header offers **Update to default** and **Reset to default**. Nothing tried out in passing overwrites what was saved.

## The data-safety constraint

`docToOps` reconciles child order, so handing it a filtered doc would read every hidden row as removed — and a removal is an unlink. While a filter or sort is on, `useNoteDoc` keeps only the ops that change a row's own value (`setText` / `setType` / `setProps`) and drops the structural ones.

The consequence is a real limitation, and it falls out of the safety argument rather than a preference: **a narrowed view edits its rows, not the note's shape.** You can tick a box or retype a line; adding, indenting, deleting and reordering belong to the note, one click away with the filter cleared. For the same reason a narrowed view has no trailing blank row — a row that swallowed typing would be a lie.

Held by tests in `src/hooks/note-doc.test.tsx`, including the worst case of the view handing back an empty root list. Also confirmed in the browser: ticking a to-do inside a filtered view and then clearing the filter leaves every row of the note intact.

## Note on behaviour

Ticking a `type:todo` row makes it vanish immediately, since the filter re-runs against the live graph. Freezing the match set until the filter is re-run is a small change if that reads better in use.

## Checks

1899 tests across 94 files, `lint`, `knip`, `check:queries`, `check:worker`, `check:changelog` and `build` all pass. Two existing assertions in `qualifier-suggestions.test.ts` and `query-box.test.tsx` were updated for the two added `sort:` keys.

Docs updated in `docs/query-language.md` and `docs/metadata.md`; changelog entry in `changelog/2026-W38/`.

author: k35o
body:
## 概要

Renovate の #676（vite-plus 0.3.0 → 0.3.1 を含む non-major 一括更新）で、全パッケージの build が install の段階で落ちています。catalog の `vite` を本家 vite から `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core` の別名に変え、それに合わせてフレームワークのアプリを `vp` で起動・ビルドするようにします。

このブランチは #676 のコミット（`6535a801`）をそのまま含み、その上に修正を積んでいます。これをマージすれば #676 は不要になります。

## 動機

#676 の Tests / Lint / TypeScript / Package / Apps & Examples は、どれも同じエラーで落ちています。

```
packages/form build: error: Failed to resolve pack command: GenericFailure,
Expected @voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@0.3.1, but found vite@8.3.0 at .../node_modules/vite/package.json.
Run `vp migrate` to align the Vite alias, then run `vp install`.
```

vite-plus 0.3.1（voidzero-dev/vite-plus#2617）から、`vp pack` / `vp dev` の前にチェックが入りました。実行するパッケージの package.json が `vite` を宣言している場合、その `vite` が CLI と同じ版の `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core` でなければ止まります。k8ordo は catalog で本家 vite を指していたので、全パッケージがこれに引っかかります。vite 8.2.2 → 8.3.0 の更新は原因ではなく、8.2.2 のままでも落ちます。

## 変更

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: catalog の `vite` を `npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@0.3.1` にしました。理由はコメントに残しています。
- `renovate.json`: `vite-plus` と `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core` を同じグループにしました。版がずれると `vp pack` が落ちるので、片方だけの PR を出させないためです。
- apps/docs・examples/static-basic・examples/server-basic: scripts の `vite` / `vite build` を `vp dev` / `vp build` にしました。テストの中でビルドを呼ぶ箇所（static-basic の `build.test.ts`、server-basic の `global-setup.ts`）も同じです。core は `vite` コマンドを持たないため、そのままだと `vite: not found` で落ちます。
- `packages/state/src/schema/object.ts`: zod 4.6.2 で不要になった `as StateValues` を外しました。#676 の zod 更新で `no-unnecessary-type-assertion` になっていたものです。

### 採らなかった案

- **使っていないパッケージから `vite` の宣言を外す**: 直接 `vite` を import していないパッケージ（ui / form / state / router / color-scheme / i18n と ui-* example）から宣言を外す案です。framework-engine / static / server は peer として宣言しているので、どのみち落ちます。さらに、宣言を外したパッケージには pnpm が peer 用に本家 vite を自動で入れるので、vitest の実体が割れて `expect.element` の型が消えます。
- **3アプリだけ本家 vite を名前付き catalog で残す**: アプリは本家 vite で動く一方、ワークスペースから link された `@k8ordo/static` などは自分の `node_modules` の vite（= core）を読みます。1つのビルドに2つの Vite 実体が混ざるので採りませんでした。

## レビューで見てほしいところ

- **k8ordo 自身のアプリは本家 Vite ではなく Vite+ の core で動くようになります。** static / server の GUIDE や docs サイトは、利用者に `vite dev` / `vite build` を案内したままです。利用者向けの案内としてはそれで正しいのですが、「利用者と同じ本家 Vite で試す」形ではなくなります。
- core の版は 0.3.1 なので、`@k8ordo/static` / `framework-engine` の peer `vite >=8.2.1` や `@vitejs/plugin-react` の `^8.0.0` を満たさず、`pnpm peers check` が警告を出します。install は通ります。
- 公開パッケージの peer 範囲や振る舞いは変えていないので、changeset は付けていません。state の変更は型アサーションを外しただけです。

## 確認

手元（worktree）で、CI の各ジョブと同じコマンドを実行しました。

- `pnpm --filter './packages/*' build`
- `pnpm --filter './apps/*' build`、`pnpm build:examples`、`pnpm test:examples`（Apps & Examples と同じ。static-basic の壊れた設定のテストも含めて全件通る）
- `pnpm typecheck`、`pnpm check`、`pnpm check:no-polyfills`、`pnpm check:peer-copies`
- packages/* 9つのテスト（ui は 424 件）

## Summary

Implements the promotion/discount module (Requerimiento 2): a `Promotion` hierarchy
with three discount strategies, persistence, a service that automatically picks the
best applicable promotion for a sale, and full integration into the sales flow.

- **Model**: abstract `Promotion` (id, name, date range, `isActive`, abstract
  `calculateDiscount(Sale)`) with three subclasses — `PercentageDiscount`,
  `CategoryDiscount` (VIDEOGAME/CONSOLE via `instanceof`), and `BulkPurchaseDiscount`.
- **Persistence**: `PromotionRepository`, CSV-backed (`data/promotions.csv`) with a
  type discriminator, following the same pattern as the other repositories.
- **Service**: `PromotionService` — registration per type, active-promotion listing,
  and `findBestPromotionFor(Sale)`, which compares every valid promotion and returns
  the one granting the highest discount (never combines promotions).
- **Integration (additive)**: `Sale` gained `appliedPromotionName`/`discountAmount`
  and `generateReceipt()`; `SaleService.registerSale` now applies the best promotion
  automatically; `ConsoleUI` got a new "Gestión de promociones" submenu (menu option
  renumbered — conflict expected on merge with sibling module branches, see PR
  discussion); `Main` wires the new repository/service.
- **Data**: `data/promotions.csv` preloaded with one promotion of each type, valid
  through the end of the month.

- [x] Full project compiles clean (`javac` across all sources).

author: bradgroux
body:
Interrupted archived actions could be assessed but remained permanently pending. Add explicit trusted-host decisions to accept verified output or close an unknown outcome after fresh worker absence. Rust records each decision separately from ordinary settlement, preserves request deduplication and cancellation, and never automatically resumes or retries work.

The host adapter prepares an inspectable review plan and rechecks action/scope/ticket, archive integrity, runtime absence and journal sequence/generation at commit. Reviewed output has a separate readback interface with provenance. Recovery report version 3 exposes recorded reviews without relabeling them as normal settlement.

Verification: 147 local tests passed (18 Rust, 127 Node, two Python), formatting, Clippy, build and documentation checks. A rebuilt Linux ARM64 image passed seven selected runtime probes: 15 reconciliation tests, 16 recovery tests, 13 archive/index tests, native startup/browser, separated supervisor, nine Codex callback scenarios and cancellation/review recovery. A probe variable-shadowing error was corrected and the affected probe passed on rerun. Final review covered the pending diff and new files. Test containers were removed and the dedicated VM stopped. GitHub CI remains disabled.

Journal format 6 rejects older fixture journals without modifying them; archive envelopes remain version 1. Review labels and worker assertions depend on trusted host setup, not authenticated human accounts. Whole-host ownership reconstruction, production task integration and power-loss testing remain open. No live inference, personal data, messaging, deployment or image publication occurred.

author: hanahmily
body:
## Summary

Implementing and reviewing time-bucket grouping (apache/skywalking#14089, #1362) surfaced three places where the merged [tag aggregation and time bucketing design](docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md) (#1360) no longer matches what actually shipped:

- **§7.5** claimed liaison-merge and index-mode ordering were bucket-ascending "by construction," same as the node-local streaming case. Both actually need an explicit sort (`BatchAggregation.SortInsertionByBucket`), added in #1362 after two review rounds found the gap. Node-local ordering is still free; the doc now says which case is which, and flags that COUNT_DISTINCT's distributed reduce (§7.4, apache/skywalking#14090) shares this same reduce path and must not re-introduce the false assumption.
- **§7.2**'s "relaxes to a pipelined operator" undersold the actual change: a `BreakerOperator` cannot be pipelined by relaxation, since `breakerStage`'s contract fully drains upstream before serving output. The doc now names the real fix (`BatchTimeBucket` as a genuine `PullOperator`, spliced in via a new `PipelineBuilder.Transform` primitive) and the follow-up fix for map-mode's terminal aggregator (`drainMapModeAggregator`), both discovered during review.
- **§3** never stated whether `group_by.time_bucket` requires `agg`. It does, for a concrete reason found during implementation (the no-`agg` shape doesn't preserve the full output schema) — recorded as a current limitation, not a permanent decision.

No behavior change — the shipped code already reflects all three corrections. This is a documentation-only PR to keep the design doc accurate for whoever picks up apache/skywalking#14090 (COUNT_DISTINCT) and apache/skywalking#14091 (BydbQL) next.

## Test plan

- Docs-only change; no code affected.
- Verified the patch applies cleanly on top of `main` (post-#1362) and section numbering/headers remain consistent.

author: vavi
body:
## Problem

Self-service created tenants only received the core plugin profile. A deployment's vertical product (concretely: the Xiaoya edu plugins) was therefore missing from every new tenant — the tenant template seeded roles/permissions/menus, but models and commands were not registered, so every product command answered `Command not found` (FR-070 positive chain blocked).

## Change

`aura.tenant.product-plugins` (comma-separated plugin source directories, absolute or relative to the builtin plugins base directory). Entries are imported for every new tenant after the core profile, in declared order, through the same preview / version-check / execute flow as catalogue plugins. The platform catalogue stays free of product entries; a missing directory is warned and skipped so a stale declaration cannot break tenant creation.

Refactors `importPlugin` into a shared directory flow and takes the plugin id from the import preview (identical behaviour for catalogue entries).

## Evidence (real stack, 2026-09-18)

Backend run with `--aura.tenant.product-plugins=<aura-edu>/plugin-aura/edu-core,<aura-edu>/plugin-aura/edu-engine`, then a fresh self-service tenant (实验小学I校):

- tenant create + template seed + space-switch + `xy_school_admin` binding: green
- `xy:create_cls` / `xy:create_stu` / `xy:create_enr` inside the new tenant: completed with record pids (previously `Command not found`)
- isolation probes P1/P3/P5 green; school-A marker/export probes skip on a separate, pre-existing platform issue (multi-mode default-tenant guarded-write denial, reproduced with the old jar on 2026-09-18 before this branch existed)
- `BuiltinPluginImportServiceImplTest`: 10/10 (3 new regression tests: ordered import from config, missing-dir skip, blank-config no-op)

…rint()

Mobile browsers render print at phone viewport width (~390px), collapsing the two-column layout and making the page much taller than on desktop. No CSS zoom adjustment fixes this because zoom scales output, not layout width.

Fix: in exportPDF(), set document.documentElement.style.minWidth='820px' before window.print() so the layout renders at desktop-equivalent width, keeping content height the same as desktop. Restore on afterprint event.

Also revert #site zoom back to 0.85 (was 0.82) with min-height:118vh.

body:
## 왜

이 계산기는 모든 비용이 "1인당" 아니면 "매출의 %"라서 명수가 분자·분모에서 약분돼 사라졌다. 그래서 20명이든 40명이든 1인당 필요 판매수량이 늘 같게 나왔고, 화면은 그걸 "명수와 무관하다"고 단정했다.

계산은 맞다. 다만 그게 참인 이유가 **"명수와 무관하게 나가는 비용이 하나도 없다"는 가정 때문**이라는 건 어디에도 적혀 있지 않았다. 영상 제작비·대행 수수료를 넣는 순간 결론이 뒤집힌다.

## 변경 내용

- **고정비 입력칸** 추가. 고정비는 명수로 나눠 1인당 지출에 얹는다.
- 결과 패널에 **"1인당 지출 (지원비 + 고정비 분담)"** 행. 답이 왜 바뀌는지 보여주는 숫자라 고정비를 넣었을 때만 나온다.
- **"1인당 지표는 명수와 무관하다"** 안내 문구를 조건부로. 고정비가 있으면 거짓이 되는 문장이다.
- **ROAS 범위 문구**도 분기. 고정비를 넣으면 분모 구성이 달라진다.
- 지원비와 고정비가 **모두 0이면 차단**. 전에는 `Infinity`가 화면에 나갈 수 있었다.

지원비 10만 · CPS 15% · 목표 ROAS 2.5 · 객단가 29,900원 기준:

| 명수 | 고정비 0원 (기존) | 고정비 500만원 |
|---|---|---|
| 20명 | 13.4개 | 46.8개 |
| 30명 | 13.4개 | 35.7개 |
| 40명 | 13.4개 | **30.1개** |

- 고정비를 넣으면 명수가 늘수록 1인당 필요 매출·판매수량이 내려간다.
- 표에 "고정비 (명수 무관)" 행이 생기고 세 열 모두 같은 값이다.
- 고정비를 0으로 되돌리면 화면이 이전과 완전히 같아진다.

## 변경하지 않은 범위

- 다른 세 견적 도구, 루트 홈페이지, `work/` 는 건드리지 않았다.

body:
## Summary

The hand-rolled `.modal-overlay` dialogs in `supplier-comparison.js` (compare page), `budget.js` (Export Budget) and `timeline-builder.js` (Add/Edit Event) were missing standard dialog accessibility that the codebase's other modal implementations already have (`Modal` in `components.js`, `Lightbox.js`):

- No `role="dialog"` / `aria-modal="true"` / `aria-labelledby`
- No accessible name on the "×" close button
- No focus trap (Tab could escape the dialog into the page behind it)
- No Escape-to-close
- Focus was never returned to the trigger element on close

- Added `public/assets/js/utils/modal-a11y.js`, a small shared utility (`window.EFModalA11y.enhance(overlay, { labelledBy })`) that wires up all of the above for an existing overlay element. It works for any of the three callers' existing close paths (`.remove()`, backdrop click, form submit) without requiring changes to how any of them close their modal, since all of them detach the overlay from `document.body` one way or another — the utility watches for that via a `MutationObserver` and cleans up/restores focus automatically.
- Gave each modal's heading an `id` and wired it via `aria-labelledby`, and added `aria-label="Close"` to each close button.
- Loaded the new utility script on `compare.html`, `budget.html` and `timeline.html`, right before the component script that creates the modal.

Purely additive — no existing markup, ids, or business logic changed; only accessibility attributes and one `enhance()` call added per modal.

## Test plan
- [x] New jsdom-based verification script exercising the utility directly against the real `compare.html` modal markup: confirms `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`/`aria-labelledby` are set, initial focus lands on the first focusable element, Tab wraps last→first and Shift+Tab wraps first→last, and Escape removes the overlay and restores focus to the trigger element.
- [x] `npx eslint` clean on all four changed/added JS files.
- [x] Targeted Jest suites touching these pages (`signed-in-mobile-quality.test.js`, `messenger-audit-closure.test.js`): 83/83 passing.
- [x] Full `npm test`: 12228/12229 passing — the one failure is the pre-existing, documented MongoDB-connectivity timeout in `marketplace-image-deletion.test.js` (environment limitation of this sandbox, unrelated to this change, reproduces identically on `main`).

author: glenbenatiro
body:
## Why

`scripts/audit.sh` writes its log to `${SCRIPT_DIR:-.}/security-audit-<host>-<timestamp>.log` — i.e. right next to the script. Every run therefore leaves an untracked file in `git status`, waiting for a reflexive `git add .` to sweep it into a commit.

This is not hypothetical: two of them appeared while working on #3 and had to be removed by hand before that PR could be opened. `gh pr create` flagged them as uncommitted changes, which is the only reason they were noticed.

## Why it matters

These logs are a full security posture dump of a live host — every listening socket, the sudoers file including `NOPASSWD` grants, `authorized_keys` owners, successful SSH login sources, brute-force origins, credential-shaped container env var names, and the paths of any unencrypted private keys.

This repository is public. Committing one would publish a map of how to attack the box, and `git` being `git`, deleting it afterwards would not remove it from history.

## The pattern

`security-audit-*.log`, deliberately without a leading slash so it matches at any depth — the script can be run from anywhere, not just `scripts/`.

author: fvnguyen
body:
Implements plan_mobile_native_feel (T1–T4 complete; screenshots + device verification still open).

## Summary

Makes the installed PWA feel like a native mobile app by eliminating browser affordances that interfere with gameplay (long-press context menu, double-tap zoom), intercepting the hardware back button on screens with unsaved state, and removing friction-inducing per-move toasts in the deck builder.

## Changes

- **Global touch/selection CSS (D1–D2):** Added `touch-action: manipulation`, `-webkit-touch-callout: none`, and `-webkit-user-select: none` to `html, body` in `globals.css` to block OS context menus and double-tap zoom. Auth inputs/textareas opt back in via `user-select: text`.

- **Android back-button guard (D3–D4):** 
  - New `useAndroidBackGuard` hook that pushes a history entry on mount so the first back press is interceptable via `popstate`, then re-arms on every cancel to prevent stack growth. `goBack()` does `history.go(-2)` to undo both the guard entry and the real navigation.
  - New `BackGuardSheet` component (reusing `Overlay`/`Button`) with exactly two actions: "Cancel" and "Leave" — no silent discard, no "Save & exit" leg.
  - Wired into `DraftRoom` (picking phase only; disabled once deckbuilding starts), `DeckBuilder` (both `/roster/[id]` and post-draft entry points; off for read-only and embedded editor), and `SeasonView` (mid-game, reusing its existing `handleExitGame`).
  - Challenge run left unguarded per D3 (already safe: half-committed to store before render).

- **Deck builder toast cleanup (D7):** Removed two per-move `toastUndo` calls for place/swap operations in `DeckBuilder.tsx` (lines 466, 479) — these are two-way drags the user can trivially reverse by dragging back, and on mobile the toast covered the roster/depth chart. Kept roster-clear and error toasts (genuinely destructive/failure cases).

- **Audits (D5–D6):** Confirmed collapsible-bar tap targets and adjacent-icon hit areas already meet spec app-wide via existing patterns (`TopKPIBand` already toggles on any chip tap; `IconButton` guarantees 44×44px via `size-control` token) — no code changes needed.

## Implementation notes

- `useAndroidBackGuard` uses refs to avoid stale closures and re-arms the guard on every cancel so the history stack never grows.
- `BackGuardSheet` stops propagation on its inner div to prevent accidental dismissal via overlay click.
- Back guard is disabled in `DraftRoom` once `draftState` transitions to `'deckbuilding'` to avoid double prompts (DeckBuilder takes over).
- All three guarded screens provide context-specific messages ("Your picks so far will be lost…", "Changes to this roster aren't saved…", etc.).

Verification: `npm test` and `npm run build` green. Still open: screenshots confirming no context menu/zoom, and manual device check that back gesture shows the guard sheet (or season view's own leave-confirm) instead of immediate navigation.

author: damianvtran
body:
Removes the per-row browser mark from the chats sidebar — the dim Globe (with its tab count, its loading spinner and its approval badge) drawn at the right of every conversation row — and retires the apparatus behind it. The operator asked for it out, and for the slot it was sitting in:

> "I don't think we need a browser button for each chat row in local-operator-ui, can you remove that? Especially since we're going to have a pin icon that should show up on hover, it takes up too much space for a button that would be infrequently used."

**This reverses the ask the control was built for, and this PR says so rather than leaving the design record contradicting the code.** Design R2 is titled "a corner affordance on every conversation row"; `3996c3749`, which is what made it unconditional, records the earlier ask as "a corner tab on EACH conversation" (review round 1's D2/A4 is that change). `docs/design/sidebar-conversation-browser.md` now opens with a superseded note quoting BOTH asks, and R2 — including its states table — carries a heading marker saying so, so a reader landing there from a search cannot take it for the contract. The body is left as the record of a decision that was taken and then reversed.

Release: patch — the sidebar's per-row browser button is gone, every title keeps the width it held, and the browser is opened from the chat header's Globe.

## What the user gets

| where | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| every conversation row | a Globe: dim when quiet, `n` beside it when the conversation has tabs, a spinner while a tab loads, an attention badge with that conversation's waiting approvals | nothing; every title keeps the **28px** the control held (`size-6` 24px + the wrapper's `gap-1` 4px) |
| the conversation you are in | open its browser from the row's Globe, or the header's Globe | the header's Globe (unchanged, `chat-header.tsx`) |
| a conversation you are NOT in | one press on its row's mark | select the conversation first, then the header's Globe |
| another conversation's waiting approval, at a glance | the mark's badge | nothing in the chrome without opening the browser — see the capability cost below |

## Impact — the capability cost, inventoried

The first draft of this section named one loss and implied a second. Four review streams independently found the same under-listing (code review R3, design D3, UX U1, QA Q17/Q18), so here is the whole inventory, with the surviving surface named for each:

- **A non-current conversation can no longer have its browser opened from the sidebar** without being selected first. What survives: select the row, then the header's Globe — the pane follows the selection, so nothing about another conversation is shown by accident (UX round 1 walked it).
- **The row was the only place outside the browser showing a conversation's TAB COUNT and its LOADING state** — for any conversation, the current one included. The header's Globe carries approvals only (`browserBadgeDrawn = browserButtonShown && browserAttentionCount > 0`), no count and no spinner. Nothing survives this; the browser itself is where a count now lives.
- **It was the only surface reporting ANOTHER conversation's pending browser approvals** without opening the browser. The header's badge counts **this** conversation only, so it is null for a foreign request. QA round 1 reached the state the UX round could not (`request_access` with `requester: session:<other>`): on the base tree the conversation's mark carries `1 approval waiting` and exactly one of eight rows lights; on this head the document-wide scan finds two browser affordances, both the header's, **zero** in the sidebar, and the header badge is **null** for that request.
- **It was the only thing that normalised the pane's lens on the way in.** The pane's scope is one sticky preference (`ui-preferences-store.ts:452`, read at `browser-pane.tsx:89`), and the deleted handler reset it to that conversation. The header's Globe is unmounted while the pane is open (`chat-header.tsx:161`), so it cannot be pressed to re-scope: with the pane last left on `All tabs`, that is where the header's Globe reopens it and the in-pane switch is the only way back. The toggle semantics and their `aria-expanded` cue went with it.
- **One surface outside this component's chrome does still report a foreign approval**, and the first draft's "nothing else in the chrome carries a count" was too absolute (design D4): `src/main/browser/consent-notifier.ts` raises a native **"Site approval needed"** banner naming the count and the oldest origin, and its click brings the browser route forward. It names no conversation and it is gated to `show === "focus"`. **It is not observed in this PR's rigs** — every run here is headless, which suppresses native banners by design — so this is a record of what the code does, not a measurement, and it is stated that way rather than implied to have been checked.

**The one-line fix that would restore the lens is named and deliberately not taken**: keep the header's Globe mounted so it can toggle and normalise the pane's scope. That is a redesign of a control this change was not asked to touch, and it would re-open the header's focus-return and spacing rules and their pinned tests. Say the word and it is a follow-up.

`useConversationBrowserSummaries` **stays** — the header's badge reads it, and that is now its only consumer. `chat-page.tsx`'s `openConversationBrowser` and its `browserPaneOpenOn` derivation are deleted rather than kept: their only caller was the sidebar's mark (the header's trigger is `chat-content.tsx`'s own `setBrowserPaneOpen(true)`), and the toggle semantics they encoded belonged to the control that is gone. `useUiPreferencesStore` fell out of that file's imports with them.

## Accepted known states, recorded rather than fixed

- **The pane's scope outlives the pane** (UX U3): open the pane, switch to `All tabs`, close it, press the header's Globe — it reopens on `All tabs` while the control says `Open browser`. One press of the in-pane switch fixes it, so this is an expectation mismatch rather than a trap; it is the same sticky preference the fourth bullet above is about, and it is accepted here rather than re-scoped in this change.
- **`Enter` on a row hands focus to the composer** (UX U4): a keyboard user stepping the list with `ArrowDown` then `Enter` ends the traversal. Unchanged by this branch on both trees (`message-input.tsx`, untouched here) and arguably intentional; recorded only because it is also why the Globe's refocus guard stays quiet after a pointer selection, so the next reader of that guard does not read it as a regression of this change.
- **The retired rows are gone from every list at once**, and the counts are **11 + 1 = 12** — eleven `browser-conversation-mark--*` capture rows (the eleven stories the deleted story file exported) plus the `chat-sidebar-status-feed--browser-marks` row whose fixture fed the mark's cascade into a real sidebar row (code review R4; the comment, this body and the manifest disagreed).

### What was retired, rather than left dark

- `features/browser/components/browser-conversation-mark.tsx` and its `.stories.tsx`;
- `docs/evidence/browser-conversation-mark/` (138 WebP + its three live PNGs) and `docs/evidence/chat-sidebar-status-feed/browser-marks/` (12), with their `manifest.json` declarations re-derived;
- the twelve capture rows in `scripts/capture-evidence.mjs`'s STORIES literal (11 + 1 above), and the `chat-sidebar-status-feed--browser-marks` story with its fixture map and the readout line that reported it;
- `scripts/renderer-driver.mjs`'s `browser-mark` scene and its `markReading` helper (the selector it drove no longer exists), with a note where the scene was naming what it used to prove and where that lives now;
- `scripts/contrast-contract.mjs`'s `conversation browser mark badge` row and its three `highlight`-ground edge pins — the control is what reached that ground, and a pin whose surfac

author: tmiw
body:
## Summary
#55 broke the macOS `lint` CI job in `freedv-gui` (PR #1498): RNNoise's own `./configure` started failing with `C compiler cannot create executables` once `CC`/`CXX` became a two-word string (`"ccache <compiler>"`).

## Investigation
That two-word form is the standard, normally reliable ccache+autotools idiom, so I tried to reproduce the failure in isolation before assuming it was structurally broken:
- Checked out RNNoise at the exact pinned commit (`70f1d25`) used by `BuildRNNoise.cmake`.
- Ran `./autogen.sh && ./configure` with the exact same `CC`/`CXX` shape, first against a trivial pass-through stand-in for `ccache`, then against the real `ccache` 4.14 binary (matching the CI log's version exactly).
- Both times, RNNoise's **full** configure — including its libtool and compiler-feature-detection checks, not just a trivial compile test — completed successfully with `Automatic configuration OK`.

So the two-word form isn't inherently broken, at least not in a way I could reproduce outside CI's actual parallel-build load on that specific macOS runner/LLVM install. I don't have a confirmed root cause for the CI failure itself.

## Fix
Rather than re-land the same construct and hope it holds up, this generates a small wrapper script (`exec "$launcher" "$compiler" "$@"`) and points `CC`/`CXX` at that instead of baking the launcher directly into a compound string. This keeps `CC`/`CXX` a single, ordinary-looking path in every case, so nothing downstream — `configure`, `libtool`, `make` — ever has to parse a compound value. It's a strictly more conservative, standard pattern regardless of what actually went wrong in CI.

## Verification
- Confirmed end-to-end locally: `./configure` succeeds with the wrapper script as `CC`, and an actual `make` compile confirms ccache genuinely gets invoked (cache miss recorded on the first compile, as expected).
- Confirmed via a standalone CMake test harness that the Apple-universal branch's generated `ExternalProject` configure command now carries a clean, single-token `CC=`/`CXX=` (no embedded spaces) in both the x86 and arm sub-builds.

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge and let `freedv-gui`'s CI (currently pinned to the pre-#55 commit to work around this) pick it up, then confirm the macOS `lint` job's RNNoise build succeeds.
- [ ] If it still fails, the two-word-CC hypothesis is fully ruled out and the next step is investigating parallel-build resource contention specifically (the failure occurred while several other `ExternalProject`/compile targets were building concurrently via `make -jN`).

author: amitsharmaak
body:
## Summary
Phase P5 of the performance plan. The first HTML now contains the data for `/` and `/feed`.

- **`src/lib/feed/feed-params.ts`** — one zod contract + read (`parseFeedQuery`, `loadFeedPage`) shared by `GET /api/v1/feed` and the `/feed` page; `feed-url.ts` holds the client-safe URL helpers.
- **`src/lib/server-render/page-data.ts`** — `loadPageData`: proxy identity handoff + one `withTenantRepositories` transaction; `null` → the island fetches (no PostgreSQL, `FEATURE_SERVER_RENDER=false`, no resolvable user, data failure).
- **`/feed`** is an async server component; **`FeedList`** is the island (URL = source of truth, filter changes via `router.replace` in a transition, load-more and status poll stay on the API, `?q=` search unchanged).
- **`/`** runs Today's selection server-side; `TodayExperience` becomes presentational with an API fallback.
- **Deleted `app/loading.tsx` and `app/feed/loading.tsx`** — see below.

## Finding that changed the design — please read
Following the brief literally (page data behind the loading boundaries) made LCP **worse**: 96 → 340 ms. The served HTML shows React 19's Fizz runtime recording the shell paint in `$RT` and scheduling every later Suspense reveal at `$RT + 300 ms`; a 15 ms data load is held to ~340 ms. The reader page has been paying the same 300 ms since P2. Blocking the document on the data instead: `/` LCP **100 → 40 ms**, `/feed` **96 → 52 ms**, TTFB +10 ms, zero API calls on load, bundle +140 B / +110 B gzip. Two more measurement-driven fixes: the first cut was statically prerendered at build time (env guard before `headers()`), and the island had pulled zod into the client (+87 KB). `cacheComponents` spike run and not adopted (build fails on segment configs; would reintroduce the throttle). Full evidence in the checkpoint "Performance P5: server-render `/` and `/feed` — 2026-09-18".

## Verification (local, `f8be846`)
- `npm run check`: 210 suites / 1,499 tests; lint 0 errors / 5 baseline warnings; tsc clean.
- `npm run test:e2e` desktop-chromium: 9 passed / 1 flag-skipped (the suite runs without a session and exercises the fallback island, unchanged).
- `npm run build`: `/` and `/feed` both `ƒ (Dynamic)`.
- `perf:vitals` (production build, Docker Postgres, legacy session, 5 runs) and `perf:bundle` vs a fresh main baseline — table in the checkpoint.

Not deployed. Production LCP/TTFB reading after merge needs a signed-in session.

author: wilsonrocks
body:
Closes #110.

## The bug

`AnimatedRegions` builds the choropleth in two effects:

- **path creation** — deps `[features, width, height]`; waits for the lazily-imported `#/data/uk-regions-geo` chunk, then `.data(features).join('path')` setting `d`/`stroke`. It never set `fill`.
- **fill** — deps `[countMap]`.

On first load `features` is `null`, so the path effect bails. `countMap` settles early (the "initialise to end frame" effect fires on mount) and the fill effect runs against an empty SVG. The geometry import resolves *later*; the path effect then creates the paths, but `countMap` hasn't changed so the fill effect never re-runs. The paths keep the SVG default fill — black — until pressing play mutates `countMap`.

The homepage thumbnail (`regions-map-card.tsx`) was unaffected: it sets `d`, `stroke` and `fill` in a single pass.

## The fix

- Seed `fill` in the same `.join('path')` chain that creates the paths (reading counts through a ref so paths aren't rebuilt every animation tick).
- Add `features` to the fill effect's deps so the colouring pass also runs once the geometry arrives.

## Testing

Added `site/src/components/animated-regions.test.tsx`, which renders the component, waits for the geometry, and asserts every map path has an explicit non-black fill. Verified it fails on the unfixed component and passes with the fix.

`npm run typecheck` and `npm run test` (25 tests) both pass in `site/`. Not yet checked in a browser.

## Summary
- Adds `modules/oligarchy-archive.nix` (`custom.archive.enable`): a thin on-demand CLI bridging `oligarchy-vault pack` → `reliquary ingest`. No timer/service; stops at ingest — pushing to USB or burning a CD-R stay separate manual steps.
- Plain module (not a sub-flake) that reaches the `oligarchy-vault`/`reliquary` packages via `specialArgs`, same pattern as `modules/hydramesh.nix`.
- Opt-in, defaults off, no ISO `mkForce` needed.

**Stacked on #33 (`feat/reliquary`)**: this module resolves `reliquary`'s package through `specialArgs`, so it needs that flake input present to evaluate. Base is `feat/reliquary`, not `main` — once #33 merges, GitHub will auto-retarget this to `main`.

## Test plan
- [x] Full manual pipeline run against disposable test data: `oligarchy-archive` → `reliquary verify` → `reliquary extract` → `age -d` recovers original bytes exactly, in both `PATH --flag` and `--flag PATH` argument orders

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## What this adds

One new file, `docs/audit-triage.md` (307 lines). No source, shader or briefing edits.

Four outside reports audited this codebase from an uploaded text dump. Each was largely right, each was wrong in different places, and they overlap heavily. This merges them into a single list where **every claim was re-checked by opening this tree at the cited line** rather than trusting the report, and keeps the refuted claims visible so nobody re-runs a dead theory.

## Headline items

**Code, not docs:**

- `march_chunk` is handed an unguarded direction by `trace_world` (`common.wgsl:2339`), `trace_local` (`:2135`) and `shadow_ray_t` (`:2238`) while its DDA divides by it (`:1381`) — a zero component gives `±inf`, then `0 * inf` = `NaN`. This is the mechanism behind the retained `validation/glass-transport-results.txt` failure. The house guard already exists at `ray_dir` (`:1006`), which is why the primary path is safe and only the secondary legs are exposed.
- `shadow_ray_t` (`:2221`) has no water-surface skip though `shadow_ray` has one at `:2098` — a divergence in an A/B the docs call exact.
- `menu.rs:111` is `Setting::ShadowPass=>p.shadow_pass=true` among three `=!p.x` neighbours. Unreachable today; an on-never-can-go-off switch the moment the row is wired.
- `SOFT_TAPS` / `SOFT_MISS_DIST` are supplied by the override table and read by no shader; `common.wgsl:2263` documents a function body that no longer exists.

**The finding with the widest blast radius:** every sample A/B recipe in `EXPERIMENTS.md:118-126` runs with the dedicated shadow pass **on**, because `--no-shadow-pass` sets it to `true` (`config.rs:974-975`). The `control.png` / `split.png` pair presented as combined-vs-split is not that comparison, and the architecture table's `Off`/`Off` row is unreachable. That does not just misdescribe the build — it retroactively voids measurements taken with those commands.

**Docs:** the `SPACING 8 → 4` cluster (15 present-tense sites, including `CLAUDE.md:506`'s row asserting the figure "cannot drift" — it drifted), the `~142 MB` / `96.5% free` VRAM arithmetic, `--probe-sun` documented as runnable when the parser only knows `--no-probe-sun` and `--probe-sun-high`, and `--water-mottle` still sold as a live control after WA01 force-zeroed it.

**Rendering:** unescaped pipes break table rows at `CLAUDE.md:149`, `ledger.md:87` and `ledger.md:136`; rows 28/28b/29 and `D1` are detached from their tables. `tests/docs.rs` cannot see any of this — it checks links and flags, not table shape.

## Claims corrected, not carried over

- The "`src/bin/` was silently deleted by the export tool, and the ledger records the binaries as landed" story is **refuted**: `docs/ledger.md:136` records that `git log --all -- src/bin` shows it was never tracked on any ref, and that HEAD carrying no `src/bin` is what made a batch-102 revert binary legitimate. What survives is the real defect — the vacuous early-return guard in `tests/bins.rs`. One of the three audits hedged correctly; two guessed.
- `docs/pitfalls.md:74` "Four of the five PDFs" is a statement about a newline heuristic, not a third count of `docs/research/` competing with `research-review.md:3-7`.
- 13.84 MiB at 1080p is the 7 B/px all-in figure for three shadow textures, not the size of the R16F blocker map (3.96 MiB).

## Deliberate exclusions

Dated batch rows are left alone. `PERF.md:338-339`, `:377` and the `ledger.md` batch 57/59/93 rows describe what those batches measured, and under this repo's own vantage convention they are correct as history. Only present-tense statements are flagged.

## Verification limits

No `cargo`, no `rustc`, no GPU in the environment this was checked in. So:

- Confirmed by reading source: every `file:line` citation above, the `=!p.` count in `menu.rs:110-120` (13, matching the report's figure), the `0..6000` settle loop in `tests/lod_stream.rs:28` and `tests/shadow_grid.rs:36`, and `tests/experiments.rs:57`'s two-row assertion.
- **Not re-derived:** the clippy warning total, the 372/10 test split, and every timing figure. Those stay the original authors' measurements and the file says so inline rather than implying this PR ran them.

Line numbers are this checkout's. The reconstructed trees the audits worked in sit one line lower in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/`, so citations differ by a constant offset while the quoted text matches exactly; that offset is documented in §0 so the next reader doesn't discard a correct citation over it.

## Guards this file was checked against before committing

- `every_relative_markdown_link_resolves` — zero markdown links added, nothing to dangle.
- `no_document_transcribes_the_test_count` — no `<digits> tests` anywhere in it.
- `the_briefing_points_at_the_five_files_split_out_of_it` — untouched; `CLAUDE.md` is not modified.
- `.gitattributes` — LF endings, matching `docs/`.
- And it does not reproduce the table bug it reports: all 23 rows parse at 3 columns.

author: proggeramlug
body:
Adopts perex's one-shot search entry on Perry's two host search paths. Continues the per-call work on #10166.

## What it does

`find_near` and `find_near_lent` each built a `Search` and then advanced it. That is two view acquisitions per JS regex call, plus a `Search` moved between them — for a search whose first quantum decides it in nearly every case. `Search::run` acquires the views once and runs that quantum in the same borrow, so a decided search never builds a `Search` at all.

`Run::Paused` falls into the existing advance loop unchanged. A pause caused by a `Frames`/`Undo` shortage is carried in perex's `state.blocked` and re-raised by the next `advance`, so it lands in the existing scratch-growth branch exactly as before — both paths behave as `Search::new` followed by `advance` did.

## Measurement

Instructions per call, control subtracted (an identical binary building the same 1M-string array and running the same loop with a trivial predicate in place of the regex), so these are the regex call alone. **One Perry commit and one perex commit, differing only by this patch** — the figures isolate `Search::run` and contain nothing else from the 0.1.9 release. Release build, min of 5 interleaved rounds, 16-core Linux host.

| probe | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.test()` anchored, 50% hit | 4,382.2 | 4,063.7 | **−7.3%** |
| `.test()` inline literal | 5,698.2 | 5,379.7 | −5.6% |
| `exec`, two capture groups | 7,566.9 | 7,237.9 | −4.3% |
| `.test()` unanchored miss | 2,438.7 | 2,133.7 | **−12.5%** |
| `.test()` unanchored hit | 5,813.1 | 5,481.1 | −5.7% |
| 200,000-character subject | 1,439,713 | 1,439,003 | −0.0% |

305 to 332 instructions whatever the pattern — the fixed cost of the call. The last row is the control on the claim: a fixed per-call saving correctly disappears against a subject long enough for matching to dominate.

All six probes return identical answers on both arms and on Node 26.5.1.

**Wall-clock figures are deliberately omitted.** The measuring host carried other sessions' builds throughout; round-to-round spread reached 68–244% against effects of 0.5–25%, enough to invert the sign of a result the instruction counts show clearly. Quoting a minimum from that would have been misleading, so only instruction counts appear here.

## Dependency

`perex = "0.1.7"` → `"0.1.9"`, for `Search::run` and `Run`. 0.1.9's `src/` is byte-identical to the commit the figures were measured against, and re-measuring against the released crate reproduced every row to 0.1 instructions per call.

Resolving 0.1.9 needed `CARGO_RESOLVER_INCOMPATIBLE_PUBLISH_AGE=allow` once, because `.cargo/config.toml` soaks releases for 7 days and 0.1.9 was hours old — authorised by Ralph for this version. **The lock entry is committed, so no override is needed to build this branch**: `validate-017.sh`'s first gate, the `--locked` build *without* the override, passes.

## Validation (local; runners are unreliable)

- `perry-runtime` lib suite: **3984 passed, 0 failed**, 4 ignored
- `--locked` build without the override: OK
- `cargo fmt --check`: OK · regex-off `-D warnings`: OK · product `-D warnings`: OK

## Considered and not done

- **`Search::run_without_captures` for `.test()`.** perex measured the capture round a boolean search skips at 88 instructions per call — a 2.2% ceiling against a 4,064-instruction call — while Perry's `find_near` builds its match span from `capture(0)` in both capture modes, so serving it means either a separate boolean host entry or making `Match.full` optional across ~12 readers. Priced and rejected; Perry's per-call cost is host-boundary bound, not engine bound.
- **`QUANTUM = usize::MAX`**, which would let perex choose its pause-check-free trial compilation. Worth a further −1.2% to −2.0% on short calls and −5.5% on a 200k-character subject, but it removes every pause point inside a single search, so it is a Perry policy change rather than an adoption. Measured, not proposed here.

The one part of this with any subtlety is the interaction with the lent path's scratch-growth branch. I verified it by reading perex's `advance` (`state.blocked` re-raises before anything else) and the 200k-character probe drives the paused path thousands of times per run with correct results — but the session that wrote `find_near_lent` has ended, so that review has no obvious owner. Worth a second pair of eyes there specifically.

author: m0rtal
body:
## What
Three timeouts that were too loose or missing, causing chain to deadlock for hours when the network blipped:

1. **`_get_meta_moex` requests.get timeout**: was a single int (10s connect-only). A slow MOEX ISS read kept the thread hanging. Split into `(5, 30)` connect/read.

2. **`_prefetch_meta` had no timeout**: 3804 to_thread calls with no upper bound. One slow MOEX ISS response stalls the entire prefetch. Now wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for(timeout=30)`; on TimeoutError the cache is left empty and `_process_one` falls back to Tinkoff for that figi.

3. **`_figi_timeout_s` was 90s**: on Tinkoff fallback. 90s × 5 concurrent slots means one figi can hog its slot for 90s even after bail-out. Dropped to 45s so a single hung ticker doesn't tie up a Tinkoff slot too long.

## Restart resilience
Already in place via `delta_only=True`: chain reads `MIN(ts)` per figi and skips ones already complete. Survives process kill (supervisor restart loop) and process restart (chain resumes from `MIN(ts) - 30 days`). `INSERT OR IGNORE` makes repeated runs idempotent.

## Live verification (will apply immediately on supervisor restart)
- After supervisor picks up the new code: prefetch can't deadlock on a single bad ticker (30s cap each).
- Tinkoff fallback figis clear in ≤45s instead of ≤90s, so throughput on rate-limited path roughly doubles.
- After process kill, the chain resumes from last completed figi via `MIN(ts)` check.

Refs: PR #74 (timeout), PR #80 (bail-out), PR #84 (semaphore split).

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
## What this closes

Competitor map row:

> **humaniq/agenda-rostering-and-resource-booking** - glpi, otobo, kanboard, znuny, forgejo, gitea. A room, a car or a piece of equipment is booked for a period from inside the case system.

Five objects already said where a person is on a date, and nothing read them together. Nothing said what a person is qualified to do, and nothing could be booked.

## What is built

**Competence on the roster.** `Shift.requiredCompetences` is a set of codes and `EmployeeCompetence` records who holds one, with a `validUntil`. A qualification stops counting on its own date, without anybody editing the record, because that is the day the roster has to refuse the shift. `RosterCheckService` gains the cross-check beside the three Arbeidstijdenwet rules, in the same act, so `occ humaniq:roster:check` and `POST /api/roster/check` still answer the whole question in one call. Findings carry a `kind`, so a working-time violation and a competence violation can be acted on separately.

**The agenda**, composed on read from six sources and stored nowhere. An entry from a sick-leave case says absent and nothing else; busy time from a subscribed calendar carries no title. Both boundaries are kept by never reading those fields, not by stripping them afterwards, so there is no later step where somebody can forget.

**Availability**, the query a consuming app actually calls: free hours per employee over a window, optionally narrowed to an org unit and to competences held on every day of it. Hours rather than a yes or a no, so a caller can tell a free afternoon from a free week. Contracted hours come from `working-hours-per-person`, never from the instance default.

**Forward capacity**, planned against that same denominator. A person with no working pattern is reported as having no contracted hours and gets no percentage, rather than being measured against a full-time week nobody recorded for them.

**Resources and bookings.** A resource carries a `quantity`, and `ResourceBookingOverlapListener` refuses a booking past it over an overlapping period in the write path, naming the booking that blocks it. One room is one room; two geluidsmeters take two overlapping bookings and refuse the third. A resource out of service refuses a booking.

**External calendars**, read only. A per employee iCalendar subscription, a poll job every fifteen minutes, and a parser that reads `DTSTART`, `DTEND`, `DURATION`, `STATUS` and `TRANSP` and nothing else. A failed poll records the degradation and leaves the previous cache, because an emptied cache makes somebody look free all week the moment their calendar server hiccups.

**The `humaniq-agenda` leaf**, both halves under one id, shipped in the `humaniq-leaves` bundle so it is not dark on a consuming page, and registered inside the same `class_exists` guard as the hours leaf so a host without humaniq renders no agenda panel at all.

Known limit, stated rather than approximated: the iCalendar parser does not expand `RRULE`, so a recurring series counts as its first occurrence. A half-expanded series would under-report busy time invisibly, so it is left to a follow-up with its own tests.

## Verified

- `php -l` on every changed PHP file, `npx webpack` builds both bundles and `humaniq-agenda` is in each.
- `phpunit --filter AgendaAndAvailabilityTest|CalendarSubscriptionPollerTest|RegisterAgendaLeafListenerTest|RosterCheck|WorkingHoursServiceTest|LeaveTypeAndScheduleTest`: 73 tests, 181 assertions, green.
- Mutation check: dropping `busy` from the committed-hours kinds in `AvailabilityService` reddened `testExternalBusyTimeIsDeductedFromFreeHours` on its own assertion (8.0 against 5.0), not on a setup line. Restored and green.
- `openspec validate agenda-rostering-and-resource-booking --strict`.
- `eslint` on every changed JS, Vue and spec file, `stylelint` on the widget.
- `npm run check:manifest` (128 pages), `verify-manifest-parity`, `check:widget-keys`, `validate-seed-refs`, `check:l10n`, `check:schema-l10n` all pass, with the manifest baseline regenerated in the same commit.

The e2e spec is written and tagged, not run: it belongs to the nightly. Every fixture it creates is its own employee, resources and bookings, all deleted in the teardown, so nothing lands on a real person's record or takes a real room away from anybody.

Deferred to the quality sweep, per the build-first phase: phpmd, psalm, phpstan, the whole-tree gates, `check:strict` and the e2e run.

author: husainbw786
body:
## The problem

The frontend creates an organisation by posting straight to MSG91:

```
POST https://routes.msg91.com/api/c/createCompany
```

The org exists the moment that returns, but its Lago customer, subscription and **wallet** do not. Those wait on the MSG91 signup webhook, and when that does not fire the org runs with no wallet at all. Every debit it produces is dropped as `billingDebitMalformedEvent` and nothing is billed. Existing orgs are fine only because they were provisioned earlier.

## The endpoint

`POST /api/organization` does both, in one request, so the wallet is in place before the org can make its first call.

```
POST /api/organization
Authorization: <jwt>            # or the proxy token; middleware takes either
proxy_auth_token: <caller's>    # required — forwarded to MSG91
{ "company": { "name": "...", "meta": { ... }, "timezone": "+05:30" } }
```

The body is the same `company` object MSG91 takes and is **passed through untouched**, since that shape belongs to MSG91. The caller's own `proxy_auth_token` is forwarded rather than an admin key, because the org belongs to them.

Response is `201` with the org, its id, and a `billing` block.

## Failure handling splits on what exists by then

| what failed | response |
|---|---|
| MSG91 | request fails — nothing was created. 401/403 passed through, anything else 502 |
| Lago, after MSG91 succeeded | **201** with `billing.provisioned: false` and the reason |

Telling the user they have no org when they do would be worse than reporting the billing gap. That case alerts as `orgProvisioningFailed` and is replayed with `POST /api/lago/provision/admin`.

`createCompany` is not called anywhere else in this codebase and MSG91 wraps payloads differently per endpoint (`data[0]` in getDetails, `data.data[0]` in getCompanies, plain `data` elsewhere). So the org id is looked for in each known shape, and a payload carrying none is a loud 502 with the response logged — never a guess at which org to provision.

The signup webhook is unchanged and stays as the safety net for orgs created outside the app. Both paths end in `ensureOrgSubscribed`, which is read-before-write on customer, subscription and wallet, so either can run twice, or both can run, with no duplicate and no second signup grant.

## Verified

- 12 checks on the id extractor across every MSG91 response shape, including "no id anywhere" and an id of `0`.
- Route guards on a running server: unauthenticated `401`, missing `proxy_auth_token` `400`, missing `company` or `company.name` `400`, and the real MSG91 payload from the frontend passing validation untouched.

**Not verified:** the MSG91 call itself. Exercising it would create a real organisation in production. The first run on dev will confirm the response shape, and if it is one the extractor does not know, it fails loudly with the payload logged rather than provisioning the wrong org.

body:
## Summary

Model-scoped weekly caps (the 50%-of-weekly Fable budget on Max plans) are reported by the OAuth usage endpoint only in the `limits[]` array. The top-level `seven_day_opus` / `seven_day_sonnet` keys are present but `null` on current accounts, so the open window set from cf49f26 never actually saw a model window.

This turns each `weekly_scoped` entry with a model scope into a `seven_day_<display_name>` window (`seven_day_fable` beside `seven_day`), so `cux usage show`, seat ranking (`modelCapped`) and the model switch all see it. The on-disk cache format is unchanged — the new key is just another flat window.

## What the endpoint returns today (live Max account, trimmed)

```json
"seven_day_opus": null,
"seven_day_sonnet": null,
"limits": [
  {"kind": "session",       "percent": 0,  "resets_at": null, "scope": null},
  {"kind": "weekly",        "percent": 54, "resets_at": "2026-09-19T02:59:59Z", "scope": null},
  {"kind": "weekly_scoped", "percent": 42, "resets_at": "2026-09-19T03:00:00Z",
   "scope": {"model": {"display_name": "Fable"}}}
]
```

`cux usage show` after this change:

```json
"seven_day":       {"utilization": 54, "resets_at": "2026-09-19T02:59:59Z"},
"seven_day_fable": {"utilization": 42, "resets_at": "2026-09-19T03:00:00Z"}
```

## Also

Top-level windows at 0% with no `resets_at` are now dropped. That is how the endpoint reports program windows that don't apply to the seat (e.g. `nimbus_quill`, 0%/null on every account); they were surfacing as noise in the cache and in `usage show`. A window with any utilization or a reset is still kept whatever its name, so the set stays open.

## Tests

One test covering both: a `limits[]` entry becomes `seven_day_fable`, `limits` itself is not stored as a window, an empty top-level window is dropped, `seven_day` is untouched. `go test ./...` green.

body:
This repo did not have a deploy path for publishing the frontend to GitHub Pages. This change adds a Pages workflow for `artifacts/x247-rewards` and ensures client-side routing works after direct deep-link loads.

- **Deployment automation**
  - Added `.github/workflows/deploy-github-pages.yml` to build and deploy on `main` pushes and manual dispatch.
  - Uses official Pages actions (`configure-pages`, `upload-pages-artifact`, `deploy-pages`) with required permissions and concurrency control.

- **Base path correctness**
  - Workflow computes `BASE_PATH` from repository naming:
    - `/<repo>/` for project pages
    - `/` for `<owner>.github.io` repos
  - Build step injects this value so Vite emits correct asset/route URLs for Pages hosting.

- **SPA route fallback**
  - Adds a Pages-compatible fallback by copying `index.html` to `404.html` in the build output, so refresh/direct access on nested routes resolves to the app shell.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated `README.md` with the expected GitHub Pages URL patterns for project and user/org pages.

```yaml
- name: Resolve BASE_PATH
  run: |
    owner="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER}"
    repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}"
    if [ "$repo" = "$owner.github.io" ]; then
      echo "value=/" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    else
      echo "value=/$repo/" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    fi

- name: Add SPA fallback
  run: cp artifacts/x247-rewards/dist/public/index.html artifacts/x247-rewards/dist/public/404.html
```
