## Summary

A substantial v2 overhaul of the personal operations workspace, focused on correctness, security, usability, and explicit operational limits.

- Replace operational BigQuery/mock-JSON CRUD with owner-scoped SQLAlchemy storage: SQLite locally, PostgreSQL in production, UUID identities, optimistic versions, atomic transactions, and Alembic migrations. Retain BigQuery as an optional aggregate-only analytics export.
- Introduce Argon2id passwords, revocable HttpOnly cookie sessions, CSRF/origin protections, private demo accounts, profile/password management, bounded data export, and account deletion.
- Persist validated assistant proposals for explicit review/confirm/discard. Apply batches transactionally and idempotently; bound model calls, concurrency, input/output, and timeouts. Clearly distinguish demo, Vertex, and disabled modes without silent fallback.
- Complete task/note/event/reminder CRUD, search/filtering/pagination, calendar date handling, and session-aware cache/error recovery.
- Rebuild the responsive light/dark interface with keyboard navigation, focus-managed dialogs, accessible contrast, self-hosted fonts, and optional browser dictation.
- Add regression/browser/accessibility tests, CI, dependency-update configuration, non-root container scaffolding, safer local/deployment scripts, maintenance/import tooling, and comprehensive documentation.
- Remove obsolete adapters/state wrappers, logs, unsafe reset tooling, and credential-bearing runtime backups from the current tree.

## Breaking changes and migration

- API routes now use `/api/v1`; opaque cookie sessions + CSRF replace the old bearer-token/localStorage contract.
- The operational database schema and resource IDs/contracts change. Production requires migrated PostgreSQL; there is no automatic compatibility with the old BigQuery tables or mock database.
- Use the dry-run-first offline importer for legacy **workspace data**. Old password hashes/JWTs are not imported or accepted; use fresh credentials.
- Removing tracked credential-bearing files does **not** remove Git history or existing clones. Affected credential rotation and owner-coordinated history cleanup remain necessary.

See the [migration guide](https://github.com/KetanDutt/GoogleCloudGenAIHackathon2026/blob/5e5954ebef535064cc0ac6258427527894e5bb8c/docs/MIGRATION.md) before upgrading an existing installation.

## Verification completed locally

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Backend, SQLite | 94 tests passed; 90% statement coverage including operator scripts |
| Backend, PostgreSQL 18.4 | Same 94 tests passed |
| Alembic | Upgrade, drift check, downgrade, and re-upgrade passed on both databases |
| Frontend unit tests | 22 passed |
| Playwright | 20 desktop/mobile tests passed, including light/dark axe checks |
| Frontend production | Clean `npm ci`, optimized build, and standalone-server smoke passed |
| Production-config backend | Local PostgreSQL startup/migration-head, secure-session contract, CRUD/export/deletion smoke passed |
| Static checks | Ruff, formatting, ESLint, TypeScript, shell syntax, documentation links, and diff whitespace checks passed |
| Dependencies | `npm audit`: 0 vulnerabilities; runtime `pip-audit`: no known vulnerabilities; `pip check` passed |
| Preview | Desktop/mobile/dark inspection and cross-site iframe partitioned-cookie login smoke passed |

These are the recorded local verification results, **not a claim that GitHub CI has already passed**. See the PR checks for remote CI status and the [testing report](https://github.com/KetanDutt/GoogleCloudGenAIHackathon2026/blob/5e5954ebef535064cc0ac6258427527894e5bb8c/docs/TESTING.md) for environment details and scope.

## Remaining public-launch gates / limitations

This is a production-oriented foundation or controlled beta, not an unqualified public-production deployment.

- Real Vertex AI, live BigQuery jobs, Docker/Compose execution, Cloud Run deployment, production load/restore tests, Windows launchers, and real microphone behavior remain unverified. No paid model calls or cloud deployment were performed during implementation.
- Verified-email/password-recovery/MFA or managed identity, distributed/gateway abuse controls, and deployment-specific IAM, secrets, backups, monitoring, privacy, and security review remain launch requirements.
- Reminders are in-app only; calendar events do not sync to Google Calendar. Model requests are independent rather than multi-turn memory. Automated accessibility checks are not a full conformance audit.
- Original hackathon media and the existing restrictive project license are preserved.

## Reviewer guide

- [Updated README and screenshots](https://github.com/KetanDutt/GoogleCloudGenAIHackathon2026/blob/5e5954ebef535064cc0ac6258427527894e5bb8c/README.md)

author: benitbuhner
body:
Supersedes #116, which GitHub closed automatically when a rebase mishap briefly force-pushed this branch to the tip of `main` (the branch was restored within a minute; GitHub does not let a PR closed that way reopen). Same seven commits, rebased onto current `main` (#120, #117; one additive merge in `src/android/platform.ts`).

Parity rows ID-02, ID-03, ID-05, ID-25, ID-36, ID-37, MW-11, MW-12. Worker services-password-fill. Engine half; the UI half (prompts, pickers, Settings rows, managers) follows on `cursor/services-password-fill-ui-24d1` as a draft.

Built on the merged credential store (#40 / #92): `CredentialStore`, `PasswordService`, `PasswordsHost { keys, reauth }` are extended, not replaced. No new visual surface: prompts open as the host's confirm dialog until the chrome renders `UIState.autofill.prompts`; the picker sits in `UIState.autofill.picker` for the UI PR; existing Settings > Passwords rows keep working.

## What changes

**Forms in pages (`src/shared/forms.ts`, `formsScript.ts`, `passkeyObserver.ts`)**
- `formsScript.ts` is injected like the page script on both hosts (Electron: `src/preload/page.ts` in the isolated world; Android: `src/android/pageScript.ts` at document start). It classifies fields from `autocomplete` tokens first, then heuristics over type, name, id, placeholder, labels and `aria-label` (login, sign-up, one-time codes, addresses, cards; `MM / YY` in one field is the whole expiry; "security code" is a card's only next to a card number), groups a container's fields (`login` / `address` / `card`; a checkout form is both), reports `focus` (with the field's visual-viewport rect and the form's fields), `moved`, `blur`, `submit` (form submit, Enter, click on a submit button) and `settled` (a single-page app that emptied or removed the password field without navigating), and executes `fill` (value setters that frameworks see: native setter, `input` and `change` events, `<select>` by value then by label) and `config` commands. Events go up the existing page-message channel as `PageMessage { type: 'forms' }`; commands come down through `TabView.sendFormsCommand`.
- `passkeyObserver.ts` runs in the main world (Electron `executeJavaScript` on dom-ready, Android directly since the page script is already there) and reports `navigator.credentials.create` / `get` outcomes for the vault's passkey metadata, without touching the ceremony.

**Core (`src/core/autofill.ts`, `credentials/fill.ts`, `browser.ts`, `tabs.ts`, `window.ts`)**
- `AutofillService` at `browser.autofill`: on a credential field's focus it lists the site's logins by registrable domain (exact origin first, then siblings labelled with their host) in `UIState.autofill.picker`, anchored in chrome coordinates from the field rect, the view bounds (`ZenWindow.viewRect`) and the zoom (`anchorInChrome`); `autofill.pick` fills the form, the first password fill of a session behind the store's `ReauthHost` / passphrase gate with the grace period; auto sign-in (`passwords.autoSignIn`, off by default) fills the one match without a picker, once per page load. Submits become `LoginCandidate`s judged at the navigation or the `settled` event (`decideSave`: save / update / already saved / never for this site); prompts queue in `UIState.autofill.prompts` and are answered by `autofill.respond`. Addresses and cards get pickers on their fields and save prompts after a submit (a card fill re-authenticates every time; CVC is never stored).
- Android provider decision: when the host reports a system autofill service and `passwords.androidProvider` is `system` (default), the forms script is switched off in every page and the Autofill Framework owns saving and filling; `zenium` keeps the framework off the pages and uses Zenium's prompts. Status is re-probed when the app regains focus.
- `PasswordService.copySecret` marks every secret copy sensitive and the toast says when it clears; `shutdown` flushes a pending clear (the Android background flush no longer wipes the clipboard early).

**Store (`credentials/vault.ts`, `store.ts`, `address.ts`, `card.ts`, `data/addressMetadata.ts`, `clipboard.ts`)**
- The vault payload is a discriminated union: `login` | `address` | `card` | `passkey`, same envelope and encryption; the store keeps the four kinds apart (`listAddresses` / `addAddress` / `updateAddress` / `removeAddress`, the same for cards and passkeys, `passkeyUsed`). Older vaults decode unchanged.
- `address.ts` formats and validates by country from `data/addressMetadata.ts`, a bundled subset of Google's libaddressinput data (Apache 2.0, licence header in the file): field order and labels per country, required fields, postal-code patterns, region lists (states, provinces, prefectures), `formatAddress` for the preview, `addressFromForm` / `addressToForm` between the vault model and form field kinds.
- `card.ts`: Luhn, network detection (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, Diners, JCB, UnionPay), expiry parsing (`MM/YY`, `MM/YYYY`, `MMYY`), expired check, masked label.
- `SensitiveClipboard`: `sensitive` writes and a timed clear (`passwords.clipboardClearSeconds`, default 60, 0 off) that only clears while the clipboard still holds the secret.

**Shared model (`types.ts`, `defaults.ts`, `state.ts`)**
- `PasswordSettings` gains `autoSignIn`, `androidProvider`, `clipboardClearSeconds`; new `AutofillSettings { addresses, cards }` under `settings.autofill`; `AddressEntry`, `PaymentCard` / `PaymentCardSummary`, `PasskeyEntry`, the prompt and picker types, `UIState.autofill`. Sanitizers so older stores load.
- Commands: `autofill.respond`, `autofill.pick`, `autofill.listAddresses` / `addAddress` / `updateAddress` / `removeAddress` / `addressFormat` / `countries`, `autofill.listCards` / `addCard` / `updateCard` / `removeCard` / `revealCard` / `copyCardNumber`, `autofill.listPasskeys` / `removePasskey`; `clipboard.writeText` takes `sensitive?: boolean`.

**Platform (`src/core/platform.ts`)**
- `PageMessage { type: 'forms' }`, `TabView.sendFormsCommand?`, `ClipboardHost.writeText(text, sensitive?)` and `clearText(expected)`, `AutofillHost { systemStatus, setProvider, onSystemStatusChanged? }` on `Platform.autofill?` (Android only).

**Electron host (`src/main/platform/webauthn.ts`, `index.ts`, `views.ts`, `preload/page.ts`, `build/after-pack.mjs`, `electron.vite.config.ts`)**
- Passkeys: Chromium serves Windows Hello and roaming security keys as is; macOS Touch ID goes through `app.configureWebAuthn` with the keychain access group `<TEAM_ID>.io.github.benitbuhner.zenium.webauthn`, the team id baked in from `APPLE_TEAM_ID` at build time and the `keychain-access-groups` entitlement added by `after-pack.mjs` only for a real signing identity (unsigned builds keep Chromium's defaults). `select-webauthn-account` (several discoverable passkeys) is answered through `browser.autofill.selectPasskeyAccount`, one prompt, one callback.
- `zen:forms` IPC carries commands into the isolated world; `ClipboardHost.clearText` compares before clearing.

**Android host (`src/android/*.ts`, Kotlin)**
- `Host.kt`: `view.forms`, `clipboard.writeText` (`SecretClipboard`: `ClipDescription.EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE` on API 33+, so the clipboard preview hides the value), `clipboard.clearText`, `autofill.status` (`AutofillManager.isEnabled`, the service component on API 28+), `autofill.setProvider`. `TabWebView.kt`: `WebSettingsCompat.setWebAuthenticationSupport(WEB_AUTHENTICATION_SUPPORT_FOR_APP)` where the feature exists, `importantForAutofill` from the provider (`NO_EXCLUDE_DESCENDANTS` under Zenium, `AUTO` under the system), `sendForms`, the forms configuration repeated to every new document with the flags. `TabHost.kt` re-applies the provider to adopted views. `previewSpec` / `preview.ts` stand-ins.
- MW-12 honesty: `WEB_AUTHENTICATION_SUPPORT_FOR_APP` serves passkeys for origins the app can prove through Digital Asset Links (Zenium's own); browser-wide passkeys for arbitrary origins (`FOR_BROWSER`) need Google's privileged-browser al

author: monjar
body:
Two commits. The first fixes four things found by riding the TestFlight build; the second builds the next four steps of the plan. They share a branch because #6 was still open when the second was ready — merge as one, or cherry-pick `a84685b` alone if you want the fixes first.

---

# Commit 1 — four things the app got wrong on the road (`a84685b`)

## 1. Rides can be deleted
The server had `DELETE /rides/{id}` and the app had `deleteRide(id:)`; nothing in the UI called it. Long-press an adventure in the Journal, or the bin on its page. Both confirm. The ride is discarded, so it leaves the journal *and* the stats — which is how the 76 km/h below can be removed from an existing account. XP stays.

## 2. The same quest dealt twice, a street apart
`generate_quests` excluded open templates but fell back to generating *without* exclusions once all were excluded ("rather than returning nothing"). And the class-balance pass judged the batch, not the board, inventing a repeat. Now: a template open is never dealt again; balance is judged against everything open; `ensure_available` retires existing duplicates on the next board load (nearer copy stays).

## 3. Max speed of 76.6 km/h
The fastest single GPS segment. A 20 m twitch in one second reads as 72 km/h, under the 90 km/h cap. Server and phone now take **straight-line distance made good over ≥5 s**. Path length inside the window wasn't enough (39.8 km/h in the test); displacement is.

## 4. "The Ley Line" wasn't a line
Three points at random bearings, a 51.6 km triangle, distance rolled independently. `regionLayout: "line"`: one bearing, nearest first, distance follows the geometry.

---

# Commit 2 — the next four (`431633e`)

## 1. Field tests — `docs/FIELD_TESTS.md`
Every bug above was in code the suite marked green. Eight protocols, one ride per question: a plain ride, a quest to completion, off route on purpose, the app killed mid-ride, the Watch alone, battery in three modes, a typed request on the road it planned, somewhere new. What to record; how to hand it over (the GPX, not a number). README status table rewritten to match reality.

## 2. The reading eval — `request-reading` workflow
`tests/test_request_reading.py` asks the real model whether it reads sentences the way the planner expects. It had never been run. Now a workflow: `workflow_dispatch` + weekly, fails fast naming the missing secret. **Needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as a repository secret.**

## 3. The Strava loop, closed
The server could upload; the app had a Never/Ask/Auto setting; nothing joined them.
- **Auto**: `process_ride_job` calls `upload_after_processing` after the ride commits — sent with nothing tapped. Never a reason for processing to fail.
- **Ask**: asked once on the ride summary, when connected.
- **Where it got to** is on the ride: `stravaUploadStatus` (QUEUED/UPLOADED/FAILED), `stravaActivityId`, `stravaError` (Strava's own message). The adventure page shows *Open in Strava*, *Sending…*, or *failed: <reason>* with **Retry**.
- Strava takes the file at once and makes the activity seconds later; the upload is polled (6 × 2 s) until it has an activity id. The old code stored the *upload* id as the activity id.
- Migration `0007` adds the two columns.

**Needs `STRAVA_CLIENT_ID` / `STRAVA_CLIENT_SECRET` as Fly secrets and `strava` in `FEATURE_FLAGS`** — the backend gates on both. Not set by this PR.

## 4. People
- `GET /users/search?q=` — by name, never oneself, never across a block. The Friends screen searches as you type; each result shows Add / Sent / Accept / Friends by standing.
- `PartyDetailView`: members with state, the quest, and only the actions the server will accept from this rider in this state (join / ready / start / leave-or-cancel). Parties and invitations open it; invitations sit at the top of Friends.
- `party_quests` enabled in `fly.toml`.

## Testing
Backend: 161 passed, 49 skipped; ruff clean. New: `test_strava_loop.py` (sent with activity id; failed with reason and retryable; auto only when asked and never twice; by hand when connected), `test_social_people.py`. Swift compiles in CI on Xcode 16.4 — the party page and the Strava rows are unverified on a device.

Two test-harness facts worth knowing: `client` and `explorer_client` are the same object (a second user needs its own `AsyncClient`), and an endpoint that enqueues a job must `commit()` first or SQLite locks when the inline job writes.

author: hugoleborso
body:
Emma reached `/catalog` and got a black screen that survived every reload. Three defects only bite together: the prod deploy pruned old bundles, no object carried a `Cache-Control`, and the worker cached the fallback HTML under the `.js` URL.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  browser[Stale index.html] --> bundle[GET /assets/index-OLD.js]
  bundle --> pruned{Still in S3?}
  pruned -->|deploy pruned it| fallback[404 to /index.html, status 200]
  fallback --> mime[Module script arrives as text/html]
  mime --> blank[React never mounts, #root empty]
  blank --> poison[cacheFirst stores HTML under the js URL]
  poison --> forever[Every later reload serves it from cache]
```

## Decisions

| Decision | Alternative | Why | Consequences | ADR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prod stops pruning | Keep pruning, fix caching only | A browser holding an older page must still load its own bundle | The bucket keeps every past deploy's assets | |
| Two deployments | One, with one header set | Hashed assets and entry points want opposite lifetimes | Two custom resources, ordered | |
| Bump the cache version | Only guard the write | Nothing else deletes a cache already poisoned | Everyone refetches the shell once | |
| Guard on content type | Trust the status alone | The fallback answers 200, so ok is not enough | Cache-first refuses an HTML asset | |
| Add an error boundary | Leave a crash unhandled | A blank page names nothing a reader can act on | One class component, the only one | |
| Lint `sw.js` | Leave `public/` ignored | It is the one source no gate read | A `.js` under `public/` is linted now | |

## Before merge

### Nothing the operator does first

No migration, no parameter, no dispatch: the `borso-shared` snapshot is unchanged. A stuck phone unblocks itself on its next visit, because a browser revalidates `sw.js` even while the page is blank. Worst case is its 24 hour cap on that check.

## Validation

### Measured on prod

`GET /assets/index-OLDHASH.js` answers `200` with `content-type: text/html`, and no object carries a `Cache-Control`.

### Reproduced in a browser

Served the prod build under those same semantics, pruned the bundle, and read `#root` empty on a dark background.

### The failure was proven permanent

After restoring the bundle at the origin, the client still rendered nothing, and `pragma-v3-shell` held `<!doctype html>` under the js URL.

### The fix was proven to recover it

That same client came back on the next visit, with only `pragma-v4-shell` left and the app rendering.

### The guard was proven to hold

A `/assets/` URL the origin answers with HTML is now served through and never written to the cache.

### Gates

Eslint, typecheck, prettier, knip, 340 infra tests, 1763 pragma tests at 100%, mutation 100% on both changed gated files.

## Notable

- The redirect to `/catalog` happens before the crash, which is why the report named that address.
- Under a dark appearance the empty body reads as black, which is the reported symptom.
- The error boundary cannot catch a bundle that never ran; the other two changes are what fix this.
- `apps/*/site/public/**` was ignored wholesale and `sw.js` was the only lintable file under it.
- `sw.js` and `sw-cache.utils.ts` still hand-copy the same predicates, with nothing making them agree.
- PR #107 touches neither the worker nor the deploy; it overlaps only elsewhere in the same two translation files.

author: verigence-admin
body:
## Summary
- The **Publish Verigence Android App** workflow's post-sign branding check failed on every real run with \`caution: filename not matched: res/drawable-v24/ic_launcher_foreground.xml\` (unzip exit code 11) -- confirmed live by actually running the workflow.
- Root cause: AGP's release packaging renames \`res/\` entries in the built APK (e.g. \`.../ic_launcher_foreground.xml\` -> \`res/zR.xml\`). The earlier "Generate Android project and approved branding" step still passes because it checks the un-renamed source-tree file; only the *post-build, packaged-APK* check assumed the same path survives, and it doesn't.
- This blocked every attempt to publish a new APK to R2 -- metadata creation, R2 upload, and evidence upload all got skipped as a result.
- Fix: locate the same resource by its own unique path-data content (\`M64,136\`) across all \`res/*.xml\` entries instead of a fixed path. Still fails loudly (and for the right reason) if no entry matches, so a genuine branding regression is still caught.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced the exact live failure via a real workflow_dispatch run
- [ ] Manual: re-run **Publish Verigence Android App** after merge and confirm it reaches R2

author: dpidiaz
body:
Implementa MLS GitHub Staging v1 como flujo adicional al editorial normal, sin reemplazar D1 ni cambiar los comandos existentes.

### Estado verificado
- HEAD actual: `d16bdde8950c`.
- CI más reciente del HEAD: **success** (run #133).
- Suite completa + pruebas funcionales staging: **success**.
- `predeploy`: **success**.
- Catálogo real generado: **10,133 targets**, dividido en shards seguros para GitHub Contents.
- Contrato de deploy: **success**.
- `wrangler deploy --dry-run`: **success**.
- Sin valores secretos en el diff.
- Workflow de producción protegido para ejecutar deploy/snapshot/post-check solo desde `main`.
- Cloudflare Free protegido con presupuesto previo de subrequests externos antes de tocar D1.
- GitHub App acepta claves PEM RSA PKCS1 y PKCS8.

### Garantías implementadas
- `start/next/status/validate/stage/cancel` reciben un entorno runtime que bloquea cualquier acceso a `WIKI_DB`.
- Snapshots versionados y runs fijados a snapshot/commit inmutable.
- Reservas persistentes en GitHub con updates fast-forward y `force:false`.
- Estado `validated` persistido.
- `drafting`, `deferred`, `needs_review`, `staged`, `integrated`, `preservedExisting` persistidos y protegidos de reselección.
- AUTOOPT staging en GitHub, no D1.
- Protección Gemma para reserved/validated/staged con verificación fuerte antes de persistencia.
- Reconciliación D1 idempotente, hasta 400 por pasada, `ON CONFLICT(code) DO NOTHING`, preservando existentes y reportando `rows_read/rows_written` reales.
- Tests funcionales en memoria cubren concurrencia, requestId idempotente, fallo/corrección, deferred, needs_review, stage, integración, preservedExisting y reintegración idempotente.
- Snapshot rechaza por adelantado un presupuesto de GitHub que exceda el límite seguro del Worker Free.

### Bootstrap preparado
Se añadió `.github/workflows/bootstrap staging.yml`.

Modo preferido:
- GitHub App instalada solo en `dpidiaz/llmchatmls`.
- Repository permission: **Contents: Read and write**.

Secrets esperados:
- `MLS_STAGING_GITHUB_APP_ID`
- `MLS_STAGING_GITHUB_INSTALLATION_ID`
- `MLS_STAGING_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`

Fallback:
- `MLS_STAGING_GITHUB_TOKEN` fine-grained, limitado al repositorio y a Contents: Read and write.

El workflow instala la credencial en Cloudflare mediante una sola operación `wrangler secret bulk`, limpia de forma atómica las credenciales del modo alternativo, crea el snapshot inicial y verifica el endpoint editorial.

No se deben pegar secretos en ChatGPT ni almacenarlos en el repositorio.

### Siguiente fase después del merge
Una vez que este PR se fusione en `main`:
1. configurar los secrets GitHub Staging en GitHub Actions;
2. ejecutar `Bootstrap MLS Staging`;
3. confirmar snapshot;
4. ejecutar `MLS staging siguientes 2`;
5. demostrar `d1RowsRead=0` y `d1RowsWritten=0`;
6. reconciliar esas 2 entradas y medir D1 real.

El PR se mantiene en borrador hasta autorizar el merge a producción.

author: yoyodine-industries
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lands the Bot Chat owner-mailbox delivery store, and closes three ways that store could strand mail or wedge its own lane: liveness that only meant "the process exists", a single unreadable record that killed every later sweep of the spool, and a queued record whose pinned owner was gone sitting silent forever.

### Stack (land in order — each PR is based on the previous one)

1. **this PR** — `feat/bot-live-delivery-store`: the owner-mailbox delivery store itself — strict liveness (a destination must prove it is live), quarantine of a dead ticket instead of wedging the spool, reclaim/expiry of a record whose owner is gone, atomic writes.
2. `feat/session-turn-lease-queue` — PR #115009 (layer 2/4): queue an inbound delivery that loses the turn-lease wait; `status=queued` on the admission receipt; FIFO waiter fairness for the lease.
3. `feat/bot-peer-receipts-durable-queue` — PR #115010 (layer 3/4): a receipt for peer sends, a durable delivery queue with content-keyed dedup, and truthfulness fixes for the hold/held-slot states.
4. `feat/gateway-bot-delivery-drain` — PR #115013 (layer 4/4): drain bot deliveries across every profile home, and never expire a record that was never offered to a turn.

Layer 1 stands alone (nothing depends on it); layers 2–4 each build on the one above, so review and merge in the order listed.

### Symptom

- A Bot Chat lease whose poll loop had stopped renewing stayed a delivery destination for as long as its process lived. A leaked lease roughly 20h old was still holding 68 queued peer messages addressed to that bot.
- One unreadable `*.json` ticket raised out of every later sweep, so the lane could neither make progress nor say why: the whole mailbox was wedged behind a single dead file.
- A queued record whose pinned owner was gone (compressed/forked session, dead lease) stayed in the queue forever and never produced a receipt.

### Bug cause

Owner resolution keyed liveness off the process only: a registry entry was a destination while its PID was alive, regardless of whether the lease still advertised the consumer capability or whether its registry stamp had been renewed recently. The spool scan treated every `*.json` as a delivery record and propagated read errors instead of isolating them. Nothing reclaimed a record whose owner no longer existed, and nothing distinguished "still waiting" from "this chat can never reach it".

## Related Issue

No tracking issue; this is the store as the production deployment needs it, distilled to the parts that are generally correct.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tools/bot_live_delivery.py` — a lease is a delivery destination only while it advertises the consumer capability **and** its registry stamp was renewed within `LIVE_CONSUMER_TTL_SECONDS`; the registry must *prove* the entry (strict liveness) and an unprovable registry yields no owner, so the caller falls back to the plain transport path instead of stranding mail.
- `tools/bot_live_delivery.py` — a bulk scan quarantines a ticket whose content is dead on disk (corrupt JSON, invalid UTF-8, not an object) to `<spool>/quarantine/`, preserved byte-for-byte, and carries on. Transient read errors stay in place with the existing warn-once behaviour, and exact-id reads still fail closed so a receipt can never be overwritten.
- `tools/bot_live_delivery.py` — a claim pass reclaims a record whose owner is gone along the compression lineage, but only after the session store proves the body is already there (sha256, then a substring fallback for locally-recovered rows), and reports what this chat can never reach as `failed`/`no_live_consumer` once it is older than `UNREACHABLE_AFTER_SECONDS`.
- `tools/bot_live_delivery.py` — records are written through the shared atomic JSON write (tempfile + fsync + replace, spool dir fsynced), the sequence counter is the high-water mark, and a foreign `*.json` is never taken for a delivery record.
- `tests/tools/test_bot_live_owner_delivery.py` — coverage for the TTL, the unprovable registry, quarantine isolation, claim-box reclaim, expiry, and the fail-closed receipt path.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/tools/test_bot_live_owner_delivery.py -q` — the file's cases cover strict liveness (a live PID with an unrenewed stamp is not an owner), quarantine of one dead ticket while the rest of the spool still drains, reclaim of a record whose body the session store already has, and `failed`/`no_live_consumer` for a record past its reachability window.
2. The 10 modules that import this store, against pristine `upstream/main` (see the checklist above): same passes plus the 11 new cases, no lost passes.
3. Drop a corrupt `*.json` into a live spool dir and run a sweep: the file moves to `quarantine/` unchanged and the sweep still delivers the other records.

author: ra100
body:
Closes #36

## Root cause
The MCP `update_knobs` tool advertised `propagationDepth` as an unbounded number in both SQLite and Postgres server registrations, while the REST API requires an integer from 1 through 5. MCP clients could set zero, negative, fractional, or excessive values and trigger invalid propagation behavior.

## Fix
- Bound the MCP `propagationDepth` input schema to `int().min(1).max(5)` in both `src/mcp/server.ts` and `src/mcp/server-pg.ts`.
- Revalidate MCP `update_knobs` tool arguments with the shared REST `knobsBodySchema` in both SQLite and Postgres tool implementations, so runtime calls are rejected even if a client ignores the advertised schema.

## Testing
- Added SQLite MCP e2e coverage that verifies the advertised schema and rejects `0`, `6`, and `1.5` at runtime.
- Added equivalent Postgres MCP e2e coverage.
- Full SQLite suite: 1356 tests, 1145 passed, 0 failed, 211 skipped.
- Full suite with isolated Postgres 16: 1357 tests, 1355 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.
- Typecheck passed.
- Lint completed with 27 pre-existing warnings; no errors.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Read-only code review found no actionable findings after fixing the test typing issue.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation
No additional operational monitoring required. Expected behavior is deterministic: invalid MCP `propagationDepth` updates now return tool errors instead of mutating session knobs. Existing MCP diagnostics and update_knobs error counts are sufficient regression indicators.

body:
## What

The generated Open Graph card at `/api/og/{path}.png` now draws everything the node can say about itself, and every page has one.

- **The node's own mark**, drawn large on the right — the same backplated `<svg>` the favicon route rasterizes (`IconRasterizer.RenderImage` is now shared, including its "parses but paints nothing" refusal).
- **Description** with the catalog-copy fallbacks `tagline` → `summary` → `headline` — the Store root has a headline and a tagline and no description, so its card and its `og:description` were empty.
- **Category** as the eyebrow (else the type's leaf: "Plugin", not "Store/Plugin"), a **price chip** when `price > 0`, and the **instance name + path** in the footer.

2026-09-18: the Store shared into iMessage as the word "Store" beside the 16-px site favicon. The card that existed was title-only, the head declared no image size, and the description was blank.

author: ashimov
body:
## Change summary

`keep-alive interval 0` is how the CLI turns keepalive off, and it rendered
`keepalive 0 0`. OpenVPN 2.7 parses both parameters with
`atoi_constrained(..., 1, PING_TIMEOUT_MAX, msglevel)`, so the daemon now
refuses to start on it:

```
Options error: keepalive ping: Must be an integer between 1 and 86400, not 0
```

This hits a new configuration and, on upgrade, every saved one that already
carries `interval 0`. The combination was deliberately left alone in
2985a69d0 (T8264), where OpenVPN still skipped its own checks on `0 0`.

Leave the directive out of the generated file instead of rejecting the value
in `verify()`. `keepalive` is only a helper that sets `ping` and
`ping-restart`, and the server branch of the template sets neither on its own,
so an absent directive is exactly the keepalive-off the interval asked for.
Nothing needs a migration and a saved configuration still commits.

author: nilsb
body:
Four commits that were written after PR #84 had already been merged, and pushed to
its branch, where nothing carried them to `main`.

PR #84 merged at `c5d6f33` on 2026-09-17 12:59 UTC. `acb1951` was committed at
13:24 UTC — 25 minutes later — onto the same, now-closed branch, followed by three
more. None of the four is an ancestor of `main`, so no shipped image has ever
contained them.

The one that matters is the first. **Logging in to the mail server is still
broken on `main`**, exactly as it was during the first live HA run: the coordinator
and in-memory store are written as `{"@type":"Redis"}`, the standalone client, while
EntKube's managed Redis is always a sharded cluster. The server starts cleanly,
logs `auth.success`, and then fails every lookup behind the login with a `MOVED`
redirection the standalone client does not follow. Nothing in the failure names the
address, so it reads as an authentication problem.

Carried over, in order:

- `acb1951` — address the sharded Redis as a cluster. `Coordinator::RedisCluster` /
  the matching `InMemoryStore` variant, `urls` as a `Map<String>` (`{member: true}`),
  and the password out of the connection URL and into `STALWART_REDIS_PASSWORD`,
  since the cluster variant has an `authSecret` the standalone store does not. Also
  reconciles the tracer set, so a verbose apply stops accumulating a second console
  tracer and the default file tracer is removed.
- `bb17834` — read the mail pods' logs after an apply instead of trusting the Job's
  exit code. `registry.build-error` now fails the apply.
- `45f76dc` — `AutoDiscover`, the third casing, which is the one Outlook sends.
- `2d787ea` — warn when the mail certificate's Ready condition is not True, which is
  otherwise invisible until expiry.

Cherry-picked onto current `main`; only `ComponentCatalog.cs` overlapped and in a
different region. Build clean, 2236 tests pass.

Note for whoever deploys this: the bug is in the generated apply plan, not in the
mail image, so **Apply configuration** has to be re-run on the mail component after
the new EntKube build before the login starts working.

body:
## Запрос и границы
Пользователь явно разрешил точечную правку backend: успешное сообщение владельцу не должно скрывать неудачную отправку студенту. Это Telegram/email для уже подключённых клиентов, не SMS/WhatsApp. Связанный frontend: bashpayy-hash/iitaly-site#34. В production этой задачей ничего не запускается, секреты/клиентские файлы не читаются, массовый /api/reminders/run не вызывался.

## Исправлено
- Независимая история попыток и подтверждений для Telegram студента, его почты и Telegram владельца. Успешные каналы повторно не отправляются из-за ошибки другого.
- Повтор неудачного канала: 15м → 30м → 1ч → 2ч → 4ч → максимум раз в 6ч; retry_after Telegram и блокировка получателя могут увеличить паузу. Тик 15 минут вместо суток. REMINDERS=off сохранён.
- Стабильные ключи: задача + точная дата + текущий порог 7/3/1 день/просрочка. Нет трёх догоняющих предупреждений подряд. Понедельничная сводка повторяется после сбоя в пределах недели. Отмечаются только задачи, фактически включённые в отправку.
- Telegram: нужны HTTP success, JSON ok:true и message_id; SMTP: принят именно нужный адрес. Это подтверждение принятия провайдером, не прочтения или push на телефоне.
- Состояние сохраняется после каждого канала, атомарно в существующем зашифрованном клиентском файле. Свежий профиль перечитывается после сетевого ожидания — /stop, настройки, выполненные задачи и документы не перезаписываются. Удалённый профиль не восстанавливается.
- Параллельные ручной/плановый прогоны используют одну выполняющуюся задачу. При сбое записи подтверждение удерживается в памяти до повторного сохранения.
- Ссылки студенту ведут на /portal без кода доступа.

## Проверено
Последний head: **2578eb0732208991b33fd2dc628cf7540dcdd29a**.

[CI — success](https://github.com/bashpayy-hash/iitaly/actions/runs/35329118757): npm ci, проверка синтаксиса, **44/44 теста напоминаний**, **18/18 прежних smoke-проверок**. Нет пропущенных/упавших тестов. CI тестирует merge-ref 804a46d с неизменённой базой 25d34be.

Проверены: независимые исходы owner/email/student; перезапуск; backoff и retry_after; /stop в ходе отправки; смена получателя/даты; завершённые/удалённые задачи; legacy-история; понедельничные сводки; пакет >6 задач; конкурентный прогон; HTTP/JSON ошибки и timeout чтения ответа; настоящие зашифрованные файлы во временной папке и ошибка атомарного rename; действующие portal/webhook handlers с перехваченными отправками.

Все 44 теста доставки работают с синтетическими данными, часами и транспортами. Smoke-проверки поднимают локальный Express с временным DATA_DIR, REMINDERS=off и без production-ключей. Никакого тестового сообщения настоящему клиенту не отправлялось; end-to-end доставка в реальный Telegram и push на телефон пока не проверены.

Скачана точная финальная версия из GitHub, все восемь изменённых файлов побайтно совпадают с локально проверенными; 44 теста повторно успешно выполнены. Временный workflow отсутствует в итоговом дереве. [TAP результатов CI](https://github.com/bashpayy-hash/iitaly/actions/runs/35329118757/artifacts/10540132770).

**Отдельное предупреждение:** npm ci сообщает 4 уязвимости в неизменённых зависимостях (3 moderate, 1 high). Manifest/lockfile в этом PR не менялись; аудит пакетов и оценка применимости этих предупреждений не выполнялись. Успешный CI не означает отсутствие уязвимостей.

## Совместимость и ограничения
Старый reminded не удалён. Его неоднозначные отметки выделены в legacySuppressed, а не выдаются за успешную доставку студенту: историческая массовая переотправка не запускается. Пропущенные ранее сообщения достоверно восстановить нельзя; следующие пороги и изменённые даты используют новую историю.

Система рассчитана на существующий один процесс/реплику и постоянный том. Exactly-once при падении между принятием провайдером и сохранением не обещается; сетевой timeout тоже может быть неоднозначным. Перед масштабированием нужен распределённый outbox. Подтверждение постоянного тома/резервной копии и отдельный тест с согласованным получателем нужны до production rollout. Детали безопасного rollout/rollback — docs/reminder-delivery.md.

Без изменений: roadmap/дедлайны, промпты, чат/проверка документов, вход в кабинет, цены, формат шифрования, manifest/lockfile и Railway config. **PR открыт, в main не слит; production не обновлён.**

author: 3pacs
body:
Three rounds of contract-first fixes in `validation/backtest.py` and `backtest/engine.py`, each defect reproduced by a failing test before the fix (23 tests in `tests/test_evaluator_contracts.py`, pure-Python `FakePITStore` fixture):

1. `predict_fn` was ignored; returns came from `matrix.iloc[:, 0]` → predictions now drive results; opposite/no-op predictors behave as expected.
2. Column-order dependence → sorted, explicit `target_feature_id` (hidden from `predict_fn`; sorted-first default logged as a warning).
3. Window-level `as_of_date=end_date` lookahead and `ffill().bfill()` → per-day as-of cutoffs, forward-fill only; duplicates deduped; explicit `n_total/n_missing/n_warmup` denominators.
4. Same-bar signal (position at t earned the t-1→t return) → signal shifted one bar; a same-bar cheat predictor can no longer win.
5. Leakage-safe walk-forward: optional `fit_fn(train_matrix) -> predict_fn` with `embargo_days`; train_end + embargo < test_start for every era; first era reported `NO_TRAIN_DATA` and excluded with a count; demonstrated that an embargo below the horizon lets an overlap-leaking predictor gain.

Not batched: a single as-of fetch plus masking is provably NOT equivalent to per-day fetches given `store/pit.py`'s `DISTINCT ON … ORDER BY vintage_date` (test included); the interface change `store/pit.py` would need is documented, not made (other lane).

**What remains before "trustworthy" (from the lane's own report):** per-day fetch cost unmeasured on real Postgres; `fit_fn`/embargo never exercised against a real model or real `PITStore`; embargo ≥ horizon is caller convention, not engine-enforced; era-splitting arithmetic edge cases untested; baseline is a single column choice; nothing verified against live `resolved_series`.

**Status:** Fable lane deliverable for review only, rebased onto the recovered baseline `a2f71acf`. DO NOT MERGE without controller sequencing; not a learning-activation authorization. No DB, no migrations; targeted pytest only.

author: numberfour8
body:
Part of the `OffchainPublicKey` split — hoprnet/hopr-types#52.

The protocol needs the decompressed key in exactly one place — deriving shared secrets for an outgoing packet — so that is where the conversion now happens, and nothing else has to widen.

`SphinxSuite` gains an `ExpandedPublic` associated type; only the bound on `G` changes. `Keypair::Public` stays compact, so the key-id mappers keep their `Hash`/`Eq` and **`MetaPacket::into_forwarded` — the relay hot path — is untouched**, since it needs the local keypair and the wire alpha but no peer key. `PathKeyData::new` reaches the expanded form through a `KeyExpander`, so memoization lives where the state's lifetime belongs: `HoprEncoder` holds a `CachingKeyExpander`, tests and benchmarks use `DirectKeyExpander`.

### Numbers

| | change |
|---|---|
| `hopr_decoder/relay` | **−21.9%** |
| `hopr_decoder/recipient` | **−19.7%** |
| `hopr_decoder/ack_recipient` | **−19.2%** |
| `hopr_encoder/ack_batch_10` | **−8.8%** |
| `protocol_throughput_pipeline` (20.3 MiB) | **+19% throughput** |
| `pipeline_e2e_forward` (3hop, 5000 pkt) | **+2–5% throughput** |
| `hopr_encoder/3hop_2surbs` | flat (+0.8% / +2.4% over two runs) |
| `packet_forwarding` / `packet_receiving` | flat (+0.55% / +0.45%) |

The decoder gain comes from deleting both `PeerId → key` caches: `from_peerid` went 4.83 µs → 5.20 ns, so the moka lookup that was hiding it cost far more than the work it replaced. That also frees ~24 MB of resident keys.

`packet_sending_*` is +3.5%, which is the deliberately pessimistic figure — those benchmarks use `DirectKeyExpander` and expand twelve keys per packet with no reuse. The production path is `hopr_encoder`, which is flat.

1330 unit + 144 integration tests pass.

### Two things worth a reviewer's eye

- **The `codec_bench` harness was rebuilding the encoder every iteration**, including a fresh redb temp file. Fixing that drops `hopr_encoder` 519 → 317 µs and `ack_batch_10` 233 → 68 µs on unmodified code; all deltas above are against the re-captured baseline. Separate first commit.
- **The last commit is a correctness fix, not wiring.** `[patch.crates-io]` applies graph-wide but does not propagate from a dependency's own manifest, so patching only hopr-types gave the *published* connector the new length-only parser without the `validate` call that compensates for it. Verified by grepping the resolved source, not just that the build succeeded.

**Draft:** carries temporary `[patch.crates-io]` entries.

### The rest of the train

Merge in order — each step needs the one above it published.

| | repo | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | hopr-types | hoprnet/hopr-types#118 |
| 2 | hopr-api | hoprnet/hopr-api#132 |
| 3 | hopr-utilities | hoprnet/hopr-utilities#32 |
| 4 | hopr-impls | hoprnet/hopr-impls#25 |
| 5 | hoprnet | hoprnet/hoprnet#8431 |
| 6 | hopr-strategy | hoprnet/hopr-strategy#64 |
| 7 | hoprd | hoprnet/hoprd#171 |

author: dakakiki
body:
Two things you saw on the phone.

## 🔴 The admin shell was being drawn over public addresses

> *„u jednom delicu sekunde imam utisak kako da je krenuo da iscrtava admin i onda renderovao public site"* — on `/?pwa=1`

The chain, measured rather than guessed:

1. `app.ts` called `app.mount('#app')` **without waiting for the router**.
2. Until the first navigation resolves, `useRoute()` is vue-router's **`START_LOCATION`**, whose `meta` is an **empty object** (checked in `node_modules/vue-router`).
3. `App.vue` picks its shell with `meta.zone ?? 'admin'` — a fail-safe default (ADR-0014: unmarked → protected) that is wrong **exactly once**, on that first frame.
4. 🪤 **And it was not one frame.** The router's `beforeEach` does `await session.ensureLoaded()` — a network call. The wrong shell stood there for a whole round trip, which is why it read as a fraction of a second rather than a flicker.

**Fix:** mount once the theme **and** the router have settled. `allSettled`, not sequential — the two wait on different things and neither may stop the boot, which is what the `.finally()` it replaces was for. The splash now covers the whole way to the first correct frame, which is what it was for.

⚠️ `?pwa=1` is not special — it only writes a localStorage flag. The same thing happened on every first load; the front page is just where it shows most. And the splash was not the cause: it happened before, against white.

## 🔴 No animation changes opacity any more

> *„kod smene ekrana ne sme da se dogodi taj flash/bljesak jer to moze da bude problem kod foto osetljivih osoba"*

The transition shipped in ADR-0113 was **travel + fade**. A screen whose opacity rises is a screen whose brightness rises out of the page behind it — and on the swap between a **navy** app screen and a **light** website one, that reads as a blink.

**WCAG 2.3.1 counts flashes, not fades**, so one fade would probably not have counted. Rather than argue the threshold, there is now no luminance change at all:

| | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| screen change | `opacity 0→1` + 8px | **8px of travel only** |
| blocks arriving | `opacity 0→1` + 10px | **10px only** |

The element is fully drawn the whole way; it only moves. ✅ Still all inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.

## Both are held by tests that read the source

The front has no test runner (ADR-0074, withdrawn):

- `SpaShellTest` — `app.ts` waits for the router **before** it mounts.
- `MotionDoesNotFlashTest` — **no `@keyframes` may carry `opacity`**, and every rule sits behind the reduced-motion question.

🪤 Checked that **both fail with the old code put back**. A test that passes on the broken and the fixed version asserts nothing.

Suite **852** green (851 + 1 skipped); type-check and build clean.

ADR-0115, amending ADR-0113.

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `383337d4-571b-4800-8656-2c8d5cef9df7` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-qwen38-125b-a6b-engine at `002e1a82f9d3c110613954a1b56fdce6abbab81d`.

Current best score: 1.97746471852911. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus
Harness: Claude Code

# PLE residual add folded into the conv epilogue

Parent: `002e1a82f9d3c110613954a1b56fdce6abbab81d` (the public crown, a redraw of
`dcf0d156`). Layer: host-ple. Two files under `Runner/FastModel/`:
`TrackFastModel.swift` and `TrackFastPLE.swift`. The mechanism is ported from
the public near-frontier tree `e0676ed7` (submission `49fe1d2`, measured
1.97709 — within ranked noise of the crown), which carries it as `HAS_RES`;
this patch grafts that single mechanism onto HEAD and nothing else from that
tree.

## What the PLE forward costs today

The PLE (n-gram) layer on layer index 1 runs once per decode step. Under the
declared MTP depth every step that reaches it is a verify window of S = 1+k
tokens, so the S>=2 branch of `pleForward` is the hot path. That branch ends
with `track_ple_conv` producing `out = gated + silu(conv)`, and then the
caller issues a **separate elementwise add** `stream = stream + output` — a
full extra kernel launch that reads two `[B,S,10240]` tensors and writes one,
purely to perform one `InT` add per element.

## The mechanism

`track_ple_conv` gains a fourth input, `residual`, and a template constant
`HAS_RES`. Its epilogue becomes:

    const InT ple = gated[o] + mlx_silu(static_cast<InT>(acc));
    out[o] = HAS_RES ? (residual[o] + ple) : ple;

The S>=2 call site passes `residual: stream`, so the conv kernel emits the
already-summed stream and the standalone `stream + pleForward(...)` add
disappears — one fewer launch per PLE forward on every verify window. When
`residual` is nil the wrapper passes `gated` as a harmless placeholder and
`HAS_RES` is false, so the placeholder is never read; the kernel is
bit-identical to before in that configuration.

The S==1 fused path (`TrackPLEFusion`, which has its own fused conv and does
not go through `track_ple_conv`) keeps the add but relocates it inside
`pleForward` — `(full, output) = (fused.0, fused.1 + stream)` — so the
function's contract becomes uniform: **every path returns the summed
stream**. The call site drops its `+` accordingly. Under MTP the S==1 path is
not reached in scored legs; the relocation exists only to keep the contract
consistent.

## Why it is bit-exact

The fold preserves operand order and operation count exactly: the elementwise
kernel computed `stream[o] + ple[o]` in `InT`; the conv epilogue computes
`residual[o] + ple[o]` in `InT` where `residual` IS `stream`. Same operands,
same order, same dtype, same single rounding. Nothing else in the kernel
changes — the conv accumulation, the silu, and the `gated` add are untouched.
`ensureRowContiguous` already applies to all conv inputs, and `stream` is a
contiguous `[B,S,W]` activation, so the extra input needs no layout handling.

## What was deliberately not done

- The rest of `e0676ed7` is NOT grafted: its rope-table cache, dtype-binding
  tidy, divisor-scalar cache, and tail-flush reorder are separate mechanisms
  whose net bundle measured -0.03% vs the crown. Only the residual fold —
  the one mechanism in that tree that removes a launch with provably
  identical arithmetic — is taken.
- The `normed -> full` concat elimination (GU261 family) is not retried: it
  scored 1.9549 when fused with prepare, and this patch does not touch the
  staging path at all.
- No changes to `prod`/`gated` strides, the host n-gram mirror, `hostRowIds`,
  or the `multipliers` readback — those are the in-flight candidate's surface
  or non-editable.

## Expected effect

One fewer kernel launch per PLE forward on every verify window — the
elementwise stream-add disappears entirely. The removed launch is pure
overhead: it moved 3 x S x 10240 elements through memory for one add per
element. The conv kernel gains one `[B,S,W]` read it did not have before
(the residual input), but it already writes `out` at the same addresses, so
the net traffic still drops by one full tensor read plus the launch itself.
Small, strictly positive, bit-exact — the same shape as the crown's other
single-launch eliminations.

## Risk assessment

The change is confined to the PLE forward path and its single call site. The
kernel signature grows by one input and one template constant; both are
compile-time resolved, so the generated code for the `HAS_RES = false`
configuration is unchanged. The only behavioral difference is where the
residual add executes — inside the conv epilogue instead of a standalone
elementwise kernel — and the arithmetic it performs is identical. The S==1
relocation is a pure code motion of the same `+` operation. Residual risk is
limited to the usual ranked-noise band; there is no correctness or
numerical-stability exposure beyond a single relocated `InT` add.

## Provenance and alternatives considered

The graft order for this turn was: Navigator TAKE items first, then NEXT, then
the layer hole. All six TAKE entries were checked against HEAD and found
already present or superseded — the two `MLXFAST-FULLTAIL` parts are in
`TrackFastKernels2.swift` at both inject-GEMV tail sites, the GDN prefetch is
explicitly rejected by HEAD's own `GDNROWS` commentary (measured +8.4% worse
at four rows), the NAX packed-word loader is superseded by HEAD's `WVEC`
vectorized stores, and the scalar-hoist mechanism already landed as
`TrackFastKernels.scalar`. Navigator NEXT (`68a84e93`, dedicated no-gate
prefill route kernel) is a scored reject at -0.75% and was skipped. A full
`yukon reset` of `e0676ed7` was rejected because its bundle nets below the
crown; grafting the single launch-elimination mechanism keeps the crown's
other wins while taking the one change that is provably non-negative.

author: akoita
body:
Slice 3b (#1799) shipped a control that schedules an erasure 30 days out.
**Nothing runs it.** This is the entry point that can, plus the operator
procedure the privacy policy names as a reason it cannot publish its deletion
section.

## The design in my own issue was wrong

I wrote #1797 saying "add a `google_cloud_scheduler_job` for
`POST /admin/erasure/run-due`". That cannot work: **every route on
`MaintenanceController` is guarded by `AuthGuard("jwt")` + `RolesGuard` +
`@Roles("admin")`.** Cloud Scheduler can present a Google OIDC token — which
authenticates it to Cloud Run — but it cannot mint an application JWT carrying
an allowlisted admin address.

There is no shape of wiring that reaches those endpoints from a schedule. That
is also the mechanical reason analytics retention (#1789) was never scheduled,
rather than an oversight anyone made — its endpoint has been unreachable in the
same way since it was written.

## What works instead

The one scheduled task in the system does not make an HTTP call.
`analytics_warehouse_load` is a **Cloud Run Job** running the backend image,
with Cloud Scheduler invoking the *job*, not the service — so it calls the
service in-process and no application authentication is involved.

`backend/src/scripts/run_due_erasures.ts` is that entry point for erasure. It is
a real file rather than the inline `args = ["-e", <script>]` string the
warehouse job embeds in Terraform: an erasure is irreversible, and its entry
point should be reviewable, diffable and testable like any other code instead of
a string literal in an infrastructure module. `npm run build` already compiles
`src/**` to `dist/**` and the Dockerfile already copies `dist`, so the image
carries it with no packaging change.

## The exit code is the contract, so it is tested

Zero only when nothing failed — **including the ordinary case where nothing was
due**, which must not page anybody. One when *any* erasure failed, not only when
all did, so a bad run surfaces as a failed execution rather than a green job that
quietly erased nothing.

Getting that backwards is precisely how #1789 went unnoticed: a working endpoint
nobody called, and nothing that ever said so. `exitCodeFor` and `parseLimit` are
pure and have their own tests for that reason.

The run logs counts and failed request ids only — naming the people whose
identifiers were just removed would put them back.

## The runbook

`docs/operations/account_erasure_runbook.md` covers the scheduled path, the
manual path for an operator with an admin token, what to check **before the
first real run against real data** (including #1796, since an erasure run while
the salt is unset can silently miss a person's analytics), how to read a failure
(durable on `AccountClosureRequest.failureMessage` before it is visible in any
log), why a partial erasure cannot happen in Postgres but analytics *can* be
erased while the account survives, and what an erasure deliberately does not
remove.

## What is still missing

The infrastructure: a Cloud Run Job, a Cloud Scheduler job, a service account
and IAM, in the infrastructure repository. **#1797 stays open until that lands**,
and the privacy policy's publication block stays in place — narrowed here to
name only the missing piece rather than the whole mechanism.

## Validation

```
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit            # clean
cd backend && npm run lint                # clean
cd backend && npm run test -- run_due_erasures   # 5 passed
```

Scoped deliberately: this adds an entry point and documentation and changes no
existing behaviour, so the focused gates are the proportionate ones and the full
suites are CI's.

## Change impact checklist

Applicable: **Data lifecycle and operational state** (a scheduled entry point
for an irreversible operation); **Documentation and roadmap alignment** (runbook,
feature page, privacy policy block narrowed). No API contract change — the
existing admin endpoint is untouched and remains the manual path. **No new
environment variables.**

## Vision

Vision-neutral compliance infrastructure (`vision:keep`). No ADR-BM-6 revenue
line, fee, price or payout is touched.

Refs #1797.

## Dlaczego to musi wejść

Nic z tej pracy nie działa, dopóki nie jest na `main` — bot startuje z niej co 5 minut (`ref: main` w `tracker.yml`). Poprzednia wersja tej gałęzi nigdy nie została scalona i to jest jedyny powód, dla którego przycisk oferty nie pojawił się na kanale.

## Dublet na kanale najlepszych — naprawione

`najlepsze.main` trzymał stan wysyłki w pamięci przez całą pętlę i zapisywał go raz, po niej. W tej pętli siedzi żądanie sieciowe (`czy_zyje` na każdą ofertę) i pauza 1,2 s, przy suficie ogniwa 8 minut. Bieg jest jednym z **siedmiu ogniw** matrycy, a krok ma `continue-on-error: true` — więc wywrotka kasowała pamięć o wszystkim, co już poszło, następne ogniwo wysyłało to samo, i nie było tego widać w Actions.

Odtworzone w piaskownicy na kodzie sprzed naprawy: **2 wiadomości wysłane, 0 zapisanych**. Zapis idzie teraz od razu po każdej wysyłce i po każdym pominięciu; koszt to ~30 kB zapisu do ośmiu razy na bieg.

## Przycisk pełnej oferty na BestDealHawku

Kliknięcia z tego kanału trafiają do kolejki `getUpdates` jego własnego bota, której `tracker` nie czyta i czytać nie może (dwa procesy na jednej kolejce gubiłyby zdarzenia losowo i po cichu). Wpięcie guzika wyłącznie w `tracker.py` znaczyło, że na tym kanale nie ma go w ogóle.

Dochodzi `klawiatura_pod_oferta`, gałąź `of|` w `czytaj_odrzuty` i obsługa `/oferta` w `obsluz_komende`. Klucz przeceny `id@cena` obcinany do samego numeru, bo inaczej komenda odbija się o własną walidację; przyciski odrzutu zostają przy pełnym kluczu.

## Generator `/oferta` z przekładem

Nowy moduł `oferta.py` składa gotową wiadomość z twardą ofertą do sprzedawcy. Czyta `seen.json` i `de_stan.json`, nie pobiera nic z sieci i **nie wysyła** — właściciel kopiuje i wysyła sam.

- Kwota z `cena_po_ogledzinach` (oba etapy targu naraz), bo wiadomość obiecuje brak dogadywania na miejscu. Przy 2 800 € VB daje 2 200 €, czyli tyle, ile właściciel wpisał ręcznie.
- Zaokrąglenie w dół do 50 €, ale sufit `NEGO_MAX_LACZNIE` bije zaokrąglenie: bez tego tanie rowery szły na 25% przy sufircie 22% (23 naruszenia na 80 kombinacjach).
- Żadnego wymyślonego dnia odbioru. Zaliczka tylko na żądanie.
- „VB" czytane wprost z pola ceny; przy sprzeczności z „Festpreis" w opisie nie twierdzimy żadnego z dwóch (1 wpis na 2 800).
- Przekład na polski pod każdą wiadomością, poza blokiem do skopiowania. Oba języki powstają w jednym rozgałęzieniu, żeby nie mogły się rozjechać po cichu.

## Testy

Trzy zestawy przechodzą: `test.py`, `test_otomoto.py`, `test_najlepsze.py`. Test dubletu sprawdzony na kodzie sprzed naprawy — pada tam, więc jest strażnikiem, a nie pieczątką. `oferta.py` dopisany do wyzwalaczy w `tests.yml`, bo wcześniej jego zmiana nie odpalała żadnego biegu.

body:
Part of the `OffchainPublicKey` split — hoprnet/hopr-types#52.

Dependency wiring only.

**No source change was needed.** The ten uses here — the network REST rendering and a key-id mapper test stub — treat the key purely as an identifier. 204 tests pass unchanged.

The second commit matters more than its size suggests. `[patch.crates-io]` applies graph-wide, but a patch declared in a *dependency's* manifest does not propagate to the crate being built — so patching hopr-types here gave the published `hopr-chain-connector` the compact key's length-only parser while the `validate` call that compensates for it lived only on the hopr-impls branch. An off-curve packet key from the indexer would have been admitted into the account and routing tables. Patching the connector itself closes that; verified by grepping the resolved source.

**Draft:** pins `hopr-lib` to a hoprnet rev and carries temporary `[patch.crates-io]` entries. Repoint at master and drop the patches once the train is published.

author: dofbi
body:
Cette PR recentre le dépôt sur l'application mobile et pose le socle du MVP. Elle
sert de base à la suite : elle ne cherche pas à livrer une application finie.

## Ce qu'elle contient

**1. Renommage vers `p2p-local`.** Le scope npm `@wantere/*` devient
`@p2p-local/*`, ainsi que le workspace, l'application Expo, ses identifiants
natifs et tous les documents. `p2p-local` est un **nom de code**, isolé dans la
configuration pour qu'un nom définitif le remplace en une seule passe. Les
identifiants de base de données et de docker sont inchangés, pour ne pas obliger
chacun à recréer ses volumes locaux.

**2. Suppression de `apps/web` et `apps/admin`.** Les deux front Next.js ne
portaient aucune surface produit. Partent avec eux la variante CSS des
design-tokens, le preset ESLint Next et le preset TypeScript Next, qui n'étaient
utilisés que par eux. `README`, `CONTRIBUTING` et `docs/architecture.md` sont mis
à jour, pas réécrits : leurs sections encore justes sont conservées.

**3. Configuration Expo SDK 57 et EAS.** `eas.json` avec trois profils —
`preview` produit un APK, seul format partageable et installable sans keystore ni
compte Apple. `app.json` complété : identifiant de projet EAS, icônes générées
depuis les design-tokens par un script, splash, sélecteur de photo et ses textes
de permission en français. Workflow de build manuel, qui attend un secret de
dépôt `EXPO_TOKEN`.

**4. Couche de données locale.** Les annonces vivent sur l'appareil, derrière une
interface `ListingRepository` dont l'unique implémentation écrit un document JSON
dans AsyncStorage. Aucun écran n'importe le stockage : l'implémentation est
injectée par un contexte, donc brancher un serveur plus tard est une classe de
plus et une ligne changée dans le provider.

Quartiers en liste fermée dans `@p2p-local/config` — un filtre par quartier
n'a de sens que si les valeurs sont comparables. Cycle de vie : expiration à 30
jours, « marquer comme donné » qui garde l'annonce visible et grisée 48 heures
avant archivage, suppression définitive qui emporte le fichier photo.

## Confidentialité du numéro

L'application **n'affiche jamais un numéro de téléphone** : ni dans une annonce,
ni dans un bouton, ni dans un texte partagé. `features/contact/whatsapp.ts` est le
seul module qui en manipule un, et il le place dans une URL `wa.me` construite au
moment du geste. Deux tests vérifient que ni le message de contact ni le texte
partagé ne contiennent de suite de chiffres.

Reste que l'auteur d'une annonce devient joignable, ce qui est en tension avec la
règle de `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Le point est signalé dans `docs/design/README.md` et
attend un arbitrage d'équipe : relais masquant, exposition assumée, ou
consentement explicite par annonce.

## Vérifications

Sur une machine propre en Node 24 :

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accepté ;
- `pnpm lint` 7/7, `pnpm typecheck` 11/11 ;
- **19 tests mobile, 11 tests API**, tous verts ;
- `npx expo-doctor` 21/21 ;
- **build EAS `preview` réussi, APK produit**.

Le build a d'ailleurs révélé un piège du monorepo : EAS installe puis bundle, il
n'exécute jamais turbo, donc les paquets partagés compilés vers `dist/` n'étaient
pas résolus par Metro. Corrigé par un script `eas-build-post-install`.

## Ce que cette PR ne tranche pas

- **Une annonce publiée n'est visible que sur le téléphone qui l'a publiée.**
  C'est la conséquence du « local d'abord », et la limite la plus lourde de ce
  socle. Si des annonces doivent circuler entre voisins, il faudra un backend.
- Le nom définitif, `p2p-local` n'étant qu'un marque-place.
- Le sort d'`apps/api`, conservée mais que plus aucune application ne consomme,
  et de `packages/api-client` qui n'a plus de consommateur.
- La PR #5 implémente la messagerie interne, que cette direction écarte au profit
  de WhatsApp. Ce n'est pas une dérive du contributeur mais une ambiguïté que le
  dépôt portait. Elle entrera en conflit avec le renommage.
- Le rôle de la branche `develop`, que le dépôt utilise de façon incohérente.

## Prérequis restants

- secret `EXPO_TOKEN` sur le dépôt, pour le workflow de build ;
- `owner` dans `app.json` une fois le compte Expo renommé, sinon un build lancé
  par un autre membre échouera.

Closes #4315

## 处置：选 **A（撤回 claim）**，不选 B（由权威源生成）

**理由**：`docs/wiki/DEV-FLOW.md` 是**人工散文节选**（技能 20 节 → 本页 8 节，且页内是摘要而不是
可机械重排的结构）。要让"同步"这句话为真，B 得先把节选搬进技能、或写一套摘要渲染器 ——
**每次技能更新都要重生成整页**，而这正是过去失败的机制（页内现值漂了 6 个月没人知道）。
**代价**：撤回后本页**不再是任何东西的真值源**（页头已明写"口径一律以技能为准"），
读者要现行口径必须去看技能；换来的是**判据可落地**（C1~C4 形状判据 + 注入式自证，零 LLM、秒级）。

## 改动（2 个文件）

`docs/wiki/DEV-FLOW.md`
- 页头：`同步副本` → 「**不是**同步副本 —— **已停止同步**（#4315）」+「流程口径**一律以技能为准**」；
  "落后多少" 改成**可复算的命令**（命令自证）而不是现值；§5 补一行指向权威源。
- 删掉会腐烂的现值（§19.2 ③「不写死易变数字」）：`当前版本：v1.3`、
  `副本 v1.3 / 权威源 1.31.0`、`migao-wt/ 下 38 个工作区里 31 个版本 ≠ main`（本机同一量已漂到 62）。
- 修掉一处**可验证为假**的引用：`walkthrough/RETROSPECTIVE.md` **仓内不存在**（页头本就写着"未入库"）。
- 只改 claim / 现值 / 悬空引用，**未重写正文节选**。

`tests/unit_ci_workflows/test_dev_flow_sync_claim.py`（新增，`# case_ids: MC-012`，形状判据 + 注入式自证）
- **C1** 肯定式「同步副本」claim（含该词的行必须带 `不是/已停止同步/不再/已撤回`）⇒ 不许出现
- **C2** 硬编码现值：`当前版本：vX` / `副本 vX` / `权威源 vX.Y.Z` ⇒ 不许出现
- **C3** 硬编码工作区计数（`N 个工作区` / `N 个的…`）⇒ 不许出现
- **C4**（正向）页头**必须**同时声明「已停止同步」+「以技能为准」

  `hardcoded-count` 登记为**未实装**的理由，本文件不冒充当它已实装）；页头「权威源：`path`」形态
  由**既有** `drift_audit` 的 `declared-source` 判据守着（无基线豁免）⇒ 本文件**不复制**该规则；
  本判据**不读技能版本** ⇒ 技能更新**不会**让它红（撤回方案要的正是这个性质）。

## 红证（`scripts/red_proof.py` 自证注入生效 + 注入前后清缓存；§19.1 元规则 ③）

基线（改动后）`docs/wiki/DEV-FLOW.md` sha256 = `af2a1c16966aa4dc5cb72f31f1946e903cad908f68950b39878c5d3e8761942a`

| 注入的失效形态 | 注入后 sha256 | 判据输出 |
|---|---|---|
| ① 肯定式「同步副本」claim + `当前版本：v1.3` + `38 个工作区 / 31 个的` + `副本 v1.3 / 权威源 1.31.0` | `2457b90757523c7e62f0cf03bf433d70df829f6a58c1c3627d63f57c9f248ec7` | **2 failed, 10 passed**（C1 报第 3、295 行；C2 报第 4、97、295 行） |
| ② 静默删掉页头的「已停止同步」关系声明 | `074a34525893975cda85b9ae5b69f87bc822fed3627cc4910b3e64ce4530882a` | **1 failed, 11 passed**（C4 报 `页头缺关系声明 ['已停止同步']`） |

还原后 sha256 与基线**逐字节一致**（`red_proof.py restored` 自证）。改动前（Red，最小实现之前）同文件为
`ffe20b587d6215fee7dcd54004ab4bacc863a95c22976f1bca41f1489b5d6386` ⇒ `3 failed, 9 passed`。

常驻自证（不依赖人工注入，永久留在测试里）：撤回前**逐字原文**作为夹具，每个探测器在它上面**必须报错**；

- `./verify-all.sh gate`（**commit 之后**）⇒ **1 通过, 0 失败**（cases 面未命中受管面，显式打印"未跑"）

## 未做 / 另开单（**超出"声明与事实不符"之外的正文时效性**，本 PR 不动）

页内还有**可验证为假**的现值陈述，但属**另一族缺陷**（CI 配置现值过期，不是"本页与权威源的关系"声明），
且按 §19.2 ③ 无零误红判据，故本 PR **不修**、另开单：
1. §3 表格仍列 `Agent Eval (smoke)` 为 CI 关卡 —— 该 job 已由 #3653 移除（`pr-check.yml:528` 注释）；
2. §3.2「每 3 天 normal 全量」—— `post-deploy-eval.yml` 现为 `0 3 * * 1`（每周一，#4262）；
3. §3.2「定时档（3 天 normal / 每周 adversarial ×2）**全部保留**」+「adversarial …对抗档为**定时保留**」+
   「xiaobu-acceptance 除定时对抗档外均为手动」—— 三条 `schedule` 已由 #4262 删除（现仅 `workflow_dispatch`）；
4. §3.2「只有 2 个必须留意」的计数随 #4262 已不成立。
另：`docs/wiki/truth-source-contract.md` §6 的 `sync-copy-landing` 未实装登记（"后续小单二选一"）

author: bihius
body:
`main` still has the Docker/Laravel skeleton. This branch is the rest of the application: a local RAG assistant that indexes documents, answers from retrieved chunks, and says so when the knowledge base does not cover the question.

## What landed

- **Ingestion.** Markdown, text, PDF, and URL import (Symfony DomCrawler). Uploads go onto a Redis queue; a worker chunks the text, embeds each chunk with `bge-m3`, and stores vectors in pgvector.
- **Retrieval and chat.** Cosine search over chunks, a distance threshold on the closest hit (`RAG_MAX_DISTANCE=0.6` for `bge-m3`), then an answer from `qwen3:8b`. Chat streams over SSE and returns the fragments it used. Below the threshold the model is not called.
- **Review loop.** Thumbs on answers, a `needs_review` queue, and a resolve action that turns a written answer into a new indexed document.
- **Interface.** Chat, documents, questions, and analytics on their own URLs. Analytics groups similar questions when embeddings exist.
- **API and widget.** REST surface documented in `docs/openapi.yaml`. `/widget.js` is a small TypeScript bundle in a shadow root, plus `/widget-demo` as a host page that is not the app itself.

## Fixes on top of that

- Tests no longer wipe the development database: `phpunit.xml` overrides container env vars through `<server force="true">`.
- Creating a document through `POST /api/documents` now queues indexing, same as file and URL import.
- Import endpoints return 201. Indexed documents report `completed`.
- The inbox watcher has a `content_hash` column to skip duplicates.
- Redis `retry_after` is 180s so it stays above the worker timeout of 120s.
- Widget source titles are rendered as text, not HTML. CORS is configured for `/api/*`. CI uses PHP 8.4.

## How to try it

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # OLLAMA_URL should be http://host.docker.internal:11434
ollama pull bge-m3 && ollama pull qwen3:8b
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose exec app php artisan key:generate
docker compose exec app php artisan migrate
docker compose restart worker
```

Then open http://localhost:8000 — import a short note, wait until its status is `completed`, and ask something it actually contains. Also hit a question it cannot know, rate a bad answer, resolve it from `/questions`, and load `/widget-demo`.

```bash
docker compose exec app php artisan test
```

Add source-specific wiki drop rates as an extra popup statistic while preserving the four configurable statistic slots. Guaranteed and unavailable rates are omitted; source variants can display a range. Preview notifications use a matching source, and GE-tradeable items retain value-based handling.

Wiki downloads now include completion data and drop rates, enabled by default with a weekly cache refresh boundary on Thursday. The existing refresh setting controls both datasets; disabling it cancels requests, and toggling it on can force a refresh subject to a one-minute limit. Requests fetch public wiki data without player names or collection contents. Local caches retain attribution and licence information.

Includes popup layout and visibility improvements, updated documentation, and tests for parsing, refresh/cache lifecycle and rendering. The item name, source and drop-rate text sit higher, and an enabled kill-count slot shows a dash when no count is available. Drop rates are display-only and do not change rarity weighting or sounds.

Adds an opt-in **Hide CoX rewards** setting: masks the collection-log chat message for Chambers uniques and holds their queued popup/audio until the raid reward interface opens. Includes unit and flow tests; this latest addition has not been tested locally as part of this push.

The Chambers reward hold applies only inside the raid the unique came from.

Source diff: https://github.com/Quentin242/drop-enhancer/compare/66dfb395188abd9f5e914846a6bf6953f4458e40...337e9f734c13394f19ed8c44b9fbb9f2fbabe69e

The cwd bug that emptied every storefront shipped because nothing asserted this,
and nothing could have noticed by accident: a missing manifest is silent by
design — the page still serves, statically, with no runtime injector and no
error. It reads as a page that has no content.

Five cases against the real class, the important one being "started from the
repo root", which is how the built image starts the app and the case that was
broken. Confirmed the test has teeth by restoring the old cwd-only lookup and
re-running: 3 failed, 2 passed, and the failure is exactly the image-cwd case.

Also pins the two properties worth keeping: an absent manifest still serves the
page rather than throwing, but now says so out loud; and a manifest entry naming
a path rather than a bare file is still refused.

author: mattn
body: `tensai run` without `-q8` or `-q4` now lets the loader choose the width instead of expanding the model to float32. The file's own quantization sets the ceiling (int4 blocks stay int4, ternary is ternary, Q8_0/Q5_K/Q6_K/float keep their precision only at int8), and int8 narrows to int4 when the weights plus their tables would not fit the memory the machine has available (MemAvailable on Linux, the total on macOS, available physical on Windows). `-v` reports the choice and the reason; `-f32` asks for float32 explicitly. `Options.Bits = BitsAuto` exposes the same to library callers.

author: azmartone67
body:
## What was measured

`brain_review_decisions` had exactly **one** production writer — `record_review_decision()` at `routes/brain_merge_reconciler.py` — and it hardcodes the literal `"approve"`. `list_merged_brain_prs()` only ever fetches **merged** PRs, so the event that actually *is* a rejection — the operator closing a brain PR without merging it — reached the database through no path at all.

That is not cosmetic. `check_rejection_skip()` is **live** at `routes/brain_v2_layer4.py:925` and reads `brain_review_decisions WHERE decision='reject'`. With no writer it could only ever return `False`, so the brain kept re-proposing work that had already been turned down.

Measured on production **before** this change:

```
/api/v1/brain/effectiveness    human_reviews_30d  128, by_decision {"approve": 128}
                               rejection_rate_pct 0.0
/api/v1/brain/self-assessment  human_review_count_60d 288
                               human_rejection_rate   0.0
                               rejection_signal       "dead"
                               false_positives_remembered 4  (of 1168 persisted issues)
```

`brain_consistency_radar.check_review_gate_never_disagrees()` has been firing on exactly this.

## What this adds

`list_closed_unmerged_brain_prs()` + `record_review_rejection()`, wired as a second pass in `run_reconciliation()`. It **credits nothing** — no `mark_proposal_merged`, no `merge_outcome`, no fix outcome — and is idempotent through the existing per-PR ledger under a new terminal state `closed_unmerged_rejected`.

## The two things that make it real rather than merely present

**1. The key agrees with the reader.** `issue_hash()` is `sha1(f"{label}|{find_text[:200]}")`, and Layer 4 looks up `check_rejection_skip(issue["issue"], find)` — label **and** search text. A rejection written the way the approve path writes one hashes `sha1("label|")` while the reader looks up `sha1("label|<find>")`; they can never be equal, and the gate would have stayed inert with a rejection row sitting right next to it. `rejection_key()` therefore reads **both halves off the proposal row** (`issue_key`, `search_text`) — the row Layer 5 wrote from the very pair Layer 4 hashes.

**2. The pass is reachable.** `run_reconciliation()` used to `return` early on an empty merged list, which would have starved this pass in exactly the window that contains only rejections — a lane reporting `ok:true` while scanning nothing.

## Verification

`tests/test_brain_merge_reconciler.py` — 31 passed (was 29 + 2 new listers, 9 new tests total).

Every new guard was mutation-tested, and each mutation was confirmed to actually apply before its result was read:

| Mutation | Guard | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `rejection_key` drops `find_text` (the pre-fix keying) | `test_rejection_hash_equals_what_layer4_looks_up` | **FAILED (good)** |
| restore the early return on an empty merged list | `test_closed_unmerged_pass_runs_with_zero_merged_prs` | **FAILED (good)** |
| lister keeps MERGED PRs | `test_closed_unmerged_lister_excludes_merged_prs` | **FAILED (good)** |
| lister drops the brain-branch invariant | `test_closed_unmerged_lister_excludes_merged_prs` | **FAILED (good)** |

The hash test uses the **real** `brain_learning.issue_hash`, not a re-implementation, and carries a must-fail control asserting the label-only hash does *not* collide with the `(label, find)` hash — so the test cannot go vacuous without failing.

`test_layer4_still_keys_on_label_and_find` pins the **reader**: if Layer 4 ever stops passing `find`, this writer silently stops matching again, and that disagreement has no runtime error.

```
python3 scripts/regression_lint.py --mode delta --base origin/main
✓ no NEW violations introduced by this PR
```

## Not verified here

Production effect is unverified until this merges and the reconciler's next pass runs against real closed PRs. The expected first-run signal is `closed_unmerged_brain_prs_in_window > 0` on `/api/v1/brain/merge-reconciler/status` and a non-zero `reject` count in `human_reviews_30d.by_decision`.

Note `check_rejection_skip` uses `reject_threshold=2`, so a single closed PR does not suppress anything — it takes two rejections on the same `(label, find)` within 30 days.
