author: ahoo-wang
body:
## What changed

A review of `packages/view-engine` found seven high-severity defects. Each is fixed here with a regression test that reproduces the original scenario, and `docs/design.md` is updated for every rule that changed.

### Runtime

- **Only admitted configs run.** A view opened on a config the definition refuses was meant to wait for a fix, but only `apply` was refused: `refresh` and `page` executed it as it stood, so a stored `pageSize: 5000` went to the wire on the first refresh. Both are now no-ops until an admitted draft has been applied (`appliedAdmitted` in `DataViewRuntime`).
- **Scope filters are admitted everywhere.** An injected scope was validated with the config at construction only; `edit` rejudged the draft alone, so one edit cleared the issue and `apply` ran the merged, inadmissible condition. `issues` is now the admission of *draft AND scope* in the constructor, `edit`, `adoptSaved` and `setScopeFilter`. `mergeFilters` appends the scope after the draft's own conditions, so issue paths into the draft's tree are unchanged (asserted).
- **Dashboard.** The host's scope was never merged into what the dashboard validated; `dashboard.panels.too-many` (path `['panels']`) belonged to no panel so every panel still ran; and a child's refusal of a new scope was discarded, leaving it on its previous scope. Now the scope is admitted with the config, whole-dashboard issues block every panel, and a child that refuses is disposed with the reasons reported at `['panels', index, …]` on that panel.
- **Unknown writes hold the target.** A second write to a target whose last write ended `unknown` minted a new `requestId`, which is exactly what the server cannot deduplicate: a first save that timed out after landing became two instances with an orphaned `pendingWrites` entry. The engine now refuses with `view.write.unknown-pending` until that outcome is retried or abandoned. `rejected` and `conflict` outcomes do not block a new intent (a conflict's choices include "save as").

### Filter kernel and UI

- **Date ranges include their last day.** A date-only `to` (or an `LTE` bound) resolved to that day's first instant, so a range through the 31st stopped before it began. The UI also stored calendar picks as local midnight with a `Z`, which the kernel rightly treats as a fixed instant, so the runtime and per-condition time zones never applied. Now a date-only string on the end edge is the last millisecond of its day in the zone (`RangeEdge`, `resolveDateTimeBound`), and `FilterValueEditor` stores `YYYY-MM-DD` when the editor carries no time of day.
- **A blank elementMatch predicate is blank.** A predicate whose only condition was unfilled counted as a condition, compiled to `ELEMENT_MATCH` over `MATCH_ALL`, and silently narrowed the result to "the array is non-empty". New `isBlankFilter` judges a predicate by its leaves with the same rule validate, compile and describe already apply. `FieldKind.isBlank` now receives `{ value, operator, field, kinds }` (this package owes no compatibility; all built-in kinds updated).
- **Metadata kinds recognise their own empty value.** `isBlank` only knew `{ items: [] }`, so a freshly added `@tenantId` / `@id IDS` row was an error the moment it appeared. The test that had codified this is corrected.

### Analysis kernel

- `defaultAnalysisConfig` carried a `sort` with no groups, which Wow refuses (`sort requires at least one groupBy`). The default is now unsorted in that case, and `validateAnalysis` reports `analysis.sort.requires-group` / `analysis.having.requires-group` so a stored config fails admission rather than the server. The default config is round-tripped through Wow's `aggregation.query()` in the test.

## Verification

From `packages/view-engine`: `pnpm test` (27 files, 883 tests, coverage above every threshold, three tsc projects), `pnpm lint:check` with zero warnings, and `pnpm build` including `verify-package`.

## Not in this PR

The review also found medium-severity items left for follow-up: structural guards in the three `validate*` entry points (malformed stored configs throw `TypeError`), `locate` advancing only the first runtime when an instance is open twice, a stale `filter` on a `DERIVED` metric still compiling, dashboard admission validating an analysis panel's filter against root fields only, `DashboardGrid` writing geometry back on mount, the workbenches keeping a disposed runtime after deleting the open view, the default `FilterPanel` never calling `setEditing`, and the metric-card trend summing non-additive metrics.

author: optimisedmath
body:
ADR-0015 landed on `main` on 2026-09-17, two days after #329 opened #251's rename. It therefore recorded the closed input-mode set under the typing value's older spelling: it says every producer returns `"radio"` or `"input"`, and #343 would have closed the wire set around `input` — a literal #251 deletes. #251 is #343's blocker, so it lands first and the set has to close around `radio` and `typing`.

This PR amends ADR-0015 in place, in the style of the #237/#286 amendments on ADR-0005 and the #302 amendment on ADR-0003. The decision, the three rejected alternatives and the reasoning are untouched — one of the two values has a different name, not a different meaning.

What changed:

- The set's literals in the opening paragraph read `radio` and `typing`.
- The dated evidence keeps its spelling. The 134-row count was taken on 2026-09-17, while the typing value was still spelled `input`, and the consequences paragraph now says that plainly instead of silently respelling a measurement.
- A new **Amended by #251** note records the rename, the glossary's **Input mode** → **Typing mode** change, that the axis keeps the name `input_mode`, and the ordering: #251 respells the nine `input` rows before #343 closes the set, so they never meet it as out-of-set values. Nothing is deployed and no Student holds a Session, so a stray old-spelling row can be dropped or rewritten — there is nothing to migrate.

No code changes. Every remaining `'input'` / `"input"` mode literal in `backend/`, `frontend/` and `tests/` is #251's to rename and is deliberately left alone here; #329 owns that branch.

Issue bodies for #343, #344, #307 and #301 are corrected separately on GitHub.

author: ixday
body:
Restores the hardened staging build for `events-processor`, FROMing the Wolfi/apko bases now published by [getlago/lago-packages](https://github.com/getlago/lago-packages) to GHCR.

```dockerfile
ARG BUILD_IMAGE=ghcr.io/getlago/events-processor-build:latest
ARG RUNTIME_IMAGE=ghcr.io/getlago/events-processor-base:latest
```

### Why this is a new PR and not #800 reopened

#800 cannot be reopened. Its branch was force-pushed onto `main` at the moment it was closed, so it now contains no changes and GitHub refuses to reopen a PR with an empty diff.

Unlike lago-front#4318 — where a pinned review preserved the pre-push commit — nothing in #800's timeline references its original head, so that version is genuinely gone. This is adapted from the copy in lago-deploy#3331, which is the same work.

### Why the Dockerfile lives here

lago-deploy#3331 put this file in the private `lago-deploy` repo, stating:

> Lives here (private lago-deploy) rather than alongside events-processor/Dockerfile in the public lago monorepo so ECR URLs, the AWS account id, and the apko base image references stay out of the OSS-facing surface.

Sound while the bases were in ECR; obsolete now. The bases are public on GHCR, so there is no account id or private registry reference to hide, and pulling them needs no credentials.

### Build logic unchanged

The paired workflow already sets the build context to `events-processor/`, so `COPY . /app/` resolves exactly as before — only the Dockerfile's location and the two `ARG` defaults change. The Rust FFI dependency is still pinned to `LAGO_EXPRESSION_REF=v0.2.0` to match the production `./Dockerfile`; bump both together.

### Companion changes

- getlago/lago-packages publishes `events-processor-base` / `events-processor-build` — both green, public, multi-arch, cosign-signed
- lago-deploy#3331 will be rewritten to build this file instead of its own copy
- getlago/lago-front#4322 is the equivalent change for the front

### Not in this PR

`events-processor/Dockerfile` is untouched and continues to serve production builds.

author: ashish1099
body:
app.kubernetes.io/name is derived from the chart name and settable with nameOverride, so keying discovery on it means a renamed chart — or anyone setting that value — makes the lookup come back empty, which reads exactly like an exporter nobody installed. app.kubernetes.io/component is hard-coded in the chart's labels and no value can change it.

Prefer it, and keep the name label as a fallback for clusters still running a chart that stamps only that one. The Services are then looked up with whichever label found the exporter, so a cluster mid-migration cannot match a Deployment by one and miss its Service by the other.

author: shiyu7
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder SWA bounded replay compacts each request to its late-layer tail, but DP communication still uses the original token counts and gathered IDs. This PR rebuilds that layout so DP attention can run bounded replay, and removes the separate DSpark PD guards that reject DP attention or different prefill/decode attention TP sizes.

Port of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39512 to this repository's `dsv4.1` branch. The Engram integration follows the target branch's current forward path.

## Modifications

- Rebuild token counts and global token IDs at the late-layer boundary, including idle/decode peers participating in the same DP batch.
- Keep attention on local tail rows; apply padding and scoped communication metadata to MoE and Engram, then restore the original metadata. Tail selection excludes existing DP padding.
- Allow DP attention and heterogeneous attention TP sizes for DSpark PD while retaining static verification, Mooncake, CP=1, and matching DSpark block size and target/draft KV layouts. Prefill CUDA graphs remain incompatible with bounded replay.
- Add CPU/Gloo regressions for uneven batches, idle/decode peers, attention TP alignment, model-forward padding, metadata restoration, argument validation, bootstrap validation, and heterogeneous TP rank mapping. Add GPU E2E coverage for bounded replay with DP attention, with and without DSpark.

## Validation

On this port (`353ddbde485c0442cab907a40534008217aede1c`, based on `b83b35b45725c8b409079816c4f7462b8f37309d`):

- `pre-commit` passed for the complete PR diff; `git diff --check` passed.
- `test_dsv41_late_layer_dp.py`: 6 CPU/Gloo tests passed, including four-process collectives and the real decoder-layer forward method with mocked attention/MoE math.
- `test_dsv41_dspark_pd.py`: 3 CPU tests passed.
- Full GPU model inference, GPU E2E tests, and end-to-end PD transfer were not rerun on this port.

## Accuracy Tests

Results reported in the [source PR](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39512), not rerun on this port:

| Evaluation | Sample count | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K | 1,319, single-shot | 96.89% |
| GPQA | 32 examples × 8 repeats | pass@1 (average of 8): 90.62% ± 1.67% (SEM 0.59%); pass@8: 93.75%; majority@8: 90.62% |

Both evaluations reported a 100% stop rate and zero truncation/error rates.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The source PR reports 593 tok/s for GSM8K and 362 tok/s for GPQA. These are evaluation throughput measurements, not a controlled before/after performance comparison. No new speed benchmark was run for this port.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add regression tests and run the CPU/Gloo tests.
- [ ] Update user-facing documentation.
- [ ] Rerun full model accuracy and speed benchmarks on the target branch.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

author: ztongci
body:
## Summary

Hoists \`cloneDeep(feature)\` + \`recursiveJSONParse\` from \`evalExpression\` (once per expression) to \`evalSimpleLayerFeature\` (once per feature). All expressions for a given feature now share one pre-computed parsed copy.

**One file changed:** \`src/mantle/evaluator/simple/index.ts\`

Zero API changes — \`evalExpression\`, \`evalLayerAppearances\`, and \`evalSimpleLayerFeature\` keep the same signatures; the new \`parsedFeature\` param is optional with a fallback to the original path.

## Before vs After (Apple Silicon, vitest v4.1.11)

| Case | Before (ms) | After (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1k  × 5  expr |   6.40 |  2.89 | 2.2× |
| 10k × 5  expr |  66.64 | 29.95 | 2.2× |
| 10k × 10 expr | 117.69 | 38.42 | 3.1× |
| 10k × 15 expr | 175.54 | 46.99 | 3.7× |
| 35k × 10 expr | 417.40 | 138.80 | **3.0×** |

Speedup scales with expression count — higher-expr cases benefit more because more clones are saved per feature.

Full numbers saved in \`perf-results/2026-09-18-after-p1.md\`.

## Why this is safe

- \`recursiveJSONParse\` is idempotent — calling it on already-parsed data is a no-op
- Expressions read from \`parsedFeature\` but do not mutate it — verified by the existing test suite
- The layer-level \`evalLayerAppearances\` call (no \`parsedFeature\` passed) falls back to the original clone path, so the +1 layer-level eval is unchanged

## Test plan

### 1. Unit tests
\`\`\`bash
pnpm test
\`\`\`
All 198 tests pass.

### 2. Benchmark
\`\`\`bash
pnpm bench
\`\`\`
Confirm numbers match the Before vs After table above (±5% is acceptable run-to-run variance).

### 3. Link into visualizer and smoke test

**Build and link core:**
\`\`\`bash
# in this repo (reearth/core)
pnpm build
pnpm link --global
\`\`\`

**Install linked core into visualizer:**
\`\`\`bash
# in reearth/visualizer
pnpm link --global @reearth/core
pnpm dev
\`\`\`

**What to test in the visualizer:**

| Scenario | What to check |
|---|---|
| Add a GeoJSON layer with marker style expressions (pointColor, pointSize, label) | Features render with correct colors and sizes |
| Add 2–3 layers at the same time | All layers render correctly, no missing features |
| Edit a style expression (e.g. change pointColor condition) | Style updates immediately on the map |
| Toggle layer visibility off → on | Layer disappears and reappears correctly |
| Pan and zoom the map while layers are loaded | No visual glitches, features stay in the right positions |
| Open browser DevTools → Performance tab, record 5 seconds while panning | Main thread should be less busy compared to before this PR |

**Pass criteria:** All features render correctly and style expressions produce the same visual output as before this PR. No console errors related to feature evaluation.

author: artui
body:
## Version

0.24.0. Floors only -- no code in this package changes.

## What moves

| Pin | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[drf-mcp]` extra | `djangorestframework-mcp-server>=0.45` | `>=0.46` |
| `[spec-tools]` extra | `djangorestframework-pydantic-ai>=0.29` | `>=0.30` |
| dev group (both, in lockstep) | `>=0.45` / `>=0.29` | `>=0.46` / `>=0.30` |

## Why the two move together

Both siblings turned the same refusal into support in the same hour: a
`ServiceSpec` declaring `many=True` is now a tool that takes its list under one
named argument, where the drf-mcp registry and the PAI toolset each used to
refuse it at build.

So these floors are a pair rather than two independent bumps. Raise one without
the other and the same spec is a working tool on one route and an
`ImproperlyConfigured` on the other -- a disagreement that reads as a defect in
the spec rather than in the versions installed, which is exactly the kind of
mismatch the comment beside each pin now names.

This also withdraws the guidance 0.23.0 gave for such a spec (leave it out, or
declare its list as a named field of an input serializer). A spec reshaped that
way keeps working; it is simply a different tool now.

## The transitive half

Both siblings floor `djangorestframework-services` at 0.53.0, and hard: every
service dispatch passes `many_as_argument`, which first exists there, so below
it a tool call raises `TypeError` rather than failing to resolve. Nothing here
declares drf-services directly, so the extras are where that constraint can be
stated -- which is what the `lowest declared versions` job resolves.

## Why no code changes

The bridge hands drf-mcp's merged `inputSchema` to pydantic-ai verbatim
(`integrations/drf_mcp.py:141`, and the comment at `:107` says so), so a bulk
spec's object-with-one-array-property schema flows through untouched. The new
capability arrives as one more tool in the list, not as a new path here.

author: derekwisong
body:
The first of phase 3's notes about the dataset's *shape* rather than its columns
(#195).

A partition written for a day nothing happened — or a job that produced a header
and no data — is invisible in every other way: it adds no rows, changes no schema,
and moves nothing on screen. But the dataset then has fewer days of data than it
has folders, and anyone counting folders gets the wrong answer.

It costs nothing to know: the footers already report each file's row count, which
is how the dataset is counted at all. `DatasetSchema` keeps the tally.

The note states it without dividing — how many of the files datui read hold
nothing is a fact about those files, and the scope line says which files those
were. On a dataset too large to read every footer it says *"1 footer holds no
rows"*, because datui knows nothing about the ones it did not open.

## Tests

Four shapes added to the notes transcript: one empty file, several, one among
sampled footers (where the noun changes), and one where the empty file is also
the file a column is missing from. Plus a hive folder with a day of no data, end
to end, and its control.

Confirmed to fail without the note. Full workspace suite green; clippy and fmt
clean.

author: fermionic-lyu
body:
Slow build-log requests could consume the CLI's 3-second live-read budget, repeatedly interrupt pagination, and delay deployment status polling. Terminal polling also shared its time budget with the final full scan, so normal API latency could skip that scan and miss delayed output.

Run archive deployment status polling and log reading independently. Status polling retains its 3-second interval; log reading emits and checkpoints each page, waits 3 seconds between completed reads, and gives each HTTP request a 20-second timeout. Cancel and drain the background reader before terminal scans and on every deployment exit. Final scans retain an independent budget of up to 30 seconds, capped by the remaining deployment deadline. HTTP failures and real timeouts remain visible; intentional shutdown does not produce a false failure warning.

Validation:
- Typecheck and all 1,625 tests across 80 files pass.
- Regression coverage includes 4-second pages and a 36-second live scan, status polling during slow reads, 20-second page timeout/resume, cancellation on terminal/error/deadline exits, and bounded final scans with delayed output.
- Read-only production verification retrieved all 60 LIVE, 100 PAGE, and FINAL markers from a retained build with no warnings, including 150 ms of injected client latency. No production configuration or resources changed.

This change is confined to CLI log retrieval and presentation; service-side build scheduling and deployment orchestration are unchanged.

author: yradex
body:
Element Template hydration builds per-slot matching tables and reparses each background node's template identity even when the main-thread and background trees already have the same structure. This adds repeated allocations and string work to initial hydration.

Check the complete child-slot identity sequence before constructing the diff structures. When lengths and normalized identities match pairwise, hydrate those pairs directly through the existing recursive path. For example, `[A, B, A] -> [A, B, A]` produces the same FIFO matches as the full matcher, including duplicate identities. Attribute differences and descendant changes are still reconciled. A mismatch falls back before any node in that slot is hydrated; bundle identity, slot boundaries, and typed-list child reconciliation retain their existing rules.

Cache background template identities by the full type string during each synchronous root hydration pass, and clear the cache in `finally` on completion or failure.

For the existing `007-four-layer-views` workload, local interleaved measurements reduced the hydrate span from 27.73 ms to 20.27 ms (26.9%, 20 measured rounds per variant). Linux Callgrind instruction counts decreased from 353.91 M to 247.33 M (30.1%). These measurements cover the hydrate workload, not device first-frame presentation. A same-length slot with a late identity mismatch incurs a preflight scan before the original matcher; its performance has not yet been measured.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests updated (or not required): ET hydration tests cover matching, attributes, bundle identities, slot boundaries, reordering, and typed lists; the matched-child failure case now exercises both pairwise and fallback paths.
- [x] Documentation updated (or not required): no public API or hydration protocol changes.
- [x] Changeset added, and when a BREAKING CHANGE occurs, it needs to be clearly marked (or not required): ET-only optimization in the private runtime package.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## What users saw
In the installed PWA (iPhone; Android shows the same symptom) an **empty, dark navy band** sat at the very bottom of the screen: the map tiles stopped above it and nothing was painted inside it — the "bottom padding / bottom bar".

## Why
`#map-section` computed its height from the `vh → --vh → svh → dvh` ladder. iOS standalone settles those numbers **one frame late** (and on some versions the dynamic viewport excludes the home-indicator band), so the section could stay shorter than the real screen while Leaflet kept the stale size — the page background (`#060E1E`) then showed through as the band.

## Fix
- `body.is-pwa #map-section` now **stretches** between the viewport edges (`position: fixed; top:0; right:0; bottom:0; left:0; height:auto`) — exact on every engine, no fallback ladder, no gap.
- `updatePwaMapLayout()` also runs on `load` / `pageshow`, twice inside the iOS settle window (800 ms / 1600 ms), and from a `ResizeObserver` on `#map-section` / `.map-frame` / `#detectlab-map`, so Leaflet's `invalidateSize` fires the exact frame the container reaches its true height.
- **No control moves**: the floating right stack (`bottom: calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 28px)`), the compass column (`.leaflet-bottom`) and the published `--pwa-bottom-controls-clearance` keep their exact offsets — only the map canvas is re-measured.
- SW cache bumped `v108 → v109` so installed PWAs pick the fix up on next launch.
- New browser-free regression test `test-pwa-no-bottom-strip.js` (passes; full suite unchanged — `test-gmaps-directions.js` and `test-premium-subscription.js` already failed at HEAD for unrelated reasons: stale v106-era expectations and a missing `jsdom` dependency).

author: virtuoes
body:
## Was drin ist

Zwei neue Ordner unter `docs/arc42/`, je eine Datei pro Eintrag — und **drei Korrekturen
an Aussagen, die beim Nachmessen nicht hielten**.

| Ordner | Inhalt | Eintrittskarte |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `review/` | Befunde aus der Durchsicht — wo der gebaute Stand von dem abweicht, was er sein sollte | eine **Messung** |
| `ideen/` | kurze Einträge zu Gedanken, die noch nicht entschieden sind | die Frage „wäre das besser?" |

## Keine zweite Offen-Liste

`CLAUDE.md` Regel 4 ist eindeutig: Alles Offene steht **nur** in `OFFEN.md`. Die Ordner
treten nicht daneben, sondern davor — die Abgrenzung steht in beiden README:

- `ideen/` = noch **nicht** entschieden. Angenommen → nach `OFFEN.md`, Eintrag hier
  gelöscht. Verworfen → ebenfalls gelöscht, Begründung in der Commit-Nachricht.
- `review/` = Befund mit Beleg. Wird er Arbeit → `OFFEN.md`. Wiederkehrende Fehlerart →
  zusätzlich `sweeps.md`, mit Detektor.
- Ein Befund an der **Dokumentation** wird nicht verwaltet, sondern sofort korrigiert.

## Die drei korrigierten Aussagen

**1. „Die Anfrage-Logzeile trägt Status und Dauer."** (Kapitel 5 und 8)
Gemessen: Je Anfrage werden **Methode und Pfad** geschrieben; den **Status** schreibt
`LoggingMiddleware` ausschließlich `if recorder.status >= 500`; eine **Dauer** wird
nirgends erhoben. Der Kommentar über `LoggingMiddleware` selbst behauptet dasselbe
Falsche — das wäre eine Codeänderung und steht als offener Punkt in `review/001`.

**2. „Gesichert wird nur die Datenbank" — ohne zu sagen, was das für den Restore heißt.**
Die `.env` liegt in **keiner** Sicherung. `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` schließt die Sicherung
auf und steht nur auf dem Host, der im Ernstfall weg ist — eine Ringabhängigkeit. Zweite
Stufe: Mit dem Backup-, aber ohne den `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` **gelingt** der Restore und
sieht wie ein Erfolg aus, während `schueler_fotos.foto_encrypted` und das gespeicherte
SMTP-Passwort für immer Chiffrat bleiben. Das ist der gefährlichere Fall.

**3. „Cover sind reproduzierbar."** (`DEPLOYMENT.md`, arc42 7.7)
`inventur/upload_handler.go`, `handleUploadCover` nimmt Bilddateien **von Hand** entgegen;
die kommen aus keiner externen Quelle zurück. Das empfohlene Zurücksetzen auf
`cover_status='PENDING'` trifft sie mit und lädt an ihrer Stelle ein fremdes Cover — oder
bei einem Titel ohne ISBN gar keins.

## Neu: der Weg zurück nach einem Totalverlust

`resilience_and_recovery.md` beschrieb bis jetzt nur den **Datenbank**-Restore. Abschnitt
**2f** ergänzt den Host: was vorher bereitliegen muss, acht Schritte, und die Gegenprobe am
Ende — ein angezeigtes Schülerfoto beweist, dass der `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` der richtige ist.

Ausdrücklich vermerkt: **am Code hergeleitet, an fremder Hardware nicht erprobt**
(`OFFEN.md` 7.4). Inklusive der Henne-Ei-Note — `restore-backup` liegt *im* Image, das man
erst bauen muss; der Build braucht aber keine Datenbank.

## Die Einträge

| Nr. | Eintrag | Kern |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `review/001` | Nach einem Vorfall ist nichts nachzusehen | Keine Anfragekennung (grep über den Go-Code: kein Treffer), kein Tracing, keine Metriken, 3 × 10 MB Aufbewahrung |
| `review/002` | Umfang gegen Anwendungsfall | 65.883 Zeilen für ~1.900 Leser — aber ein Dutzend Regelwerke aus fremder Vorgabe. Wahr ist: `api/` trägt 42 % und darin auch Fachlogik |
| `review/003` | Der Restore endet an der `.env` | Die Messung zu Korrektur 2 und 3; zwei Punkte erledigt, die Entscheidung zum zweiten Ort offen |
| `ideen/001` | Anmeldung über einen Identitätsanbieter | Die Anwendung **sieht** das Passwort im Klartext (IMAP-Bind). Nächster Schritt ist eine Frage an den Träger, keine Zeile Code |
| `ideen/002` | Einmal-Link per Mail | Als zweiter Weg fürs Kollegium denkbar, an der Theke untauglich |
| `ideen/003` | Was könnte weg? | Streichliste mit Kandidaten und der Regel, vorher eine Nutzungszahl zu besorgen |
| `ideen/004` | Vergleich mit OpenLibry und OpenBiblio | Sieben Achsen. Über beide Systeme steht dort **nichts als ihre Namen** |
| `ideen/005` | Log und Trace ohne ein neues Bauteil | Netto **ein Bauteil weniger**; 340 `log.Printf` ohne Kontext und **0** `slog.*Context` schließen den naheliegenden Weg aus |
| `ideen/006` | Zweiter Ort ohne S3 | `rsync` oder getauschte externe Platte statt Vertragsfrage; die Offline-Kopie überlebt zusätzlich einen Verschlüsselungstrojaner |

## Gate-Lücke, die beide README benennen

`docs/stand_angaben_test.go` sammelt über `*.md` und `*/*.md` unterhalb von `docs/`. Die
Dateien in diesen Ordnern liegen **eine Ebene tiefer** und werden nicht geprüft. Steht so
in beiden README, damit niemand einen Schutz annimmt, den es nicht gibt.

## Prüfung

```
go test -count=1 ./docs/   ok
go test ./db/              ok
```

Alle relativen Links auflösbar, `Stand:`-Zeilen der geänderten Kapitel gezogen, kein Datum
jenseits des Kopfes. `main` ist eingemergt, keine Konflikte. Markdown unter `docs/` ist im
Projekt nicht prettier-formatiert (CI prüft `frontend/src` und `e2e`).

**Keine Go-, SQL-, Svelte- oder Konfigurationsdatei berührt.**

author: apeloff1
body: ## Summary Privileged `workflow_run` consumers now subscribe to **every completing head**, including slashed feature branches, and evaluate, drain, or record **all** trusted PRs associated with that completion. GitHub often leaves `workflow_run.pull_requests` empty or capped, and list endpoints are paginated. Previous automation/drain paths treated `pull_requests[0]` as identity or stopped at the first page, so feature-branch completions could be dropped or attributed to the wrong PR. ## Changes - Match `*` and `**` on `workflow_run` for PR automation, repair intake, obsolete-run drain, and idle studio so non-default heads are delivered. - Resolve PR identity from immutable `head_sha` + `head_ref`. - Consume the complete `pull_requests[].number` array as JSON hints; `pull_requests[0]` is no longer treated as identity. - Evaluate and drain every same-repository PR whose head matches the completing branch and whose base is allowed. - Paginate `/commits/{sha}/pulls`, live Actions run listings, PR commit listings, and Idle Studio run/issue/PR snapshots; exhausted identity scans fail closed instead of truncating. - Canonicalize `workflow_run.head_sha` and live PR head SHAs as 40-hex commit OIDs before API lookup, default-branch open-PR sweep, drain environment context, repair fingerprinting, check-run/status fetches, drain membership, sweep classification, and Idle Studio git object lookups. Abbreviated, whitespace-padded, and non-hex values fail closed. - Drain commit-PR association HTTP errors abort instead of treating the run as unlinked. Sweep aborts on truncated association scans rather than preserving an unclassified prefix. - Gate-status publish quotes a canonical commit OID; runtime error reporting skips malformed live head SHAs instead of posting to an abbreviated URL. - Idle Studio rejects cross-repository `workflow_run` heads and validates the trusted snapshot base SHA as a 40-hex OID. - Repair intake fails closed without SHA/branch identity, records every associated PR hint, and fails closed when fingerprint search is capped. - Default-branch completions still sweep recently updated open PRs; feature-branch completions no longer fall back to that unrelated set. - Add a fail-closed `check_workflow_run_branch_completions.py` gate covering automation, drain, repair-intake, idle-studio, and sweep identity. Backend Quality now runs the drain identity tests. ## Safety - Privileged workflows still load from the trusted default branch. - Fork heads, disallowed bases, incomplete identity, malformed hint JSON, malformed head SHAs, truncated live snapshots, association HTTP errors, and exhausted pagination fail closed. - Event/input context still crosses the shell boundary through environment variables. ## Testing - Focused pytest cases covering resolver identity, JSON hint parsing, multi-PR drain, paged commit/run association, 40-hex SHA canonicalization, association HTTP fail-closed, quoted status URLs, idle snapshot/git OID bounds, workflow contracts, and existing PR automation policy. - Merge-readiness, quality-gate parity, workflow security, and workflow input-security gates passed locally.

author: aliyazji
body:
## Summary

Seven fixes/changes before Phase 0 can merge, each with a regression test that fails against the pre-fix code and passes against the fix (where applicable).

- **fix(reports)** — `trial_balance()`/`income_statement()`/`balance_sheet()`/`UNCLOSED` plus helpers `account_balance()`, `chart_of_accounts_balances()`, `account_ledger()`: exact to real `entry_date`, correctly treat voided entries as historically real (`status IN ('posted','void')`, entry_date decides scope — a later void never retroactively changes an already-published historical report). `chart_of_accounts_balances()` restructured as a pre-aggregated CTE after EXPLAIN ANALYZE caught a ~675ms/107k-buffer regression from its pre-existing per-account correlated-subquery shape now scanning transaction-level data — a plain index was tried and empirically didn't help, so the query was restructured instead (~8ms/1.2k buffers, ~85x faster, identical output). Landed across `20250911004100`–`20250911004500`.
- **fix(security)** — `journal_entries`' RLS `je_write` policy was one `FOR ALL` gated only on `gl.create`, with no awareness of `status`: a member holding `gl.create` alone could bypass `post_journal_entry()`/`void_journal_entry()` via a direct `UPDATE`, including `posted -> void` with no real reversal ever created (silently invisible now that reports count void entries). Split into `je_insert`/`je_update`/`je_delete`, each keyed on `status = 'draft'` on both sides of any direct write — every real transition is now only reachable through the two RPCs (`SECURITY DEFINER`, unaffected by RLS). `20250911004600`.
- **fix(pos)** — Cashier now shows composite items (previously invisible/unsellable); a cash sale requires an open shift on the selected register. No costing-logic or voucher-module changes.
- **fix(onboarding)** — `create_organization()` rejects unimplemented sector templates outright instead of silently falling back to the restaurant/hotel chart.
- **fix(cash-shifts)** — `open_cash_shift()`/`close_cash_shift()` carry the same explicit grant/revoke every other write-RPC has.
- **chore(ci)** — Node runtime 20 → 22 for the web/ETL CI jobs, `engines.node >=22` on both `package.json`s, `.nvmrc` (root + `web/`) — `@supabase/supabase-js` and the Azure SDK packages ETL's `mssql` pulls in both declare `engines.node >=22.0.0` (confirmed by reading the installed packages, not just asserted). No dependency upgrades.

No old (already-shipped) migration was modified. No pharmacy/supermarket/sector work, no composite-item costing changes, no new voucher module, no `is_contra`/`normal_balance`/`accounts.nature` changes, no UI redesign, no dependency upgrades or `--force`, no changes to `00e3f2b`'s reporting fix, no Wasmer/Supabase Cloud changes.

## Known, deliberately out-of-scope findings (documented, not fixed here)

author: bogdaniel
body:
Closes #238.

## Root cause

A provider subprocess being alive was the only evidence the runtime had that engineering work was happening.

`run-07b3a0390329eb86beb9bdf3d0ed6342` consumed **8h55m16s of active-work budget with 0s of external wait** and terminalized as `run_wall_budget_exhausted`. The laptop had no network for most of that interval. The Codex process stayed alive and silent, and every minute of that silence was charged to the budget that exists to bound real work — so the run-wide wall budget, which is the outer safety ceiling, was acting as the stall detector, nine hours late.

The gap was structural, in three places:

1. **Nothing observed silence.** One invocation is one blocking call into `CommandExecutor.Run`, which hands back a `CommandOutput` only once the process has already exited. Between `CLIAgentProvider.Execute` and the operation deadline there was no point at which a provider that had stopped moving looked different from one that was thinking.
2. **The no-progress machinery was never wired.** `RunOperation.NoProgressBudget`, `NoProgressExceeded` and `Scheduler.Heartbeat` all existed; `NoProgressBudget` was never set by any caller, `Heartbeat` was never called outside a store test, and `BudgetState` — the only reader — was never called at all. "No progress" had no observation behind it.
3. **A restart refunded the window.** (Found by review of `8cbb1f2`, fixed in `96cf4dd`.) `Start` stamped `LastProgressAt = now` unconditionally, and that is exactly the datum the remaining window is computed from — so every reclaimed operation began with a fresh full window. Charging the orphaned interval to `ConsumedExecution` proves the *wall* budget did not reset; it is a different authority and was standing in for a proof it cannot give.
4. **Connectivity had no class.** An explicit transport diagnostic fell to `FailureUnknown` → `RouteStop`, and silence produced no diagnostic at all.

## Implementation

A third bound beside the run's active-work budget and the operation's total wall bound:

```
provider invocation
  ├─ output arrives            → refresh the inactivity window
  ├─ explicit transport error  → provider_unavailable, bounded external wait
  ├─ recognized quota          → unchanged
  └─ nothing for the window    → terminate the process group,
                                 provider_no_progress, bounded retry
```

**Enforcement lives where output arrives.** `boundedBuffer.Write` is the one place a running child's bytes are observed, so the inactivity watch is fed from there and armed inside `OSCommandExecutor.Run`. Reaching the window cancels the invocation's context with `ErrProviderInactive` as the *cause*, which runs the **same** graceful-then-forced process-group stop a deadline already runs — no second way to end a child, no second scheduler.

**The cause is why the adapter can still tell three things apart.** Through `ctx.Err()` alone, an inactivity kill, a supervisor drain and a deadline are one answer; `context.Cause` keeps them three. A stall is not a deadline (the operation still had authority), not a shutdown (the controller is fine), and not unknown.

**Progress is bytes on stdout/stderr.** Deliberately *not* the process existing, not a lease heartbeat, not a clock tick. Observed progress is written durably through a new narrow `Scheduler.RecordProviderProgress` — never through the lease heartbeat, because a controller being alive is a different claim from the work moving, and #238 is the cost of letting the first stand in for the second. Durable writes are throttled to a quarter of the window.

**The budget.** `budgets.provider_inactivity_seconds`, persisted in `RunBudgets`, narrowing the configured bound exactly as `WallLimit` does, tighten-only from `.zenchron.json`, and finite always. There is no spelling that disables it: an explicit `0` reads as absent and resolves to the default, a negative value is refused. Default **600s**, justified from this repository's own conventions — a third of the documented 1800s wall limit, ten times the 60s watch interval, long enough for a CLI to reason or run a slow test inside one invocation, and already this repo's bound for "a bounded operation that has produced nothing is stuck".

**Silence is never classified as offline.** Only a provider that *names* its transport failure becomes `provider_unavailable`: Codex's reqwest vocabulary (`dns error`, `error sending request`, …), the libuv/undici errno tokens the three Node CLIs emit (`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`, `ECONNREFUSED`, …), and HTTP's own gateway statuses. `ETIMEDOUT` and undici's bare `fetch failed` are deliberately excluded as ambiguous. Unavailable waits under the existing #83/#229/#232 accounting — a host with no network is not working — while silence becomes `provider_no_progress`, a runtime bound reached, charged exactly as execution is.

**The planner path is bounded too.** Arming happens inside `CLIAgentProvider.Execute` from `ProviderBudget.InactivityLimit`, so the producer path and the planner path cannot drift. The planner is the stage that needed it most: it runs unattended in a read-only mode against the same CLIs.

**A restart does not refund the window.** `Scheduler.Start` distinguishes two durable shapes, and the distinction is the whole of acceptance 10:

| | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **abandoned** | `ActiveSince` still set at the next `Start` | nobody finished this attempt and nothing observed how it ended, so the successor **inherits** the progress datum: 4m of proven silence leaves 6m, not 10m |
| **settled** | `Finish` ran, outcome journalled and classified | a stall is `provider_no_progress` → **bounded retry**, and a retry that inherited an exhausted window would refuse before dispatch forever, so it resets; the attempt ceiling is what ends it |

Without the second row the repair is self-perpetuating: one long reclaim gap exhausts the window, every successor refuses without calling the provider, and the run dies of attempt exhaustion having dispatched nothing.

`NoProgressKey` is cleared per physical attempt — the other side of the same distinction. It is a cumulative byte count of *one* process's output; carried forward, a successor's first bytes would be compared against a dead process's total and read as "nothing new". The **fingerprint** is per-attempt state; the **datum** is authority for the logical operation.

**Nothing resets.** A stall is not continuation-eligible, inherits no prior observations, refunds no attempt or execution budget, and its retry takes a fresh attempt identity under #236/#237 with the previous transcript byte-identical and still un-overwritable. `execution.completed` is not journalled, so no candidate success is inferred from partial output.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `runtime/provider_inactivity.go` | **new** — the policy, the context carrier, the per-process watch, the remaining-window arithmetic, the justified default |
| `runtime/sandbox.go` | `boundedBuffer.observe`; `OSCommandExecutor.Run` arms the watch |
| `runtime/cli_agent.go` | arms the bound for every caller; classifies the stall; records the window in provenance |
| `runtime/adapters.go` | `ProviderBudget.InactivityLimit`; `FailureProviderNoProgress` → retry; `FailureProviderUnavailable` → wait |
| `runtime/agent_specs.go` | per-provider connectivity `diagnosticSignal`s; shared gateway statuses |
| `runtime/reconciler.go` | wait reason + external-wait accounting; persisted window narrows the configured one |
| `runtime/operations.go` | derives the remaining window from durable state; supplies the progress recorder; refuses an exhausted window rather than dispatching unbounded |
| `runtime/scheduler.go` | `RecordProviderProgress` |
| `runtime/controller.go` | `RunBudgets.ProviderInactivityLimit` + default; `OperationStatus` progress fields |
| `runtime/config.go` | config member, resolution, validation, tighten-only |
| `runtime/supervisor.go` | the planner invocation carries the

author: whitelotus1998
body:
Closes #99, the follow-up DECISIONS/0018 deferred from issue 9.

## Decided

- **`Attack(unit, target, slot?)`.** The slot names the weapon to strike with. `Resolver.ChooseWeapon` validates it (`EmptySlot` out of range; `NotUsable` naming the reason: an item, a healing spell, a spell spent for this battle, or a weapon the class cannot use) and `BattleUnit.WithSlotInFront` moves it to slot 0 before the combat, so durability comes off that weapon and the counter on the enemy phase uses it. A `WeaponEquipped` event fires only when the front changed; naming the equipped slot is the same as naming none, and a test shows the canonical states equal.
- **The forecast takes the slot** (`Queries.Forecast(..., slot)`), built from the same reordered unit the resolver would fight with, so `forecast <unit> <target> [slot]` in the CLI shows the chosen weapon's numbers and `attack <unit> <target> [slot]` prints that forecast first. A bad slot prints the resolver's own rejection message.
- **`Legal` names slots only when there is a choice.** A unit with one usable weapon gets slot-less attacks, so every existing script and gate stream replays unchanged (the journaled winning script still wins); a unit with two gets one attack per usable slot per target. Gates 6 and 8 cover the choice on any roster that carries two weapons; the synthetic cadets carry one, so today only the tests exercise it.
- **The enemy planner keeps its first slot.** Section 8's scorer prices the equipped weapon; a planner that prices every slot is a separate line once a template carries a real choice.

## Unsure

- Whether the reorder should be visible as a persistent inventory change (it is: the chosen weapon stays at the front for the rest of the map, and `show` lists it first) or whether the slots should keep their authored order with an "equipped" marker. The reorder is the simpler state and it is what 0018 described; say if the between-map screen (#74) wants stable slots.

## Next

Issue 12 (Sim harness and gates) has its review-before-building comment posted this run; the next Builder run starts it there. Then 13.

author: snymrova
body:
Answers the four open questions in `docs/RESEARCH-PROWLER-INGEST.md` §9 that P3-1 and P3-3 depend on, taken before P3-0 because the one the note called most important could have rewritten the design. It did not; it cost a build item.

**The answer is no.** Prowler serialises its own command line exactly once in the codebase — `prowler_args = " ".join(sys.argv[1:])` at `__main__.py:646`, into a Slack message — and no output file records it. The compliance OCSF array has no header: no scan id, no arguments, no mutelist, no start/end pair. `--status` drops findings inside `execute_checks` (`check.py:754-760`) before any writer exists. A `--status PASS` scan and a clean scan are the same document.

**The constructive half**, new build item P3-3a: the pinned framework names the AWS checks each KSI expects, the file names the ones that reported, so `reported / mapped` is computable per KSI. It is a real defence — hiding a FAIL removes that check from the reported set unless the same check passed on another resource, a narrow residual that can be named rather than assumed.

**Three corrections**, from reading the writer rather than the table:

- §2d documents the **CSV** row; the adapter reads **OCSF**, where `Status`, `CheckId`, `Requirements_Id` and `Muted` do not exist. §10a is the field table. Muted is `status == "Suppressed"`; a `MANUAL` row is a different constructor with no `compliance.checks` and no `resources`.
- A scan's own config can force a requirement to `FAIL` while the nested check still reads `PASS` — upstream publishes a stable marker for it on purpose — so rampscan evaluates the effective `status_code`, the stricter of the two readings.
- Zero findings means **no file at all**, not an empty one, and no thirteen `MANUAL` rows either. A missing document is a refusal.

**Computed:** the P3-0 pin (`1b228d59`, sha256 `cc1a5fa8…`, 89,892 bytes, `framework` `FedRAMP-20x-KSI`, `version` `2026.07.14.01`), and that **no published Prowler release ships this framework** — 5.42.0 predates its only commit by three days — which qualifies §8's public claim to `master`.

Docs only, no code. §9's items are struck through where answered rather than edited into hindsight; the header count is four of six, not five, because two stay open.

author: alexander-bain
body:
**Pillar TRUTH.** Declares #6614; this push closes it.
**Tier A** — frontend-only, no data writes, no migrations, no env. jkl=A(d): labels/layouts, no cert.

## What a reader gets back

`/events/15298749` — Torreense @ Lillestrom, Europa League, **final 1–2**. Torreense **won as a 21% underdog** and the settled hero printed no pregame mark at all. Photographed at 390×844 before the fix: `artifacts/ux-1330/BEFORE-6614-15298749-390.png`.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| settled hero, away winner | *(nothing)* | **Upset · 21% pregame** |
| live non-complement card | `Opened 32%` | `Opened 32% – 40%` |
| complement pair (16/25) | withheld | **withheld, unchanged** |

## Why the sport was the wrong question

#6238 taught this page to withhold the away figure wherever the sport prices a draw, because `current_odds.away_probability` is derived as `1 - home` — "the home team does not win", away win **or** draw. Correct for that pair; it was applied to both.

`opening_odds` is not that pair. Since #1011 it is de-vigged across the whole quoted board, so `home + away ≈ 0.76` and the missing ~0.24 **is** the draw. Both legs are real, independently sourced prices.

**Re-taken on production 2026-09-18 ~08:58Z** (the filed 2026-09-16 population, re-measured on a fresh slate), `/api/feed?mode=sports`, 25 soccer cards:

| pair | sums to 1.0000 | sums to 0.72 – 0.84 |
|---|---|---|
| `current_odds` | **25 / 25** | 0 |
| `opening_odds` | 16 / 25 | **9 / 25** |

Both arms are live traffic, so a blanket flip in either direction is wrong. The two opening values and the `Opened` separator now ask `awayIsTheComplement` about **their own pair**; the hero's current pair keeps the blanket rule.

## Scope held deliberately

`settledWinnerPregameProb` is **not touched**. Its existing `openingHomeProb !== null && openingAwayProb !== null` gate passes by itself once the away value survives, because a non-complement pair has two real legs. Loosening it would newly print a mark on the 16/25 complement pages — a population this issue never reasoned about, and one where the number still *is* the complement.

Acceptance item 4 checked: the other four `awayWithheld` sites (hero pair, chart, chart readout, fullscreen chart) are all the **current** pair and correctly unchanged.

## Guards — and one removed on purpose

New suite renders the **real page** against the **production payloads**, both arms on one sport plus a two-way control. Six mutants killed:

| mutant | result |
|---|---|
| opening values back to `printableAway` | ✅ killed |
| render gate back to `awaySlotWithheld` | ✅ killed |
| rule never withholds | ✅ killed |
| rule always withholds (pre-fix behaviour) | ✅ killed |
| **predicate fed the 0–100 percent pair** instead of the 0–1 prob pair | ✅ killed |
| `sportPricesADraw` forced true (two-way control) | ✅ killed |

🪤 A "current away is still withheld" control was written and **removed**, because three mutants proved it could not fail — `resolveProbability` hands this page a null `servedAwayProb`, so nothing downstream can put that figure on the page and `not.toContain(…)` was passing on a number that never renders. The reason is recorded in the suite where the next person will look for it. A control that cannot fail advertises a protection that is not there.

#6238's source-scan guard is **narrowed from four values to two** by the same measurement, not relaxed: its refusal of a raw served value reaching a render is intact on both pairs, and a mutant that moves the current pair off `printableAway` still reddens it.

## Gates (this exact sha)

- `npm run build` (ESLint gate) — **exit 0**
- `npm run typecheck` (TS gate) — **exit 0**, `70 (baseline 70)`, no new errors
- Focused: `aRealOpeningAwayPriceSurvivesOnADrawPricedSport6614` + `aDrawIsNotTheAwayTeamOnWeb6238` — 36/36
- Neighbours (`drawPricedCardFamily6238`, `eventHeroDuelInvariant`, `openedPairCapture`, `venueSettledHero6381`, `liveProjectionNeedsAScore5697`, `finishedGameStopsSayingWhereToWatch5741`) — 135/135

Notice 48 N/A — no `HEAVY_TASKS` module touched, frontend only.
After-LOOK on the production page owed once merged and deployed.

| #477–#486 `contradictory-type-checks` | `ReconciliationService` | Removed the five unreachable `else if (… instanceof ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor)` branches — it *is* a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, so the first branch always wins. |

author: joshiag1106
body:
Removes the 5-analysis cap while the product is not yet charging anyone, without deleting the metering machinery — this will need to come back before commercial launch.

### The design

One flag, `QUOTA_ENFORCED` in `lib/quota`, default `false`. `consume()` only blocks when it is `true`, so re-enabling before launch is that single line — nothing else in the file, and no page that reads `quotaState()`, needs to change.

A second flag, `previewUnlimited`, is kept deliberately **distinct** from `unlimited`. `unlimited` means a paid Pro plan everywhere it is read — the pricing page's `current`/`active` badges, the "You're on Pro" panel, the account page's plan label, the "Cancel Pro" button. Folding the free-preview state into that flag would make all of those say **Pro** to a visitor who has never paid anything, which defeats the point of a pricing page that still needs to sell Pro once launch happens.

### What changed downstream

Ten call sites updated to read `previewUnlimited` alongside `unlimited`:

- The nav badge now says **"Free preview"** rather than a stale `X/5` count or a false "Pro".
- The five near-identical "Y of Z remaining" nudges on the dyad, person, network, events and country pages are suppressed — nothing true is left to say while nothing is capped.
- The account page's "Remaining" stat no longer turns red and shows `0` once usage passes five, which it would have kept doing forever with nothing actually blocked.
- The pricing page's free-tier card says what is true — "Free while Kautilya is in preview" — with its feature list built at request time instead of module load, so the "deep analyses" bullet can say "Unlimited, for now" instead of a number that is no longer real.

### Verification

477 tests, `tsc --noEmit` clean. Verified against the deployed site before this PR was opened: eight distinct country profiles opened in one session with none paywalled (well past the old cap of 5), nav reads "Free preview", the old remaining-count text is gone from a gated page, and pricing correctly shows Analyst as "current" without claiming Pro.

author: lohnn
body:
## Summary

Completes the hive-board subport: **`/awaken` now registers a work item** for the awakened coordinator, and **`hive_dream_complete` promotes the owning session's item to done** — on the same `.opencode/board/` store the OpenCode-era harness already uses, byte-compatible and dual-run-safe (no migration, no fork).

Sequel to #33 (the `/awaken` gate): this PR adds the `@hive/dsh-board` package and wires the two seams. It contains exactly the six board slices plus the capstone verification; the awaken arc itself is already on main via #33 (the branch was rebuilt on top of it — adopted cleanly, zero conflicts, which is also a checksum-style proof that the squashed merge matched the working base bit-for-bit).

## The two seams

- **Awaken seam** (`packages/evolution/src/index.ts`, full-flip step 4 — the junction left as a stub by #33): guarded `autoRegister(directory, sessionId, sessionId, title)` — depth>0 belt-and-braces guard; group_id := self (dsh has no session groups); title = raw `/awaken` input else `Session <id>`; `try/catch → log.warn` — **the flip never fails on board trouble**. The outcome note rides both surfaces: the awaken brief (`### Board` block — the only model-visible channel, since dsh commands are model-invisible) and the command's returned text.
- **Done seam** (`packages/tools/src/index.ts`, in `hive_dream_complete`): `resolveCaller(exec)` → `markItemDoneFromDream(boardDirectory, sessionID, dreamId)` with the original promo lines and logging discipline; **board failure never fails the dream**; no-owner stays silent; pre-compaction dreams close nothing (zero new transitions — W-126). Both stale "board promotion hook is omitted" comments updated to truth.

## Design decisions (settled in the arc's decision log)

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D1 | Vertical lifecycle slice: 8 of 9 model tools + byte-identical module core (`board-store`/`board-transitions`/`board-read`/`invariants`/`recency`) + both seams. Non-goals: viewer, OpenChamber reconciler, `workspace_map`, live `todo_mirror` mirroring, title back-fill (recorded behavioral delta — dsh exposes no session title) |
| D2 | Keep formats byte-compatible; read/write the live store in place; `directory` stays the profile-level fixed root |
| D3 | New `@hive/board` package; `tools` and `evolution` both depend on it (acyclic) |
| D4 | `owner_session` = dsh session id; eligibility read from the **existing** awaken ledger (`hive-sessions.json` — no second registry to drift) |
| D5 | Awakened top-level coordinators own; children read/propose only; **done only from the owner's own dream completion**; owned items refuse foreign respec (outcomes land in fresh items) |
| D6 | Direct call paths, no events, no summons (a summon the model can skip would break the 1:1 invariant) |
| D7 | Advisory board-wide lock verbatim (its threat model is dual-run co-tenancy with the still-usable OpenCode writer) |
| D8 | Same `hive_board_*` names; joined the single `HIVE_TOOL_NAMES` const (19→27); tool-gate-sync guard covers them |
| H1 | **`hive_board_start` deliberately NOT shipped** — dsh cannot mint top-level sessions; `startItem`/`promoteItem` remain module-resident, compiled, tested, uncalled |

## Verification

- `pnpm -r typecheck` and `pnpm -r test` green (board: **244/244** — full 1:1 ports of the OpenCode bun suites to node:test, incl. the entire `markItemDoneFromDream` decision matrix: noop-no-owner / pre-compaction skip / DRM_NOT_COMPLETE / done / already-done / redefined / NOT_IN_PROGRESS; authoring refusal classes; absorption matrix; read rank/budget/⚠-marker renders with the no-verdict/no-threshold divider test).
- Per-slice **live-boot gates** in a fake `DSH_HOME`: plugin load proven by full-profile headless boots; the denied-catalog negative captured from decoded `session.v3.jsonl.zstd` — one real session showing **24 tools/0 hive while dormant** (restrict-stripped, not denied) → **51 tools/27 hive/8 board while awakened**.
- DefineTool notes: dsh *does* validate declared params (unlike OpenCode) — the WI-065 runtime hardening remains load-bearing for the schema-open root (forbidden keys refused by name).
- End-to-end capstone on a fresh fixture board (60 real-format items, live store untouched): handler-driven flip → `WI-062` registered session-first → one model turn running `hive_board_search` → `hive_board_read` → `hive_board_respec` → owner's dream close. Final item file: `status: done`, `dream_id` stamped, artifacts mirrored from the authoritative DRM file, and three transitions telling the whole story: `hive_awaken` → `hive_board_respec:<session>` → `board:dream-complete:DRM-001`. Bonus finding en route: the board **refused a foreign session's respec live** and the model reported the ownership rule back — the invariants held on-line.

## Install / rollout note

This ships code + tests into the monorepo only. Making it live in a running harness (profile kit refresh + `dsh web` restart, web stopped first) is deliberately a separate, user-attended step. Until then, new sessions on the old kit behave exactly as before.

author: sylwiaszunejko
body:
Only last 6 commits matter to be rebased after https://github.com/scylladb/gocql/pull/1090 is merged.

Fixes: https://github.com/scylladb/gocql/issues/1095

## Commits

**`stop table properties from injecting CQL`** — both option renderers built a
CQL value by marshalling to JSON and rewriting its double quotes, or by running
that rewrite over an already-escaped string. A comment of
`x" AND gc_grace_seconds = 0 AND comment = "y` left `ToCQL` as three
properties, two of them forged, with no error. JSON has the mirror problem: it
writes an embedded `"` as `\"` and leaves `'` alone, so one reaches CQL as a
backslash escape the grammar lacks and the other closes its string. Both now
render CQL directly; `fixQuote` is deleted.

**`bounds-check the encryption options blob`** — `UnmarshalBinary` read every
length field unchecked, so a short or truncated server blob panicked on a slice
bound. The entry count is also checked before it sizes the map: a blob claiming
`1<<30` entries asked `make` for about a gigabyte.

**`don't panic on a non-[]byte table extension`** — `blob.([]byte)` without the
comma-ok form, on a value from the exported `Extensions` map.

**`strip frozen only when it wraps the type`** — the two trims in `stripFrozen`
were independent, so `stripFrozen("map<text, int>")` was `map<text, int`.

**`report a value escape cannot render`** — `escape` returned `""` for any
unhandled type, so the caller wrote `'replication_factor': ` and nothing else.
It now errors, and handles the integer and float widths that reach it through
`StrategyOptions`.

**`quote identifiers that need quoting`** — every name was interpolated raw, so
a UDT created as `"z-type"` dumped as `CREATE TYPE ks.z-type (`. Two quieter
cases: a name with upper case dumps bare and the server folds it, so `MyTable`
comes back as a *different* table, and a column named `order` or `select` is
parsed as syntax. `ident` is applied at every site — templates, `SFUNC`,
`FINALFUNC`, field and argument names, columns, primary key, clustering order,
and `indexToCQL`. Left alone, because the server already rendered them: the
view's `WHERE` clause, type names, and the non-JSON index target.

## Behaviour changes

All in output that was previously invalid or wrong:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `{'k':'v'}` | `{'k': 'v'}`, matching `DESCRIBE` |
| `caching = null` for an unset map | `caching = {}` |
| `CREATE TABLE ks.MyTable` | `CREATE TABLE ks."MyTable"` |

`ident` quotes only what must be quoted, so a schema of ordinary lower-case
names with its maps populated — every schema a server reports — dumps
byte-identically. No existing test needed changing for the quoting commit.

author: dwin-gharibi
body:
## Summary

`storage local delete k` used to parse as a read of a key named `delete`, printing `delete: null` and exiting 0. Those two operation names are now rejected with a message that points at the supported forms.

## Closes

Closes #1915.

## What changed

- `parse_storage` in `cli/src/commands.rs` gains an `UNSUPPORTED_OPS` constant of `delete` and `remove`, checked against `rest.get(1)` before the existing operation match.
- A match returns `ParseError::UnknownSubcommand` whose `subcommand` names the storage type and the operation and suggests `storage <type> clear` or `storage <type> set <key> ""`, with `valid_options` set to a new `OPS` constant of `get`, `set`, `clear`.
- The rejection is deliberately limited to those two names so the bare-key shorthand (`storage local mykey`) keeps working for every other word.

## Tests

The bug was reproduced end to end against the shipped 0.37.1 binary driving real Chrome first: after `storage local set k v1`, `storage local delete k` printed `delete: null`, exited 0, and `storage local` still showed `k: v1`.

- `test_storage_unsupported_operation_rejected`: covers `storage local delete mykey`, `storage local remove mykey`, `storage local delete`, `storage session delete mykey`, and `storage session remove mykey`, asserting each is an `UnknownSubcommand` whose message names the operation and mentions `clear`, with `valid_options` equal to `["get", "set", "clear"]`.
- `test_storage_key_named_like_unsupported_operation`: `storage local get delete` still reads the key `delete`, and `storage local set remove v` still writes the key `remove`, so an explicit operation keeps the next word as a key.

## Docs

None needed. No documented form changes; `delete` and `remove` were never supported operations, and the error text names the supported replacements inline.

## Behaviour changes

`storage local delete` and `storage local remove` (and the `session` equivalents) now exit non-zero instead of performing a read. A key literally named `delete` or `remove` must be addressed with an explicit `get` or `set`.

## Risk

Low. The guard is two string comparisons ahead of an unchanged match, and the second test pins that the bare-key shorthand and explicit operations are unaffected.

author: pecsorabs
body:
Three more open bugs for the reliability release. All three share a shape: a
config field that was declared, documented, and in two cases *validated* — and
then never acted on. A knob that silently does nothing is worse than a missing
one, because the operator believes the guarantee it advertises.

## #609 — connector configs were never deserialized at validate time

`faucet validate` (and `faucet template register`) checked an entry's *shape*
but never parsed it into the connector's own config type, so a misspelled or
malformed connector field passed validation and failed on the first page of a
real run — after the pipeline had been scheduled, or a template released.

`registry.rs` gains `check` / `check_with` helpers plus generated
`validate_source_config` / `validate_sink_config` dispatchers (37 kinds), and
each entry's `validate()` now runs too. Wired into `commands/validate.rs` (after
`check_transforms`, skipping `NodeRole::Discovery` rows, whose configs are
completed at run time from parent records) and into `templates/store.rs::register`.

Turning it on immediately caught real defects, which are fixed here:

- **`RestStreamConfig` required 22 fields.** Only `base_url` is genuinely
  required; the rest now carry per-field `#[serde(default)]` /
  `#[serde(default = "…")]`. Deliberately *per-field* rather than a container
  `#[serde(default)]` — the container form empties the JSON Schema's `required`
  array, which breaks `faucet init` (it comments out every field and emits a
  null `config:`).
- **`query_params` was accidentally required** on the rest and xml sources.
- **16 shipped examples could not run**: `column_mapping` written as internally
  rather than externally tagged (11), wrong enum-variant casing (8), and fields
  that never existed (`url:`, `endpoint:`, a nested `PageNumber` `config:`, an
  s3 `file_format: {type: …}`).
- Template fixtures used `url:` for the rest source, which is not a field.

## #620 — `sink-delta`'s `target_file_size` was validated, then ignored

The value was rejected when zero and otherwise never read: the writer was built
with no sizing and the only `flush_and_commit` ran at end-of-run. A bulk source
emits no bookmarks, so that meant **one commit per run and a parquet buffer
holding the whole dataset** — an OOM on a large table.

delta-rs offers no target-size parameter (`RecordBatchWriter` writes exactly one
file per commit), so file size is governed by flush cadence and wiring the knob
*is* the memory fix. `commit_buffered` is extracted and `roll_if_over_target`
runs after each write on both the `Value` and columnar paths, keyed on the
writer's own `buffer_len()`. The tests assert it through the observable
consequence — the number of Delta versions and parquet files — with
`batch_size` set below the row count so the roll is exercised *within* a single
`write_batch`, which is the property that actually bounds memory.

## #619 — `concurrency` did nothing on the object-store streaming path

`buffer_unordered(concurrency)` only ever existed in the eager
`fetch_with_context` batch path. `stream_pages` — what every real run drives —
read objects strictly one at a time, so s3 / gcs / azure-blob accepted a
documented knob and ignored it; the sftp source had no such field at all.

Each source now prefetches through an **ordered** `buffered(concurrency)`
look-ahead:

- reads overlap — a 60-object scan is >2× faster at concurrency 15, asserted
  against MinIO with warm-up excluded so the comparison measures overlap rather
  than client setup;
- pages still arrive in listing order and a failing object is still blamed at
  its own position, so concurrency changes throughput and nothing an operator
  can observe;
- `concurrency: 0` is clamped to 1 rather than producing a `buffered(0)` stream
  that yields nothing forever — pinned by a test so the clamp cannot be
  refactored into a hang.

What the look-ahead holds differs by format, and that difference is the memory
contract: `json_lines` prefetches only open body readers (opening an object does
not download it), so peak memory stays `O(batch_size)`; `json_array` /
`raw_text` / `parquet` hold up to `concurrency` whole bodies — the bound the
knob already advertised. Documented per source.

sftp gains `concurrency`, defaulting to **4** rather than 10: every read shares
one SSH channel and servers commonly cap concurrent handles.
`faucet-common-sftp` re-exports the open-file handle as `SftpFile` so the source
can name it without depending on `russh-sftp` directly.

### …and Parquet objects are no longer buffered whole

The issue's other acceptance criterion. Both sources pulled an entire Parquet
object into `Bytes` before decoding — on the row path *and* the columnar one —
so peak memory was the size of the largest object, which for this format is
routinely gigabytes.

Parquet is random-access by design: its footer locates every row group. Each
source gains a `parquet_range` adapter implementing the parquet crate's
`AsyncFileReader` over ranged reads (`GetObject` with a `Range` header for s3,
`read_object` with a `ReadRange::segment` for gcs), and both paths now drive a
`ParquetRecordBatchStream` with the Arrow batch size capped at `batch_size` —
a row-group bound alone is not enough when one row group holds millions of rows.

`object_store`'s `ParquetObjectReader` (which the issue suggests, and the
parquet source uses) would have done this, but these crates authenticate
through the vendor SDKs — their own credential chains, `endpoint_url`/host
overrides, checksum options — so adopting `object_store` here would mean a
second, divergent way to authenticate, for one format.

Two configurations keep the whole-object path, because each is a guarantee
worth more than the memory saving: `verify_checksum` (the stored checksum
covers the whole object, so verifying it means reading all of it) and a
resolved `compression` codec (a compressed member is not randomly
addressable, so the footer cannot be located without inflating everything).
`verify_length` needs no exception — it guards a truncated *transfer*, and the
ranged reader enforces exactly that per fetch: a short range is an error
naming the object, never bytes quietly missing from a row group.

Tested against MinIO on a multi-row-group object: the ranged reader yields
byte-identical rows to the buffered path (an off-by-one offset would produce
plausible-but-wrong values, the worst outcome available here), the first page
arrives measurably sooner than the whole object could have been downloaded,
the columnar path honours `batch_size`, and a divergent later schema is still
rejected.

## Scope notes

- Additive only: new config fields with defaults, a new re-export, new
  dispatcher functions. No signature changes, so this is a minor bump per the
  declared semver contract.
- The GCS tests are `#[ignore]`d for the same reason as the rest of that file —
  `fake-gcs-server` speaks REST while the connector uses the gRPC data plane —
  so the gcs half shares the s3 design but is covered by compilation and review
  rather than by an emulator. The s3 (MinIO) and azure-blob (Azurite) suites run
  unignored.
- **The sftp concurrency path has no end-to-end test.** Neither sftp crate has a
  container harness (only conformance), so the new field is covered by config
  unit tests and the shared design, not by a real SSH session. Its correctness
  rests on `russh-sftp` multiplexing concurrent requests over one channel —
  which its `&self` API asserts — and the default of 4 is deliberately
  conservative for that reason. Worth adding an `atmoz/sftp` suite as its own
  change; say the word and I will.
- Both sftp crates gained the workspace's
  `[package.metadata.cargo-semver-checks.lints]` block; without it the new
  `concurrency` field reads as a major break, which is exactly the contract the
  API-evolution policy declares per crate.
- The committed `schemas/faucet.schema.json` is spliced, not regenerated: a
  regeneration reorders ever

author: defenwycke
body:
Part of #380 — see [the correction there](https://github.com/bitcoin-ghost/hazync/issues/380), because the
issue as I filed it was wrong.

## What was actually missing

The live bridge is defined by **seven** drop-ins. Four were already committed; three were not, and two of
the four had drifted from what runs.

**Added, taken straight off the box:**

| file | what it carries |
|---|---|
| `memory.conf` | `MemoryHigh=40G` / `MemoryMax=44G` — the room bitcoind gives back after sync |
| `storage.conf` | `RequiresMountsFor=/srv/bulk`, `After=bitcoind.service` |
| `zz-emit-from.conf` | `HAZYNC_BRIDGE_EMIT_FROM=967500`, and the bridge's own binary |

`zz-emit-from.conf` is the one that matters. It holds the setting the entire bundle-gap problem descends
from (#347, #378, #379), and it documents why the bridge runs a **non-canonical guest id `05a5a279`**: a
RISC0 image id absorbs the build's absolute paths, so only the fixed-path container build yields
`37987b85`. The bridge never proves, so it does not matter there — and the file explicitly warns not to
point the coordinator at that binary. I raised that id as an alarm earlier today; the answer was sitting
in an uncommitted file.

**Corrected to match the box:**

```
height-cap.conf   HAZYNC_BRIDGE_TO   220000 -> 967300
paths.conf        HAZYNC_BRIDGE_OUT  /var/lib/hazync/... -> /srv/bulk/hazync/bridge_bundles
                  ReadWritePaths with it
```

A box rebuilt from this repo would have written bundles to the 2 TB system disk instead of the 6 TB block
storage, and stopped walking at height 220,000.

## How this was checked

⚠ **By directives, not bytes.** The repo copies carry explanatory comment blocks the deployed files do
not, so a byte diff reports *every* tracked file as drifted and tells you nothing — I reported exactly
that before checking properly. Comparing effective directives separates the two real differences from the
four harmless ones. All six now match directive-for-directive against the box.

`hardening.conf`'s `ProtectSystem=full` is **left alone deliberately**: `paths.conf` sorts after it
alphabetically and sets `strict`, the base unit sets `strict`, and `systemctl show` confirms the box runs
`strict`. A superseded line, not drift — deleting it would be a behaviour change dressed as tidying.

## The guard for this already exists and runs nowhere

`scripts/check-unit-drift.sh` would have caught all three missing files on its first run. It is referenced
by no workflow, no unit and no script; it is not installed on the box; `hazync-run-check` does not know
it. Twelve of the `scripts/check-*.sh` family run in CI and this one does not — the same shape as #382.

It cannot simply be added to CI, since it needs SSH to a live host. That decision is left in #380.

author: outof-place
body:
Stacked on #485. Base is `chore/agent-context-layers`, so this diff is only the Codex half.

## What changes

The context budget from `.claude/context-budget.tsv` now reaches Codex, not just Claude Code.

- `.claude/hooks/context-budget-core.mjs` holds what counts as too large and the exact wording the model reads. Both guards import it, so the two harnesses cannot drift apart.
- `.claude/hooks/context-budget-guard.mjs` is now a thin Claude Code adapter over that core.
- `.codex/hooks/context-budget-guard.mjs` is the Codex adapter. `PreToolUse` parses the `apply_patch` envelope and projects the resulting size (adds minus removes, a moved file measured at the path it lands on); `PostToolUse` stats the budgeted files on disk, which is the only way to catch a write made through the shell.
- `.codex/hooks.json` registers both events. Each command resolves the repository root first, because a hook command runs from the session's working directory and a relative path would silently lose the guard in a session started in a subdirectory.
- The over-ceiling message now says "The edit is not blocked", because a Codex run read the old wording as a refusal and started deleting whitespace to make room.

## Evidence

Start `8fe8416b`, candidate `a52d02ffe2da5f91447540122cda45f4c994abca`.

author: irfanhathoti
body:
## The bug (live on prod)
Copied **closes** on SnapTrade subscribers get **REJECTED "No matching position to close"** even though the subscriber **is holding** the contract, and are **never retried** — leaving the subscriber stranded long.

Confirmed live (AAPL $337.5 CALL): **Shruti** and **ikokujin** each still hold **3** at the broker, but their close came back REJECTED "no matching position." The trader is flat → real open exposure.

## Why
It is **not** our pre-check skipping the close (those produce different messages). The sell **was placed**, and **SnapTrade rejected it** with a "no position" error — its **order-placement view lags its positions view**, so a close fired right after the entry fills is refused even though `get_positions` shows the contract held. `is_order_conflict_error` didn't match that message, so `_place_mirror_with_conflict_resolve` re-raised immediately → normalized to "No matching position to close" → REJECTED, no retry.

## The fix
`_place_mirror_with_conflict_resolve` already re-confirms the **live held quantity** and retries (short wait) for same-contract conflicts. This routes a **"no position" close rejection into that same path**, and retries **only when `live_closeable_quantity` confirms a held position (> 0)**. A genuinely flat account still raises `position_already_flat` and is **never** retried, so this can't open a naked short. The retry loop's 3× 0.5s waits give SnapTrade's order view time to catch up.

New classifier `is_no_position_close_error` mirrors the `clean_broker_error` "no position" match and **excludes** the durable "liquidation only" restriction.

## Test
`tests/test_no_position_close_retry.py` — recognizes SnapTrade "no position" rejections, excludes liquidation-only, ignores unrelated errors (buying power / throttle / wash-trade), and keeps it distinct from a conflict. 4 new + existing close-clamp tests pass.

## Scope
SnapTrade/Webull subscribers; real-money close path — please review the retry guard (retry only on confirmed live holding). No auto-merge.

Note: this is a distinct issue from PR #283 (stuck "Submitted" via id mismatch). Together they cover the two halves of the subscriber fill/close problems.

author: malkreide
body:
## Was ändert sich

Ein Absatz in `docs/codex-reviews.md`, der einen Befund **festhält statt ihn zu beheben**. Das ist die bewusste Entscheidung, nicht das Ergebnis von Bequemlichkeit.

**Der Befund** kam vom Rückgriff auf dem schon gemergten #104: Die beiden Richtungen des Irrtums beim Portfolio-Vorfilter gelten nur, solange die Thread-Antwort die einzige einschlägige Bot-Aktivität am PR ist. Trägt derselbe PR schon ein Review-Objekt und bekommt später eine Thread-Meldung, findet ihn `reviewed-by:` weiterhin — verloren ist dann der *Nachweis*, dass der spätere Lauf scheiterte, nicht der PR. Er ist zutreffend, und die Sammlung führt PRs mit gelungenen *und* gescheiterten Läufen; der Fall ist nicht theoretisch.

**Warum nicht behoben.** Die Korrekturschleife war bei einer Reihe von Befunden derselben Klasse angelangt: eine Regel geschärft und den zusammenfassenden Satz daneben eine Stufe zu breit gefasst. `CLAUDE.md` beschreibt genau diese Lage unter «Zum Verfahren für Doku-PRs» — wer davorsteht, entscheidet sie nicht über eine Regel, sondern mit einem Menschen, und schreibt hin, was offen blieb. Beides ist geschehen.

Der neue Absatz sagt das auch von sich selbst, damit ein späterer Leser die Lücke nicht für ein Versehen hält.

Gates lokal mit dem gepinnten ruff: alle grün, 137 Tests.

## Checkliste

- [ ] Codex-Review beantwortet oder behoben — kein offener Befund beim Merge
