author: alexisnorthcoders
body:
Fixes #7

Opened automatically after a `claude issue:…` run from the WhatsApp bot.

**Branch:** `claude/issue-7-hud-player-name-is-blank-because-it-is-drawn-bef`
**Base:** `main`

**Original prompt (truncated):**

# GitHub issue #7

**Repository:** alexisNorthcoders/snake-phaser
**URL:** https://github.com/alexisNorthcoders/snake-phaser/issues/7
**State:** OPEN
**Labels:** ready-for-agent
**Title:** HUD 'Player:' name is blank because it is drawn before the name is loaded

## Body
## What to build

The HUD at the top of the game screen shows **"Player:"** with no name. It should show the player's name: "anonymous" for guests, or the username for logged-in players. After a guest logs in or creates an account from the save-score modal, the HUD should switch to the new username.

This is a client-side bug.

## Root cause

In `src/scenes/GameScene.ts`, `create()`:
- About line 143 builds the HUD text: `this.playerNameText = this.add.text(400, 10, \`Player: ${this.name}\`, ...)`.
- `this.name` is only set later in the same method, at about line 234: `this.name = userData.username;`.

So the text is created while `this.name` is still empty, and nothing updates it afterwards.

Also, the modal's `onAuthSuccess` callback in `onGameOver` (about line 434) sets `this.name = userData.username` but does not update the HUD either.

## Plan

1. In `create()`, move these lines so they run **before** the HUD text is created (before the `this.playerNameText = this.add.text(...)` line):
   ```ts
   const userData = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('userData') || '{}');
   this.name = userData.username;
   this.playerId = String(userData.userId);
   ```
   Then remove the original copies further down (about lines 232-235). Code later in `create()` also uses `userData` (for example `socketManager.connect(String(userData.userId), userData.token, this)` and the welcome text), so keep a single `userData` declaration that is in scope for all of it. Don't declare it twice.
2. In `onGameOver`, inside `onAuthSuccess`, add this after `this.name = userData.username;`:
   ```ts
   this.playerNameText.setText(`Player: ${this.name}`);
   ```
3. Don't touch anything else in `create()`. Keep the order of the other HUD elements the same.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `npm test` passes.
- Manual check (both apps run under pm2; restart with `pm2 restart snake-phaser`, and never run `npm run dev`):
  1. Open http://localhost:5173 and choose "Play as Guest". The HUD reads `Player: anonymous`.
  2. Log out, then log in with an account. The HUD reads `Player: <username>`.
  3. As a guest, finish a round and create an account or log in from the save-score modal. The HUD switches to the new username.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The HUD shows `Player: anonymous` for guests.
- [ ] The HUD shows `Player: <username>` for logged-in players.
- [ ] The HUD name updates after logging in or registering from the save-score modal.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

author: hivinaynair
body:
Two changes that share a branch: account abstraction in the checkout demo, and a
recipient bound into the AP2 mandate.

26 commits, 295 tests, gate green.

## 1 · ERC-4337, without the SDK learning what it is

`PaymentSigner` is three fields because the host owns its wallet stack. ERC-4337
is a genuinely different execution model — different submission, different hash,
different failure mode. If it drops in without changing the public surface, the
design is proven rather than asserted.

**What moved in `packages/`:** 12 files, and every line is either the
`TxHash` → `SettlementHash` rename or an unrelated error improvement. Total
ERC-4337 vocabulary that reached the SDK: one doc comment. `apps/` took roughly
a thousand lines. `measure-settle-kit.mjs` now makes that a build failure —
verified by deliberately importing `viem/account-abstraction` into core and
watching the build reject it.

**The bug this exists to avoid.** A user operation bundled into a transaction
whose status is `success` can still have reverted: the EntryPoint catches a
failing operation so the rest of the bundle settles. Confirming on the
transaction receipt marks unpaid purchases as paid. `createUsdcMethod` already
exposed an injectable `receiptClient`, so the fix needed no core change — a
4337-aware client reads `UserOperationEvent.success`, and a reverted operation
then walks the identical state path as a reverted ERC-20 transfer.

**What the demo does now.** The visitor gets a smart account in their browser,
counterfactual until it pays. A faucet funds it, a paymaster covers gas, the
account pays the merchant. Still no wallet connection, no signup. This deletes
the signer whose `address` was the *merchant* and whose `sendTransaction` threw
— the one that made the demo bypass its own SDK, balance preflight included.

Phase 2 then widens what correctness demanded: `SettleAdapter.id` was the
literal `"usdc"`, so `methods` was an array that could hold one thing and
`selectMethod` had nothing to select.

## 2 · A mandate now names its merchant

`MandatePayload` said how much and until when, and never said to whom. A mandate
issued for one resource was equally valid at any other, and no verifier could
catch it because the field it would check did not exist.

`payTo` is part of the signed struct, compared against the payment's actual
recipient at both the verify and settle gates — and in `verifyMandateLocal`,
which is the helper hosts use and which was checking signature, expiry and agent
while ignoring the merchant entirely.

Found by reading Skyfire's token spec, which binds every token with an audience
claim for exactly this reason.

## Notable decisions

- **Bundler and paymaster both proxy through `/api/paymaster`.** CDP serves them
  from one endpoint whose path is the API key, so neither is reachable from a
  browser. Every request is checked against a sponsorship policy first, which is
  what makes the burner key in `localStorage` worth nothing to a thief.
- **The access gate reads logs, not calldata.** Under 4337 the transaction is the
  bundler's, `to` is the EntryPoint, the calldata is `handleOps`. The operation's
  sender must be the burner we funded, and the hash is claimed once, so one
  payment cannot release two reports.
- **No "deploying" UI phase.** The account deploys inside its first payment. A
  third step would look better and be a lie.
- **`Settlement` uses `?: never`, not a branded union.** The hex brands are
  optional phantom properties, so a union of them admits any hex string and
  narrows to nothing.

## Before merging — two things this needs

**The mandate change is breaking.** Every existing signature is invalid and the
wire format refuses the old shape rather than defaulting it. The 7 mandates in
`apps/agent/mandates.json` need reissuing with `bun run lycoris:bootstrap`.

**The database migration is applied** (`lycoris:migrate-4337`, idempotent,
verified by running it twice), but a fresh environment needs it too.

## What has not been proven

295 tests pass and every one uses a fake. **Nothing here has met a real
bundler.** This branch already caught three places where viem's actual shapes
differed from the plan — `getUserOperationReceipt` throwing rather than
returning null, the Drizzle schema silently reverting the migration, and
`readSponsoredRequest` rejecting a second field — so a fourth is likely.

The CDP gas policy also needs USDC allowlisted, and probably the account factory
too: the first payment from each visitor deploys their account, so if only USDC
is sponsored, every *first* payment fails and every second succeeds.

Design notes: `docs/plans/2026-09-18-erc-4337-design.md`

body: ## Problem On Mac LMS Run Live Class, the first-stage **Set Class** UI was missing: the school-day calendar and Module / Live class dropdowns never appeared. Fresh or reminted sessions jumped into an older join/attendance shell. Two causes stacked: 1. **Bootstrap skip** — leftover `/run-live` sessions were treated as in-progress, so `resumeLiveClassIfNeeded()` auto-began attendance and never entered `validate` / `setupPhase`. 2. **JS never booted** — `staff_ap.js` statically imported missing `/static/bank_mc_picker.js`, so the ES module graph aborted and the calendar never painted. After restoring the picker, shared `common.js` also lacked live-question HTML helpers that later stages import. ## Fix - Persist a `class_set` teacher-state flag. Fresh / reminted sessions stay on Set Class until date + module + slot are chosen and Next is pressed. - First-paint HTML starts `#ap-root` in `is-set-class` with `#ap-panel-validate` current, so heading + dropdowns show even before JS. - `run=1` and `!class_set` refuse resume-into-attendance; later stages (teams / names / rounds / live) still resume when `class_set` is true. - Restore `lms/static/bank_mc_picker.js` (dynamic import from staff_ap) and export `formatQuestionHtml` / `questionFieldHtml` / `questionImageHtml` / `renderLiveQuestionMath` from `tools/math-game-show/static/common.js`. - Bank-import APIs and Artifact mint paths are unchanged. ## Tests - `lms/test_live_shell.py::test_run_live_opens_on_set_class_validate` - `lms/test_live_teacher_state.py::test_class_set_defaults_false_until_patched` - Existing live-shell + live-teacher-state + module-bank-import suites Verified at `http://127.0.0.1:8787` (Cloud Agents Window plug; laptop `:8788` is the same staff course tab). Sacred login untouched. No Fly. author: robsonlupo-dev
body:
## Problema

Admin e moderador logavam mas levavam **403**: `RedirectsToHome::homeRouteFor()` mandava todo usuário não-performer para `catalog`, e o catálogo exige role de **consumer**.

## Correção

No trait `RedirectsToHome::homeRouteFor()`, antes do fallback de consumer, resolver staff pelos helpers do model (`isAdmin()` / `isModerator()`, PR #225) para `admin.dashboard`. Moderador usa o mesmo painel/fila de moderação.

O trait é compartilhado pelas **duas portas web** (login por senha `LoginController` e login por código `OtpLoginController`), então ambas ganham o mesmo destino — sem divergência.

Diff mínimo: **7 linhas** no trait + testes.

```diff
+        if ($user->isAdmin() || $user->isModerator()) {
+            return 'admin.dashboard';
+        }
+
         if ($user->role !== 'performer') {
             return 'catalog';
         }
```

## Testes

Novo `tests/Feature/LoginRedirectAdminTest.php` (6 testes / 30 asserts, verdes):

- Admin loga (senha) → `admin.dashboard` (não 403)
- Moderador loga (senha) → `admin.dashboard` (não 403)
- Consumer loga → `catalog` (sem regressão)
- Performer ativa loga → `performer.members` (sem regressão)
- Performer em KYC loga → `performer.onboarding` (sem regressão)
- Admin por **OTP** → `admin.dashboard` (trait compartilhado, mesmo destino)

Regressão conferida: `WebPhase7Test` + `OtpLoginTest` + `AdminDashboardTest` = 58/58 verdes.

author: lemollon
body:
## Summary

Mobile half of Apple In-App Purchase support for IronForge iOS (Guideline
3.1.1 fix). Backend endpoints (`POST /api/billing/apple/verify`,
`POST /api/billing/apple/notifications`, `provider` on
`GET /api/billing/membership`) are a separate PR — this one assumes they
exist exactly as specced and does not touch `ironforge/webapp`.

- **`expo-iap` 5.6.2** (StoreKit 2, installed via `npx expo install expo-iap`
  to match Expo SDK 54) added to `package.json` and `app.config.ts` plugins.
- **`src/billing/apple-products.ts`** — hand-written mirror of the server's
  product catalogue (`ironforge.{both,spark,flame,community}.monthly` ↔
  Stripe lookup keys), `productIdFor()` / `planFor()`.
- **`src/billing/apple-iap.ts`** — `initIap()` (connect + wire the
  purchase-updated/purchase-error listeners once per session), `loadProducts()`
  (StoreKit-localized pricing for the 4 products), `purchase(productId, userId)`
  (sets `appAccountToken` to the signed-in customer's UUID), `restorePurchases()`
  (newest-expiry-per-product wins), and the purchase-updated handler: verify
  with the server, **only then** `finishTransaction` — a rejected or
  network-failed verify leaves the transaction unfinished so StoreKit replays
  it rather than losing it silently. User-cancelled is silent; a genuine
  network failure retries once before surfacing an error.
- **`src/billing/store-policy.ts`** — `canPurchaseInApp('ios')` flips to
  `true` (Android/web stay `false`, Play Billing is out of scope); new
  `manageSubscriptionUrl(provider, platform)` pointing an Apple-provisioned
  iOS membership at `https://apps.apple.com/account/subscriptions`.
- **`app/enroll/billing.tsx`** — iOS now shows the real product for
  `enrollment.selected_plan` (name, what it includes, StoreKit's own
  localized price), a Subscribe button, Restore Purchases, and the mandatory
  Apple subscription disclosure block (title/duration/price/auto-renewal
  terms) with tappable Terms of Use / Privacy Policy links pulled from the
  same `getLegal()` codes (`TERMS` → `/terms`, `PRIVACY` → `/privacy`) the web
  legal step already uses. On successful verify it re-resumes the enrollment
  and continues forward exactly like "I already subscribed on the web".
  Android/web are unchanged (still the disabled "Coming soon" button).
- **`app/(tabs)/account.tsx`** — Apple-provisioned memberships on iOS get a
  "Manage subscription" link to Apple's own subscription settings;
  Stripe-provisioned (or unknown-provider) memberships on iOS get plain,
  non-actionable copy, per 3.1.1. Android/web unchanged.
- **`src/api/types.ts`** — `MembershipResponse.membership.provider:
  'stripe' | 'apple' | null` added to match the server contract this PR
  assumes.
- Tests: `apple-products.test.ts` (both-direction mapping), `apple-iap.test.ts`
  (purchase-flow handler — cancel/silent, success→verify→finish, verify 403
  no-retry-no-finish, plus a network-retry case, with `expo-iap` mocked),
  `store-policy.test.ts` extended for `canPurchaseInApp` and
  `manageSubscriptionUrl`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 30 files / 310 tests passing
- [ ] Manual iOS build + sandbox purchase (orchestrator runs `eas build`,
      not done here per instructions)

author: mattkram
body:
## Bug: Delete button returns 404 for orphaned listings

The Delete button on a package detail page returned `mattkram/anaconda-cloud/noarch/aext-assistant-4.57.0-py_jl4_0.conda not found`. That key genuinely 404s and the repodata listing is **stale** — an artifact of the original bug where the R2 object was deleted but repodata was never rebuilt (pre-PR #49). The `head()` guard in `handleDeletePackage` 404'd *before* doing anything, so orphaned listings could never be cleaned up through the UI.

**Fix**: drop the `head()` 404 guard — `handleDeletePackage` is now idempotent. R2 `delete()` on a missing key is a no-op, and `container /delete-package` prunes purely from the shard (it never touches the package object), so the shard entry is removed, `SubdirIndexMerger` rebuilds repodata without the dead file, and a new debounced cold reindex reconciles everything. Only genuinely-unlisted builds now 404 (`removed: false` from the container).

## Feature: every delete now triggers a background conda-index reindex

Consistency is currently guaranteed only by the manual shard operations; `conda-index` was never run on the normal path. Per request: deletes now also schedule a full `conda-index` reindex as a debounced background follow-up off the hot path, so the hot (shard-merge) and cold (conda-index) paths are eventually reconciled.

- **`src/do/channel-reindexer.ts`** — new `ChannelReindexer` Durable Object, one instance per `{channel}/{subdir}`, mirrors `SubdirIndexMerger`'s debounce/backoff pattern. Alarm wakes `getContainer(env.INDEXER, "{channel}/{subdir}/_cold-index")` and calls `/reindex`.
- **`wrangler.toml`** — `COLD_INDEX` binding + migration `v5`.
- **`container/entrypoint.py`** — `POST /reindex` now runs `conda-index` in a background thread and returns `202`, so it can't exceed the Worker's ~30s container-fetch timeout.
- **`src/browse/pages.ts`** — delete handler schedules the cold reindex up front (still best-effort even if the hot prune fails), then notifies `SubdirIndexMerger` as before.

Deferred (as discussed): comparing shard ops vs conda-index output per operation and reporting discrepancies — the cold reindex logs `reindex.done` with expected/seen counts for manual post-hoc checking in the meantime.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` clean
- `npm test` — 38/38 pass
- Live check confirmed the fixture object is gone from R2 (namespaced + flat prefixes both 404), i.e. a true stale listing

**Needs redeploy to take effect** (`wrangler deploy` rebuilds the container image; requires Docker). For the `anaconda-cloud` cleanup, `python scripts/channel_manager.py purge --channel mattkram/anaconda-cloud --yes` will also wipe the channel wholesale.

author: jamesarich
body:
## Why

kzstd 0.2.1 published to Maven Central today, and this SDK carries kzstd into every consumer's POM — `takpacket-sdk-jvm`'s published POM lists `kzstd-jvm` at `runtime` scope. Tagging 0.9.2 against 0.2.0 would ship a release pointing at a dependency that was superseded the same morning.

Caught before 0.9.2 published: the tag was pushed, its Release run was still queued behind the runner backlog, and nothing had reached Central, PyPI, npm or NuGet (all 404). The run was cancelled and the tag removed, so this lands in 0.9.2 itself rather than needing a 0.9.3 whose only content is a no-op bump.

kzstd 0.2.1 is a maintenance release — its committed ABI dumps are byte-identical to 0.2.0, so nothing this SDK compiles against moved. It picks up zstd-jni 1.5.7-16 on the JVM backend, plus Kotlin 2.4.20 and toolchain work that does not affect the artifact.

## 🧹 Chores

- `kzstd` 0.2.0 → 0.2.1 in the version catalog.
- Record it in the existing `## [0.9.2]` CHANGELOG section, so the release notes describe what the release actually contains.

## Testing Performed

Verified both coordinates resolve on Central before bumping:

```
kzstd-jvm/0.2.1/kzstd-jvm-0.2.1.pom  → HTTP 200
kzstd/0.2.1/kzstd-0.2.1.pom          → HTTP 200
```

and that the release workflow's own gate still passes:

```
$ awk -v v="## [$(cat VERSION)]" 'index($0, v) == 1 { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' CHANGELOG.md
CHANGELOG has ## [0.9.2]
```

The five language coordinates are untouched and remain at 0.9.2; `v0.9.2` gets re-tagged on this commit once merged.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated the 0.9.2 changelog to note the `kzstd` 0.2.1 release and its ABI compatibility with 0.2.0.
  - Documented the JVM backend’s adoption of zstd-jni 1.5.7-16.

- **Chores**

author: thinkbig1979
body:
Adds migration 17 and the `docker_cleanup_runs` table, with the database layer to insert and list rows. First task of the scheduled-Docker-cleanup epic (`agent-os-fn7x`); nothing calls the new functions yet, which is expected for a layered bead.

## What this is

`docker_cleanup_runs` is its own table rather than a seventh `backup_runs.kind`. `backup_runs.kind` carries a CHECK constraint and SQLite cannot alter one in place, so migration 16 had to DROP and recreate both `backup_runs` and `backup_run_items` just to add `'verify'`. The new table deliberately has no CHECK-constrained kind column, so a future cleanup kind costs an INSERT rather than a table rebuild.

`min_age_hours` is stored per row on purpose: a history entry has to stay interpretable after the policy changes, and "why did this run remove so much" is unanswerable without the age floor that run actually applied.

## The part worth reviewing

`RunMigrations` reads `migrations[len(migrations)-1].Version` as the version this binary understands — the **last** element, not the maximum. A migration spliced in mid-slice still applies, so the database stamps to 17 while the binary reports 16. Nothing fails at migration time. The **next** boot hits the forward-version guard's FATAL refusal, telling the operator their image is older than the database and pointing at `CAPSTAN_ALLOW_SCHEMA_DOWNGRADE` — both untrue, and the wrong remedy.

The test pins this by asserting the slice is **strictly ascending by Version**, not that 17 is last. That catches a mid-slice insert of any migration and does not become a booby trap for whoever adds 18. An earlier revision of this test pinned the literal `17`; under a correctly-appended migration 18 it failed with "migration 17 must be appended at the end", which is false in exactly the situation that produces it.

Seen failing first: migration 17 moved between 15 and 16, byte-identical otherwise. Two independent assertions go red — the ascending check, and `stamped == migrations[len-1].Version`. The `MAX(version)` check four lines away passes under that mutant, because `MAX` is order-independent; that is why the two are different instruments rather than one repeated.

## Also here

`wantSchemaMigrations` moves 16 → 17 in `handlers/backup_test.go`. That test is a deliberate tripwire — its comment says the friction is the feature — and it is in another package, so `go test ./internal/database/` cannot see it. Its docblock now names migration 18 as the next one to trip it.

`GetDockerCleanupRuns` scans `error_message` through `sql.NullString`. `GetBackupRuns` scans the equivalent column straight into a `string`, so a single NULL row there returns the whole list as an error. That is pre-existing and is filed as `agent-os-1m58`, not fixed here.

## Verification

- `cd backend && go test ./... -count=1` — exit 0
- `cd backend && go test ./... -count=1 -race` — exit 0 (the CI race job; no acceptance criterion names it)
- `go test ./internal/handlers/ -count=10 -shuffle=on` — exit 0, 560s (re-run of closed bead `agent-os-80n`'s acceptance)
- 16 closed beads declare a file this diff touches; their acceptance re-run, all green

Filed from the review, not fixed here: `agent-os-fn7x.8` (timestamp normalisation, blocks the service bead), `agent-os-fn7x.7` (no retention path for cleanup history), `agent-os-1m58` (the `GetBackupRuns` NULL scan).

author: yyjeqhc
body:
## Summary

- productize the existing durable Job terminal wait + MCP App continuation carrier by projecting parser-ready `suggested_call` only when the current MCP Host can actually present the App
- add bounded visible/hidden App polling backoff while preserving exact wait/binding/attempt fences and exactly-once `ui/message` dispatch semantics
- extend native `run_process`, `run_script`, and `run_detached_process` execution lifetime ceilings to 7 days without broadening shell, structured validation, Skill, direct-sync, MCP, or HTTP timeout ceilings
- extend terminal retention from 15 minutes to 24 hours under existing count/byte bounds and derive Job terminal-wait horizons from execution form + recovery grace + terminal retention
- retain detached supervisor/restart/replacement recovery, stop routing, idempotency, and Runner concurrency semantics

## Independent reviewer follow-up

Reviewer commit `7712c8c4 fix(jobs): align auto-resume continuation contract` closes two contract issues found after the implementation report:

- reuse the repository-wide canonical parser-ready `suggested_call` representation for Host continuation presentation instead of introducing a second `resume_setup` vocabulary; the projection remains MCP-App-capability-specific and absent on unsupported Hosts
- because the Host still exposes no authoritative turn/supersession generation, the automatic continuation message now explicitly reconciles terminal completion against the current conversation and refuses to resume old work superseded by newer user instructions; this does not pretend to prevent the extra best-effort wake itself

Reviewer reruns: Job terminal Rust slice 25/25, Job terminal App JS 14/14, form-specific 7-day core lifetime test 1/1, long-process wait-horizon test 1/1, `cargo check --locked -p webcodex --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check` all passed.

## Review hardening

A live dogfood observation exposed a Host/App race: Job terminal completion could reach the card while the invoking model turn was still active. The App's `ui/message` RPC was accepted and surfaced text, but no fresh second model turn followed. The previous implementation then finalized delivery as accepted, so the exactly-once fence correctly prevented a blind resend.

This review hardens that boundary without inventing a Host turn identity:

- `suggested_call` is now projected only for `state=waiting` + `delivery_state=not_ready`; an already-triggered wait already has terminal truth for the current model turn and does not arm a redundant carrier
- the App begins auto-resume eligibility only after the initial presentation tool result and enforces a bounded 10s turn-yield grace before `prepare -> ui/message` may run
- Tool guidance requires continuation presentation to be the final meaningful action when blocked, followed by prompt yield/end of the current turn
- `ui/message` acceptance is documented honestly as Host dispatch acceptance, not proof that a fresh model turn consumed the continuation
- there is still no canonical per-turn generation/turn-idle signal; ClientWindow/openai-session/audit timing are not used to fabricate one

The review also found a long-run operational issue: detached output checkpoints were fsync+rename persisted as often as every 250ms. For a chatty multi-day training process this can create millions of durable writes. Detached running-output recovery tails now checkpoint every 5s; stop/control polling remains independent, and terminalization still performs a bounded final drain and durable final-tail commit.

## Lifetime policy

| Path | Default | Max |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `run_process` | 60s | 604800s / 7d |
| `run_script` | 60s | 604800s / 7d |
| `run_detached_process` | 60s | 604800s / 7d |
| `run_shell` | 60s | 3600s |
| structured validation | existing | 3600s |
| Skill resource | 60s | 3600s |
| direct synchronous structured request | n/a | 120s |

`MCP_DISPATCH_HARD_TIMEOUT=150s` and whole-service HTTP hard timeout `300s` are unchanged.

Terminal retention is now 86400s / 24h. Existing maximum retained terminal inventory/receipt counts remain 64. Long process/script/detached terminal attention uses the form-specific execution ceiling + 1h recovery grace + 24h terminal retention, giving a bounded maximum registration horizon of 694800s (8d1h).

## Validation

- Job terminal App race/backoff/exactly-once JS harness: 14/14
- all shared MCP App JS harnesses after deterministic clock change: 255/255
- Job terminal Rust focused suite: 25/25
- Core form-specific long Job encode/decode: 1/1
- ToolRuntime 6h same-execution handoff: 1/1
- Server long Job terminal-wait horizon: 1/1
- Runner detached 6h / >7d admission: 1/1
- detached 24h terminal reclamation: 1/1
- detached real-process output flood/final-tail durability (`runner-real-process-tests --ignored`): 1/1
- detached restart recovery preserves terminal output: 1/1
- ToolSpec form-specific lifetime description contract: 1/1
- affected packages `cargo check --all-features`: passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- workspace hygiene: clean; active Jobs: 0

The only build warning is the pre-existing `webcodex-runner` unused import `ShellCommandExecutionState`; this branch does not modify that line.

## Scope boundaries

- no fake detection of newer user/model turns
- no Server-to-Host push protocol redesign
- no blind continuation redispatch
- no change to Job concurrency quota
- no GPU/cluster/Slurm/Kubernetes scheduler
- no claim that detached native processes survive host OS reboot or power loss
- complete training logs/checkpoints remain application/project-file responsibilities; Job tails stay bounded

The branch was merged with current `origin/main` during review without rebasing or rewriting the original feature commits. No deployment, restart, release, or tag operation is part of this PR.

body:
Le site était en violet et magenta (`#9333ea`, `#7e22ce`, `#581c87`, `#ec4899`), hérités de la palette Tailwind d'origine. Le nouveau logo (#6) est en roses pastel et bordeaux sur fond crème : les deux ne s'accordaient plus.

## Les teintes viennent du logo

Échantillonnées directement dans `static/sopatiss.jpg` (k-means), sans réinterprétation :

| teinte | rôle |
|---|---|
| `#fdf6f0` crème dominant | fonds hero et tarifs |
| `#fae0dc` blush | bouton secondaire |
| `#edc5c0` rose pâle | bordures, icônes du pied de page |
| `#eba1a5` rose | boutons pleins |
| `#c48387` rose moyen | dégradé « Fécamp » |
| `#9a4856` bordeaux | liens, nom dans l'en-tête |
| `#763440` bordeaux foncé | titres, survols de liens |

Une seule teinte dérivée s'y ajoute, `#5e2a34`, pour le texte posé sur les fonds pastel.

## Le texte des boutons passe au bordeaux

C'est la conséquence directe du pastel : un fond assez clair pour être pastel ne donne au texte blanc qu'un contraste de 2 à 3:1, très en dessous du seuil lisible. Les quatre boutons pleins du site (accueil, en-tête, formulaire de contact, page de remerciement) portent donc du bordeaux `#5e2a34` au lieu du blanc.

## Contraste

| | |
|---|---|
| Titres `#763440` sur blanc | 8,99:1 |
| Titres `#763440` sur crème | 8,40:1 |
| Liens `#9a4856` sur blanc | 6,11:1 |
| Liens `#9a4856` sur crème | 5,71:1 |
| Texte sur bouton primaire | 5,48:1 |
| Texte sur survol primaire | 5,10:1 |
| Texte sur bouton secondaire | 9,03:1 |
| Texte sur survol secondaire | 7,84:1 |
| Icône sociale sur pied de page sombre | 9,33:1 |

Tout passe AA. Pour mémoire, l'ancien bouton secondaire `#ec4899` en texte blanc plafonnait à 3,53:1 et ne le respectait pas.

## Ce qui n'a pas bougé

Les gris, le blanc, le rouge d'erreur `#dc2626` et le jaune `#fef9c3` des encarts « à compléter » des pages légales : ils ne portent pas l'identité de marque.

Les fonds gris froids des pages contact et articles (`#f9fafb`) sont conservés. Ils voisinent un peu froidement avec le rose chaud ; un `#faf7f5` les réchaufferait, mais ça sort du remplacement des couleurs de marque.

## Vérifications

- `npm run build` passe.
- Rendu contrôlé au navigateur sur le build de production : accueil, tarifs, contact, articles, pied de page, et mobile 390 px.
- Plus aucune occurrence des anciennes teintes dans `src/`.
- `prettier` et `eslint` remontent exactement les mêmes fichiers et erreurs que sur `master`, rien de nouveau.

Indépendante de la #7 : les deux partent de `master` et ne touchent pas les mêmes fichiers.

author: mastacontrola
body:
## The defect

`fogLogStatusFile()` is FOG's own addition to partclone's `progress.c`
(`Buildroot/package/partclone/partclone-0.3.47.patch`). It is the only writer of
`/tmp/status.fog`, which `fog.statusreporter` forwards to `service/progress.php`.

It called `exit(0)` when it could not open that file.

`exit(0)` is a SUCCESS status. `funcs.sh` reads `$exitcode` after the partclone
pipeline and calls `handleError` only when it is non-zero. So partclone quitting
halfway through a restore is recorded as a good deploy: the task completes, the
client reboots, and the partition is partially written with nothing said on
screen or in the log. `/tmp` in FOS is a ramdisk, so a full one is enough to
reach it.

Progress reporting is best effort. It now warns once on stderr and returns. The
restore continues, and the cost is a stalled percentage on the web UI.

## Two more defects in the same function

Both were in front of me while editing it.

| Was | Why it is wrong | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `sprintf(total_str, filesize_conv(totalsize, buf, max_len))` | the converted string is passed as `sprintf`'s FORMAT argument, so a `%` in it reads an argument that was never passed | `filesize_conv(totalsize, total_str, sizeof(total_str))` — it already writes into the buffer it is handed |
| `int max_len=15;` sizing two VLAs, plus a shared `buf` | a variable for a constant, and both conversions aliased one scratch buffer | `char total_str[16];` / `char current_str[16];`, no shared buffer |

## The gate

`tests/checks/partclone-status-patch.sh` checks the patch as text:

- no `exit(` anywhere in `fogLogStatusFile()`
- a failed `fopen` returns (so removing the `exit` without replacing it cannot pass)
- no `sprintf` whose format argument is a call's return value
- every `@@` header's counts match the lines under it

The last one is not incidental. The added code is `+` lines inside a unified
diff, so editing it by hand moves counts that nothing else recomputes. `patch`
will often apply a wrong count anyway and silently drop or duplicate a line; the
failure then lands in the middle of a Buildroot build, far from the edit.

## Verification

- The patch applies with no fuzz and no offset against pristine `partclone-0.3.47`
  (`patch -p1 --dry-run`).
- `make partclone-dirclean && make partclone` in `fssourcex64` re-extracts,
  re-patches, re-configures and rebuilds it to a linked `partclone.restore`. The
  function in the extracted tree is the new one.
- Each of the four assertions was driven red by restoring the defect it covers:
  `exit(0)` back (2 red), the `return` deleted (2 red), the computed `sprintf`
  format back (1 red), a stale hunk count (1 red).
- `tests/run-all.sh`: 24 passed, 0 failed.

**Verification gap:** this has not been run against a real deploy with a full
`/tmp`. The path that was changed is the failure path, which is exactly the one a
normal lab run never takes. What is proven is that the patched source compiles
and that the success path is byte-identical in behavior to before.

FOS is not branched, so this init runs against 1.5 and 1.6 servers alike. The
wire format written to `/tmp/status.fog` is unchanged.

author: prawkonaraz100
body:
Implements NEWSROOM-N5-005 by reusing the existing IndexNow queue/submission pipeline.

Scope:
- after-commit newsroom IndexNow event + listener
- first publish -> local EVENT_CREATED
- substantive public update / republish -> local EVENT_UPDATED
- archive stays silent because canonical detail remains 200 and current renderer/robots do not change
- withdraw -> local EVENT_DELETED only after committed withdrawn/410 state
- restore-to-review stays silent; later publish queues updated
- published slug change queues old redirect path and new canonical as updated
- draft/scheduled-before-time/noindex/public-gate-off do not queue
- outer rollback creates no submission row
- listener isolates queue failures from the publication transaction

Protocol stays unchanged:
- existing IndexNowSubmissionService still sends only host + key + optional keyLocation + urlList
- local event_type is queue metadata only and is explicitly regression-tested as absent from HTTP payload
- existing dedupe/debounce/retry/safety filters remain the only queue/submission pipeline

No docs changed in this implementation PR. Docs will be synchronized only after verified merge and post-merge Quality Gate.

author: mendestrading21
body:
## Contexte

Signalé par l'utilisateur après la fusion de V2.8 : la page Abonnements (livrée dans V2.3, déjà dans le code et la navigation) restait invisible dans son navigateur malgré un déploiement réussi. La cause n'avait rien à voir avec la page elle-même.

## Cause

`scripts/build-offline.mjs` génère `dist/sw.js` (service worker de l'app hors-ligne). Ses gestionnaires `install`/`activate` n'appelaient ni `self.skipWaiting()` ni `self.clients.claim()` : un nouveau déploiement restait « en attente » indéfiniment et un onglet déjà ouvert (ou l'app installée) continuait de servir l'ancien shell tant qu'il n'était pas entièrement fermé puis rouvert — un simple rechargement ne suffisait pas. Un utilisateur ayant l'app ouverte avant un lot pouvait donc ne jamais le voir, sans indice sur la raison.

## Changements

**`scripts/build-offline.mjs`** — `self.skipWaiting()` à l'installation, `self.clients.claim()` à l'activation.

**`src/main.tsx`** — distingue la toute première prise de contrôle (chargement normal, déjà à jour) d'un changement de contrôleur alors qu'un contrôleur existait déjà (vraie mise à jour pendant que l'onglet reste ouvert). Dispatche un événement (`finance:update-ready`) plutôt que de recharger directement.

**`src/swUpdateEvent.ts`** (nouveau) — nom de l'événement partagé entre `main.tsx` et `App.tsx` pour éviter toute dérive.

**`src/App.tsx`** — affiche un bandeau persistant (« Une nouvelle version de Finance est disponible. Recharger ») avec un bouton explicite, dans la vue déverrouillée uniquement. Sous-titre de la page Abonnements mentionne désormais « factures » et « charges récurrentes » pour la découvrabilité (la fonctionnalité — récurrence Nature « Charge » — couvrait déjà ce besoin, seule la formulation manquait).

**`tests/finance.spec.ts`** — nouveau test e2e simulant un second déploiement, isolé sur sa propre copie de `dist/` et son propre serveur HTTP (`node:http`) pour ne jamais partager de fichiers avec les autres tests exécutés en parallèle.

## Pourquoi deux commits de correctifs

Le premier correctif (rechargement automatique direct) a été relu indépendamment par l'agent `finance-verification`, qui a trouvé deux défauts réels avant publication :

1. **Rechargement silencieux** : le coffre ne vit qu'en mémoire (`vault.ts`), donc un rechargement automatique reverrouille systématiquement le coffre et perd toute saisie en cours, sans avertissement. Corrigé par le bandeau explicite décrit ci-dessus.
2. **Risque de collision** : le test mutait `dist/sw.js`/`dist/index.html` partagés avec le serveur utilisé par tous les autres tests, alors que `playwright.config.ts` a `fullyParallel: true` (ce que la CI utilise réellement). Corrigé par l'isolation décrite ci-dessus.

## Vérifications

- `pnpm run typecheck` : 0 erreur. `pnpm run test` : **135/135** (inchangé). `pnpm run build` : OK.
- `pnpm run test:e2e` : les 9 scénarios rejoués individuellement, tous verts.
- Double contrôle négatif sur le nouveau test (fichier d'avant le correctif restauré, rebuild, test rejoué → échec propre à ~15s ; correctif restauré → test repasse), reproduit indépendamment par le relecteur.
- Essai en parallélisme réel (`--workers=2`, configuration par défaut comme la CI) : les échecs observés dans ce bac à sable sont des plantages génériques de Chromium single-process déjà documentés ailleurs dans ce dépôt (erreurs dbus/SSL, « browser has been closed »), jamais une collision de contenu — aucune assertion du test PWA n'a échoué sur un contenu inattendu.
- Relu indépendamment par l'agent `finance-verification` (distinct de l'auteur), avec reproduction du contrôle négatif et des scénarios de cycle de vie du service worker.

Détail complet dans `docs/STATUS.md` (section « Correctif — mise à jour du service worker PWA »).

## Limites honnêtes

Aucune page « Factures » distincte n'a été créée : la fonctionnalité existante (récurrences classées « Charge », filtre dédié sur la page Abonnements) couvre déjà le besoin décrit (factures mensuelles récurrentes + extras occasionnels via Mon mois), seule la découvrabilité était en cause. À confirmer avec l'utilisateur que cela répond bien à sa demande.

author: hoelzl
body:
## Root cause

A build whose target set lacks the `recording` producer (e.g. `-T shared`) adds an **implicit** Recording-HTML execution per notebook to warm the executed-notebook cache for the consumer HTML it did request. That block in `NotebookFile.get_processing_operation` ignored the topic's `html="no"` flag, while the explicit output list (`output_specs`) honours it. So a deck with **no HTML outputs at all** — one that never executes in a full build and therefore has no HTTP-replay cassette by construction — was executed as soon as the target list was narrowed, and its unmatched requests went to the network live under the `new-episodes` replay mode. The failure then surfaced as a deterministic `[User Error]` on a deck that had "been building fine", with nothing pointing at the target list.

Why the full set was fine: with `speaker`/`recording` in `-T`, the producer is *explicit* and goes through `output_specs`, which drops HTML for `html="no"`, so the resolver has no implicit executions and nothing runs.

## Fix

Implicit cache-producer executions now skip `skip_html` topics (one condition). There is no HTML consumer such a run could serve, and the deck now behaves the same under every `-T` selection. Its non-HTML outputs are unaffected.

## Tests

`tests/core/test_implicit_execution_skip_html.py`, mirroring `Course.process_stage_for_target`'s iteration so what it collects is what a real build submits:
- control: without the flag the narrowed target set still schedules the implicit recording execution (the behaviour #890 pinned);
- regression: with `html="no"` nothing is scheduled in the producer stage (failed on the unfixed code with an `is_implicit_execution=True` op present);
- neighbour: a section mixing an `html="no"` topic with a normal one executes exactly the normal topic;
- the `html="no"` topic still produces its notebook output.

## Not in this PR

The issue's two hardening directions — replay-only cache repopulation (a warm-up run should report a cassette miss rather than fetch live) and a summary warning when a narrowed `-T` will execute what the full set replays — are recorded in `docs/claude/TODO.md` under "Cache repopulation should never fall through to live network (#871 residue)".

## Verification

- Deterministic tier: 8689 passed, 0 failed.
- `clm info spec-files` (`html` attribute row) updated.
- Adversarial review skipped: a one-condition change in `core/` with the control/regression/neighbour tests pinning both sides of the gate.

Fixes #871

author: krzysztof318
body:
Closes #1556

**People becomes the client's second built space.** `src/routing/spaces.ts` names `mail` and `people` in `implementedSpaces`, and the other five stay placeholders.

## The wire

`Client.Backend/src/contacts.ts` and `Client.Backend/src/contactCorrespondence.ts` reach the routes #1552 and #1553 built: the paged read of the asserted book and of the collected one, one contact, recording, promoting and erasing one, and the correlation of a person's addresses with the mail this caller already holds. Every answer is bounded and every field checked before it becomes a value a screen may render. A `404` on a route naming one person is `missing` rather than `unavailable`, because a contact no book in this caller's scope holds is something to let go of rather than to retry.

`pageArguments` is written out rather than composed with `URLSearchParams`: this package declares no browser API.

## The screens

`contactBook/` draws the book — a windowed `listbox` with a roving tabindex over the `--spacing-contact-row` token, the two-book pill, the count, and the per-book hint. Its rows answer a modifier-held click, a right-click and a long press **through the shared `contextMenu/` components #1633 built** rather than a second implementation, which is why `messageList/messageSelection.ts` moves to `contextMenu/rowSelection.ts` — it was already shared and was sitting in one list's directory.

`people/` draws the rest: `PeopleSpace` composes the two panes, the selection bar that replaces the toolbar while a selection is held, the new-contact dialog and the erasure confirmation; `PersonPage` draws who somebody is and the acts on the record; `RelationshipReading` and `PersonCorrespondence` draw what MailFathom and the mailbox have to say. Each of those three sections carries its own loading, empty and error state, so none of them blocks the rest of the page — which is what the issue asks of every section fed by children 2 and 3.

Below `--breakpoint-panes` the list and the person are one pane with a way back, and the new-contact control becomes the floating one the design draws there. No colour, spacing, radius or type size is written outside the token layer, and every user-visible string is a catalogue key in both `en.ts` and `pl.ts`.

## The grant

Reading the address book is its own grant and changing it a second. `shell/capabilities.ts` maps `readContacts` to `mailfathom.mail.contacts.read` and `writeContacts` to `mailfathom.mail.contacts.write`; the space is offered to a credential holding the first and to no other, and a credential without the second meets a book it may only read rather than controls that refuse.

## Writing to somebody

A `ComposerOpening` of kind `new` may now name recipients. Opening the composer while a message is already being written **adds** them to it rather than starting a second, and somebody already addressed is not written down twice.

## Held against the design

The screen was compared with the design project as images before this was finished — People at 1440×900, one person's page at 1440×900, and People at 390×844 under a coarse pointer — and the copy, the two book names (*Own* / *Collected*), the per-book hints, and the card headings are the project's own rather than this session's.

**What the design draws and no route backs is left undrawn rather than drawn inert**, and each of these is owed a correction to the design or a route of its own:

- the five toolbar actions beside *New contact* — *Write*, *Schedule a meeting*, *Merge duplicates*, *Import*, *Export*;
- *Export* on the selection bar, which the issue's acceptance names;
- *Propose a meeting* in the row menu, which the issue's acceptance names and which its own *Out of scope* covers — it navigates to Calendar, still a placeholder;
- the company and the role on a record, which `Contact` does not carry;
- the last-contact date and the *waiting on us* pill on a row, which the book's page does not carry;
- the suggested next action, the pattern chips, and the `OPEN` and `CASES` stats, which wait on the relationship-note run;
- the message count on a shared thread and the file size on a document, which the correlation route does not carry — the client shows the date it does carry instead.

`design/parity.json` names none of `people`, `people-collected` or `person`, so `scripts/capture-design.sh` refuses all three and the design half of the parity pairing is still owed; `frontend/design-parity/screens.json` carries the client half of each.

## Register

Two Material Symbols outlines join the family already registered — `add.svg` and `person_add.svg`, the same `wght300_24px` form at the revision the row records — and `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` moves from eighty-one outlines to eighty-three. No package was added and no pin moved.

author: shahar-biron
body:
## Summary
A user reported that after upgrading to v1.1.8 the control-plane's persistence PersistentVolumeClaim fails with a \"Permission Denied\" error, requiring them to manually patch in `securityContext.fsGroup: 10001` on the Deployment (a change lost on every Helm upgrade).

## Root cause
The control-plane container runs as non-root user `appuser` (uid 10001, see `control-plane/Dockerfile`), and the kubernetes-execution-backend runner Jobs/Deployments run as non-root user `runner` (uid 10002, see `docker/runner.Dockerfile`). Freshly-provisioned PVCs are typically owned by `root:root`, so without a pod-level `securityContext.fsGroup` matching the container's group, writes to the mounted volume fail.

## Fix
- `deploy/helm/dm-sql-to-falkordb/values.yaml` / `templates/deployment.yaml`: add `controlPlane.podSecurityContext` (defaults to `fsGroup: 10001`) applied at the pod level for the control-plane Deployment, plus an overridable `controlPlane.securityContext` for the container.
- Also fixed the same class of bug for dynamically-created kubernetes runner workloads (which mount a shared PVC at `/workspace` when `kubernetesRunner.sharedPvc.enabled`): added `kubernetesRunner.podSecurityContext` (defaults to `fsGroup: 10002`), wired through a new `CONTROL_PLANE_K8S_POD_FS_GROUP` env var / CLI flag to `control-plane/server`, which now sets `securityContext.fsGroup` on the pod spec of generated runner Jobs/Deployments.

Both settings are overridable in `values.yaml` if a deployment uses different UIDs/GIDs or wants to opt out.

## Testing
- `helm template` rendering confirms the pod `securityContext.fsGroup: 10001` and the `CONTROL_PLANE_K8S_POD_FS_GROUP` env var render correctly.
- `cargo check --release` and `cargo test --release runs::` pass (existing kubernetes execution backend unit tests updated for the new config field).

## Note
The user also mentioned FalkorDB-Browser's Helm chart has the same class of issue; that's a separate repository not present here, so it isn't addressed by this PR.

Co-Authored-By: Warp <agent@warp.dev>

author: jmwri
body:
## Summary
- `mkdir -p "$dir"` left the install directory's permissions to the caller's umask, so a looser umask (0002, or 0000 in some containers) left it group- or world-writable.
- Since replacing a file only needs write access to its containing directory, that let another local user or group member swap out a binary that updates and runs itself with this user's own privileges.

## Change
- Add `chmod 755 "$dir"` right after creating it, mirroring the explicit chmod already done for the binary itself two lines below.

## Test plan
- [x] `sh -n cmd/sitegen/assets/install.sh` (syntax)
- [x] `go test ./cmd/sitegen/...` — passes (the actual install.sh execution tests skip on Windows, but TestInstallScriptsParse and the rest pass)

author: markgoodbody-bit
body:
Bounded product proof only.

Question:
> Can a small source-bound representation make source dependence, attribution, contradiction, correction and unknowns easier to inspect without manufacturing certainty?

Current v0:
- no LLM/API/browser/agent;
- deterministic evidence engine;
- three pressure fixtures sourced from current THR work: flak ancestry, Hannibal translation/source criticism, R. Vale unresolved identity;
- fail-closed source/dependence/correction validation;
- text + static HTML "Show me why" output;
- preregistered proof/kill contract.

This is intentionally **not** an Open Agent submission or THR schema change.

Promotion requires a fourth ordinary case not used to design v0. If that requires ontology changes rather than data, stop.

```text
AGENT != PRODUCT
PRETTY GRAPH != BETTER EPISTEMICS
REPETITION != CORROBORATION
UNKNOWN != ABSENT
SOURCE_REPORT != DIRECT_OBSERVATION
```

author: kojoampia
body:
Closes **docs row 162**.

## The defect

`languagesValue: "4"` was a hand-written literal in all four catalogues, and `LANGUAGES` has four members — so it was **right by accident**. That is item 149's defect exactly; 149's number was also correct once.

⚠ **This list is more likely to move than the roles list was.** `language.constants.ts` carries a `jhipster-needle-i18n-language-constant` — *"JHipster will add/remove languages in this array"* — so it can change **without anyone editing it deliberately**. And the three i18n gates stay blind for the same structural reasons: `isTranslatable` strips digits, `catalogues.spec.ts` compares key sets and never a value against code, `brand-terms` is a denylist.

## What was decided

Item 149's shape, copied: the number leaves the catalogues (`"{{count}}"`) and is rendered from `LANGUAGES.length` through `[translateValues]`. `language.constants.ts` is **untouched** — the needle is preserved byte-identically.

Guards split the way 149 split them: render and per-locale derivation in `auth-shell.component.spec.ts`, source-of-truth agreement in a new `language.constants.spec.ts` beside the list.

## The trap this row did not name

`web/` declares the language set in **four** places, and the count reads only one. The dangerous direction is *a catalogue directory with no entry in `LANGUAGES`* — built, served, unselectable, uncounted — so the new spec asserts set equality **in both directions**.

⚠ **An honest qualification the author volunteered:** `catalogues.spec.ts:182` already pins `LOCALES` to exactly these four, so a fifth locale was *already* loud — for a product reason that says nothing about this panel. Row 162 is still real; it is just not the only thing that goes red.

## What the review found

**One blocking gap, fixed in `7f58374`: the fourth copy is `dayjs.ts`**, and the first commit's docstring — which sets out to map its own exclusions, naming the pipe and the webpack list with an argument for each — did not mention it. An omission, not a deliberate silence, and it is the copy whose failure is quietest.

**The review measured the cost rather than assuming it.** `main.component.ts:57` calls `dayjs.locale(lang)` on every switch, and an unregistered locale is a **no-op**: dayjs does **not** fall back to English, it stays on the previously selected language. Month names, weekday names (`format-medium-date.pipe`) and humanized durations then render in whatever was chosen before — per-locale, silent, invisible in English testing.

Guarded off `dayjs.Ls`, dayjs's own registry, so nothing is hand-kept. **Verified red-first:** adding a language with no dayjs import fires it by name.

**Two smaller findings, also fixed:**

- **The locale-shape regex failed its own stated standard.** It allowed one subtag, while `generator-jhipster` 8.1.0's `languageTag` list includes four script+region forms — `az-Latn-az`, `kr-Latn-kr`, `uz-Cyrl-uz`, `uz-Latn-uz` — all refused. The comment beside it says refusing a legitimate locale is "a guard that punishes the correct change"; widened to two subtags, still refusing a needle written as a string.
- **A template comment asserted a property the code no longer had** — *"three of the four describe the product rather than counting anything"*. Two do now. Corrected, and it says why: **a comment describing a count is itself a count**, and goes stale the same way.

**One nuance the review added to the author's mutation report, worth knowing before anyone weakens the spec.** "Exactly 2 red per locale" holds only when the literal *disagrees* with the count. Reverting one locale to `"4"` — the realistic regression — gives **1 red**, because `"4" === String(LANGUAGES.length)` **today**, which is the coincidence this row is about. **The template check (`toContain('{{count}}')`) is the load-bearing guard**, not the rendered check.

**Verified sound otherwise:** `LANGUAGES` is clean (the needle is a `//` comment inside the array literal and cannot inflate `.length`); emptying it fires **both** vacuity guards and `it.each([])` errors outright rather than running zero cases; `['en']` with a stale `"4"` gives 3 red, so it is not vacuous at n=1; an orphan `i18n/pt/` fires set-equality naming `"pt"`; item 149's `rolesValue` coverage survived the spec rewrite.

## Gates

**102 suites / 1143 tests / 0 skipped** with `ng build` first (base 101/1124). Lint and `prettier --check` clean. Built `target/classes/static/i18n/*.json` carry `"languagesValue":"{{count}}"` in all four.

## Outstanding

- **Not exercised:** no browser; the merged catalogue's rendering on a served page is verified at roll time.
- **Assumed:** that "Languages" on the panel means *locales the portal is served in*. `LANGUAGES` is the only list that could mean it, and the label sits beside three other portal facts.
- **Left alone deliberately:** `recordsValue` and `rostersValue` are product claims, not counts — the row says so, and the new spec now asserts they render verbatim so a later pass cannot quietly "derive" them.

author: raulmoracode
body:
## Summary

When the window is resized to its minimum size while on the **Packages** tab, a black / unpainted strip appeared at the bottom of the window and the content looked pushed up.

### Root cause

The three columns (All / Formulae / Casks) had a fixed `.frame(minHeight: 520)`, so the detail `VStack` could not distribute the leftover vertical space. The extra space below the cards was left unpainted, letting the window's dark background show through as a black band.

### Fix

- Removed the fixed `minHeight: 520` on each column's list area and replaced it with `maxHeight: .infinity`.
- Made each column and the columns `HStack` fill the available height (`maxHeight: .infinity`).

The columns now shrink and stretch with the window height (the lists are still scrollable), so no leftover space remains at the bottom.

### Notes
- The list areas keep their scrolling behavior since they are constrained by the window height.

author: brunoamaral
body:
## Problem

Registry-ID lookups missed trials that are in the database, for two reasons.

- **IDs written in free text were never parsed.** OCTOPUS (trial 519) lists its EudraCT number `2021-003034-37` only in `secondary_id`, so `eudract=2021-003034-37` returned nothing. On dev, 1,285 trials have a registry ID in `secondary_id` that isn't in `identifiers`.
- **Stored IDs keep their source's format, and the filters compared exact strings.**
	- A value stored as `euctr: EUCTR2020-004505-32-DE` can't be found by `eudract=2020-004505-32`.
	- On dev, only 79 of 926 stored EudraCT numbers and 285 of 346 CTIS numbers could be found by their plain number.
	- Prod example: `eudract=2020-004505-32` returned trial 6975 but not 4550, which is the same STHENOS trial.

This covers item 2 of the WHO/ICTRP enhancement request, plus the larger defect found while verifying it. It follows #874.

## Changes

- **`Trials.identifiers_normalized`** is a derived list of `"type:VALUE"` strings, for example `["eudract:2021-003034-37", "isrctn:ISRCTN14048364"]`.
	- It's registered in `NORMALIZED_TRIAL_FIELDS`, so `save()`, `backfill_trial_normalized_fields` and the admin recompute action keep it current.
	- GIN index: `trials_ids_norm_gin_idx`.
	- `identifiers` is unchanged. It stays the raw per-registry record the importers match on.
- **`normalize_trial_identifiers`** (`gregory/utils/trial_identifiers.py`) sorts its inputs by how much to trust them:
	- **Always counted:** every `identifiers` key except `org_study_id`, plus ClinicalTrials.gov secondary IDs typed `EUDRACT_NUMBER`, `CTIS` or `REGISTRY`.
	- **Free text, dropped only when a trusted ID of the same type differs:** `secondary_id`, `org_study_id`, and untyped or `OTHER` entries.
	- **Skipped:** grant-typed entries (`NIH`, `OTHER_GRANT`, …).
	- Every value goes through `extract_identifiers`, so a value's own format decides its type.
- **The parser recognises more registries.**
	- New: Dutch (`NL-OMON…`, `NL####`, `NTR…`), Peru (`PER-…`), Lebanon (`LBCTR…`), the WHO Universal Trial Number (`U1111-…`) and JAPIC (`JapicCTI-…`). The `jRCT` pattern and old-format `CTRI` IDs are widened.
	- The `NL` pattern takes exactly 4 digits, so Dutch ethics-committee dossier numbers (`NL67805.068.18`, 453 of them in dev secondary IDs) aren't mistaken for trial IDs.
	- ClinicalTrials.gov sends JAPIC numbers bare; one rule based on the entry's domain maps them onto the same ID.
- **`Trials.ctg_secondary_ids`** stores ClinicalTrials.gov's `secondaryIdInfos` exactly as sent. `[]` means none listed; NULL means not fetched yet.
	- The importer now keeps it, through a shared `ClinicalTrialsGovAPI.extract_secondary_ids`. The `secondary_id` text is unchanged.
	- `backfill_trial_secondary_ids_from_ctgov` fills existing rows.
- **Filters `nct`, `eudract`, `euct`, `ctis` and `identifiers`** keep today's exact comparison on the stored keys, OR'd with a match on `identifiers_normalized`.
	- Results are therefore a superset of today's by construction, including before the backfill runs.
	- An ID's format decides what it matches, whichever of these parameters it arrives in.
	- `identifiers=` now accepts any recognised registry, for example `ISRCTN14048364`.
- **Output:** `identifiers_normalized` appears in the API trial serializer, the MCP `compact_trial` payload and the XLSX export, with a Glossary entry. `ctg_secondary_ids` stays internal.
- **MCP guidance:** the registry-ID rule describes the broader matching, and `fields_read` for the ID filters is `["identifiers", "secondary_id", "ctg_secondary_ids"]`.

**Behaviour change:** a lookup can return more than one row when the same trial was imported from two registries and hasn't been merged. For example, `eudract=2020-004505-32` returns both 4550 and 6975. Merging duplicates is a separate project.

## Verification (dev DB, read-only)

- **Findability:** a simulation with the new normalizer finds every stored EudraCT and CTIS number by its plain number. Before, the dev audit found 79 of 926 and 285 of 346.
- **Spot checks:**
	- `eudract=2021-003034-37` → 519;
	- `eudract=2020-004505-32` → 4550 and 6975;
	- `ctis=2023-507431-37-00` → 4550;
	- `identifiers=ISRCTN14048364` → 519.
- **Article text:** across 53,054 article titles and summaries, the new patterns add 23 matches. All are genuine once the dossier numbers are excluded.
- **Query plan:** with the index built before the column is filled, as the migration and backfill do, `eudract=` with three IDs uses a BitmapOr of `trials_ueudract_idx` and `trials_ids_norm_gin_idx`, in 6 ms.

## Docs

- **`docs/02.1-database-tables-and-fields.md`:** rows for `identifiers_normalized` and `ctg_secondary_ids`, and an updated `identifiers` row.
- **`docs/03-api-and-rss-feeds.md`:** a new "Registry identifier filters" section (accepted formats, sources, format decides, possible duplicate rows) and the new output field.
- **`docs/07-mcp-server.md`:** the ID parameters, `fields_read` and the output field.
- **`docs/trials-field-normalization.md`:** a new section on `identifiers_normalized` covering sources, trust levels, the canonical format, the JAPIC rule and known gaps.
- **Also updated:** the filter help text. `schema.yml` is regenerated.

## Tests

- **Parser:** the new registries, labelled tokens (`EudraCT No.: …`), dossier numbers that must not match, and the non-ID secondary IDs from a real ICTRP export.
- **Normalizer:** trust levels, the `org_study_id` clash rule (trial 30842's foreign NCT), typed ClinicalTrials.gov entries, skipped grant types, the JAPIC rule, and non-string JSON values.
- **Model and importer:** the field is computed on create and on `save(update_fields=[...])` for each input, and the ClinicalTrials.gov importer stores `ctg_secondary_ids`, including `[]`.
- **Filters:** existing tests are unchanged (only added to). New tests cover format-decides lookups, `identifiers=` for ISRCTN, DRKS and UTN, and NULL rows matching through the old comparison.
- **Importer regression:**
	- the OCTOPUS fixture from #874 gets `["eudract:2021-003034-37", "isrctn:ISRCTN14048364"]` and is found by `eudract=2021-003034-37`;
	- a second fixture, trimmed from a real ICTRP export with contact fields removed, checks that free-text secondary IDs add nothing.
- **Other:** the backfill command against a mocked API, and the export's Glossary entry.

Results, from a throwaway container with this branch mounted:

- **Full `pytest`:** 3,527 passed.
- **`mcp-server` pytest:** 235 passed.
- **`manage.py check --database default`, `makemigrations --check`, and `migrate` on a brand-new empty database:** clean.

## Deploy

1. **Django image.** Migration `0101` adds two nullable columns (metadata-only) and the GIN index.
2. **Fill the derived field from stored data.** Fast, with no external calls; lookups improve right away:
   `docker exec gregory python manage.py backfill_trial_normalized_fields --field identifiers`
3. **Fetch the typed secondary IDs from ClinicalTrials.gov.** About 135 requests at the default batch size of 100; each save also recomputes that trial's `identifiers_normalized`:
   `docker exec gregory python manage.py backfill_trial_secondary_ids_from_ctgov`
4. **`gregory-mcp` image.**

After deploy, `search_trials(eudract="2021-003034-37")` should return trial 519.

body:
## Change

Transient transport and server failures after visible output now use preserved-turn continuation. The normal replay veto previously stopped those turns, while manually typing continue worked.

body:
## Intent

Finish the Tambiz project: the manual rewritten against the app as it now is, a licence, and a README worth pinning. Nothing about the app's behaviour may change in this task; if a test fails, something went wrong (no source code under src/ is touched).

1. The manual, rewritten and kept in the repository. The old 100-page manual described screens that were deleted (class roll, advisers, groups and members pages, private links, release machinery, group codes) and every screenshot was of a version that no longer exists. Rewrite it against the app as it stands: seven coordinator tabs (Data, Judges, Scoring sheet, Progress, Results, Judge profiles, Close the event), the judge's two screens, one workbook in, two files out. Keep the captain's style, asked for by name after his FIN1209 activity sheet: numbered steps in green circles, one action per step, a screenshot under almost every step with a caption, "type exactly this" boxes, and an "if it goes wrong" note where things go wrong. Cover, and no more than: (1) what Tambiz is and how it thinks: event per year, groups, judges, two halves, what submitted means, what closing means; (2) preparing the workbook: staff build their own file from the template and do NOT upload the registrar's export; one Students sheet and one Judges sheet, a worked example built a few rows at a time, checking formulas, and the honest note that a wrong email and a wrong section import silently; (3) setting up: sign in, the event, the scoring sheet wording, the upload, the judge sign-in slips, opening judging; (4) how a score becomes a grade with a worked example through to the FEU letter band; (5) the judge's side click by click with phone screenshots; (6) the evening: progress, correcting a score with a reason, what stops the event closing, closing it; (7) results, individual grades, judge profiles, the workbook; (8) the two files and sending emails through Power Automate; (9) running and looking after it: what it is made of, accounts, changes reaching the live site, passwords, the yearly cycle, the month-before checklist, troubleshooting as symptom and fix, keeping records, handing it to a successor; (10) what is not built yet, honestly. Every screenshot taken from the running app after the finish landed; nothing from the old version survives. Keep it at docs/manual/: HTML source (manual.html), its images, the rendered Tambiz-Manual.pdf, and a short README with the render command so a successor can rebuild it. Screenshots were taken from a local production build on a scratch PGlite database with invented data (Tambiz 2028: 6 groups, 18 students, 4 judges; example criterion wording is invented and labelled as such), never the live app or Neon. The committed PDF and JPEG images are deliberate binary artifacts. A separate private copy of the manual with account details filled in is produced outside the repository and never committed or uploaded; the public manual.html marks the two places with <!--PRIVATE-ACCOUNTS--> and <!--PRIVATE-WHO--> comments for that purpose. Power Automate screens are not pictured (no FEU Microsoft 365 access) and the manual says so with "Confirm on first use" boxes, as it does for Vercel/Neon dashboard steps.

2. A licence: LICENSE with the MIT Licence, copyright "2026 Benjamin C. Sotelo" — MIT so another department or university can take this and run their own awarding without asking. A short NOTICE file, referenced from the README, making unambiguous that the MIT grant covers the code, not the marks: the FEU seal, FEU wordmark and IABF crest are Far Eastern University's property, included for use by FEU, and anyone reusing the software must replace them. (The brief said the marks are in public/; they actually live in src/assets/brand/, and NOTICE names the real files.)

3. A README worth pinning on the captain's GitHub profile: one line saying what it is (judging, results and grades for the annual Tambiz awarding at FEU Manila); a screenshot near the top copied into the repository (docs/images/sign-in.jpg, from the finish screenshots); what it does in five or six bullets in a reader's language; how to run it locally and what it needs (Node, a Postgres connection string or the local PGlite fallback); how it is deployed (Vercel and Neon, both free); a link to the manual in docs/manual/; the licence and the marks notice; no badges, no emoji headings, no marketing. Deployment detail from the old README (setup steps, env vars, preview isolation, seed passwords, emergency reset) is kept because AGENTS.md names README.md as the deployment guide. AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md symlinks to it) gains two lines pointing at the manual and the marks notice.

## What Changed
- Adds the rewritten coordinator's and maintainer's manual in `docs/manual/`: an A4-print HTML source (`manual.html`), 87 fresh screenshots and spreadsheet renders taken from invented Tambiz 2028 data, the rendered `Tambiz-Manual.pdf`, and a README with the Chrome headless rebuild command and how to retake the pictures. `docs/how-to-run-an-event.md` is cut down to a pointer to it.

The deployment details from the old README are kept. `AGENTS.md` gains two lines, one pointing at the manual and one at the marks notice. Nothing under `src/` changes.

author: diegomatheuss
body:
Primeira rodada de robustez real para fontes longas e importação YouTube.

### YouTube
- Alinha metadata/download ao limite de **7 horas**.
- Feature flag explícita na API e no worker.
- Local/homologação usam `YOUTUBE_ENABLED=true` por padrão; produção continua configurável.
- Suporta youtube.com/www/m.youtube.com/youtu.be.
- Mantém SSRF/DNS guard, HTTPS, sem cookies/login/playlists.
- Metadata/download ganham retries e timeouts configuráveis.
- Restrição/indisponibilidade é diferenciada de falha transitória.
- Pré-validação de tamanho quando o YouTube fornece `filesize`/`filesize_approx`.
- Diagnóstico manual `python -m cortes_worker.youtube_check <url>` para smoke test real sem depender de URL fixa no CI.

### Podcasts de 4–7h
- Working master evita transcode integral quando vídeo já é H.264/HEVC/MPEG-4 <=1080p: faz remux/cópia de stream de vídeo.
- Timeouts/deadlines de normalize e extração de áudio ampliados.
- Seleção de IA passa a usar janelas long-form configuráveis (15 min + overlap por padrão).
- Candidatos de todas as janelas são ordenados por score antes da segunda revisão, evitando viés para o começo do episódio.
- Limite de arquivo permanece 30 GB.

### Testes/UX
- Testa exatamente 7h, rejeita 7h+1s e tamanho >30 GB.
- Testes usam o limite atual de lease.
- Mensagens amigáveis para YouTube/fonte restrita/download/duração.
- Modal de login distingue arquivo de link YouTube.
- README/status e `docs/YOUTUBE_LONGFORM.md` atualizados.

Este PR não declara homologação externa concluída: o smoke/download real ainda deve ser executado no ambiente alvo com uma URL pública escolhida pelo usuário.

Substituído pelo PR #24, que consolidou estas mudanças sobre o main já atualizado com o E2E do #21.

### Summary
`GitService` did two unrelated jobs: it handled the bare repositories the local version control server holds, and it checked repositories out to work on the copy. This splits the bare half into `BareGitRepositoryService`, which takes `GitService` from 1336 lines to 871 and off the large-class list. Pure move, no behaviour change.

### Checklist
#### General
- [x] I tested **all** changes and their related features with **all** corresponding user types on a test server.
- [x] Language: I followed the [guidelines for inclusive, diversity-sensitive, and appreciative language](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/language).
- [x] I chose a title conforming to the [naming conventions for pull requests](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/development-process#pr-naming-conventions).

#### Server
- [x] **Important**: I implemented the changes with a [very good performance](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/performance) and prevented too many (unnecessary) and too complex database calls.
- [x] I **strictly** followed the principle of **data economy** for all database calls.
- [x] I **strictly** followed the [server coding and design guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/server-development) and the [REST API guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/rest-api).
- [x] The existing tests move with the code they cover; no behaviour changed, so no new assertions were needed.
- [x] I documented the Java code using JavaDoc style.

#### Changes affecting Programming Exercises
- [x] **High priority**: I tested **all** changes and their related features with **all** corresponding user types on a test server configured with the **integrated lifecycle setup** (LocalVC and LocalCI).
- [x] I tested **all** changes and their related features with **all** corresponding user types on a test server configured with **LocalVC** and **Jenkins**.

### Motivation and Context
Follow-up to #13873, where the review noted that `GitService` had grown past a thousand lines and that the fix made it longer still.

The class was not merely large, it was two classes sharing a file:

- **bare repositories** — the ones LocalVC serves out of the local VC base path. Opened, health-checked, copied. No working tree, ever.
- **working copies** — clones Artemis makes under the clone path to read and modify. Checkout, commit, stage, pull, push, reset, list files, delete.

The seam is clean rather than convenient:

| | |
|---|---|
| Bare block calls methods that stay behind | none |
| Remainder calls into the bare block | 1 (`getCommitInfos`) |
| `repoClonePath`, git identity, in-progress clone map | used **only** by the remainder |
| `localVCBasePath`, `defaultBranch` | config, available to both |

### Description
**`BareGitRepositoryService`** (new, `localvc/service/`, extends `AbstractGitService` like `GitService` does) takes `getBareRepository` (both overloads), `getExistingBareRepository`, `isBareRepositoryHealthy`, `copyBareRepositoryWithoutHistory`, `copyBareRepositoryWithHistory`, `buildAndPublishBareRepository`, `verifyRefUpdateResult`, `logCommits`, `getFirstCommitPersonIdent` and `buildCleanTreeFromSource`.

`getCommitInfos` moves with them. It opens the repository where it lies rather than checking it out — its javadoc claimed otherwise, and that is corrected — so leaving it in `GitService` would have been the single thing keeping the two services coupled. Moving it means neither service depends on the other.

**Callers.** Because `getLastCommitHash` and `getFirstCommitWithMessage` live in the shared parent, most callers swap one collaborator for the other rather than taking both:

- swap: `AbstractVersionControlService`, `LocalVCService`, `GitRepositoryExportService`, `ExerciseReviewService`, `ExerciseReviewVersionChangeService`, `ExerciseReviewRepositoryService`, `DeimosAnalysisService`
- both: `RepositoryService` and `ProgrammingExerciseParticipationService`, which genuinely use checkouts and bare repositories

**Tests.** The Spring base classes gain a `bareGitRepositoryServiceSpy` so the integration tests can keep stubbing the moved methods. `GitServiceRepositoryCopyTest` and `GitServiceRefUpdateResultTest` now exercise the new service, so they are renamed to `BareGitRepositoryCopyTest` and `BareGitRepositoryRefUpdateResultTest`.

**Quality gate.** `GitService` drops off the large-class list, so the count goes from 18 to 17 and `max_large_classes` is tightened back to 17 — the ratchet the workflow comment asks for.

### Steps for Testing
This is a pure move: no endpoint, no payload and no stored state changes, so there is nothing new to click through. What is worth confirming on a test server is that repository handling still behaves, since every call site moved:

Prerequisites:
- 1 Instructor
- 1 Student
- 1 Programming Exercise on an integrated code lifecycle setup

1. As the student, start the programming exercise. The participation is created and the repository is reachable.
2. Clone the student repository, push a commit, and confirm the build runs.
3. Open the commit history of the participation (this is `getCommitInfos`, which changed owner).
4. As the instructor, export the student repository and import the exercise into another course.

You can manage test servers using [Helios](https://helios.aet.cit.tum.de/). Check environment statuses in the [environment list](https://helios.aet.cit.tum.de/repo/69562331/environment/list). To deploy to a test server, go to the [CI/CD](https://helios.aet.cit.tum.de/repo/69562331/ci-cd) page, find your PR or branch, and trigger the deployment.

body:
#### Describe the changes you have made in this PR

`main` CI is red after two green PRs merged back to back: [#6307](https://github.com/Tracer-Cloud/opensre/pull/6307) made `record_install_analytics` in `install.sh` pass `OPENSRE_INSTALL_MARKER_STATE="$install_marker_state"`, and [#6313](https://github.com/Tracer-Cloud/opensre/pull/6313) (based on the commit before #6307) added `test_macos_warmup_does_not_consume_installer_analytics`, which calls `record_install_analytics` without first running `snapshot_install_marker`. Under the installer's `set -euo pipefail` that is `install_marker_state: unbound variable` and the function aborts.

Fix in the installer, not the test: `record_install_analytics` now uses `${install_marker_state:-unknown}`. `unknown` is the documented "check was inconclusive" value, so a record step that runs without a snapshot reports exactly that instead of crashing the installer or fabricating `absent`. The test's fake binary now also logs the marker env var and pins `unknown` for the no-snapshot path.

### Demo/Screenshot for feature changes and bug fixes

Failing on `main` (`dac688001`):

```text
FAILED tests/cli/test_install_sh_path.py::test_macos_warmup_does_not_consume_installer_analytics[0]
  AssertionError: Preparing OpenSRE for first launch...
    bash: line 1052: install_marker_state: unbound variable
```

After the fix: `tests/cli/test_install_sh_path.py tests/cli/test_install_matrix.py` — 68 passed. `make pre-push`: 9/9.

---

## Code Understanding and AI Usage

**Did you use AI assistance (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) to write any part of this code?**
- [ ] No, I wrote all the code myself
- [x] Yes, I used AI assistance (continue below)

**If you used AI assistance:**
- [x] I have reviewed every single line of the AI-generated code
- [x] I can explain the purpose and logic of each function/component I added
- [x] I have tested edge cases and understand how the code handles them
- [x] I have modified the AI output to follow this project's coding standards and conventions

**Explain your implementation approach:**

A semantic merge conflict between two independently green PRs. The alternative was to make the test call `snapshot_install_marker` first, but that would leave a helper that crashes the whole installer if ever invoked out of order under `set -u`; defaulting to the documented inconclusive value is the safer contract and keeps the analytics semantics honest.
