author: hjewkes
body:
## Summary

TP-118 proposed a missing `tailTranscript(path, turns)` export. That premise was partly wrong. `readRecentSessionTurns` (0.3.0) already does the bounded tail read that relay and agent-chat each duplicate. It reads from the end, skips a partly written final record, reports byte and turn truncation, and observes the model and branch. agent-chat's `readTurns` is effectively the same code. This PR adds the two gaps relay actually has, and no new tail function:

- **`projection: "text"`** on `ReadRecentSessionTurnsOptions`. It keeps only user and assistant text blocks and drops tool calls, tool results, thinking and system rows. It applies `maxTurns` after that filter. Without it, a caller that filters afterwards gets fewer turns than it asked for. The default `"activity"` is unchanged.
- **`claudeSourceFromPath(path, namespace)`**. relay gets a transcript path from the agent-chat roster, not a cwd plus session id. For `agent-<id>.jsonl` the helper uses the agent ID as the native ID.
- **Model fix:** `model` now skips `<synthetic>`, the placeholder Claude Code writes on locally generated API-error rows. agent-chat's `observedModel` has the same bug and can hand teleport `--model <synthetic>`.

Left out deliberately:

- **Denial extraction.** `summarizeSession` already keeps native `toolDenialKind` evidence apart from generic `is_error`. Porting agent-chat's `findDenials`, which counts every errored tool result as a denial, would reintroduce the known misclassification.
- **Stripping injected context** from user text (`isMeta` rows, command wrappers). That belongs to TP-108.

## Measured cost

On a real 50 MB transcript with the text projection and `maxTurns: 20`, median of 10 runs:

| Window | Time | Spoken turns returned |
|---|---|---|
| 256 KB | 1.1 ms | 11 |
| 1 MiB | 3.4 ms | 20 |
| 4 MiB | 11.6 ms | 20 |

Reading and parsing the whole file took 146 ms. Across 40 real transcripts of 5 to 50 MB, 20 spoken turns needed 247 KB to 3 MB of tail. So relay's current 256 KB window usually returns fewer turns than requested. The README recommends 4 MiB.

## Test plan

- [x] New scenario tests: spoken-turn counting after activity is dropped, fewer turns than requested, empty file, partly written final record, subagent sidechain addressed by path, a 4 MB+ file read through a 16 KB window, Codex messages only, invalid projection, `<synthetic>` model, `claudeSourceFromPath` cases.
- [x] Mutations checked: slicing before the filter, ignoring the projection in the Claude renderer, and dropping the synthetic skip each fail a named test.
- [x] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm dag:check && pnpm docs:build` all pass (989 tests).

author: ratoaq2
body:
## Summary

The built-in rule set was small and some patterns changed correct dialogue. This branch adds a large set of OCR, tidy and spam rules, keeps each pattern as narrow as it must be, and pins the behaviour with regression cases. It builds on the tooling work that is already on `main` (#68).

## Changes

New cleaning rules

- Add OCR rules for all languages, for English and for Portuguese (`cleanit-ocr.yml`, `cleanit-ocr.en.yml`, `cleanit-ocr.pt.yml`).
- Add tidy rules. They include `drop-orphan-dash-lines[tidy]`, which removes a line that holds only a speaker dash after an SDH bracket is removed.
- Add pt-BR spam rules:
  - `drop-ads-and-credits-regex[no-spam:pt]` for upload credits, for example `Legenda enviada por: <nick>`.
  - `drop-sync-credits[no-spam:pt]` for sync and resync credits, for example `Sincronia para 720p: <nick>` and `Resinc: <nick>`.
  - `drop-anti-piracy-notices[no-spam:pt]` for anti-piracy notices. The words `pirata` and `crime organizado` are also common in dialogue, so the rule needs them together in one entry.

Patterns that changed correct text were made narrower

- `replace-O-to-0-in-numbers[ocr]` needs two or more digits, so `O2` (oxygen) stays.
- `replace-V-to-v-mid-word[ocr]` is a word list, so names like TiVo and DeVille stay.
- `replace-l-|1-in-contractions[ocr:en]` does not read `1's` as `I's`, so `Number 1's` stays.
- `fix-broken-c-cedilla[ocr:pt]` does not match across a line break, so two-line entries do not merge.
- `fix-l-to-i-words[ocr:pt]` only matches lowercase `nolte`, so the surname `Nolte` stays.

Tests

- Replace the flat sample files with self-contained cases in `tests/data/cases/<slug>/`. Each case has `meta.yaml`, an input file and an expected file. The language comes from the file name, as it does for real files.
- Add a regression case for each pattern listed above.
- Add examples to the rules, which include negative examples. Each example is also a test.

Project setup

- Add `CLAUDE.md` with project instructions.
- Add a Claude Code hook that runs ruff and mypy after a Python file is edited.

## Testing

```
bash scripts/test.sh
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy cleanit
```

The new pt-BR spam rules were also run against a local corpus of real subtitle files. In the pt-BR files they removed 64 more entries than before. All 64 entries were credits or notices.

author: matiasbenedetto
body:
Core changes some font names when it treats CSS values as plain text. For example, `O'Reilly Sans` produces an invalid unquoted `@font-face` descriptor. This PR preserves the decoded name through font validation, storage, resolution, and CSS output.

Trac ticket: https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/63568

```diff
-@font-face{font-family:O'Reilly Sans; ... }
+@font-face{font-family:"O'Reilly Sans"; ... }
```

The fix also preserves commas inside quoted names, significant spaces, percent sequences, CSS escapes, and punctuation. It keeps a named family such as `"serif"` distinct from the generic keyword `serif`.

**Implementation.** The new internal class `WP_CSS_Font_Family` parses CSS values and serializes decoded names.

- `parse_list()` returns typed entries for named families, generic families, and reserved keywords. It consumes the complete value.
- `parse_list_with_plain_names()` adds compatibility for plain names that earlier WordPress versions accepted, including `O'Reilly Sans` and `O"Reilly Sans`.
- `parse_descriptor_name()` selects the first family for a face, including the supported legacy list input.
- `serialize_name()` emits a quoted CSS string with escapes for quotes, backslashes, control characters, and HTML-sensitive characters.
- `serialize_list()` preserves family order and the distinction between names and generic keywords.

The parser uses anchored regular expressions for identifier bytes and `strspn()` for hexadecimal digits. It uses no recursion. The serializer replaces only characters that require an escape. The KSES splitter copies complete declaration substrings and respects quotes and escapes.

The `generic()` parser accepts only `kai`, `fangsong`, `khmer-mul`, and `nastaliq`. It validates the decoded argument before it emits CSS. This prevents an escaped argument from introducing a second declaration. Tests cover valid escaped arguments and rejection through both the parser and REST.

The font utilities, resolver, face output, collection schema, and both REST controllers use the shared parser. Invalid REST values return a 400 error. Invalid face values produce a diagnostic and no face output. Core loads the parser before KSES.

`safecss_filter_attr()` uses the font grammar to accept punctuation inside valid names. Other values still use the current safety checks. The `safecss_filter_attr_allow_css` filter remains in the path.

**Compatibility.** Named families now use quotes in canonical CSS. Generic families retain their keyword form. The preset can contain `"ACME, Sans", sans-serif`, while its face descriptor contains only `"ACME, Sans"`.

The serializer escapes `<`, `>`, and `&` so names survive HTML output and KSES post filters. Backslashes use hexadecimal escapes because `wp_kses_no_null()` can remove a literal backslash before zeros. Short hexadecimal escapes retain their terminator spaces.

Font face comparison keys use decoded names so equivalent CSS escapes identify the same face. Percent sequences protect punctuation that can otherwise change key boundaries or post titles. Ordinary names such as `Open Sans` retain their previous key format. This PR performs no bulk data migration.

A value with additional CSS syntax, such as `"A"; color:red`, fails REST validation. In a style attribute, `font-family:"A;B";color:red` remains two permitted declarations. The semicolon inside the quoted name stays part of that name.

**Client dependency and limits.** Core accepts valid CSS without the special escape scheme from [Gutenberg PR #76782](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/76782). Upload clients must serialize metadata names with commas, parentheses, or angle brackets to preserve each name as one CSS string.

Display-name storage remains outside this fix. The family controller still applies `sanitize_text_field()` to the display name in `post_title`. A display name with markup can therefore lose that text, independently of the CSS identity.

**Current automated results.** These checks cover commit `7c82a49985`.

| Command or check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run test:php -- --group fonts,kses,restapi-global-styles` | Passed: 1,169 tests, 3,698 assertions. |
| `npm run test:php -- -c tests/phpunit/multisite.xml --group fonts,kses,restapi-global-styles` | Passed: 1,170 tests, 3,701 assertions. |
| `npm run typecheck:php -- --no-progress` | Passed: no errors. |
| PHPCS on the five files in the latest commit | Passed: no errors or warnings. |
| PHP compatibility checks on those files, with `testVersion 7.4-` | Passed. |
| `npm run test:php` | 26,611 tests, 4,561,027 assertions; one failure, 86 PHPUnit deprecation warnings, and 44 skipped tests. |

The full-suite failure is `Tests_Script_Modules_WpScriptModules::test_default_script_module_files_exist`. The local environment lacks `src/wp-includes/js/dist/script-modules/dashboard-init/index.js`.

The same test fails identically with the source code from PR base `74bb9334f5129ad64bab5b630157067bf5f24931`. The control run restored all eight modified pre-existing source files through temporary Docker mounts. It retained the same local build assets. The test and script-module registration code do not differ from the base. The failure therefore does not originate in this PR.

A comparison across 60,516 inputs checked the three parser entry points, name serialization, and the KSES splitter against the previous PR revision. The only differences were the intended rejections of invalid `generic()` arguments. The corpus included random input, every byte value, and long names, lists, comments, and escape sequences.

The regression suites cover REST storage and responses, repeated saves, duplicate detection, legacy records, generated presets, face output, and injection attempts. The new invalid-argument tests failed before the validation fix.

**Browser evidence and limits.** The earlier implementation report records Chrome 143 checks at revision `a5795c3`, with Twenty Twenty-Five and a local DM Sans fixture. A REST-installed family named `O'Reilly, Sans` loaded after a public page reload. Its canvas metrics matched a control face from the same file and differed from fallback fonts. A name with HTML-like text remained inert. Those checks did not repeat for the latest commit.

The Site Editor upload workflow, a new Playwright spec, Firefox, WebKit, and the two Trac font attachments remain unverified through the interface. The current automated results above do not claim those checks. CI results for earlier revisions do not establish the result for this commit.

## Use of AI Tools

AI assistance: Yes

Tool(s): Claude Code and Codex

Model(s): Claude Opus 5 and Claude Fable 5.1, as recorded by the implementation author; GPT-6 for this review.

body:
## Summary
A hint bar in the header popped up and immediately disappeared, recurring on its own, after a normally-shown hint was dismissed.

Root cause: several TIP_HINTS gate on a pane's status, which flips idle/working on every tool call a busy agent makes, and the pool is filtered afresh on every render, so the same tipIndex can land on a different entry as pool membership shifts. Once dismissing whatever stable hint used to occupy the slot let a status-gated entry take it, that flip showed and immediately took the hint away again on the very next state push.

## Change
`renderHintsFromState` — the one call site driven by full state pushes — now requires a pick to hold for `HINT_SETTLE_MS` (1.2s) before it swaps which TIP_HINTS entry fills an already-occupied slot, or clears one for nothing. Reverting to what's already shown within that window cancels the change outright, so no flash happens at all.

Deliberately *not* gated, since none of these are the source of the flicker and existing tests require them instant:
- Showing where nothing was shown yet.
- Any PRIORITY_HINTS entry (explains something already on screen — an amber dot, an exited pane — that needs saying the moment it's true).
- Every other caller of `renderHints`: prefs syncing, the tip-rotation timer, dismissing a hint, and "show them again" — all unaffected.

## Test plan
- [x] Added `TestAStatusGatedTipDoesNotFlickerWithTheStatusItGatesOn`, reproducing the exact bug (a status-gated tip flipping in and out) and confirming no flicker, while confirming it does clear out after genuinely settling idle.
- [x] All existing hint/tip tests pass (7 total) — including ones that would break under a naive blanket debounce (dismiss, reset-tips, stale-prefs-push races, and the "waiting" amber-dot PRIORITY_HINTS test).
- [x] Full `internal/webui` suite passes.
- [x] `go build ./...`

author: humuhumu33
body:
`hologram serve` with `registry.provider = "kappa"` builds the provider straight from `AppState::build`, which is async. The kappa client is a blocking reqwest client, and building one on a runtime thread panics.

## The result that matters

On `main`, a debug build configured with `provider = "kappa"` (any endpoint) dies on every start:

```
thread 'main' panicked at tokio-1.53.1/src/runtime/blocking/shutdown.rs:51:21:
Cannot drop a runtime in a context where blocking is not allowed.
ERROR reqwest::blocking::client: Failed to communicate successful startup
```

An optimized build can win that race and start, which is how it went unnoticed: release binaries have been serving a kappa-backed hub without showing it.

## The change

`build_registry()` in `src/app.rs` goes through the existing `blocking()` helper. Nothing else moves. Every other construction site already does this, and `kappa_client` documents why: `cli/pull.rs:50`, `cli/push.rs:62`, `cli/run.rs:155` and `cli/serve.rs:96` all build the client inside `spawn_blocking`. The daemon start was the one place that did not.

## Test

`app::tests::the_kappa_provider_is_built_off_the_async_runtime` builds the provider under `#[tokio::test]` against `http://127.0.0.1:1`. Before the change it fails with the panic above; after it passes. No network is touched.

## Not verified

Whether dropping `AppState` at graceful shutdown can hit the same panic. A killed daemon never gets there, and I did not manage a clean `hologram stop` in my test setup.

author: adammatthewsteinberger
body:
## What & why

Closes #211.

`WorkerLoop._heartbeat_forever` caught only `CancelledError`. Any other exception from `heartbeat()` (a pool timeout, a Postgres failover) ended the heartbeat task with that exception stored. `run_once` awaited the task in its `finally`, so the exception was re-raised there. `_settle` was never reached: a session that had **succeeded** was never acked, its lease expired, and another worker paid to do it again. The exception then escaped `run_once`, `cli/errors.py` re-raises anything that isn't a `VibeyError`, and the worker process died, taking every parallel `drive` loop under `asyncio.gather` and their in-flight work with it.

The issue also asked for the settle booleans to be checked. `ack`, both `nack`s and `park` threw away their results, and so did `grant_attempts` and the per-kind lease extension right after the claim. `defer` was the only write that checked (PR #181).

## Changes

`src/vibey/application/worker.py`
- **`_beat(job, lease) -> bool | None`**: one lease extension that never raises.
  - If `heartbeat()` raises: logs `job.heartbeat_failed` at warning (job_id, project_id, phase, kind, `error=repr(exc)`) and returns `None`.
  - If `heartbeat()` returns `False`: logs `job.lease_lost` at warning (`reason="lease no longer held by this worker"`) and returns `False`.
- **`_heartbeat_forever`** now takes the `JobRecord` for log fields and beats through `_beat`.
  - A failed beat is retried at the next interval.
  - A refused beat stops the loop, because nothing is left to keep alive.
  - `except CancelledError` is kept. It is a `BaseException`, so the new `except Exception` can't swallow it.
- **Initial per-kind extension** (was `:89`) goes through `_beat`. If it fails or is refused, the job carries on at the default lease the claim took.
- **`_landed(applied, *, event, job) -> bool`** is the one private helper for every lease-guarded settle write. When a write is refused it logs at warning, never raises, and returns the bool so the caller can stop. New events:
  - `job.ack_rejected`
  - `job.nack_rejected` (both nack sites)
  - `job.grant_rejected`
  - `job.park_rejected`
- **`job.defer_rejected`** keeps the same name, fields and level, and now goes through the same helper.
- **A refused `grant_attempts` returns without the nack.**
  - The grant always widens the row's bound: `granted > attempts >= max_attempts`, and only a lease-guarded write ever changes `max_attempts`. So a refusal can only mean the lease is gone.
  - A nack without the grant is the `failed` dead end ADR-0024 rejects, and the same guard would refuse it anyway.
- **`_job_fields(job)`** is a static method holding the shared log coordinates. `job.deferred` now uses it too; its key set is unchanged.

`src/vibey/application/interfaces/worker_interface.py` (new) and `interfaces/__init__.py`
- Adds `WorkerLoopInterface`, a `runtime_checkable` Protocol declaring `run_once`. ADR-0016 requires an interface for changed classes. It is exported from `application.interfaces` because `test_interfaces_convention.py` requires every Protocol there to be exported.

`tests/application/test_worker.py`
- Inline `_FlakyQueue(FakeJobRepository)`. It runs a script of heartbeat results (an exception or a bool) and can refuse named settle writes. `tests/application/fakes.py` is untouched.
- The handler waits on beat counts rather than wall time, so the timing tests are deterministic.

`CHANGELOG.md` gets an entry under `### Bug Fixes`. `docs/guides/greeter-live-demo.md` gets two troubleshooting bullets for the new warnings.

No configuration keys are added. The beat cadence stays at `lease / 3`.

## Verification

All commands run in the worktree's own `.venv`, with Postgres 17 on localhost:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `ruff check .` | All checks passed |
| `ruff format --check .` | 1878 files already formatted |
| `mypy --strict src/vibey` | no issues in 178 source files |
| `lint-imports` | 6 kept, 0 broken |
| `bandit -q -r src/vibey` | exit 0 |
| `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --cov=vibey --cov-branch` | 1726 passed, 4 skipped |
| `coverage report --fail-under=100`, domain / application / infrastructure / cli | 100% / 100% / 100% / 100% |

- 11 new tests: heartbeat raises mid-handler and the job is still acked; raises once then keeps beating; refused beat stops the loop and the refused ack is logged; the loop ends on its own after a refusal; nack rejected; grant rejected with no nack; nack rejected after a grant; park rejected; initial extension raises; initial extension refused; interface conformance.
- Against the **original** `worker.py`, all 10 behavioural tests fail; with the fix they pass.
- `tests/application/test_worker.py` ran 6× under `-n 8` with no flakes.
- The existing exact log-line assertions (`job.deferred`, `job.defer_rejected`, the caplog test) are unchanged and pass. Nothing new is logged on the happy path.

## Out of scope / remaining

- **An exception (not a `False`) from a settle write still escapes `run_once`.** For example, `ack` hitting a pool timeout would still kill the process through `cli/errors.py`. Making the `drive` loops in `cli/main.py` survive one loop's exception was scoped out of this lane, as were `cli/errors.py` and `bootstrap.py`. #211's text asks only for the heartbeat path and the settle booleans, and both are done, hence `Closes #211`.
- **A lost lease does not cancel the handler in flight.** The worker still finishes the session, and its settle is then refused and logged. Cancelling or skipping on `job.lease_lost` would save the spend and is a design question of its own.
- **If the initial extension is refused, the same loss is logged twice.** It shows once as `job.lease_lost` at the extension and again at the first loop beat. Harmless, and not special-cased.

## Surprises

- **`grant_attempts` has two documented meanings for `False`:** lease lost, or "a value at or below the current bound is a no-op". I checked that the second can't happen at this call site (reasoning above) before treating a refused grant as lease loss.
- **`park_rejected` can leave an orphan gate.** `_raise_and_park` raises the gate *before* the park. If the park is then refused, the gate row stays for a job this worker no longer holds. The next owner's park path won't duplicate it, but if the next owner succeeds, the gate is left open. This was already true before this PR; the new warning now makes the case visible.

author: anderdc
body:
## Summary

`alw vault recycle` was rejected by the node on mainnet before it ever reached the contract:

```
{'code': 1010, 'message': 'Invalid Transaction', 'data': 'Inability to pay some fees (e.g. account balance too low)'}
```

Two causes, both fixed here.

**1. `recycle_fees` was submitted with `DEFAULT_GAS`.** The node reserves the fee for the whole gas limit up front. At `DEFAULT_GAS` (300B ref_time) that hold is about 0.15 τ, and the signing hotkey held 0.142 τ. The call itself costs about 0.003 τ. `withdraw` and `lock` already got a measured cap (`BOND_OP_GAS`) for this reason; recycle did not.

- New `RECYCLE_GAS = {ref_time: 16B, proof_size: 300k}`.
- Measured on finney 2026-09-18 by dry-run against the live vault: `gas_required` ref_time 5,307,979,122 / proof_size 85,572, so the cap is about 3x.
- `BOND_OP_GAS` can't be reused: recycle runs the `add_stake_recycle` chain extension, and a dry-run under `BOND_OP_GAS` fails out of gas. Under `RECYCLE_GAS` it returns `Ok(())`.

**2. The CLI signed with the hotkey, which usually holds little or no free TAO.** `recycle_fees` is permissionless in the contract (no `caller()` check; the pot can only go to `add_stake_recycle(staking_hotkey, netuid)`), so the signer only pays postage. Dry-runs against the live vault from the coldkey and from an unrelated account both return `Ok(())`.

- `alw vault recycle` now signs with the wallet **coldkey** by default.
- `--hotkey` keeps the passwordless signer for cron and other unattended runs. With the gas cap, a hotkey needs only a few thousandths of a τ.
- `ALLWAYS_VAULT_SURI` still overrides both, so `e2e_lock.sh` is unaffected.

No contract change.

## Tests

- `test_recycle_carries_its_own_measured_gas_limit`: recycle submits with `RECYCLE_GAS`, which stays at least 2x the measured figures and well under `DEFAULT_GAS`.
- `test_recycle_signs_with_the_coldkey_by_default` and `test_recycle_hotkey_flag_keeps_the_passwordless_signer_for_cron`.
- `pytest`: 2291 passed.

author: kaivaryn
body:
## Summary

A packed decode step's GDN in- and out-projections run `pf_gemm_fp8_kernel`, 31% of a linear-attention layer's critical path at c32, and with a 64-byte K tile each CTA reads 64 bytes of each of its 128 weight rows before returning to the first — 128 DRAM streams at 64-byte granularity, which is why it streams the checkpoint's FP8 weights at 0.93 TB/s where the row-at-a-time FP8 GEMV reads the same weights at 1.40. The tile is 128 rows tall where such a step has 8 to 32, so it is now 32 rows tall at those widths and spends the shared memory that frees on a 128-byte K tile, halving how often a CTA returns to the top of its row set. `SPARKINFER_FP8_GEMM_NARROW_M=0` restores the 128-row 64-byte tile, which is main byte for byte.

## Proof of speedup

- [x] Tested on **RTX 5090** (`sm_120`)

**Target model(s)**

- [ ] **Muse Glimmer**
- [x] **Qwen3.8-27B** (ModelOpt NVFP4 / DSpark)
- [ ] **Shared / both**

**Decode tok/s** (end-to-end, from `bench/scripts/bench.sh` — fill if this PR targets decode):

| | decode tok/s |
|---|--:|
| before (main) | 502.9 |
| after (this PR) | 545.1 |

**Prefill pp tok/s** (fill if this PR targets prefill; use `--ctx 4096`, `32768`, `65536`, or `131072` and copy the `prefill pp` line — report your best context. Keep the row labels as-is):

| | prefill pp tok/s |
|---|--:|
| before prefill (main) |  |
| after prefill (this PR) |  |

```text
unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 dir, RTX 5090 sm_120 (525 W), main 89504f6; bench.sh measures prebuilt releases, not this path.
Bot invocation: SPARKINFER_QWEN38_{PREFILL,DECODE}_NVFP4=1 SPARKINFER_KV_INT8=1 qwen3_gguf_cb_bench <dir> <c> 256 256 512, agg_tok_s.
            main           this PR        PR knobs=0 (same binary)   delta
 cb @c8   502.9/503.8    545.1/545.0            -                    +8.2%

Flat: c2/c4 never reach this GEMM (8-row floor); the 32k guards and decode@256k are single-request, so M=1 takes the FP8 GEMV, not this tile.
Guards PR/main decode|prefill: Qwen3.6 32k .997|.996, ModelOpt 32k .998|.994, Muse 32k .998|.996, qwen3.8 prefill@16k .995, decode@256k 1.000.
```

Adds `luria.user_agent`. Independent of #293. Also fixes #295, found on the way.

## What it was doing

`Python-urllib/3.11` from every request: the language and nothing else, not the tool, not the project, not a way to be reached, and the shape of traffic a metadata host rations first.

Three call sites, and they had **already drifted**:

| site | before |
|---|---|
| `sources._once` | `urlopen(url)` |
| `remotes._fetch_bytes` | `urlopen(url)` |
| `remotes._head` | `urlopen(Request(url, method="HEAD"))` |

Two passed a bare URL, one built a `Request` for its `method`. A header added to the obvious place would have covered two endpoints out of three — and a tool that identifies itself on two out of three has not identified itself. So this extracts `luria/fetch.py` and all three go through `request()`; the headers are one fact rather than three habits (`DP-004`), and a fourth call site is now `request(url)`.

## The default: `luria/<version>`, and nothing more

Two constraints meet here and the string satisfies both.

**Honest about the software** — the shape `curl/8.0` and `Wget/1.21` have used for decades — so a host reading a log sees what is actually calling it.

**No contact.** A URL or mailbox in a shipped default routes every user's traffic to whoever happens to maintain luria: a person who did not agree to that, and not the operator a host wants to reach anyway. The contact is the project's to add:

```yaml
user_agent: 'luria/0.29 (+mailto:you@example.org)'
```

Both rejected alternatives are in the ADR, and they lose from opposite directions. **A browser string** (the first draft of this branch) gets served, but it's a lie told to the party least able to check it and is exactly what a rate-limiter is trying to see through — goodwill now, blocked by pattern later, and it forfeits the benefit that motivated setting an agent at all. **A hardcoded project URL** was my first proposal and is worse in a quieter way: a contact nobody consented to publish is not politeness.

The cost, stated: no project gets polite-pool treatment without opting in. That's the right side to err on when the alternative is publishing a maintainer's inbox on other people's behalf.

## Also fixes #295

The header needed luria's version, which surfaced this:

```
luria.__version__  -> 0.1.0
metadata.version() -> 0.28.2.dev0+gf8bc04e82.d20260918
```

Hand-written, wrong for twenty-seven releases. `pyproject.toml` derives the version from git tags *precisely so the two cannot drift*, and its own comment said "nothing in the package reads its own version" — which is what kept anyone from checking the copy sitting two lines into the package it was protecting. A user agent honest about the software shouldn't misreport its version in the same breath, so both now read distribution metadata, the comment is corrected, and `test_the_package_version_is_not_hand_written` fails if a literal is written back.

## Not a fix for #292, and checked rather than assumed

Worth stating plainly because I'm the one who originally misdiagnosed it that way:

```
explicit UA (luria/0.28.1 +url):        HTTP 406
empty UA:                               HTTP 406
default urllib UA:                      HTTP 406
Accept: */*  /  application/atom+xml:   HTTP 406
```

All 406 while the condition held, all 200 after it lifted. The two changes are independent and **neither is evidence for the other**; the ADR records that so a future reader doesn't take this as the throttling fix.

Branched off `main`, not off #293. The two touch adjacent lines in `_once` — merge order shouldn't matter, but flagging it.

## Tests

Nine, written before the code and confirmed failing. Beyond the obvious:

- `test_the_default_names_the_software_and_nothing_else` — asserts both constraints at once: starts with `luria/`, no `Mozilla`, no `@` and no `http`. Pins the decision rather than a string.
- `test_a_head_request_keeps_both_the_method_and_the_agent` — the site a naive fix would have missed.
- `test_remote_discovery_sends_it` / `test_the_head_probe_sends_it` — all of luria's traffic or none.
- `test_the_version_comes_from_package_metadata` / `test_the_package_version_is_not_hand_written` — #295.

Full suite **1367 passed, 33 skipped**. One failure en route worth mentioning: `test_every_scalar_key_is_described` failed until the new config key had prose in the generated reference — the check doing exactly its job.

Verified end-to-end against the live arXiv API:

```
UA on the wire: luria/0.28.2.dev0
HTTP 200 -> Attention Is All You Need
```

## Checks

`luria link --fix`, `luria index`, `luria lint` run; output identical to main's baseline. Views regenerated locally and reverted.

body:
## Summary
Extends the atomic budget-reservation ledger (PR 6d / #2076) with the multi-scope helpers that the follow-up gateway wiring (**PR-A2**) needs. **Dark** — no callers yet, ``BUDGET_LEDGER_ENABLED`` stays off by default.

## What's new on ``BudgetLedger``

- **``reserve()`` signature extended** with four nullable scope kwargs: ``agent_identity_id``, ``source``, ``client_tool``, ``request_id``. When populated they're written to the ``budget_reservations`` columns added in migration 0140 (#2093), so the durable log carries request/agent/transport correlation. Existing single-scope callers see zero behavior change (kwargs default to ``None``).
- **``reserve_all(applicable_budgets, ...)``** — all-or-nothing multi-scope reservation. Iterates rows from ``lookup_applicable_budgets()`` (from #2096), calls ``reserve()`` once per hard-cap-enabled budget with a ``hard_limit_usd`` set, and unwinds prior accepted reservations atomically if any refuses. Returns ``(decision, accepted_or_None, refusing_budget_or_None)``. The **empty-list ACCEPTED case** (no hard cap applies) is a valid outcome — dispatch is unconditionally allowed.
- **``release_all(reservations)``** — releases each; individual ``release()`` is idempotent, so a second call is a no-op.
- **``commit_all(reservations, actual_cents)``** — commits each with the **same** ``actual_cents`` (not proportional): each budget the request drew from receives the full charge on its committed counter. Individual failures are logged but do not stop iteration; the reconciler catches orphaned open reservations later.

## Tests (7 new cases)

- ``reserve_all`` accepts when every budget permits.
- ``reserve_all`` unwinds prior accepted reservations when any budget refuses. **Verifies both counters back to zero** after the failed call.
- ``reserve_all`` returns ACCEPTED with an empty list when no budget has hard enforcement enabled.
- ``reserve_all`` skips budgets with ``hard_cap_enabled=True`` but no ``hard_limit_usd`` (misconfigured — no-op, don't crash).
- ``release_all`` idempotent across the list.
- ``commit_all`` moves every reservation to committed, each budget receives the full ``actual_cents``.
- ``reserve()`` accepts the new scope kwargs without error.

**20/20 pass locally** (13 pre-existing + 7 new). Ledger primitive's P1/P2 correctness proofs — double-release safety, commit atomicity, cold-worker NOT_READY, TTL preservation, concurrent-reserve cap adherence — remain green.

## Explicitly out of scope

- **Gateway lifecycle wiring** — **PR-A2** will call these methods from ``gateway_lifecycle.py``, add dispatch-boundary tracking (release only when definitely no wire bytes flew), and gate everything behind ``BUDGET_LEDGER_ENABLED``.
- **Millicents.** Ledger still operates in cents at the DB layer. If sub-cent rounding matters (very small requests), that's a follow-up schema change.

Depends on: #2093 (merged) — needs the scope columns on ``budget_reservations``.
Feeds into: PR-A2 — the wiring PR is where behavior changes.

## Test plan
- [x] ``pytest apps/api/tests/core/test_budget_ledger.py`` — **20/20 pass** locally.
- [ ] CI: existing spend + ledger + gateway suites remain green (nothing touched in the enforcement path — this is dark).

author: hexagonstorms
body:
Closes #383.

Spec: `docs/plans/2026-09-18-383-back-nav-alpine-and-listener.md`

## The issue's diagnosis was wrong, and the real defect is worse

#383 guessed that Back followed by a sidebar click threw `_x_dataStack` of null, and called it cosmetic. The spec required writing the repro **before** the fix, and that is what surfaced this.

**The sidebar click contributes nothing.** With the error collector armed from before the first navigation and a tally taken at each step: Back onto the class composer produced **180 uncaught errors before the sidebar was touched**, and the click that followed added zero. `_x_dataStack` never appeared in any repro. `@click` on a nav Alpine never re-initialised is not a handler that throws; it is not a handler.

**What actually happens.** htmx builds its history snapshot by serializing the body's `innerHTML`, and this body is not the markup the server sent, because Alpine renders into it. The composer's scheduler is four `x-for` templates, so the snapshot captures their output as ordinary elements sitting beside the templates that made them. On restore Alpine initialises those orphaned clones, whose bindings name a loop variable that no longer exists, **and** re-renders each template from data on top of them.

Measured on one Back: start-time menu **32 options to 64**, duration menu **8 to 16**, the single scheduled session listed **twice**. A member pressing Back onto a class they were scheduling sees it doubled.

## Three defects fixed

**1. Back duplicates everything Alpine rendered.** Fixed by `htmx.config.historyCacheSize = 0` in `hub_boot.js`.

Neither candidate direction in the spec works. Re-initialising on `htmx:historyRestore` does not help, because the tree is already initialised, just over markup that should not exist. Cleaning up at `htmx:beforeHistorySave` cannot be done from a handler, because htmx clones the history element *after* firing that event, so the only tree a handler can reach is the live one. The snapshot itself has to go.

Setting the size to zero also makes htmx drop any stored cache on its next save, and it saves on the way into every restore, so a member still carrying snapshots from an earlier visit is cleaned out rather than served one more broken Back. The restore then misses and refetches: the same request a boosted click already makes. **Cost is one request per Back**, which is what every forward navigation here already costs. This tradeoff was put to the maintainer explicitly and accepted.

**2. The wiki editor silently discarded everything typed after Back.** This was *inferred* during #437's review and had never been observed. It is real, and it is data loss.

`plRteInitAll` claimed each mount with `mount.dataset.rteReady` — an attribute, which is markup, which the snapshot serializes. After Back every restored mount arrived already claimed and the init no-opped. The page looked perfect: one toolbar, one container, one editable body. Typing reached nothing, the hidden field the form posts never changed, and **there was no error anywhere**. The ready key is now a property.

**3. The `htmx:afterSettle` listener accumulated per boosted arrival.** The defect #383 actually filed. Guarded on `window`, because the file is an IIFE that htmx re-runs in a fresh scope. The listener is a wrapper rather than a direct reference, so the single binding always calls the current definition instead of pinning the first arrival's closure.

**The two Back fixes are not redundant**, verified by disabling each in turn. Cache off but attribute restored: editor alive, because Back is a server fetch and nothing arrives pre-claimed. Property but cache on: editor alive but the restored page carries **two** Quill toolbars.

## Corrected after review: I checked the blast radius the wrong way round

The first version of this PR said "every other `HX-Request` branch in the codebase is `@require_POST`... I checked all five rather than taking that claim on trust." **That check was backwards, and the claim was wrong.**

Excluding `HX-Boosted` is not a safety guard against a restore. A restore is *precisely* a non-boosted `HX-Request`, so the branches that exclude boosted are the **reachable** ones, not the safe ones. I read that as protection and moved on.

The one that was missed is `classes/views.py:318` `public_list`, which has no decorator, and it is the most reachable surface in the app: the catalog is also the one page that pushes history by design (`hx-push-url` on both the category filter and the pagination links). Measured with a real request:

| request | status | bytes | doctype |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal GET | 200 | 341,276 | yes |
| history restore GET | 200 | **339** | **no** |

htmx swaps those 339 bytes in as the entire document: no topbar, no sidebar, no hero, no filter form, and the `hx-swap-oob` div stranded as a literal element.

Re-enumerated all **nine** `HX-Request` sites (not five). Eight are `@require_POST` or already fixed; this was the ninth. The rule now lives in `core.htmx.wants_fragment` rather than being rewritten at each call site, because it is easy to get backwards and it was got backwards here.

## Corrected after review: the two navigation guards never ran on a Back

Both guards in `hub_boot.js` listen on `htmx:beforeSwap`, and htmx's cache-miss loader never fires it. While the hub kept a history cache that did not matter, because Back made no request. Every Back being a refetch is exactly what makes them necessary, and without them this PR shipped two regressions of its own:

- **Session expired, tab left open, one click, then Back.** The refetch is redirected to login, the browser follows it silently, htmx sees a good 200 and swaps the login page into the hub document. Wrong layout, no matching CSS (head-support merges the login page's head and drops the hub's), the address bar still on the page that was asked for, and `?next=` lost.
- **Back onto something deleted.** htmx swaps nothing on a non-2xx, so the address bar has already moved while the screen still shows the previous page. Back looks broken and the branded 404 never renders.

Both now navigate for real, on `htmx:historyCacheMissLoad` and `htmx:historyCacheMissLoadError`. Neither event is cancelable, so the swap runs for an instant before the load replaces it.

**Both new scenarios were built wrong twice before they measured anything**, which is worth stating because this PR's own review found the same class of problem: the first pointed Back at a public page, where an expired session changes nothing; the second read the document immediately after `go_back()`, which is an htmx restore and not a document load, so the load-state wait returned at once and sampled the old document. Both now fail with their guard removed.

## A reviewer finding that did not reproduce

The review also blocked on scroll position being lost on every Back, reasoned from htmx source rather than driven in a browser (the reviewer said so). **Measured both ways in a real browser: scroll is 285 before and 0 after, with the cache on and with it off.** Scroll was already not restored on a boosted Back before this PR. Not a regression, and the tradeoff put to the maintainer was not understated.

## Folded in, because this PR is what makes it reachable

`hub/views.py` `orientation_checkout_return` decided between the whole page and the polling card on `HX-Request` alone. Dropping the history cache turns a Back into a refetch carrying `HX-Request` without `HX-Boosted`, so a member pressing Back onto their Stripe return URL would have got a bare card swapped into the body.

Every other `HX-Request` branch in the codebase is `@require_POST` and so cannot be reached by a restore, which is a GET. I checked all five rather than taking that claim on trust. This one is reachable because it is where Stripe lands the member.

## Test evidence

All verified by the orchestrator independently, and every new scenario was proven to **fail with its fix reverted*

body:
문서 + 실험 하네스 한 파일. 제품 코드 변경 없음.

사장님 지시 *"도면의 그림을 배경 이미지에 합성 시켜서 그대로 실제처럼 구현할 수 있는지 철저하게 연구"* 에 대한 답이다. 문헌 조사에 더해 **실제로 얹어 봤다.**

## 한 것

플래너 정면 입면(디테일 모드 `PlannerCapture front`, 1530×1600)을 회사 포트폴리오 사진 두 장(정면·비스듬)에 **벽 호모그래피로 워프**해 얹었다. 브라우저 캔버스만 썼고 서버·GPU·라이브러리 없음. 하네스 `test-utils/photo-composite-bench.html` — 사진·입면 PNG 를 골라 넣으면 A~D 를 그려 준다.

## 본 것

| 단계 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| A 그냥 얹기 | **원근은 정면·비스듬 둘 다 정확히 맞는다.** 도면은 한 픽셀도 다시 그려지지 않는다 |
| B + 사진 음영 이식 (Wayfair 특허 US11770496 방식) | **여기서부터 붙은 느낌이 난다.** 간접등 빛이 상부장에 실린다 |
| C + Reinhard 색 정합 (절반 강도) | 방의 색온도로 끌려온다 |
| D + 접지 그림자 띠 | 미미 — 진짜 그림자는 three.js 몫 |

## 남은 티 네 가지 (= 다음 일감)

1. **기존 가구가 남는다** — 합성은 지우지 못한다 → 이미 있는 REMOVE FIRST 로 벽을 먼저 비운다. 공사현장 사진이면 불필요하고, 그게 실제 고객의 경우다.
2. **앞의 물건을 덮는다** → 전경 마스크 (브라우저 SegFormer / Depth Anything V2)
3. **납작하다** → 2.5D 옆면·상판 평면
4. **입면이 구조 모드 색이다** → 예림 마감 + PBR 켜서 캡처 (이미 있는 기능)

## 벽 네 점 검출 — 정직한 현황

조사 결과 비전 LLM 좌표는 **초기값 수준** (Gemini 박스 mAP 0.34, 포인팅 34~45%). 1순위는 SegFormer 벽 마스크 + 직선 피팅, VLM 은 초기값, 그래도 안 되면 **네 귀퉁이 탭 4번** — 끌어 맞추는 옛 UI 가 아니다. 이것마저 접을지는 [확인 필요].

계획서 §4.6·§4.7·§6 갱신.

author: ashleycribb
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced repeated O(N) vector scans (Vec::retain and Vec::position) in TileFusionEngine::fuse_telemetry_tiles and Compactor::compact with std::collections::HashMap<(u32, u32, u64), TelemetryRecord> for record deduplication and tombstone removal.

🎯 **Why:** Previously, deduplicating telemetry records during tile fusion and compaction performed repeated linear scans over the accumulated vector for every record, resulting in O(N^2) runtime complexity. Utilizing a HashMap keyed by (sensor_id, metric_id, timestamp) brings deduplication down to O(N) expected time.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
Benchmarked tile fusion with 20,000 telemetry records:
- Debug mode: 626.86 ms → 37.37 ms (16.8x speedup / 94.0% reduction in time)
- Release mode: 84.09 ms → 8.09 ms (10.4x speedup / 90.4% reduction in time)

## Summary

Parameterizes the Alloy Playwright e2e suite so every authenticated scenario runs **once in light mode and once in dark mode**, and adds real WCAG contrast coverage for the admin surface.

## Changes

- **`alloy/test-helpers.ts`** — adds `ALLOY_THEMES`, `alloyIsDarkTheme()`, and `applyAlloyTheme()`. `applyAlloyTheme` drives the top-bar **Admin User → Dark Theme** switch and waits for the CDK overlay/menu panel to detach before returning, so a subsequent menu interaction can't race a lingering backdrop. Theme is a no-op when already active.
- **60 spec files** — each authenticated spec is wrapped in `for (const theme of ALLOY_THEMES) { test.describe(\`${theme} theme › …\`) }`, with `applyAlloyTheme(page, theme)` applied right after `authenticateWithKeycloak`. The theme persists via `@cmusei/crucible-common`'s auth store (localStorage `akita-alloy-ui`), so applying it once after login holds across the in-test navigations.
- **New `alloy/tests/accessibility-and-usability/theme-contrast-compliance.spec.ts`** — measures actual painted colours and asserts:
  - WCAG 2.1 AA **1.4.3** text contrast (Administration heading + first column header) in both themes, plus a light/dark direction check.
  - WCAG 2.1 AA **1.4.11** non-text contrast for the primary "Add Event Template" action icon (≥ 3:1) in both themes.

**Left un-parameterized (intentional):** 3 non-authenticated specs (`admin-enlist-endpoint`, `user-login-flow`, `unauthorized-access-redirect`) and 3 theme-behavior specs that toggle the theme themselves (`theme-toggle-light-dark-mode`, `user-menu-theme-toggle`, `color-contrast-compliance`).

## ⚠️ Upstream dependency

These tests rely on upstream Alloy.Ui PR **[cmu-sei/Alloy.Ui#718](https://github.com/cmu-sei/Alloy.Ui/pull/718)**. Specifically, the dark-mode **"Primary action icon contrast (WCAG 1.4.11)"** assertion passes only with that PR's app-side fix, which splits the top-bar `--app-topbar-*` tokens out from `--mat-sys-primary` and lightens the dark primary so the action icon clears 3:1 (previously ~2.06:1). Without #718 deployed, that dark variant will fail — as intended, since the assertion states the correct WCAG requirement rather than working around the app defect.

## Verification

`./run-tests.sh alloy --browser chromium` against a stack running Alloy.Ui #718 → **133 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed**.

author: hasamba
body:
closes #1266

**The concrete harm, verified against real source**: `mispPush.ts` sets `to_ids: true` (MISP's
automated-IDS/blocking flag) on every ip/domain/hash/url IOC, and `reports/iocBlocklist.ts` is a
literal acting block-list export. So a forged `X-Originating-IP` was shipped as a blockable
network indicator, indistinguishable from a sensor-observed peer. The issue's fallback ("confirm
no enforcement path consumes IOCs unmarked") is false; option (a) landed.

**Mechanism**: one asymmetric literal `provenance?: "client-reported"` on `SiemIoc`/`IOC`, set at
exactly one site today — `emailImport.ts`'s `originatingIp`. Absent is NOT "verified"; it is
"extracted the ordinary way", every IOC's state before this field. The lure's own URL/host/
attachment IOCs stay unmarked on purpose (content vs attribution — blocking a lure host is the
point; blocking a claimed relay on the claim alone could block a legitimate MTA).

**Merge lattice**: plain wins at every sink (`addIoc`, `mergeRowIocs`, `stateMerge`, `iocMerge`).
An existing marker is cleared only by a later ordinary sighting that carries `extractedFrom` — the
one signal every model delta already has stripped at `stripAiExtractedFrom` — so a model can
neither mark an IOC nor un-mark one by restating it.

**Consumers**: block-list (txt/csv/stix) excludes marked values outright and says so in its
header; MISP push `to_ids: false` + explanatory comment; IRIS description-first + `client-reported`
tag; report IOC table and geo table suffix the value. Enrichment, provenance-chain and the
synthesis prompt deliberately unchanged (see `RECOMMENDATION-1266.md`).

**Real defect found by the end-to-end test the code review asked for**: `platformImports.ts`'s
email delta builder whitelisted `{ id, type, value }` and dropped the marker — it never reached
`mergeDelta` in production while every unit test passed. Fixed; the new
`iocClientReportedEndToEnd.test.ts` runs a real `.eml` through `pipeline.importEmail`, a save/load
round-trip, both block-list formats, and a later Zeek conn sighting that clears the marker — and
was confirmed red with the fix reverted.

**Also**: the IOC-sink section (`addIoc`/`mergeRowIocs`/`resolveExtractedFrom`/`SiemIoc`) moved
verbatim from `siemImport.ts` into `iocSink.ts` for the file-size ledger, re-exported so every
importer is unchanged; one unrelated comment merge in `markdown.ts` for the same ledger.

**Reviews** (Ollama, glm-5.3:cloud): design round "accept with fixes" — HIGH (model restatement
would clear the marker) fixed via the `extractedFrom` gate, plus 2 MEDIUM/8 LOW applied; code round
"accept with fixes", no High — MEDIUM-1/2, LOW-4/5/6/7, NIT-9 and all named test gaps applied;
LOW-3 (a marker can outlive unlinked telemetry, fails toward under-blocking) and NIT-10 (already-
pushed MISP attributes keep `to_ids`) accepted and disclosed.

Gate pass: build/typecheck/lint/format:check, all four `check:*` gates, full `npm test`
(971 files / 17043 tests) after merging master. Secret scan of the diff clean.

body:
Closes #3. Delivers the visual-regression gate that actually holds: deterministic capture, CI-native baselines, hardened CI, and the examples restructured as production-grade references.

## Deterministic visual gate (ADR-005)
- The harness froze volatile content (wall-clock header, live perf figures, tick-drifted prices) that made baselines unmatchable across hosts — CI failed webkit-mobile at 0.574% and a local win32 run failed firefox-mobile at 0.389% with zero structural pixels differing.
- The suite now freezes the capture after measurement and hard-fails if the harness cannot prove it froze. Evidence: two consecutive runs, 0 differing pixels across all 12 captures; visual gate 84/84 on the ubuntu runner (run 35401478662).
- Baselines win32 + linux committed; regeneration via `baselines:update` or the new `baselines` job (workflow_dispatch, exact verify container, artifact for review). Threshold unchanged (0.3%).

## CI hardening
- Container image digest-pinned (Greptile P2); `baselines` job added; build job now runs `check:types`, `check:docs`, `check:commits` (PR range, merge commits excluded).
- Two CI-only bugs found and fixed by the first pushes: `--print-counts` ran after the harness/dist check (fresh checkouts have none), and the subject gate flagged GitHub's auto-generated merge commit.

## Gates
- `check:types` — tsc strict over @trade/ui.
- `check:docs` — documented check counts must agree with the suite's own `--print-counts`; baselines exception must exist in README/AGENTS/CONTRIBUTING; stale pre-restructure paths fail.
- `check-style` extended to example-app stylesheets (88/88); contrast contract now 69/69 pairs (added onSurfaceDisabled and primary/surface-1).

## Examples (production-grade)
- `apps/demo` → `apps/example` (component reference), `apps/trading` → `apps/example-trading` (trading workspace); `verify:example-trading` now runs in CI for the first time.
- Trading ticket: default order is affordable so the primary button shows active on load; orders above buying power warn inline and disable submit; Reset (outline, visible body) restores side + all defaults from one TICKET_DEFAULTS constant (Greptile-caught).
- Disabled buttons: flat grey fill + light grey label via the new `onSurfaceDisabled` role (all 3 themes, contrast-gated visibility floor).

## Docs
- README, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, STATUS.md updated; check-count drift (72 vs 84) now impossible; ADR-005 records the frozen-capture decision.

## Checklist
- [x] Visual gate gates on ubuntu CI (verification job, run 35401478662)
- [x] Greptile findings from earlier reviews: P1 baselines env, P2 count, P2 digest — all closed
- [x] Baselines committed under the documented exception only

author: nadvolod
body:
The MVP, built so that every Temporal piece is still yours to write.

The game is complete and playable right now in mock mode. `src/temporal/` is
empty scaffolding on purpose.

```bash
cp .env.example .env
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # localhost:3000
```

## What's here

**A playable game.** Grow wheat, build a bakery, bake and sell three loaves,
finish on 30 coins in about two and a half minutes. Winning earns a keepsake
you choose and keep, which visibly makes the next town faster — the loop has a
reason to be replayed.

**No Temporal vocabulary on the game screen.** A worker being down reads as
"your town is resting". Everything technical lives behind the bee button:
systems touched, the real HTTP traffic log, town metadata, and your player id
with copy-and-restore.

**One pure rules module, two backends.** Validation and state transitions have
no I/O, no clock and no randomness, because a workflow replays them. The mock
backend is the reference behaviour for the workflow — stale-version rejection,
action-ID dedup, recorded outcomes, rewards applied exactly once — minus the
durability.

**Ten labs and a red test suite.** Every function under `src/temporal/` throws
an error naming its lab. `pnpm test:labs` fails in 1.4s pointing at Lab 2, and
goes green as the labs are completed.

## Reviewing

The commits are split to be read in order. If you only read two things, make
them [`CONTEXT.md`](CONTEXT.md) for the vocabulary and
[ADR-0002](docs/adr/0002-signals-and-queries-over-workflow-update.md) for why
commands are signals rather than updates — that one is a deliberate trade of
convenience for understanding, and it is the decision most worth arguing with.

## Verified

- `pnpm test` — 43 passing (35 rules, 8 mock backend)
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build` — clean
- `pnpm test:labs` — 8 failing, deliberately
- A full game played through the API: refusals carry readable reasons, the
  bakery is charged at acceptance and opens on completion, victory lands on 30
  coins, post-victory commands are refused, three identical action IDs produce
  one wheat, and a stale command is accepted for delivery then ignored
- `GAME_BACKEND=temporal` returns 500 naming the unimplemented lab, with no
  silent fallback to mock

## Known gaps

- The victory/keepsake flow and the behind-the-scenes pane have no automated
  tests — they are client-only and would need Playwright
- Keepsakes live in `localStorage` for v0.1: editable and lost with cookies.
  They move into a player workflow in v0.2 ([ADR-0006](docs/adr/0006-keepsakes-live-outside-the-town.md))
- Whoever holds a player id owns that town. No accounts in v0.1
- Local only. A serverless function can host a Temporal client and can never
  host a worker

## One thing to decide

This repo is public and named **mini-township**. The project is now **Ziggy
Hollow**, because Township is Playrix's trademark and this is going open-source
([ADR-0005](docs/adr/0005-name.md)). The code and docs are renamed; the repo
URL is not. Worth renaming on GitHub — it redirects, so nothing breaks.

# Pull Request

## Summary
- One attended outlining session per `plan/2026-09-17-story-outline.prompt.md`. Builds `axiomancer-mechanics/content/story/story-overview.md` from nothing — the structural successor to the overview retired on 2026-09-17, and the first story this game has since.

The prompt's §4 condition 2 (three or more events leaning on one unresolved tension) fired after event 5 and the pivot was recommended; **T declined it and the road kept walking.** Condition 2 is now spent and is not raised again unless something new fires it.
- `content/story/story-overview.md` now exists, so THE BLANK PAGE ¶1 ("no canon exists") is lifted. ¶2–¶5 stand: X is still X, shipped narrative is still not canon, the loop still does not invent story facts the road does not carry.

## Affected package(s)
- [x] `axiomancer-mechanics` — the TypeScript game engine + CLI (docs/content only here; no `src/` touched)
- [ ] `axiomancer-mobile`

## Change Type
- [x] Documentation / design

## Context / Source Material
- Source doc(s): `plan/2026-09-17-story-outline.prompt.md` (the handoff prompt this session ran), `plan/bearings.md` → THE BLANK PAGE
- Prior art / references: the seven shipped maps, inventoried in the overview's own "Shipped inventory" section — read as evidence of what an old draft assumed, never as canon

## What Changed
- **New: `axiomancer-mechanics/content/story/story-overview.md`.** Header (session, X, status), a seven-map shipped inventory read this session, a `Standing facts` section for facts T set that are not beats, six numbered events with tag lines, `Noted for the pivot`, and the pivot recommendation (kept, marked declined).
- **`plan/bearings.md`** — THE BLANK PAGE ¶6 now records that ¶1 is lifted and names what still stands. Marker line repointed at the overview.
- **`axiomancer-mechanics/CLAUDE.md`** — "THERE IS NO STORY" becomes "THE STORY IS THE ROAD", pointing at the overview and keeping the X / non-canon / do-not-invent rules.
- **`axiomancer-mechanics/content/story/README.md`** — superseded. Kept in full as the historical record of the clearing, with a header saying it is no longer in force and what did not change with it.
- **`axiomancer-mechanics/docs/story.md`** — catalogue header points at the overview and warns that the catalogue is downstream of it.
- **`.claude/skills/world-spec/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/character-spec/SKILL.md`** — "read first" tables point at the overview instead of the no-story README.

Commits are one per turn, as the prompt requires, so a session that died mid-road would have lost one event rather than the road.

## Verification
No code changed — no `src/` file, no test, no build input is touched. The repo's commit guard (`.claude/hooks/guard.mjs`) ran on every commit and its `check-lexicon` leg passed each time:

```bash
$ git commit ...
check-lexicon: 242 live file(s) clean against 21 retired term(s)
```

- [ ] `npm run verify --workspace axiomancer-mechanics` — not run; markdown-only diff, no engine input
- [ ] `npm run verify --workspace axiomancer-mobile` — not run; not touched
- [ ] `npm run verify:visual --workspace axiomancer-mobile` — not run; no UI change
- [ ] `npm run type-check --workspace axiomancer-card-editor` — not run; not touched

## Test Coverage
- [x] Test debt accepted — explain why: the deliverable is one markdown outline plus five doc pointers. There is no behavior to cover, and the prompt's §5 forbids this session from producing specs, code, or game text.

## UI / Balance Evidence
- None. No UI, no numbers, no content libraries touched.

## Callouts for Reviewer
- **This changes story law, not code.** THE BLANK PAGE ¶1 is lifted by this PR. After it merges, "there is no story" is no longer the correct answer — "the story is whatever `content/story/story-overview.md` says, and it is six events long" is. Anything the overview does not cover still does not exist, and the loop still says so and stops.
- **The road diverges from the build, deliberately and unresolved.** T's first write-in put X in a castle dungeon; the game starts at `fishing-village` fv-1. No shipped map is a castle. That conflict is filed under `Noted for the pivot`, not patched — the prompt forbids this session from resolving structural questions mid-walk, and nothing in the build changed.
- **X picked up identifiers the prompt's §2 said X would not have** (a pronoun and a station, both from T's own write-ins). Recorded as written, flagged for the pivot, not argued with. §2 anticipated that who X is would be an output of the road; it happened by accretion rather than by decision, which is itself the finding.
- **The pivot was recommended and declined, and that is recorded in the file.** The `Pivot recommendation` section is kept rather than deleted: its four questions (is the lie survivable; what the second guard is for; where the annexation puts the shipped maps; whether addiction wants mechanical expression) are still the right four whenever the pivot does happen. `Status` reads `walking`.
- **Content warning for readers of the outline:** the road T directed is deliberately brutal — a child's death, a suicide, an exploited grief, an addiction X propagates to the person sheltering him. It is outline prose, not scene prose, but it is not decorative.
- **The overview supersedes the README rather than merging with it**, per the README's own instruction. The README is kept whole as history because the record of what was cleared, and why, is load-bearing for anyone who later finds the deleted docs in git.

Additional callouts:
- `docs/narrative/` is untouched. It is craft law (how copy is written), never story law, and this session had no business in it.
- LOCKED MECHANICS are untouched. The pivot's question 4 asks whether addiction and withdrawal want mechanical expression; it does not presume they do.
- The session is still live. More events may land on this branch before it merges; each arrives as its own commit.

- Rollback plan: revert this branch's commits as a block. That restores THE BLANK PAGE ¶1, the no-story README as the live marker, and every pointer, in one move.

author: gajanan-choudhary
body:
### PR Category
Feature

### Summary
Fixes #56688.

Brings the experimental Quasar `sdpa_decode` fork (`experimental/quasar/transformer/sdpa_decode`) from compile-only to numerically correct on Quasar. Every change is `ARCH_QUASAR`-guarded (host: `device->arch() == QUASAR`), so the Wormhole/Blackhole path is textually unchanged.

Main changes:
- **Compile / LLK-compat:** swap the fused experimental SFPU softmax primitives (`ckernel_sfpu_sdpa.h`, no Quasar impl) for generic Quasar SFPU tile ops; apply the exp scale via a separate multiply (Quasar `exp_tile` only supports scale=1.0); semaphore-API migration + Gen2 DFB structure; dtype validation restricted to bf16/Int32; `Os` compute opt (the batch1 tree-path kernel overflows the trisc code region at O2/O3).
- **Intra-Tensix DFB tile-counter budget (Quasar cap 8):** fit the tree-reduction temps by reuse, merge the SUM ping-pong into one DFB, and drop the `kt` staging DFB in favor of the matmul's native SrcA transpose for QK^T (→ 7 DFBs). MAX stays split.
- **Multi-chunk online-softmax:** MAX split, SUM merged via an fma ring-rebase (a weak `cur_pos=128` test had hidden the ≥3-chunk bug).
- **Quasar packer/unpacker operand retargeting** (WH re-targets by named buffer; Quasar needs an explicit `pack_init`/`copy_init` at each operand switch): gate `pack_init` on the actual output-operand change; re-point the packer for the QK and QK@V matmuls; fix the tree-reduction buffer routing in `correction_block`/`move_block`.

### Test plan / status
- **Wormhole n150 (baseline):** 6/6 — batch1 + batch32 × {seq256 kc32/kc128, seq1024}. Non-regression.
- **Quasar emulator:** batch1 seq256 + seq1024 (single-core path).
- **craq-sim (Quasar):** 6/6, incl. the batch1 multi-core tree-reduction path.

### Dependencies
Depends on two prerequisites that are merging into `main` separately (and were dropped from this branch): the SrcA-transpose matmul LLK (enables the `kt` removal) and the `wait_front` block-fix + `read_tile_value` dataflow support. Please merge this after those land.

### Notes for reviewers
- All Quasar changes are `#ifdef ARCH_QUASAR` / arch-gated; WH/BH is unchanged.
- The multi-core tree-reduction path is validated on WH + craq-sim; the current Quasar emulator (≤6 cores) runs batch1 single-core, so that path isn't yet exercised on silicon.
- Config paths the model/tests don't exercise (paged, sharded page-table, attention sink, row-major-Q, non-causal) are out of scope here and tracked as follow-ups on #56688. Eager Llama-3.2-1B decode uses the non-paged causal path this PR covers.

Antigravity needs a subscription-account CLI transport before it can serve as a Meridian backend. This draft adds an opt-in research harness and recorded live evidence; production Meridian behavior is unchanged.

The official `agy` CLI (1.2.6, macOS arm64, Gemini 3.8 Flash Low) completed streaming, explicit resume, persistent stdin, concurrent conversations, and a synthetic HTTP client-owned tool round trip through a pending MCP response. ## What

Adds `WorkflowWorkspaceResourceAdapter`, the first real (non-fake) `WorkspaceResourceAdapter`, and registers it for the `workflow` resource type in `server.py`'s `create_app()`.

Closes `docs/workspace-plan.md`'s new `P5-E` row (added by this PR — the plan's PR-sequence table jumped straight from `P5-D` to `P6-A` with no row for "wire a real adapter").

## Why

Phase 5 (`P5-A` through `P5-D`, already merged: #345–#348) built a complete, well-tested release state machine — governance, break-glass, durable adapter execution, runtime lineage — but the only adapter ever registered in production was **none at all**. `app.state.workspace_resource_adapter_registry` was never set anywhere in `server.py`, so `routes/workspace_release_operations.py`'s own fallback (`_registry()`) always returned an *empty* registry. Every real release operation failed closed with "no adapter registered" before it could even reach the fake in-memory adapter the test suite uses. In production today, a Workspace release deploys nothing, for any resource type.

This PR closes that gap for one resource type — a Workflow Studio workflow — whose deploy mechanics (alias rotation) are already mature, deterministic, and heavily tested via `caliber.workflows.promoter`.

## What changed

- **New `WorkflowWorkspaceResourceAdapter`** (`caliber/src/caliber/workspace_release_workflow_adapter.py`): deploys a workflow pin by rotating its deployment alias through the existing `promoter._rotate_alias` primitive, exposed here via a new public `rotate_alias_to_version` wrapper. Fails closed rather than silently skip a deploy gate the workflow's own author configured for the target alias — `rotate_alias_to_version` deliberately does not run the expensive/non-deterministic `evaluate_deploy_gates` check, so `_refuse_if_gated` refuses the release instead of rotating past a gate nobody evaluated.
- **`server.py`**: `create_app()` now constructs a `WorkspaceResourceAdapterRegistry` with this adapter registered for `"workflow"` and sets it on `app.state`. Every other resource type remains unregistered and still fails closed exactly as before — this PR does not claim to close the gap for source-control-backed resources or anything else Workspace names.
- **Protocol signature change**: `WorkspaceResourceAdapter.apply_release`/`observe_release`/`rollback_release` now receive the caller's own SQLAlchemy `Session` instead of opening a second connection. This adapter's "provider" is the *same database* the release operation runs against — a second connection writing while the caller's transaction is still open deadlocks against SQLite's single-writer lock for the caller's entire remaining transaction (not a timeout — an unconditional wait, since nothing releases the lock until the outer transaction commits or rolls back). Sharing the session also more correctly commits the operation's state and the provider mutation as one atomic unit, instead of leaning on `reconcile_required` to paper over a window where one succeeded and the other didn't. `FakeWorkspaceResourceAdapter` and its callers in `test_workspace_release_operations.py` were updated to match (mechanical: an added/ignored session parameter).
- **Fixed a real, pre-existing bug** in `workspace_release_operations.py`'s `_prepared_from_item`: reconstructing a `PreparedAction` from a stored operation item never restored `prepared.metadata` (only `resource_type`), silently dropping every adapter's own metadata (project id, environment name, etc.) at apply/observe/rollback time.
- **`docs/workspace-plan.md`**: added the missing `P5-E` row.

## Design note: the mypy Protocol-variance fix

The Protocol types every `session` parameter as `object` (so the Protocol module never needs to import SQLAlchemy). The new adapter's Protocol-facing methods (`resolve`, `snapshot`, `validate`, `apply_release`, `observe_release`, `rollback_release`) match that exactly and narrow with `assert isinstance(session, Session)` at the top of each — typing the parameter as `Session` directly is a genuine mypy Protocol-variance error (a narrower parameter type violates substitutability). This was only caught by running `mypy src` against the whole package, not just the changed files, since nothing had previously assigned this adapter into anything typed as the Protocol.

## Testing

- `mypy src` (391 files): clean.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on all changed files: clean.
- Targeted: `test_workspace_release_workflow_adapter.py` (10 new tests), `test_workspace_release_operations.py`, `test_workspace_release_operation_routes.py`, `test_workspace_release_governance.py`, `test_workspace_runtime_lineage.py`, `test_workflow_promoter.py` — **109 passed**.
- Full backend suite: `pytest -n auto --dist loadgroup` — **7088 passed, 11 skipped** (integration/Postgres/UI-bundle tests requiring opt-in infra not present in this environment). No regressions.

## Risks / limitations

- Every resource type other than `"workflow"` is still unregistered and still fails closed — this PR is scoped to one resource type.
- `evaluate_deploy_gates` (the eval-dataset quality gate) is still never run by this path by design; `_refuse_if_gated` only checks whether a gate is *configured*, then refuses — a release to an alias with a configured gate must still go through the workflow's own promotion endpoint.
- Revision materialization (writing real `CaliberWorkspaceRevisionResource` pins from an import) doesn't exist yet, so this adapter is exercised by directly seeded pins in tests, matching `FakeWorkspaceResourceAdapter`'s existing precedent.

## Deployment / migration implications

None — no schema change. Purely additive wiring plus a Protocol signature change that's fully covered by the existing adapter test suite.

body:
Three more Pacific/Oceania countries (46 authored total; 54 to 100).

**Solomon Islands (SLB)** — unitary-small, single country-wide WHOLE entry. English is the language of government and the courts; Pijin (ISO 639-3 `pis`) is the de facto national lingua franca and is carried as `locallySpoken`, not official, since it has no statutory official status. New language file: `pis`.

**Palau (PLW)** — unitary-small, single WHOLE. Palauan (`pau`) and English are both de jure official (Constitution Art. XIII §1). New language file: `pau`.

**Micronesia, Federated States (FSM)** — classified **federal** with four curated states (Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae) alongside the WHOLE fallback. Each state makes its own language co-official with English under its state constitution (Yap Art. XIV §5, Chuuk Art. III §6, Pohnpei Art. 13 §1, Kosrae Art. XIII); Ulithian (`uli`) is carried as a locallySpoken language of Yap's outer islands rather than a national official. FSM is fully dollarized (US dollar, no central bank). New language files: `chk`, `pon`, `kos`, `yap`, `uli`.

All statistics are source-cited (national statistical offices, state constitutions, US State Dept IRF/ICS, CIA World Factbook as secondary) and the standard gate passed: `validate.py` (0 errors), `yamllint` (no new-line-at-end-of-file), `codespell` clean, `pytest` 28/28.
