author: powellwameir
body:
Prompt C of the audit v5 split. **Based on `fix/audit-v5-b-typography` (B), which is based on A** — so this PR's diff is C only. Merge A → B → C in order, or retarget this to `main` once B lands.

The rule applied throughout: **density, not eradication.** The plain word in body/marketing copy; the technical word wherever it is the precise one. That is why several instances of the same word stay put while others change.

---

## Per-page: swapped vs. deliberately kept

### Home (`app/page.tsx`)
| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| *Hero subhead:* "Better tools. Faster answers. Stronger communities." | "We buy HOA management companies in Greater Houston with our own money, and we run them ourselves." |
| *Approach band quote:* "We're operators, in it for the long term." | "We run what we buy, and we're not leaving." |
| "We buy HOA management companies with our own capital and operate them ourselves." | "Which is why we spend on the things that take years to show up: the team, the service, the software." |
| "Experienced operators, guided by an industry veteran." | "Two founders and an advisor who has done this before." |

The third row is not a register swap — once the hero says what we buy and with whose money, the teaser repeated it word for word. It now says what the ownership *changes*. I rewrote it twice: my first version duplicated a sentence on `/approach` verbatim.

### Selling (`app/selling/page.tsx`)
| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| *Subhead:* "A confidential conversation with operators who plan to own what they buy for the long term." | "A private conversation with two people who'll run your company themselves and keep it." |
| "We buy with our own capital, backed by friends and family…" | "We buy with our own money and money from people who know us…" |
| *Meta:* "buys with its own capital… own it for the long term" | "buys with its own money… plans to keep it" |

### Approach (`app/approach/page.tsx`)
| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| *Subhead:* "We acquire established HOA management companies in the Houston area with our own capital, backed by friends and family, and we run them ourselves." | "We buy established HOA management companies around Houston, and we run them ourselves." |
| *H1:* "We operate what we buy, and we build for the long term." | "We run what we buy, and we plan to keep it." |
| *Eyebrow:* "Why the long horizon" | "Why we are not leaving" |
| *H2:* "Where the long term shows up." | "Where staying changes what we do." |
| "…we treat boards, residents and founders **accordingly**." | "…like people we will still be working with in ten years." |

### Team (`app/team/page.tsx`)
| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| *Eyebrow:* "Team" (bare nav-label repeat) | "Two founders and an advisor" |
| *H1:* "Experienced operators, guided by an industry veteran." | "The people who will run your company." |
| "We put in our own capital" | "We put in our own money" |
| "We're putting our own capital into this" | "We're putting our own money into this" |

The H1 dropped "guided by an industry veteran" because the new eyebrow now carries the advisor; keeping both repeated it two lines apart.

### FAQ (`app/faq/page.tsx`)
| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| *Eyebrow:* "FAQ" (bare nav-label repeat) | "For founders, boards and residents" |
| *Lede:* "From founders thinking about a sale, and from boards and residents asking what we'd change." | "Short answers. Where we can't promise something, we say so." |
| *Q:* "Will my company be integrated with others?" | "Will my company be folded into another one?" |
| "Our own capital, backed by friends and family… for the long term." | "Our own money, and money from people who know us, not a fund. We buy each company to own and run it ourselves, for years." |
| "Wameir hasn't **acquired** its first company yet" | "hasn't **bought** its first company yet" |

**Deviation, flagged:** the prescribed eyebrow "For founders, boards and residents" would have duplicated the existing lede almost word for word — and G-09's own rule is "drop it or give it a job," which a duplicate is not. So I used the prescribed eyebrow **and** gave the lede a different job. If you'd rather keep the old lede, drop the eyebrow instead.

### Working toward (`app/working-toward/page.tsx`)
"has not yet **acquired**" → "has not yet **bought**"; "As we **acquire and operate**" → "As we **buy and run**".

### Seller process (`components/SellerProcess.tsx`)
| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| "Cash at close, plus **a seller note**, so we stay partners through the transition" | "Cash at close, plus **part of the price paid over time**, so we both have a stake in how it goes" |
| "**A seller note** keeps you invested in how the community does next" | "**Part of the price paid over time** keeps you invested…" |
| "Shaped around your goals" | **cut** (watch word) |
| "support, tools and **capital** behind them" | "support, tools and **money** behind them" |
| "**Capital** behind investments you couldn't make alone" | "**Money** behind investments…" |
| *Stage:* "Long-term ownership" / "We operate it and hold it" | "We stay" / "We run it, and we keep it" |
| "We're **owner-operators**, here to stay" | "We run the company ourselves, and we are here to stay" |

The stage title and the `STRIP` label were changed together (5 stages, 5 labels — verified).

### Shared copy (`lib/`)
- `sellerPoints.ts` — "Long-term ownership" → "Owners who stay"; "We invest our own **capital** and keep the businesses we **acquire**." → "our own **money** … the companies we **buy**."
- `seo.ts` — site description "its own capital" → "its own money".
- `goals.ts` — cut "**in a way**"; "own these companies for **the long term**" → "**for decades**".
- `team.ts` — only "He advises Wameir on how to buy and **integrate** companies well." → "…how to buy companies and bring them in without breaking what works." That sentence describes what *Wameir* will do to a seller's company, and "integrate" there quietly contradicts the FAQ promise that the name and local identity stay.

---

## Deliberately kept (and why)

- **Mitch's and Bob's bios** — "acquisitions", "diligence", "closing", "integration", "mergers and acquisitions", "interim CFO". This is real career history, and on a Team page the credential *is* the reassurance. Plainer words would read as hiding it.
- **"At Wameir he leads finance and acquisitions"** (`lib/team.ts:28`) — a role description, where the technical term is the precise one. **Flagged**: this is the closest call in the PR. If you want it plainer, say so and I'll change it.
- **`icon: "long-term"` and `Icon.tsx` `"long-term"`** — identifiers, not copy.
- **`app/working-toward/page.tsx:29`, "start them with a **capital**"** — a code comment about capital *letters*. The exact trap a find-and-replace would have fallen into.

## Flag for a human

**The Home hero subhead was marked owner-chosen** (`§15 #10`) in a code comment. The audit prescribes replacing it, so I did, and rewrote the comment to record what happened and why. If the owner wants their three-beat line back, that is a one-line revert.

**"not a fund"** appears once, in the FAQ answer to "Where does your funding come from?". It is the swap table's own prescribed wording, but `00-README.md` says no comparisons to funds "even implied." I used it only where the question directly asks about funding, and left it out of every marketing band. Worth a decision either way.

## For D–G
Pull this branch (or A→B→C) before editing page bodies. C touched prose in `/`, `/selling`, `/approach`, `/team`, `/faq`, `/working-toward` and in `lib/sellerPoints.ts`, `lib/goals.ts`, `lib/seo.ts`, `lib/team.ts`, `components/SellerProcess.tsx`. **F: the Team and FAQ eyebrows and the FAQ lede are already done — don't re-edit those lines.**

## Verified
`npm run build` clean (lint + 15/15 static pages). Copy read back from the rendered DOM on `/`, `/selling`, `/approach`, `/team`, `/faq` — no leftover finance terms outside the keeps above, and no duplicated sentences between Hom

author: sahithrajesh
body:
Officers had no way to publish weekly bootcamp material without a deploy — the curriculum was a frontend constant and the notebooks lived in a separate repo and on Deepnote. An enrolled member opening `/club/bootcamp` saw a "work in progress" card and nothing else, because the syllabus sat in the branch that only renders for people who *aren't* enrolled.

Admins now manage a workshop table at `/admin/bootcamp` — week, title, session date, materials ZIP, solution ZIP, recording link — and publish rows when they're ready. Enrolled members see the published rows at `/club/bootcamp` and download from there.

## Member page

Room `D.M. Smith 115` and time `6:30–7:30 PM, Tuesdays` are set, the placeholder copy is gone, and the heading reads "Welcome to the Fall 2026 Bootcamp".

The enrolled and not-enrolled branches were mutually exclusive, so an enrolled member saw only the status card. The enrolled arm now renders the materials table too — without this the feature would have been visible to everyone *except* the students it's for.

## Schema

`bootcamp_workshop`, unique on `(term, week)`, drafts by default. No FK to `event`: deleting a session must not take the notebooks with it, and material gets posted for weeks whose event row was never created.

Created automatically on deploy — `drizzle-kit push` already runs in `buildCommand`, and this is additive so push won't refuse it. Note `db:check` is columns-only, so the unique constraint and index aren't covered by it; both were verified by hand against a real Postgres.

## Storage

ZIPs go to Cloud Storage (`BOOTCAMP_BUCKET`); Postgres holds metadata and the object key, mirroring the resume book. Bytes move over plain route handlers because `uploadProcedure` caps at 2MB and superjson base64s the body — a single tutorial notebook in `dsgt-bootcamp-f26` is already 1.7MB before you add a dataset.

Two decisions worth reviewing:

- **Objects are keyed by the immutable workshop id, not `(term, week)`.** With a week-based key, editing a row's week leaves it pointing at the old object, and a new row for that week silently overwrites it — then deleting either row destroys the other's file.
- **Uploads stream into the bucket rather than buffering.** At `concurrency: 80` on a 1GiB instance, holding a 20MB body plus its `Buffer` copy per request is not safe. The cap is 20MB (Cloud Run's HTTP/1 request ceiling is 32MiB, so this is headroom, not the platform limit).

## Access control

Writes gate on `isAdmin`. Downloads require staff, **or all of**: enrolment, current term, published, and non-null metadata for that kind — otherwise `404`, not `403`, so a guessed workshop id can't confirm a draft exists. "Enrolled or staff" alone would have let any enrolled member pull drafts and past-term material.

Downloads are proxied, never redirected to a signed URL, which would leave the origin and the auth check behind.

Publishing is a separate `setPublished` procedure rather than a field on the save. If it rode along with the edit, a row could go visible before its uploads landed and stay published if one failed.

## Session dates

Setting a date upserts the underlying bootcamp `event` for that `(term, week)`, so the date has one source of truth and that session also gets attendance and QR check-in like any other club event.

- The QR code is minted on **insert only** — regenerating it on edit would invalidate any printed sign pointing at it.
- Clearing a date **detaches** the event rather than deleting it, because deleting an event destroys its check-ins.

## Test-suite fix included

Eleven suites hand-build a `vi.mock("@query/db")` that lists its exports. `routers/bootcamp.ts` now references `bootcampWorkshops` at module scope, so every suite importing `root.ts` failed to *collect* — 363 tests passing but 11 suites dead. `bootcampWorkshops` (and a missing `events`) were added to those mocks.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm test` | 35/35 suites, 797 tests, 0 failures |
| `pnpm lint` | 8/8 tasks, 0 errors, no suppressions added |
| `pnpm typecheck` | 9/9 workspaces clean |
| `pnpm build --filter=web` | exit 0, all 4 bootcamp routes in the manifest |

Exercised against a real local Postgres, not just mocks: member view returns only published rows while admin also sees the draft; setting a date creates the event and surfaces it in both views; re-saving changes the date and leaves the QR code untouched; the publish toggle works both directions.

## Not yet done — needed before this is usable

1. **The runtime service account needs `roles/storage.objectAdmin` on `gs://dsgt-bootcamp`.** Creating the bucket does not grant this. Until it's run, every upload and download returns **502** while the rest of the feature works normally. Mirror whatever SA holds that role on `gs://dsgt-resumes`.
2. **No real ZIP has round-tripped through GCS.** There were no credentials available in the dev environment, so the upload path is covered by unit tests and correct status codes only. The first production upload is the real test.
3. Confirm `gs://dsgt-bootcamp` has `--uniform-bucket-level-access` and `--public-access-prevention`. These are student notebooks, and the proxied download is undermined if the bucket is directly readable. The bucket is `US-EAST4` while `dsgt-resumes` is `us-central1` — correct either way, but cross-region egress applies on every download.
4. Run `graphify update .` after merge — the committed graph predates the portal bootcamp pages and points at the public marketing page instead.

## Known limitation

A concurrent upload and remove of the same file can race, since the object write and the row update can't be one transaction. Low impact with a handful of officers, but it's real.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New file upload/download paths and access rules affect enrolled members and GCS; misconfigured bucket IAM or publish timing could block materials or leak drafts if checks regress.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **bootcamp workshop materials** so officers can publish weekly ZIPs, solutions, recordings, and session dates without a deploy, and enrolled members can download them from the portal.
> 
> A new **`bootcamp_workshop`** table stores per-week metadata (draft by default, unique on term/week) while ZIP bytes live in **`BOOTCAMP_BUCKET`** (`dsgt-bootcamp`), mirroring the resume book. The **bootcamp tRPC router** gains member/admin workshop lists, create/update, separate **`setPublished`**, and **`upsertSession`** (QR-backed events keyed by term/week; clearing a date detaches the event without deleting check-ins). **Next.js route handlers** stream uploads/downloads with enrollment + publish checks (opaque **404**), ZIP validation, and a 20MB cap.
> 
> **Admin `/admin/bootcamp`** gets a materials table, modal workflow (metadata → session → ZIP upload), and publish/delete controls. **Member `/club/bootcamp`** replaces the WIP card with a welcome header and published materials table. **`BOOTCAMP_BUCKET`** is wired in App Hosting, Turbo `globalEnv`, and ops docs. Test mocks across API suites add **`bootcampWorkshops`** exports; **`bootcamp.test.ts`** and route/unit tests cover auth, conflicts, recording URL allowlist, and storage edge cases.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c130374bf829bc739127da9da7f666d6638b59d3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: tyagiquamar
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1004

When calling \client.insert({ table, values })\, table names containing special characters such as hyphens (e.g., \my-custom-table\) resulted in ClickHouse SQL syntax errors because the table identifier was interpolated unquoted into \INSERT INTO <table> FORMAT <format>\.

This change updates \getInsertQuery\ to format table identifiers:
1. Enclosing plain and hyphenated table names in backticks (e.g., \\\my-custom-table\\\).
2. Splitting qualified names by dot and quoting each component individually (e.g., \\\my_db\.\my-table\\\).
3. Preserving already quoted identifiers (starting/ending with backticks or double quotes).

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added

author: minll
body:
## Summary

SkyrimNet now loads virtual entities from the content library as `entities/*.entity.yaml` (Core #1295, `ContentRoot::VirtualEntities`). This onboards the root on the hub side, the same way `knowledge/` was.

- **content-rules.mjs**: `entities` joins `CONTENT_ROOTS` with the exact `.entity.yaml` suffix. Stems read before the first dot, so `foo.entity.yaml` is `foo` on both sides.
- **path-cases.json**: the five `entities/` cases Core's `tests/test_data/path-cases.json` already carries; the two copies are byte-identical again.
- **validate.mjs**: parse-only like a trigger, plus what the engine would swallow silently: a non-empty `entityName`, no plugin copy of a fixed entity (Player Thoughts, Narrator, System Voice, Game Master), `conversationMode` private or public, one file per name within a plugin (case-insensitive, since the bio slug is lowercased), and a 32 KB cap. No name==stem contract: the engine keys by `entityName`. Entities route to agent review; only actions force a human. Listings still cannot ship them.
- **build-index.mjs / index.schema.json**: `contents.entities`, optional and additive within schema v2 on the `knowledge` precedent.
- **README / CONTRIBUTING / docs/AUTHORING.md**: the root, the validator rules, and what the reviewer looks for (bio at `prompts/characters/<slug>_virtual.prompt`, record and bio agree, mode choice).

author: nicolas-maman
body:
A driver (ae3d's `tools/drive_editor.py`) launches the app with `AETHER_UI_TEST_PORT` set and waits on `/widgets`. The win32 and macOS backends start the test server from the variable; GTK4 never read it, so on Linux nothing answered and the driver reported the editor never came up while the same run passed on the other two backends (first seen when ae3d's CI began building its editor on Linux, nicolas-maman/ae3d#351).

The GTK4 run loop now starts the test server on the app's root when the variable is set (in `aether_ui_app_run_raw`, so an app built by hand gets it too), and `aether_ui_enable_test_server_impl` starts one server only — an app that also asks for one inside its window block does not bind the port twice (the win32 backend guards the same way).

Für die Unterseiten von Help Desk, Übergabeprotokoll und Einkauf fehlten aktuelle Screenshots, und das Gesamt-Handbuch (`handbuch.pdf`) war dadurch veraltet. Diese Änderung aktualisiert die Dokumentation mit frischen, vollständigen Bildern.

- **Isolierte Docker-Umgebung** auf den Ports 8090/3308 gestartet, um die parallel laufende Instanz nicht zu beeinflussen.
- **Beispieldaten** über einen neuen, eigenständigen Seeder `bin/seed-demo.php` eingespielt (Assets, Mitarbeiter, Tickets, Wissensartikel, Übergabeprotokolle, Bestellungen). Der Seeder ist idempotent und liegt bewusst in `bin/`, nicht in `database/seeders/`.

author: maxy-player
body:
## The problem

`Publish sandbox images` dominates the Release workflow. It builds `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` in a single job on an amd64 runner, so the arm64 half of every stage runs under emulation — including a full Rust release build.

Measured on the last two releases:

| BuildKit step | v0.5.10 ([run 35279020046](https://github.com/MakePrisms/maxplayerai/actions/runs/35279020046)) | v0.5.9 ([run 35097736399](https://github.com/MakePrisms/maxplayerai/actions/runs/35097736399)) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[linux/arm64 builder 4/4] cargo build …` (emulated) | **6,664.8 s = 111 min** | 6,825.4 s |
| `[linux/amd64 builder 4/4] cargo build …` (native) | 821.2 s = 14 min | 857.3 s |
| `[linux/arm64 stage-2 2/12] apt-get …` (emulated) | 168.7 s | 173.3 s |
| `[linux/arm64 stage-2 3/12] npm install -g …` (emulated) | 158.8 s | 165.1 s |
| export + push | 342.8 s | 225.7 s |
| steps marked CACHED | 0 | 0 |

The same crate is 8.1× slower emulated than native. In v0.5.10 the image job ran 118 min of a 127 min release; v0.5.9 took 161 min. `release` and `publish` both `needs: publish-images`, so this job gates the entire tail of the release. Releases before v0.5.8 — the release that introduced this job — ran 13–18 min.

## The change

One file: `.github/workflows/publish-sandbox-image.yml`. Each platform is built on a runner of its own architecture and the results are merged into a manifest list, which is Docker's documented "distribute build across runners" pattern. Three jobs replace the single job:

- **`plan`** — the existing "Determine image tags" logic, now as job outputs (`version`, `tags`, `netfilter_tags`, `commit`, `prerelease`). Resolved once so the two legs cannot disagree about the version, the tag set or the `MAXPLAYER_BUILD_COMMIT` stamp. Read-only: no registry write.
- **`build`** — a matrix leg per platform: `linux/amd64` on `ubuntu-latest`, `linux/arm64` on `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (already this repo's linux-arm64 builder in `.github/release-platforms.json`). Each leg builds **both** images natively and pushes them **by digest only** (`push-by-digest=true`), then uploads the digests as artifacts with `retention-days: 1`. Cache scopes are per image and per architecture. `fail-fast: false`, so a broken platform does not hide the other's log.
- **`merge`** — applies every tag from `plan` to a manifest list built from the two digests with `docker buildx imagetools create`, then inspects the published tag and **fails unless it lists both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`**. It records the resulting manifest-list digests in the step summary (same table as before) and as job outputs `digest` and `netfilter_digest`.

No emulation remains anywhere in the file. Tags are written only by the merge job, so a version tag never points at a single-architecture image, not even briefly.

Expected: the image job becomes bounded by the slower *native* cold build (~15 min) with the two legs in parallel, rather than by the emulated one — release total ≈ 25 min instead of ~2 h.

**What this does not do.** It does not make the cargo cache warm, and the workflow comments say so explicitly rather than implying a speedup that will not happen. The Dockerfile's cargo caches are `RUN --mount=type=cache` mounts; `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max` exports *layers*, not cache mounts. The v0.5.10 run imported its gha cache manifest and produced zero CACHED steps, because `COPY . .` precedes the build and the source changes every release. Every build here is still a cold build; the win is native-vs-emulated only.

**Unchanged contract.** `release.yml` is not touched. The reusable workflow keeps its `tag` input, its `release`/`workflow_dispatch` triggers, the tag rules (version must start with `v`; a prerelease or any manual dispatch never moves `:latest`), the image names `ghcr.io/makeprisms/maxplayer-sandbox` and `ghcr.io/makeprisms/maxplayer-netfilter`, the digest table in the step summary, and `packages: write` at job level only — requested by the two jobs that write to the registry, while `plan` stays `contents: read`. The digests now recorded are the manifest lists' digests, which is what a seat pulling by tag actually resolves to; the per-architecture digests are an implementation detail of the merge.

## Gates run on this branch

| gate | result |
| --- | --- |
| `./scripts/verify-release-workflow.sh` | exit 0 |
| `actionlint .github/workflows/publish-sandbox-image.yml` (v1.7.12) | exit 0, no findings |
| `grep -c setup-qemu .github/workflows/publish-sandbox-image.yml` | 0 |
| `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD` | 1 file changed, 256 insertions(+), 44 deletions(-) |

Tail of `verify-release-workflow.sh`:

```
ok: verify-surface runs in dry runs and gates release and publish (the #249 fix)
ok: sandbox images are published before the Release and before npm, and neither can proceed without them
ok: release, publish and publish-images are gated on a tag push
ok: 'npm publish' appears only in the publish job and the fenced npm-probe job
ok: npm-probe is dispatch-only, needs a named package, and can publish 0.0.<n> of a payload package only
ok: no other workflow publishes to npm
ok: the publish job requests id-token: write and has no silent-skip path
PASS: .github/workflows/release.yml publishes no RELEASE without a pushed tag, cannot skip publishing quietly, and its one dispatch-triggered publish reaches nothing a release can name
```

## Verification a maintainer has to do — this workflow has not been run

**The workflow has not been executed and this PR makes no claim that it has.** Pushing to `ghcr.io/makeprisms/*` needs this repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN`; a dispatch from a fork would 403. The end-to-end proof is therefore a maintainer's step:

1. Run **Publish sandbox image** by `workflow_dispatch` on this branch with a throwaway prerelease tag, e.g. `v0.0.0-native-runners-test`. A dispatch is treated as a prerelease by design, so it can never move `:latest` — a failed test cannot damage the stable pointer.
2. Confirm two platforms: `docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/makeprisms/maxplayer-sandbox:v0.0.0-native-runners-test` should list `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. Same for `ghcr.io/makeprisms/maxplayer-netfilter`. The merge job asserts this itself and fails if either is missing, so a green run is already evidence; this is the independent check.
3. Delete the throwaway package versions afterwards.

## Follow-up, deliberately not in this PR

The release matrix already builds `maxplayer` natively for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` with `--features wallet,acp` in 4–5 min and uploads them, and the image job already `needs: build`. A second PR can stop compiling Rust inside Docker altogether and `COPY` those artifacts in by `TARGETARCH`, which would take the image job to ~5–8 min and make the release binary and the image binary the same artifact. That needs `mcp-http-bridge` and `tool-mcp-bridge` added to the release Build job first, since the matrix does not build them today. Separate change, separate review.

author: th3mouk
body:
## Summary

`validate (24.x)` has been failing on `main` since 2026-09-08 (verified directly on that CI run) — unrelated to #57, reproduces locally on any Node version, and stems from two independent bugs where a verification step re-resolves dependencies fresh instead of honoring the pinned `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, so it silently fails whenever any transitive dependency publishes a compatible release between commits.

- **`test:npm-shrinkwrap`**: `sync-npm-shrinkwrap.mjs` ran `npm install --package-lock-only` in an *empty* temp directory, so npm had no existing lock to preserve and always resolved every transitive dependency to the registry's current latest. Now seeds the existing `npm-shrinkwrap.json` into the temp directory first, so npm only touches entries that no longer satisfy `package.json`.
- **`test:pack`**: `verify-packed-artifact.mjs` installed the tarball as a dependency of a throwaway project and asserted the installed tree matched `npm-shrinkwrap.json`. That can only pass by coincidence — npm does not honor a nested dependency's own shrinkwrap when resolving it as someone else's dependency (confirmed for both local and global installs). The check now extracts the tarball and installs from inside it, the one mode where `npm-shrinkwrap.json` is actually enforced; the functional smoke tests (`--help`, `init`, `workspace install --dry-run`) keep the original dependency-style install, since that matches real consumer usage.

No dependency versions changed — `npm-shrinkwrap.json` is untouched by this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm check` passes locally end-to-end (multiple consecutive runs, confirming stability rather than a one-off pass)
- [x] Manually tampered a `npm-shrinkwrap.json` entry and confirmed `test:npm-shrinkwrap` still fails on a genuine mismatch (the fix removes false positives, not the check's ability to catch real drift)
- [ ] Confirm this PR's own `validate (24.x)` CI run goes green

The release fingerprint could miss Python behavior or API changes when module filenames stayed the same. Add an additive `python.contract` component covering normalized package ASTs and Python build/dependency metadata. The isolated stdlib parser never imports or executes candidate code, and older snapshot JSON remains readable.

Also correct the installer completion probe for public v0.1.0, whose historical CLI has no `--version` flag. body:
## What

Drops the `if: github.repository != 'devopscoop/aws-eks-template'` line from both jobs, as requested.

## Why it's safe here

The deploy workflow carries that guard because the cluster in the template repo isn't real. This workflow never touches a cluster. All three lookups are account-level and read-only:

| Lookup | Needs a cluster? |
|---|---|
| `/aws/service/eks/optimized-ami/.../release_version` (SSM) | no |
| `aws eks describe-addon-versions --kubernetes-version` | no |
| `aws eks describe-cluster-versions` | no |

And running it here is the point: the pins in this repo's `terraform.tfvars` are what a fork inherits on day one. #104 traded surprise node rotations for the risk of shipping stale pins to every fork — letting the weekly job run here is what makes that trade free.

## ⚠️ One thing that must happen before this does anything useful

`role-to-assume` is still the placeholder both jobs copied from the deploy workflow:

```yaml
role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/github-actions-dev-tf-Role-REDACTED
```

In a fork that gets replaced by hand with the real deploy role. **In this repo it is fake**, so with the guard gone both jobs will now fail at the credentials step every Monday instead of being skipped.

The good news is the role it needs is small — read-only, no cluster access, no write:

- `ssm:GetParameter`
- `eks:DescribeAddonVersions`
- `eks:DescribeClusterVersions`

So it does not need the deploy role. Point `role-to-assume` at a minimal read-only role in whichever account the template repo may read from and both jobs work.

If you'd rather not hardcode a second ARN, I can make it a repository variable with the current value as fallback, so forks keep the existing convention and this repo just sets the variable. Say the word.

## Verification

YAML parses, `zizmor .github/workflows` reports no findings. The behaviour of the jobs themselves is unchanged from #105 — this only removes the skip condition. AGENTS.md updated, since it previously documented the guard as present.

- Retain saved multipart sessions across transient recovery failures and discard them only when the upload session is explicitly missing.

Chores:
- Remove migration and cleanup support for legacy unscoped multipart resume keys.

body:
Reading a saved configuration back needs more than `json.load`: JSON loses a tuple, a dict's key type and a date, and what each field is declared to hold is what puts all three back. That walk, and the `to_jsonable` that writes it, are defined on the STAR driver's configuration module, so a driver that wants to save and load its own configurations has to import from the STAR to get them.

They move to `pylabrobot.utils.configuration_json`, unchanged.

- `to_jsonable`, and the walk that reads a value back against the type its field declares: `Optional`, fixed- and variable-length tuples, lists, dicts including the int keys JSON writes as text, dates, and nested dataclasses. A name the class no longer has is left out, so a file written by a driver that has since dropped a field still loads.
- `star/driver/configuration.py` loses the two definitions and reads with the shared ones instead: 79 lines out, 2 in.
- The five places that wrote with `to_jsonable`, `star/driver/master.py` and four test modules, import it from its new home.

Behaviour: the same walk over the same declared types. Nothing is written or read differently, and no configuration file that loaded before stops loading.

Tests: `configuration_json_tests.py` comes across with the module. The full suite passes (3410 passed, 4 skipped, 952 subtests), under pytest 9.0.3 and 9.1.1 both, since the two differ on `caplog`. `make lint`, `make format-check` and `typos` are clean, and every tracked source parses under Python 3.9. `make typecheck` reports only the nine errors in `li_cor/odyssey/odyssey_tests.py` that are already on `main`, in a file this branch does not touch.

## What

`refaudio/` — an index of real-hardware recordings now available to this project for training and verifying the design (89 packs, 172,182 WAVs, ~121 h) — and `tools/refaudio_fetch.py` to pull a named recording from operator-side storage. **The index is committed; the audio is not.**

## Why here

`docs/discrimination.md` §4: the true floor needs multi-take material, *808 From Mars* "would supply it; it was **not purchased**." It has been purchased. Checked against the index rather than assumed: the clean bass drum is **24 settings × 6 takes** — repeated takes at one setting are the Δ = 0 pairs missing from the left edge of the curve.

## What it does *not* do

**M3 stays blocked.** It needs a real Minimoog filter self-oscillating. The Minimoog pack is patch multisamples; a search of all 3,669 file names finds nothing labelled self-oscillation, resonance, sine or sweep. The README says so, plus the two limits on all of it: **no panel settings ship with any pack** (the Legowelt disqualifier from `moog-recording-protocol.md`), and the recording chain is in every file. No claim in the repo rests on any of this yet.

## Conventions followed

- **Plain text only (#84).** The per-file index is TSV. The full index is 21 MB of text — 4× this repo — so only four packs are indexed by file (both 808 editions, Minimoog, Micromoog); the other 85 are described to folder level in `catalog.json`.
- **Python, not bash.** Status comes from the process.
- **REFUSED is a first-class outcome** (exit 2): no route to the storage, unknown archive, or an escaping path → nothing attempted. It is the normal answer on most hosts.
- **The false green it is built around:** `unzip -p` of a missing member prints nothing, so a naive tool saves a zero-byte `.wav` under the right name. Empty result = FAIL; partial files never survive; a size that disagrees with the index = FAIL.
- Storage address comes from `REFAUDIO_SSH` / `REFAUDIO_ROOT`, so none is committed. Hosts without them: open a `reference-audio` issue (label created).

## Evidence

- `python -m pytest tools/test_refaudio_fetch.py` — **12 passed**, no network (`ssh` stubbed on PATH).
- **Injected-defect control: 5 mutations, 5 caught.** Wrong-then-right, for calibration: the first run caught **4 of 5**. Deleting the zero-byte guard went unnoticed, because on an *indexed* member the size check rejects an empty file too. The test now targets an unindexed pack — where that guard is the only one there is.
- Against the real storage: two fetches (size matches index), a missing member (FAIL, nothing left on disk), no environment (REFUSED).

Not done: `make test` does not collect `tools/` (it doesn't for `test_run_all.py` either), so these run by hand. Left alone rather than changing the Makefile in this PR.

author: sftimeless
body:
## Summary

The scheduled **TSA trust bundle maintenance** job has failed on every run: 100 of the last 100. Each run refreshed and proved the bundle, then died opening its pull request:

```
pull request create failed: GraphQL: GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests (createPullRequest)
```

This repository has "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (`can_approve_pull_request_reviews: false`). Three consequences:

- **No refresh PR was ever opened**, so the release-pinned CRL snapshots went stale. The earliest `next_update` was 2026-09-16T21:36:52Z, and the freshness guard fails every keel-verifier PR and release until they are refreshed.
- **About 90 branches accumulated**, one timestamped `chore/tsa-trust-refresh-*` branch per run.
- **The failure was silent in practice.** A scheduled run fails in the Actions tab, not on anyone's PR.

This PR does two things.

### 1. The refresh itself (commit authored by `keel-tsa-maintenance`)

This is the job's own newest proposal, taken unchanged from `chore/tsa-trust-refresh-20260918T095549Z`, which run 35331873481 pushed. That run proved it before failing: every CRL's issuer matched the vendored issuer certificate and its signature verified, and Ruff, the historical compatibility corpus, the TSA real-crypto tests and the full suite passed (1,157 passed). It updates the three DigiCert CRL snapshots, the trust bundle, the embedded release manifest, the coupled receipt fixtures, and the pinned bundle digest in `verifier.py`.

### 2. The job fix

The proposal step moves into `scripts/propose_tsa_trust_refresh.sh`:

- **One standing branch.** Each run replaces `chore/tsa-trust-refresh` instead of creating a new branch.
- **No duplicate PRs.** If a review PR from that branch is open, the run refreshes it. Otherwise it opens one.
- **No failure when the token may not open PRs.** The run files one standing issue, "TSA trust refresh ready for review", or comments on the existing one. The issue carries a one-click link to open the ready PR. The run then succeeds, and the issue is the signal.
- **Unchanged:** the job never merges; a person merges trust material. The proof steps before the proposal are untouched. The workflow gains `issues: write`.

The repository setting stays as it is. The job now works without it; turning it on would only let the job open the PR itself.

## Validation

- `tests/test_tsa_maintenance_workflow_contract.py`: 7 passed.
  - 2 contract tests, now covering the script.
  - 5 behaviour tests that run the script against a throwaway git remote with a stubbed `gh`: the first proposal opens a PR; a blocked PR falls back to one issue; an existing issue is commented on rather than duplicated; an open PR is refreshed rather than duplicated; repeated runs replace the single standing branch.
- `scripts/check_tsa_trust_bundle_freshness.py --min-valid-days 7`: passes on this branch.
- `tests/test_tsa_trust.py`: 27 passed.
- `ruff check .`: clean.
- The full suite ran green on the refresh commit in run 35331873481, as above. CI runs it again here.

## After merging

- **The 89 older `chore/tsa-trust-refresh-2026*` branches** are superseded and can be deleted. Not done here.
- **The next scheduled run** should find the bundle current and succeed without proposing anything. `workflow_dispatch` can confirm it straight away.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a way to find full PNR records stored in Google Drive by the six-digit bag-tag serial and automatically populate missing PNRs on CBS cases. 
- Avoid blocking the unresolved-baggage list render on Drive I/O by performing record lookups asynchronously in the background.

### Description
- Add `cbsRecordParser.js` with `bagTagSectionHasSerial` and `extractPnrRecordsForBagTag` to locate bag-tag sections and extract PNR records by serial. 
- Extend `googleDrive.js` with Drive helpers (`listDriveChildren`, `readCbsRecordFile`, `cbsRecordDateKeys`) and a new `findCbsPnrRecordsByBagTag` function that searches configured Drive folders and returns deduplicated matching records. 
- Hook into the app (`index.js`) to normalize bag-tag inputs, determine candidate cases, and add `syncMissingCbsPnrRecords` / `startCbsPnrRecordSync` for background synchronization plus a `POST /cbs-record-sync` endpoint. 
- Update the unresolved-baggage listing to set `Cache-Control: no-store`, return the list immediately, and schedule background PNR sync with `setImmediate`. 
- Update the public UI `cbs.html` to use `AbortController`, a client-side timeout for the `/cbs-unresolved-baggage` fetch, and add a Firebase header for `cbs.html` to prevent caching. 
- Export the new Drive lookup (`findCbsPnrRecordsByBagTag`) and wire it into the module exports. 

### Testing
- Added unit tests `test/cbsRecordParser.test.js` to verify parsing and `test/cbsPage.test.js` assertions for the new server and client behavior, and ran the test suite using the existing `node:test` harness.

author: matheusciocca
body:
## Por que

A geração de quiz estava quebrada em produção: o modelo que o app mandava por padrão para a Groq (`llama-3.3-70b-versatile`) não existe mais e respondia 404. Quem abria o gerador e não trocava o modelo na mão não gerava nada, e o erro estourava na tela do professor.

Na raiz disso estava um catálogo de modelos mantido por digitação humana, que envelhecia calado. Quatro dos oito modelos oferecidos no seletor já não existiam, o contexto cadastrado estava errado para menos em todos os vivos, e o app só descobria isso na cara de quem estava usando.

## O que muda

**A geração volta a funcionar e para de mentir.** O modelo padrão passa a ser resolvido pelo catálogo ativo, por uma política determinística (`llmModelPolicy.js`), em vez de um nome fixo no código. O `groqClient` para de completar a lista duplicando questões com "(variação N)" e a tela informa quantas questões vieram de verdade.

**Cadeia de fallback entre modelos.** Um modelo que sumiu do provedor passa a vez para o próximo da política, e a troca vira aviso informativo em vez de erro. Só um 404 de modelo avança a fila: limite de tokens ou chave inválida param na hora, porque repetir com outro modelo não resolveria.

**O catálogo se mantém sozinho.** `scripts/syncLlmModels.mjs` puxa a lista real da Groq, filtra por capacidade declarada e roda um canário por candidato, porque metadado não garante que a conta consegue usar o modelo. Dry-run por padrão, três portões de sanidade e nunca apaga registro: aposentar é `isActive: false` com motivo. Roda todo dia pelo novo workflow, às 06:00 de Brasília.

**Orçamento de tokens a partir do catálogo.** As duas pontas que decidiam sozinhas (corte do PDF e reserva de saída) viraram uma conta só, alimentada pelos campos sincronizados. Um pedido de 30 questões agora volta com 30; antes voltava com ~10 por causa de um piso de 1024 tokens.

**Importação de questões por JSON.** Quem já gerou as questões em outro lugar passa a ter por onde importá-las pelo app, caindo na mesma área de conferência do gerador por PDF. Era a origem das questões sem `id` que quebraram um quiz em 17/09.

## Três coisas medidas contra a API real, que mudaram o desenho

- o limite de tokens por minuto é **por modelo**, não por conta: 8.000 no `openai/gpt-oss-120b` contra 70.000 no `groq/compound`, com o mesmo contexto de 131.072;
- existe um **teto por requisição** que nenhum cabeçalho anuncia: 16.000 tokens numa chamada ao `compound-mini` devolvem 413, com 36.590 tokens ainda livres na janela do minuto;
- os melhores modelos do catálogo gastam parte do `max_tokens` **raciocinando** antes de escrever, e sem reserva para isso a resposta volta vazia.

## Como foi verificado

Suíte em 805 testes, 59 arquivos, incluindo os 215 de emulador. Geração real conferida contra a API da Groq: 5 questões pedidas voltam 5, e 30 pedidas voltam 30 completas numa tacada. O script de sincronização já rodou em produção e no emulador, e o catálogo está com os seis modelos ativos e os campos de capacidade corretos.

## Depois do merge

O workflow agendado só passa a existir para o GitHub depois que este arquivo chegar na branch padrão. O primeiro disparo automático é no dia seguinte; dá para antecipar pelo disparo manual, que tem um `dry_run` para conferir o diff sem gravar.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw logs --follow` exiting when the Gateway connection fails with `Opening handshake has timed out`, as reported on Discord.

## User Impact

Log following reconnects after this transient handshake timeout and resumes output when the Gateway recovers. Repeated failures still stop after the existing eight retries; authentication and pairing failures keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The follow retry owner recognized typed transport errors and plain Gateway close/request-timeout errors, but omitted the plain timeout message emitted by the WebSocket client. This adds that exact message to the existing retry classification and consolidates duplicate retry-exhaustion test setup.

## Evidence

- The recovery and retry-bound regressions failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- Four focused logs CLI suites passed: 68 tests covering the CLI, runtime, plain/color output, and port selection.

1: 1fa5e9c9c3d = 1: 796f3287968 fix(cli): retry log follow after a Gateway handshake timeout

The stable patch IDs also match, so the existing scoped-clean P1 review stands. author: miroslav-jokovic
body:
**B7.** Two additions to the wizard, and neither touches the machinery under it.

### 1. An untouched link opens on what it involves

Eight screens, about thirty minutes, the list of them with an estimate each, what to have to hand
(addresses, employment history, licence, and the four documents the capture screen will ask to
photograph), and the two things nobody expects — that the carrier's permissions are signed *before*
the form, and that the signature on the application itself is a second, short visit.

The length of this application used to be discovered by walking it. A driver who opens the link with
four minutes to spare and meets §391.21(b)(11)'s ten years of driving history abandons it, and the
answers they did type are worth nothing to anybody. The screen is the decision — start now, or this
evening — with the two facts a person needs to make it.

⚠ **It sits ahead of the 7001(c) consent, and that does not disturb D-APP5.** A4's ruling is that
nothing is ASKED and nothing is WRITTEN before the consent; this screen has no field on it and writes
nothing, so the consent is still the first thing the driver *does*. Behind the consent and the four
signatures it would have set expectations for the form only — and the permissions coming first is the
part nobody expects.

**Nothing about having seen it is remembered.** `linkHasBeenUsed` derives "has this person started"
from a consent, a signed permission or a saved draft — no column, no write on an unauthenticated
route. Somebody who opens the link twice having done nothing is told the same thing twice, which is
the right answer to having done nothing.

### 2. Per-step estimates on `ApplyProgress`'s list

The list now answers "how much is left" with a quantity instead of a count of screens, on every row
including the ones behind the driver.

⚠ **Q-AX1's three rulings are untouched**: the bar still only INDICATES (and a test pins that it
renders no text at all), forward is still fenced at the high-water mark, and everything navigable is
still a real button.

### The minutes are a property of the section

`APPLICATION_SECTION_MINUTES` lives in `applicationSections.ts`, keyed by the union beside the labels
and the citations, so **a screen cannot exist without an estimate** and the expectations screen and
the step list cannot disagree about how long a screen takes. `APPLICATION_FILLING_MINUTES` is their
sum rather than a number anybody types, and it is rounded to the nearest five on the way to the
screen — printing a sum of eight guesses to the minute would dress a judgement up as a stopwatch.

⚠ They are judgements from the shape of each screen, **not measurements**. Nothing times a driver
today; `application_drafts.furthest_section` plus its timestamps is a measurement of exactly this,
and A10's sweep is where these constants should eventually be checked against a clock.

### Verification

- **Walked at 390px and 1440px** with the invitation `route.fulfill`ed — the expectations screen, the
  step list's estimate column, and Start through into the form, in both the wording-published and
  wording-draft states. Ten steps running have shipped a defect the whole suite was green for.
- **Eight mutations, eight correct failures** — every row showing the same estimate; no estimate at
  all; the capture *vocabulary* instead of the *requested* list; the certification listed as a screen
  of this visit; the rounding removed; the abandoned-ceremony disjunct dropped; the permissions
  sentence shown unconditionally; the screen yielding to the consent gate.
- ⚠ **Twelve `ApplyPage.test.ts` tests failed on the first run and nine were right to** — their
  fixtures describe a link nobody has touched, which is now exactly the case that opens on this
  screen. Three press Start through a helper that *asserts* the button is there; the rest passed again
  once `linkHasBeenUsed` counted a draft with something typed into it.
- Gates: `typecheck` · `lint` · `lint:filesize` · `lint:funcsize` · `lint:boundaries` ·
  `lint:comment-claims` · `lint:surfaces` · `lint:ui-adoption` · `--filter web lint:tokens` · web
  (2,017) and shared (2,955) suites.

**No migration** — 0344 is still the head, 0345 still next. Stacked on #883, which lifted the sending
half out of `ApplyPage.vue` to make room; that is merged and this is rebased on main.

author: gebner
body:
Follow-up to #4395: the generic test-suite extraction rule now runs Custard,
so the legacy `--codegen OCaml`/`FSharp` pipeline is no longer exercised by
the test suites. The bootstrap (F*, Pulse, plugins) is deliberately left for a
later PR.

### The lever

`mk/test.mk`'s `$(OUTPUT_DIR)/%.ml` and `%.fs` rules run
`--codegen Custard --custard_entry_module <M>`, which is what `--extract_module`
was. That switches twenty-odd directories at once. `%.krml` deliberately stays
legacy.

### Goldens

29 `.ml`/`.fs` goldens regenerated across `tests/bug-reports/closed`,
`tests/extraction`, `tests/extraction/cmi/{1,2,3}`, `tests/micro-benchmarks`
and `tests/tactics`. Seven became empty, which is correct and is explained in a
comment: a whole-program compiler with no roots extracts nothing.
`tests/extraction/backends` keeps its legacy legs on purpose --- comparing the
backends is what it is for --- and six of its XFAIL cells are retired.

### Defects the legacy suites found

* **`noextract_to` was ignored entirely** (§126.3), and §4.3 claimed otherwise.
  `noextract_to_this_backend` now filters entry-module rooting. New test
  `tests/custard/NoExtractTo.fst`. The *reaching* half is still a gap and the
  doc now says so.
* **An erasable effect with a `repr` was reified rather than erased** (§125.10):
  such an effect is both erasable and reifiable, and Custard tested
  reifiability first, so a `MGhost int` came back as an `int`. New test
  `tests/custard/ErasableEff.fst`.
* **Two coercion bugs around values of no representation** (§126.6), found by
  CI and not by the local gate. A lambda binder whose type is exactly `TAny`
  bound nothing, so no use of it was coerced and OCaml inferred a type from one
  `match` branch that the next contradicted; and a call over-applying a head
  that returns `TAny` was coerced only when the expected type was known. New
  test `tests/custard/AnyLambda.fst`.

### The Makefiles that are documentation

`tests/{simple_hello,dune_hello}`, `examples/{dependencies,data_structures}`
and `examples/layeredeffects/extraction` are read as examples of how to build
an F* program, so they are rewritten rather than patched (§126.4).
`examples/dependencies` collapses four build steps to one extraction run and
one `ocamlopt`; `examples/data_structures` drops the hack of appending
`let _ = test()` to the extracted module for `--custard_main`.

### Two losses, both recorded

* `tests/floats/Test01` loses its `Float32` half (§126.7). Custard refuses
  binary32 on the OCaml backend by design (§66.4) --- OCaml has one float type
  and it is binary64 --- where the legacy backend emulated the rounding in a
  realization. The coverage moves to `FloatExtract` and
  `tests/custard/Floats.fst`.
* `fsharp/tests/{Hello,Test00}` drop their hand-written projects for the one
  Custard generates, and grow a `main` (§126.8): .NET has no load-time
  execution, so a module whose top-level effect prints is a program on OCaml
  and a library that does nothing on F#.

### What stays behind, and why (§126.5)

* The **plugin** tests (`tests/tactics`, `tests/semiring`,
  `examples/native_tactics`): a plugin's OCaml links against the compiler's own
  OCaml names, which Custard learns from a `.cui` that only a Custard-built
  compiler produces. Blocked on the bootstrap.
* `pulse/test/pool`: erasing every parameter of a function whose result is an
  `stt_div` leaves Custard *forcing* a suspended computation, so a worker loop
  would run inline in the spawning thread. Pulse effect handling, not test
  plumbing.

### Testing

`make -C tests all`, `make -C examples all`, `doc/book/code`, `pulse/test` (cold
cache), `pulse/share/pulse/examples`, `tests/custard` and `tests/custard/pulse`,
`make custard custard-smoke custard-plugin`, all seven `check-*` targets, and
`make -C fsharp all`.

author: claude[bot]
body:
Closes #619

## What changed

A pin button (tooltip "Pin: keep showing this" / "Unpin") in a
popped-out tool window's own frame (`PaneFrame`, `pane_frame.slint`) -
only there: `PaneFrame` gains `pinnable`/`pinned` and a `pin-clicked`/
`unpin-clicked` pair, but only `file-pane`'s own instantiation in
`app.slint` sets `pinnable: true`, so Folders and Contents windows
never offer it, since they are the selection.

Pinning freezes what the tool slot is showing - its own file or
folder preview, or edit in progress - independent of the shared
selection every other window follows (`App::pin_current`, a
`PinnedWindow` snapshot keyed by a `PinId` that never repeats). The
window's title gains the pinned item's name. Several pinned windows
can coexist: popping the File tool out again opens another window
rather than reusing a pinned one (`PaneWindows.pinned:
HashMap<PinId, MainWindow>`, separate from the single-slot `popped`
map Folders/Contents/the live File pop-out still use).

- **Unpinning** drops the snapshot and returns the window to following
  the shared selection straight away (plain `sync_ui`, the same as
  any other live window).
- **Docking a pinned window, or closing it from the platform's own
  decoration,** closes it outright: there is no pane slot of its own
  left in the main window to return into, since a fresh pop-out never
  reclaims a pinned window.
- **Editing while pinned** works exactly as unpinned - its own
  keystrokes, undo/redo, cut/copy/paste, tab and view choice, and Save
  writes through the service the same way - but a pinned save never
  reaches into the shared selection's own reload bookkeeping (the
  pinned file may not even be in the folder currently browsed); it
  re-requests its own fresh preview once the write lands instead.
- **A pinned path that goes away** (deleted or renamed, from inside
  this application or outside it) is noticed against the filesystem
  directly - the same reasoning `classify_root_problem` already gives
  for the Repos Directory's own root, rather than trying to tell
  "gone" apart from "unreadable" by parsing the service's error
  strings - and the pane says so ("`name` is no longer there."), with
  Unpin still offered rather than the window closing on its own.

### Implementation shape

`App`'s file-pane and editor methods (`file_text`, `file_lines`,
`edit_key`, `begin_file_edit`, `save_file_edit`, ...) each had their
logic lifted into a free `..._of(file_view, ...)` /
`..._of(editing_file, ...)` function; the existing method becomes a
thin wrapper over the shared selection's own fields, and a new
`pinned_...` method wraps the same function over a `PinnedWindow`'s
fields. Neither copy can drift from the other, and every existing
call site and test is untouched.

`PaneWindows.pinned` windows are wired once, up front, in
`wire_pop_out`: their pin/unpin/dock/close callbacks read a shared
`pin_slot: Rc<Cell<Option<PinId>>>` rather than being replaced when
the window is actually pinned - replacing a callback from inside its
own invocation (pinning, from the very `pin-requested` handler a
click just entered) panics Slint's generated code ("Callback Handler
set while called").

### Out of scope

Layout persistence across launches (GUIDANCE.md §2.6's "which panes
are popped out, and where") is #620's, not this issue's.

## Acceptance checks

- [x] Unit tests: a pinned view keeps its own file while the shared
      selection moves on; unpinning drops its snapshot; a save while
      pinned never touches the shared selection's own reload; a
      pinned path going away is noticed and still offers Unpin
      (`crates/gui/src/app.rs`, `app::tests::pinning_keeps_its_own_file_while_the_shared_selection_moves_on`,
      `unpinning_drops_its_own_snapshot`,
      `saving_a_pinned_edit_does_not_touch_the_shared_selections_own_reload`,
      `a_pinned_files_disappearance_is_noticed_and_still_offers_to_unpin`).
- [x] A window test pops out the tool slot on file A, pins it, selects
      file B in Contents, and asserts the pinned window still shows A
      while a fresh pop-out shows B; then unpins and asserts it shows
      B (`crates/gui/tests/pin_the_pane.rs::pinning_keeps_its_file_while_the_shared_selection_moves_on_and_unpinning_follows_it_again`).
      Docking and closing a pinned window are covered too
      (`docking_a_pinned_window_closes_it`,
      `closing_a_pinned_window_from_its_own_decoration_closes_it_too`).
- [x] A window test deletes the pinned file through the application
      (`App::request_delete`/`confirm_delete`, the same flow the
      keyboard drives) and asserts the "no longer there" message and
      that Unpin stays offered
      (`crates/gui/tests/pin_the_pane.rs::deleting_the_pinned_file_through_the_application_is_noticed_and_still_offers_to_unpin`).
- [ ] Driven in the built window, with a screenshot of a pinned editor
      beside the main window - **not captured**. Same conclusion #657
      and #655/#628 before it reached: this factory's environment is
      Linux with no display and carries no screenshot or
      window-driving tooling of its own; a human should confirm
      before merging.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` - clean.
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` -
      clean.
- [x] `cargo test --all-features -p gui` - every unit test and
      integration suite in the crate, including the new ones, green.

author: kinfe123
body: ## Problem Reasoning content can move between scroll containers through portals or layout changes. After its first animation, `useScrollLock` keeps locking the original container, leaving the current container unlocked and modifying the wrong element. ## Root cause The hook caches the first scrollable ancestor for its entire lifetime and never invalidates that cache when the animated element is reparented. ## Change Resolve the nearest scrollable ancestor whenever a lock begins. The previous lock is still cleaned up first, so styles and listeners move cleanly from the old container to the current one. ## Verification - `pnpm vitest run src/primitives/reasoning/useScrollLock.test.tsx --reporter=dot` - `pnpm exec oxlint packages/react/src/primitives/reasoning/useScrollLock.ts packages/react/src/primitives/reasoning/useScrollLock.test.tsx` - `pnpm --filter @assistant-ui/react... build` - `pnpm changesets:check` The added regression test locks one container, reparents the animated element, and confirms the old container is restored while the new container receives the lock. It fails with the previous permanent ancestor cache. ## Public surface - `@assistant-ui/react` behavior only. - Patch changeset included. - No export, documentation, or template changes.

author: thestuartchan
body:
**What happened.** The #179 squash-merge landed on main at 20:22Z. Vercel had built the data commit twenty minutes earlier (0961e2e, still live) and registered a preview of the branch eight minutes later, and never registered a production deployment for the merge at all. The checker waited on it to its timeout reporting "queued".

**Change.** `verdict` takes the commit's age. Once a commit is older than `DROPPED_AFTER_MIN` (10 minutes) with no deployment registered and the site serving a build that does not contain it, the checker says the push event was missed and names the remedy — a follow-up push to main. The wait loop stops there instead of running down the clock. The commit time is read from GitHub; when it cannot be, the wording stays "queued", never assumed.

**This merge is also that follow-up push:** it re-triggers Vercel and carries #179 (phone archive editing) with it.

**Verification.** checkDeploy 40; full suite + guards green; lint unchanged at 58. Run live against the #179 merge, the checker now prints:
```
✘ Vercel registered no deployment for 0e55d7f in 10 min — the push event was missed, not queued
  dvcap.vercel.app is serving 0961e2e, age 615s, which does not contain it.
  A follow-up push to main re-triggers the build: the next merge or data commit carries this one with it.
```

author: kinfe123
body: ## Problem `pnpm create @farm.js/app@beta` can continue launching an older cached initializer after a newer beta is published. Existing guidance only disabled pnpm's release-age policy, so users could still receive an old `@farm.js/create-app` beta from the `create`/`dlx` metadata cache. ## Root cause `minimum-release-age` controls whether newly published packages may be installed; it does not refresh the metadata cache used to resolve a `dlx`/`create` dist-tag. The documented command therefore addressed dependency eligibility but not stale `beta` tag resolution. ## Change - Use `--config.dlx-cache-max-age=0` to force fresh `create`/`dlx` metadata. - Keep `--config.minimum-release-age=0` so a just-published beta and its dependencies remain eligible. - Normalize the pnpm option to its documented kebab-case spelling. - Update every pnpm beta scaffold command across docs, package READMEs, starter READMEs, homepage UI, playground, generated OG copy, setup output, and the Farm skill. - Add a repository-wide regression test that rejects incomplete pnpm beta scaffold commands. ## Safety and compatibility Both settings are scoped to the single initializer invocation and do not change the user's global pnpm configuration. npm, Yarn, and Bun commands are unchanged. Template selection and generated application behavior are unchanged. ## Verification - `node --test scripts/scaffold-beta-command.test.js` - `pnpm --filter @farm.js/create-app test` (16 passed) - `pnpm --filter @farm.js/create-app type-check` - `pnpm docs:check-navigation` - `pnpm --config.dlx-cache-max-age=0 --config.minimum-release-age=0 config get dlx-cache-max-age` - `pnpm --config.dlx-cache-max-age=0 --config.minimum-release-age=0 config get minimum-release-age` - `pnpm exec oxfmt ` - `git diff --check` ## Documentation and release Updated all maintained beta scaffold instructions and UI copy. No package version was edited; the corrected guidance ships with the next docs/create-app release. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `pnpm create @farm.js/app@beta` so it always resolves the newest published beta instead of reusing a cached older initializer. The old `--config.minimumReleaseAge=0` setting only allowed newly released packages; it did not refresh pnpm's `create`/`dlx` metadata cache, so users could still scaffold from a stale beta. The command now also passes `--config.dlx-cache-max-age=0` to force fresh metadata, and both settings are scoped to the single invocation without touching global pnpm config. **Changes** - `--config.dlx-cache-max-age=0` now refreshes pnpm's cached `create`/`dlx` metadata before resolving the `beta` tag. - Kept `--config.minimum-release-age=0` so a just-published beta and its dependencies remain eligible. - Normalized the pnpm option to its documented kebab-case spelling. - Updated every pnpm beta scaffold command across docs, READMEs, homepage UI, playground, generated OG copy, setup script, and the Farm skill. - Added a regression test (`scripts/scaffold-beta-command.test.js`) that fails any pnpm beta scaffold command missing the two config flags. - npm, Yarn, and Bun scaffold commands are unchanged. Written for commit 195a24d30f5064fc11158bd7e6b47b9c3867753d. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
## Summary
Corrige les 3 points relevés lors de l'audit de responsivité du site, chacun vérifié visuellement en local (Playwright, plusieurs largeurs 320–1440px) avant de passer au suivant :

- **`components/home/Newsletter.tsx`** — Les paddings fixes en pixels (`md:pl-[110px]`, `md:pr-[120px]`) resserraient le formulaire juste après le breakpoint `md`. Remplacés par un palier intermédiaire `md:`/`lg:` plus souple. La vérification a aussi révélé un bug plus profond : `flex-1` sur le champ e-mail, combiné à `flex-col`, transformait son axe principal en hauteur et écrasait `h-14` (le champ s'effondrait à ~20px de haut) — préexistant sur mobile (<640px), mais amplifié par le nouveau point de bascule `lg:flex-row`. Corrigé (`w-full lg:flex-1`), champ et bouton restent à 56px de haut à toutes les largeurs.
- **`components/home/IndicateursSection.tsx`** — Ajout d'un palier intermédiaire `sm:grid-cols-3`. Le saut vers 5 colonnes a aussi été repoussé de `md:` (768px, où le texte se resserrait/cassait mal) à `lg:` (1024px, où il y a réellement la place).
- **`components/layout/nav/DropdownMenu.tsx`** — Ajout d'une détection de bord d'écran pour le sous-menu de niveau 2 : mesure de sa position réelle après ouverture (`useLayoutEffect`) et bascule automatique de `left-full` vers `right-full` s'il déborderait du viewport, sans régression sur le cas normal.

`npx tsc --noEmit` et `npm run build` passent sans erreur.

## Test plan
- [x] Vérification visuelle locale (captures à 320/375/640/700/768/900/1024/1100/1280/1440px) pour chacun des 3 correctifs
- [x] Test explicite du basculement du sous-menu (simulation d'un item proche du bord droit) confirmant `right-full` s'active et que le cas normal (`left-full`) n'est pas régressé

author: jorgefilipecosta
body:
Fixes the Term Template block reading `termQuery` keys that the markup can leave out. When a Terms Query block is written by hand or shipped in a pattern, its `termQuery` attribute can carry only some keys. The Block Bindings documentation itself uses `{"taxonomy":"category","perPage":5}`. The editor copes with that: its REST request simply omits the missing keys, so the terms endpoint defaults apply (ordered by name, ascending, empty terms included) and every term is listed. The server-side renderer read `perPage`, `order`, `orderBy` and `hideEmpty` unconditionally instead. On PHP 8 each missing key logs an "Undefined array key" warning, `WP_Term_Query` adds two `strtolower(): Passing null` deprecations, and the `null` arguments make the front end order the terms newest first while the editor preview shows them by name. To fix this we fall back, with `??`, to the values the editor effectively requests for missing keys: all terms, `asc`, `name`, empty terms included, and `category` as the taxonomy. This is the shape core uses in `build_query_vars_from_query_block()` for the Query block. For published content with partial markup the only visible change is the order, which now matches the editor; nothing is logged any more. Markup that sets the keys renders exactly as before, including `perPage: 0`, which means "all terms". A PHPUnit test covers the partial markup and checks that explicit values still take precedence. Rendering the documentation markup on a taxonomy with six populated terms and one empty term, on trunk and with this change: | | Trunk | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | | Log | 3 undefined key warnings, 2 deprecations | nothing | | Terms rendered | 5, newest first | 5, by name, as in the editor preview | This block's PHP ships in WordPress core through the package, so the same change reaches the core copy with the next package sync. ## Testing Instructions 1. Enable `WP_DEBUG` and `WP_DEBUG_LOG`. 2. Create six categories with a published post each, plus one category without posts. 3. In the code editor of a new page, paste the markup from the [Block Bindings documentation](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/blob/trunk/docs/reference-guides/block-api/block-bindings.md#coreterm-data) and publish the page: ```html

Category Name

``` 4. View the page. On trunk the debug log gains "Undefined array key" warnings for `order`, `orderBy` and `hideEmpty` and the terms are listed newest first. With this PR the five first categories by name render, in the same order as the editor preview, and nothing is logged. 5. Run `npm run test:unit:php:base -- --filter Tests_Blocks_RenderTermTemplateBlock` and verify both tests pass. AI usage disclosure: fix, tests and description drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by me.

author: cirwel
body:
## What

Makes PR review a gate like tests: one command, keyed on the diff, started automatically, and checked by CI.

- `scripts/dev/review.sh`: has the **other** model review the PR diff (codex reviews `claude/*` and others, claude reviews `codex/*`, and it refuses a branch's own model). Read-only, 30-min budget. Posts a **review record** comment.
- `ship.sh` starts it in the background on every PR push (`SHIP_NO_REVIEW=1` skips it).
- `.github/workflows/review-gate.yml` sets a `review` commit status from the latest record for the PR's **current diff**:
  - CLEAN → green
  - FINDINGS(n) with a numbered disposition per finding → green
  - findings not yet answered, or no record → pending
  - reviewer crashed or ran out of time → FAILED
- A later CLEAN on the same diff does not clear open findings, and one disposition answers one findings record.
- `review.sh record` accepts any review as the record: a council, a human, another model. CI uses GITHUB_TOKEN only and calls no model (execution-cost policy).
- The diff key is sha256 of `git diff --raw` (path, mode and blob of each changed file) against the merge base with the PR's base branch. A base merge that doesn't touch the PR's files keeps the key.

## Why

"Review round joined" before marking ready was prose. Across the last 60 merged PRs, reviews appear as free-form text in some bodies and comments and not at all in others, and nothing could check which.

## Limits, stated rather than papered over

- **Bootstrap:** `pull_request_target` loads the workflow from the base branch, so **this PR cannot get its own `review` status**. The review records below are real and ran through the new path; the check starts working once this merges.
- **The gate proves a review was recorded, not that it was honest.** Every agent posts through the same GitHub account, so no comment-based gate can tell an author's own record from a reviewer's. It makes a review impossible to forget and visible to check, not impossible to fake. This is documented in the script and in the conventions doc.
- Making `review` a **required** check in branch protection is the maintainer's step, after merge.
- Bot PRs get no exemption: the ruff bump that masked the suite for 26 days was a dependency bump.

## Dogfood

Every push to this PR went through `ship.sh` → background codex review → record. Six rounds so far found 11 findings; 8 were fixed, with regression tests in `tests/test_review_gate.py` (30 tests). The recurring "author can post their own record" and "fetch updates `origin/<base>`" findings are answered in the dispositions.

## Tests

`tests/test_review_gate.py` (30), `tests/test_ship_workflow.py`, `tests/test_stuck_draft_audit.py`, shared-contract check, repo-scope guard.

author: gouarin
body:
Second of three, on top of #66. Third adds the cell deltas and descriptions to the
header.

`trysquare watch <matrix dir>` serves the directory a launch is filling, on
`127.0.0.1`. The header, the progress and the cell counts come from `state.json` and
`measures.json`; the runs in flight come from `live.json`.

## A reader, and only a reader

Three routes, named one by one, rather than a URL mapped onto a file. A test asks for
`/secret.txt`, `/state.json`, `/../../etc/passwd` and `/runs/a/diff.patch` and gets four
404s. Another compares every `mtime` in the tree before and after serving. Nothing in
the measurement path imports this module.

Loopback only. A matrix directory holds prompts, diffs and session transcripts, which
are the work of whoever ran it and not something a harness puts on an interface because
a dashboard was convenient.

## Counts, and never a verdict

While the matrix is incomplete a cell is `4/7` and nothing else. Runs are interleaved by
repetition, so every cell holds about the same handful at any moment, and an interval
drawn over four runs would swing visibly at each one that lands - on a projector, in
front of a room. `resolve` already refuses to write a synthesis for a launch restricted
by `--only`, and a screen is not a better reason than a command line was.

On completion the page links to `synthesis.html`. The verdict is that file's to give:
recomputing it here is how two answers to one question come to disagree.

The counts do not apply the scenario's `validity` filter, which lives in a file this
command is not given, so they can exceed the published ones. The page says so rather
than leaving a number that quietly means something else.

## Two counts per run

`tok/s` comes off `message_end` and is exact. `maj/s` is the pulse of the stream updates
the sieve throws away, about two characters each, and is labelled as a writing rhythm
rather than a token rate.

## Measured

Eighteen runs on `ilaas`/`gemma-4-31b`, watched from a browser end to end: twelve in
flight with their model, turns, tokens and pulse; the grid filling cell by cell; the
completion flipping the badge and revealing the synthesis link. The dashboard's counts
match the synthesis it then links to (`nothing`: `delivered 2/2`, `suite_lancee 0/2`,
`rebond_briques 1/2`). No console errors.

A launch killed with `SIGKILL` leaves `finished` empty and its runs marked running; the
heartbeat from #66 is what turns that into `silent`, confirmed against a real killed
launch.

Four things the browser caught that reading the file did not: `td.warn` did not exist,
so a retried run sat in the same grey as everything else; a completed matrix wore the
red badge of a stop; twelve metrics dragged the page sideways and clipped the last
column; and scrolling to reach it lost the cell names. The tables now scroll in their
own box with the first column pinned.

The cheat sheet and the README follow, because the suite pins the number of subcommands
and refuses the ninth until it is documented.

author: dextheking1
body:
## Proposed change

The Blink coordinator called `self.api.refresh(force=True)` on **every** scheduled update. In BlinkPy, a forced refresh is propagated to each sync module as `force_cache=True`:

```python
async def refresh(self, force=False, force_cache=False):
    if force or force_cache or self.check_if_ok_to_update():
        ...
        await sync_module.refresh(force_cache=(force or force_cache))
```

`force_cache=True` makes a sync module re-download media it has already cached, so identical motion-clip MP4s were downloaded again on every 300 second poll. Reporters measured ~230 GB of downstream traffic in a week with 14 cameras, with the same `cv_motion/<media_id>.mp4` URLs requested repeatedly at five minute intervals.

This change drops the forced refresh. BlinkPy's own default refresh rate is 30 seconds while the integration's scan interval is 300 seconds, so `check_if_ok_to_update()` still returns true on every scheduled poll and state updates on the same cadence, but cached media is no longer re-fetched.

Fixes #182552

## Type of change

- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Additional information

- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #182552
- This PR is related to issue: 
- Link to documentation pull request: 
- Link to developer documentation pull request: 
- Link to frontend pull request: 

I verified the call contract directly against the installed BlinkPy (`blinkpy==0.25.9`): `MIN_THROTTLE_TIME` is 2s, `DEFAULT_REFRESH` is 30s, and the throttle decorator only sleeps briefly, it never skips the call. So a non-forced refresh still runs on the 300s scan interval. The added test asserts a scheduled poll calls `refresh()` with no arguments; against the previous code that same assertion fails with `force=True`.

body:
## Problem

A neighbor-MISS frame could be parked with its translated pending decision while the shared slow-path outlet copied the original untranslated decision. That exposed the internal source and delivered the packet twice when neighbor retry later replayed the translated frame.

## Change

- Preserve the composed NAT decision for non-buffered MissingNeighbor fallthroughs.
- Suppress the slow-path copy for parked frames and for duplicate/capacity/seed-refused MISS outcomes that are recycled rather than delivered.
- Add interface-SNAT, static-SNAT, and NPTv6 RED/GREEN cells, including real `retry_pending_neigh` cross-UMEM delivery assertions.
- Add a duplicate-hop fail-on-revert pin and preserve the production outlet source guard.

## Verification

- `afxdp::tests_slow_path_disposition`: 28 passed (`artifact://41537`).
- #10311 interface-SNAT/static-SNAT/NPTv6 cells: 3 passed (`artifact://41518`); each parks once, performs no slow-path copy, then queues exactly one translated replay after neighbor resolution.
- Duplicate-hop fail-on-revert cell: 1 passed (`artifact://41521`).
- Production source guard: 1 passed (`artifact://41527`).
- RED evidence: NAT cells (`artifact://41467`), duplicate-hop cell (`artifact://41474`).
- Parent-verified `BASELINE-RUST` failures are unchanged and not in scope: `poll_descriptor_stamps_neighbor_mac_epoch_from_outer_neighbor_shard_not_logical_6075`, `txn_flow_cache_hit_replays_input_filter_then_count_3777`, `txn_flow_cache_hit_reclassifies_ba_dscp_per_packet_3778`, `txn_flow_cache_hit_ttl_check_precedes_egress_accounting_3779`, `txn_flow_cache_hit_reclassifies_ba_pcp_per_packet_4422`, and `txn_flow_cache_hit_ttl_expired_does_not_charge_three_color_policer_4422` (`artifact://41535`).

author: eren0315
body:
## 번들 타깃

`"targets": "all"` 인데 **nsis 하나만** 나왔다. 에러도 경고도 없었고, MSI 가 13번의 릴리스 동안 안 나온 것을 아무도 몰랐다.

| | |
|:--|:--|
| 문서 | `"all"` = 지원하는 형식 전부 |
| 실측 | `"all"` → nsis 만 |
| 실측 | `--bundles msi` → 잘 나온다 (WiX 정상, candle·light 동작) |

⚠️ **왜 갈리는지는 모른다.** 문서가 답하지 않는다. 그래서 `"all"` 을 안 믿고 만들 것을 배열로 적는다 — `["nsis", "app", "dmg"]`. Windows 에서 macOS 타깃을 같이 적어도 안 깨지는 것을 실측으로 확인했다(해당 없는 것은 건너뛴다).

MSI 는 기본에서 뺐다. 13번 동안 아무도 안 찾았고, 필요하면 `npm run tauri build -- --bundles msi` 로 그때 만든다.

막는 장치 둘 — 목록의 주인은 `scripts/bundleTargets.mjs` 하나이고 둘 다 같은 것을 읽는다:

- `scripts/bundleTargets.test.ts` — `"all"` 로 되돌아가는 것 · 오타 · 한쪽 머신만 덮는 설정
- `npm run bundle:check` — 만들기로 한 것이 실제로 나왔는지 버전까지 대조

카나리아로 넷 다 우는 것을 봤다.

## PRACTICES.md

작업 규칙을 **커밋되는 파일**로 옮겼다. `CLAUDE.md` 는 gitignore 대상이라 다른 머신에서 못 읽는다.

⚠️ 옮기면서 규칙 자체가 틀린 것을 발견했다. 예전 규칙은 "손으로 쓴 기능 지도를 먼저 읽어라"였는데 재 보니:

| 근거 | 잘못 올렸던 후보 6 | 최근 기능 4 | 커밋됨 |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| CHANGELOG | 5 / 6 | 4 / 4 | ✅ |
| 손으로 쓴 지도 | — | 0 / 4 | ❌ |

지도는 버전 도장이 여섯 릴리스 뒤처져 있었다. 규칙을 CHANGELOG 검색으로 바꿨다.

⚠️ 이 조사 중에 `grep -E` 에 `\|` 를 써서 "CHANGELOG 에 그 기능이 없다"는 **틀린 결론**을 낼 뻔했다. ERE 에서 `\|` 는 리터럴 파이프라 늘 0 이 나온다. `PRACTICES.md` 에 적었다.

## 검증

| 게이트 | 결과 |
|:--|:--|
| `npm run check` | 0 errors / 0 warnings (5504 파일) |
| `npm test` | 2664 passed (198 파일) |
| `npm run check:mcp` · `check:cli` · `check:arch` | 통과 (402 파일 · 규칙 8개) |
