author: mihaibojin
body:
`release-guard` fails a pull request when a project changed without recording a release: its version has to move, and, where you ask for one, its changelog has to open a section naming that version.

A repository that is one versioned thing needs no inputs at all, because a pull request already says what it is against:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v6
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0

- uses: releasetools/actions/release-guard@v0
  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
```

A repository of many declares them in groups, each saying which files govern which directories:

```yaml
    projects: |
      - path: packages/*
        manifest: package.json
        changelog: CHANGELOG.md
      - path: crates/*
        manifest: Cargo.toml
```

## What it does

**Projects.** `path` takes one name or a list, as paths or globs: `./` is the repository, `./*` every directory at the top, `packages/*` every one under `packages`. A directory only counts as a project if it holds one of its group's manifests, so a name that does not is an error and a glob that turns one up walks past it. A directory two groups reach belongs to the first. A pattern matching nothing fails the run.

**Versions.** `manifest` takes a list, and every file a project holds has to declare the same version; one it does not hold is not its business. The kind is read from the name: any `.json` takes its top-level `version`, `.toml` the version of its `package`, `project`, `tool.poetry` or `workspace.package` table, `.yaml` a top-level `version:`, `.properties` a `version=` line, and anything else is a file holding the version and nothing else. XML is refused rather than guessed at, since a `<version>` in a `pom.xml` can be the project's or its parent's.

**Changelogs.** `changelog` names the file for that group; left out, it owes none. A section counts as `## 0.2.0`, `## 0.2.0 - 2026-09-19`, `## [0.2.0] - 2026-09-19` or `## v0.2.0`.

**What counts as a change.** The files a release writes, its group's changelog and manifests, never count as the change being recorded, or the check would ask for a release whose only content is the sentence announcing it. `ignore-files` adds to that and defaults to `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`; setting it replaces those rather than adding to them. Patterns match the end of a path, so one entry covers every depth, and `case-sensitive` decides whether case matters. A version that moves is a release however little came with it, so bump-and-forget is still caught; a manifest edit moving no version asks for nothing.

**The comparison** resolves through `git merge-base`, which is the diff GitHub shows under Files changed, so a base branch that moved on does not read as this branch's change. It counts untracked files alongside the diff, and leaves out whatever git is ignoring.

**Reporting.** One `info` line per project that recorded a release, and one annotation per failure, titled `Version not bumped`, `Changelog not updated` or `Release guard could not run`. Label a pull request `skip-release-guard` and it passes with a notice saying so.

## Paths that leave the repository

The working tree on a pull request is written by whoever opened it, and this action reads versions out of files and prints them. A manifest that was a symlink to a file on the runner was read and its contents printed as the project's version, which is a way to publish a token into a public job log. Every path now resolves through its links and is checked against the repository root before anything is opened; one that lands outside is refused with a message that does not name where it went.

`path`, `manifest` and `changelog` are refused at parse time if they are absolute or climb out with `..`. Two things already held and now have tests saying so: a glob never follows a symlinked directory, and `!!js/function` and its family are not in js-yaml 4's default schema.

## Where the rule comes from

`scripts/check-version-bump.mjs`, duplicated byte for byte across `MihaiBojin/agent-plugins` and `releasetools/agent-plugins`, CI-only in both, and already drifting. Differences from the script it replaces, beyond everything above: an unreadable manifest becomes one error line instead of throwing, so the other projects still get checked, and version segments are read with `parseInt`, so `0.2.0-rc1` no longer compares greater than everything through `NaN`.

## Tests

129 across the repository, 104 of them here: the rule with git injected, the config parser, project globs, ignore matching, the version readers for five kinds of manifest, and sixteen driving a real temporary repository, three of which build symlinks, two of those out of it.

Every configuration the guide shows was run through the built bundle rather than written from the source.

## Documentation

`release-guard/README.md` carries the rule, the inputs and five worked examples. The site gets a page at `/release-guard` in [releasetools/website#18](https://github.com/releasetools/website/pull/18).

## The other commits

`510e64a` upgrades ncc, whose bundled terser could not parse a computed class field in undici, so `--minify` had been failing silently on every build. `signed-push` drops from 1485kB to 710kB on unchanged code. `release-guard` is 684kB, 61kB of which is js-yaml.

author: odenrider
body:
## What changes

The `branch` job leaves `test.yml` for a workflow of its own, `branch.yml`. It runs on `opened`, `edited`, `reopened` and `synchronize` for pull requests into `main`, so a pull request whose body is edited after its head was pushed is checked against the edited body. Runs on one pull request share a concurrency group and the earlier run is cancelled, so the run that stands is the one with the later text. The checkout does not persist the token: the step runs scripts from the pull request's own tree, and they read only the local clone.

`test.yml` keeps the `test` and `secrets` jobs; the only edit to them is the comment on the checkout step, which now points at `branch.yml`. No script changes. Removing the old job also stops a skipped `branch` check being published on every push to `main`.

## Why

Two of the three branch checks read the body, and the body arrives in the event payload. A payload is the pull request as it stood when the event fired: a run started by a push carries the body at the push, and a re-run of that run replays the same payload. A body edited after the push therefore reached no run, and the check reported on text the pull request no longer carried. The Register check already lists `edited` for the same reason.

`edited` is not added to `test.yml` itself. A body edit changes nothing the test, mutation and secret jobs measure, and a job that an `if` skips on the edit event still publishes a check under its name with conclusion `skipped`, which a required status check treats as success, so a failed test run on a head could be followed by one that satisfied the requirement having run nothing.

## Verification

- Both workflow files parse. `test.yml` carries `test` and `secrets`; `branch.yml` carries `branch`.
- `scripts/check-branch-selftest.py` 8 cases, `scripts/check-delta-selftest.py` 17 cases, `scripts/check-branch.py` OK on this branch at its head.
- On this pull request: the Branch workflow ran on open at `2638ba0`, run 35392205487, and passed. The first body edit started run 35392287102 three seconds later on the same head, and it passed; the `PR_BODY` block in the two job logs differs by the edited line, so the second run read the edited text. This edit is the third case.

`branch` is not a required status check on `main` today; only `register` is. Making it required is a repository setting outside this change.

author: tontinton
body:
The prompt was a single slot, so when seven subagents ran at once the second ask overwrote the first on screen, and since the agent only accepts an answer naming the request it parked on, that first tool call waited forever.

Asks now sit in a `VecDeque` behind the one being shown, and `handle_key` pops the front itself and hands back the id and subagent it belongs to, so nobody can answer without settling the queue.

Asks may only exist while something can answer them, which is why `close` still drops them all on cancel or session switch and `drop_subagent` now runs next to `subagent_answers.remove` when one subagent is cancelled on its own.

Closes #1044.

author: ljosberinn
body:
The sweep collected every deferral — a release the player held a file open on, and every release a 503 declined — into one list and retried it once, after the last batch. That was written when a sweep was seconds long. Since 82l the sweep survives its failures and since 82o (#185) it no longer parks on declines, so it runs the library to exhaustion: about ninety hours, which is how long an album left playing now waits to be filed, and long enough for the list to reach every declined release in the library before anything retries one. The reproduction in the issue took a restart to free one album after thirty-five minutes.

Both deferrals are drained at the end of the batch that made them instead. They are kept apart because different things bound them: the player holds at most the playing track and the prepared next, so a release still open simply goes back on its list, while a service that goes on declining offers a quarter of every batch and has to be shed. One rule covers both — whatever is still playing goes back on, everything else is done with for this sweep. A release that declines a second time keeps no row, so the next sweep has it back, and `next_sweep` returns `TICK` while the last one got through anything at all. The tail after the loop goes with this, since the last batch is drained before the survey comes back empty.

`summary.deferred` counted the batch visit and the tail visit separately, so one release read as two. It counts a state rather than a cost and now counts each release once, and a repeat deferral writes no `library.place` line either — an album left on all evening would otherwise write one per batch. `summary.failed` is the opposite case, since a second visit is three more requests, so it stays per exhausted lookup and now says so.

Whether a release was retried at the end of its batch or at the end of the sweep is not visible in any counter, so the new tests assert it by the order of the log lines.

### Before merge

- [ ] An album played through a real pass: one `library.place status=playing` line for it however long it plays, and `deferred=1` on the `pass.sweep` line.
- [ ] That album filed within a batch of the track ending, rather than when the sweep does.
- [ ] A pass over a declining MusicBrainz reaching the end of the library, with no sweep-long list behind it.

author: allocsys
body:
## Summary
Splits the SSR dashboard/login/session logic out of `backend` into a new dedicated Worker (`src/dashboard-worker.js` + `wrangler.dashboard.toml`), which talks to `backend` via a service binding. `backend` is now private (`workers_dev = false`) and unauthenticated at the HTTP layer — trusted only through the service binding — so an unconfigured login now fails closed everywhere instead of serving an open dashboard.

## Changes
- New `src/dashboard-worker.js` + `wrangler.dashboard.toml`: owns login, session cookie, and UI (server-rendered, reuses existing `views/*`)
- `backend`'s `src/index.js` / `src/dashboard/routes.js` trimmed: no more HTML/login; `wrangler.toml` set `workers_dev = false`
- `login.js`: fixed stale disabled-notice copy to match fail-closed behavior
- `package.json`: dev/deploy scripts for the new dashboard Worker
- `deploy.yml`: new path-filtered `deploy-dashboard` job (own concurrency group, owns only `DASHBOARD_USERNAME`/`DASHBOARD_PASSWORD`/`JWT_SECRET`/`SESSION_TTL_SECONDS`, depends on backend's deploy job); removed now-obsolete "set dashboard login secrets" step from backend's job

author: gerrrt
body:
`Refs #418`, `Refs #148`, `Refs #76` — no close keywords. The drives are fitted and nothing after the bays has happened; the measurement is what closes #418.

## What happened

Both SM863a drives went into `Saruman`'s bays 3 and 4 on 2026-09-18. The iLO reported them in the 20:11 UTC scrape, absent at 20:10 — both in the same minute:

| Reading | Bay 3 (idx 2) | Bay 4 (idx 3) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpqDaPhyDrvSerialNum` | `S3F3NX0K601487` | `S3F3NX0K806107` |
| `cpqDaPhyDrvModel` / `FWRev` | `SAMSUNG` / `GXM5304Q` | same |
| `cpqDaPhyDrvSize` | `915715` MB | same |
| `MediaType` / `RotationalSpeed` / `Type` / `NegotiatedLinkRate` | `3` solidState / `5` rpmSsd / `3` sata / `4` | same |
| `Condition` / `Status` / `SmartStatus` | `2` / `2` / `2` ok | same |
| `ConfigurationStatus` | `3` notConfigured | same |
| `SmartCarrierAppFWRev` / `BootldrFWRev` | `11` / `6` — the same as bays 1–2 | same |

`cpqDaLogDrv*` still reads index `1` only; `cpqDaAccel*` and `cpqDaCntlr*` are unchanged from the 2026-09-17 baseline; `scrape_duration_seconds{device="shiva"}` is `11.4` s either side of the fit. No alert on `device="shiva"` fired for it, and no silence existed — step 1's silences are for step 5's sync, and inserting a drive into an empty bay moves no condition column.

**This is step 4 of the runbook and no other step.** No `ssacli`, no logical drive, no thin pool, `alexander` still on the HDD mirror, no fio, no cache reading for #76.

## What this PR does

- **`fit-the-saruman-ssds.md`** — status block rewritten for 2026-09-18; step 4's tray precondition becomes past tense with the carrier firmware as the proof; step 11's *Observed* column is filled for the physical-drive rows; items 2, 3 and 5 of "what this runbook does not know" are struck through with the reading that settled them; step 1 says to create its silences immediately before step 5, not before step 4.
- **`hardware.md`** — the Compute table's Storage column moves, as the accessories entry said it would on the day #418 fitted them: `2× 1 TB SAS HDD, RAID 1; 2× 960 GB SATA SSD, unassigned`. The SM863a entry carries both serials, the firmware and the link rate in the S3520 entry's shape, and says whose reading they are. The tray entry is fitted. The duplicated "reading them back afterwards" sentence in the SSD entry is gone.
- **`roadmap.md`** — the trays leave *still moving*, the SSDs leave *on hand*, and a dated note records the fit; the #418 entry says fitted-and-stopped-at-the-bays; the #414 paragraph no longer says the drives are on a shelf.

## Three things the runbook predicted wrongly

- **The model string.** Step 11 expected `MZ7KM960...`; the iLO reports `SAMSUNG`. It names a third-party SATA drive by vendor where it gives the HPE disks their part number. The part is proved by size, firmware and serial prefix instead, and the row now says so.
- **The walk cost.** Step 10's table predicted 13–17 s; two more drives cost the walk nothing measurable.
- **Labels first.** Step 4 said to read the serials off the labels before insertion, because reading them back afterwards is reading them through the tool the fit is meant to verify. That was not done. The runbook now records that while both drives are `Unassigned` a label check is still safe — a drive that is a member of nothing can be pulled and reseated — and that the window closes at step 5.

## Two readings worth having

- **Wear is blank on the SSDs**: `cpqDaPhyDrvSSDWearStatus` `1` other, `SSDPercntEndrnceUsed` / `PowerOnHours` / `SSDEstTimeRemainingHours` all `4294967295`, as on the HDDs. `cpqDaPhyDrvHasMonInfo` also reads false on all four, and the MIB allows an unconfigured drive to go unpolled, so step 11 re-reads these after step 5. If they are still blank once the drives are in a logical drive, the closing paragraph's `smartctl -d cciss` issue gets opened — not before.
- **`cpqDaPhyDrvMaximumTemperature` is a lifetime figure**: `62` °C on Bay 3 against a `60` threshold, `51` on Bay 4, both at 30–32 °C now. Second-hand drives carrying their previous life's number — the kind of reading direct SMART would have shown at purchase.

## What is deliberately not here

**No ADR changes.** ADR-0029's ninety is stale the day step 8's measurement lands, not the day the drives did. **No `network.rules.yaml` silence paragraph and no test-fixture changes** — no silence exists yet. **No wear issue** — gated on the re-read after step 5. **No thin-pool blind-spot issue** — the pool does not exist.

Also seen and not chased: the iLO's SNMP was unreachable 14:54–15:03 UTC the same day (`InstanceDown` fired on `10.0.30.10`); `Saruman` and `alexander` stayed up throughout.

## Blast radius

Documentation only.

- [x] No change to network segmentation or firewall rules
- [x] No new port published to a VLAN that could not already reach the service
- [x] No credential added outside `secrets/*.sops.yaml`

`python3 scripts/check_docs.py` → `docs OK — 83 Prometheus + 18 Loki rules, 7 dashboards, 141 panels, 10 assertions`
`./scripts/lint.sh --require-all` → `lint passed`
Serials and bays in the diff re-read from Prometheus at commit time and match.

- [x] `make validate` passes (check-docs and lint stages; rules unchanged)

## What is next, and who runs it

From the Mac, on `Saruman`: step 2 (`ssacli`, record which path worked), step 3 (capture the Cache Ratio and Interface Type lines verbatim — the #76 and item-12 readings), the optional label check while both drives are unassigned, then step 1's silences from `prometheus` **immediately before** step 5, steps 5–9 on the Mac, steps 10–11 from `prometheus`. author: sarollahi
body: Console CI has been red on `develop` for the last five pushes. One assertion fails in `verify`, and because `npm run build` sits behind it in the same job, the build never runs either. The `ui` (Playwright) job passes on every one of those runs, so this is a test bug, not a product defect. ### Why it cannot pass `UsersPanel.tsx:144` emphasises the role: ```jsx Platform Owner{' access to this tenant without membership'} ``` `getByText` matches against `getNodeText(node)`, which concatenates an element's **direct text-node children only**. For that `` that is `' access to this tenant without membership'` — `Platform Owner` sits inside a child `` and is excluded. No element's own text ever equals the full sentence, so `/Platform Owner access to this tenant without membership/` can never match. That is exactly what the error message was pointing at: > This could be because the text is broken up by multiple elements. `c6a2cb4` ("Keep owner access notice accessible as one phrase") aimed at this, but wrapping the role in `` still splits the DOM text. ### Fix Assert on `textContent`, the approach Testing Library's own hint recommends for split text. The bold emphasis stays, and the markup was already announced as one phrase by screen readers — `` does not introduce a boundary in the accessibility tree — so nothing about the rendered UI or its accessibility changes. 12/12 tests pass locally.

author: carteratate
body:
Closes #105.

## The symptom

A focused search (quota 10, Bible only) for *"Best psalms for when I don't feel close to God, feel lack of faith…"* returned **4** passages — Ps 42, 13, 22, 88 — all scoring 96–99%, with `delivery_outcome: underfilled` and the notice *"Only 4 Passages met this search's relevance and diversity rules."*

That notice was false. The passages existed and were ranked at the top. They were cut by a diversity cap that treated the entire Psalter as one source.

## The cause — and why the issue's proposed fix was not enough

#105 proposed adding `"bible"` to `_CHAPTER_KEYED_COLLECTIONS`. Necessary, but on its own it would not have fixed anything.

`apply_dedup` gated on `per_document_cap` **before** `source_key` was computed, and that gate keyed on a bare `document_id`:

```python
document_count = document_counts.get(chunk.document_id, 0)
if per_document_cap is not None and document_count >= per_document_cap:
    continue
key = source_key(chunk, chapter_grain)   # ← too late
```

Focused search passes `max_passages_per_document` as **both** caps (`runner.py:379-385`), and `ingest/bible.py` builds one Document per book, so the whole Psalter is one `document_id`. The chapter grain was computed and then had no effect.

**This was never Bible-specific.** The Summa, Catechism and Canon Law are each stored as a single document too, so a focused search against any of them was capped at 4 however many distinct articles or canons ranked. The Bible is simply where it got noticed.

Restoring the old `document_key` at runtime shows the inversion plainly:

```
5 distinct Summa articles -> STANDARD=5  FOCUSED=4   (focused < standard: True)
```

Focused mode, whose whole purpose is to return more, returned fewer.

## The fix

1. `"bible"` joins `_CHAPTER_KEYED_COLLECTIONS`. A Bible chapter is a cleaner grain than the existing members — a psalm is a topical unit, not the Catechism's mechanical 100-paragraph bucket — and ingest already writes `chapter_key` on every verse chunk.
2. A new `document_key()` gives `per_document_cap` the same grain as `source_key`, in **both** `dedup` and `steps/min_floor`.

## Behaviour, measured

Both versions run over identical candidate pools, through `quota_cap`:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Focused (q10) Bible — 12 distinct psalms | 4 | **10** |
| Focused (q10) Summa — 12 distinct articles | 4 | **10** |
| Focused floor — 6 distinct psalms | 4 | **5** |
| Standard (q4) Bible — 12 distinct psalms | 2 | **4** |
| Focused — 12 verses of *one* psalm | 4 | 4 |
| Focused — `chapter_key` missing (degraded) | 4 | 4 |
| church-fathers *(control)* | 4 | 4 |

Diversity is intact: one psalm still cannot flood a result set. The degraded path is byte-identical — the fix fails closed.

## Verification

- **648 tests passing.**
- Both halves red-checked independently: reverting `document_key` fails the focused tests; removing `"bible"` fails the Bible tests.
- The invariant most at risk — degraded never looser than healthy — brute-forced over 6,000 pools across four cap combinations in both `dedup` and `min_floor`: **zero violations**.
- Cost bound verified rather than assumed: `quota_cap` keeps at most `quota` per collection and focused search is single-collection, so the worst case is +6 explanation streams and `retrievals` rows on a focused search, +3 on a standard one.

## Reviewed twice

The first review found that `min_floor` had the identical defect — its `document_has_room()` still keyed on a bare `document_id`, returning 4 where the floor's own limit (`min(quota, _FLOOR_N)`) called for 5. Fixed in commit 2.

The second review, run with full tooling and mutation testing, found no behavioural defects and several places where my own documentation overclaimed. All corrected in commit 4:

- **`per_document_cap` is now inert at production values.** `document_key` strictly refines `source_key`, so it cannot bind unless strictly smaller than `per_source_cap` — and `runner.py` passes them equal. Verified over 4,000 random pools: zero outputs differ with the cap removed. Kept rather than deleted (that touches `runner.py`, two module signatures and CLAUDE.md §18, which is an architecture decision, not part of a bug fix) and tracked as **#107**.
- **The tests I rewrote encoded a written requirement, not an accident.** Issue #28 required *"a hard cap of four Passages per underlying document only in focused mode."* That spec was self-contradictory — the same issue also required *"Return exactly ten when ten Passages survive"*, which a hard per-document cap makes unreachable for single-document collections. #105 is that contradiction reported from production. The history now says so rather than implying the original author was careless.
- Four tests were named for a cap they do not exercise. Renamed.
- CLAUDE.md §18, the COST comment and the `analyze_eval.py` methodology note all corrected.

## Not verified

**The original query has not been run end-to-end.** Every number above comes from driving `apply_dedup` and `min_floor` directly with synthetic candidates, which isolates the change but assumes the ranked pool really contains those distinct psalms. After merging, run the #105 query and check both the result count and that `dedup: chapter grain unavailable` does *not* appear in the logs. If the count is still short with the grain applied, the constraint is upstream in the reranker and that is a separate issue.

**Guest spend rises.** Guests reach focused mode through the same `resolve_search_plan`, so a trial search now streams up to 10 explanations instead of 4. Bounded, and the behaviour the feature always promised, but worth a conscious decision.

author: eszter007
body:
## Summary

* **What is the goal of this PR?** Let a card keep the firmware's folders hidden — `/.system`, `/.dictionaries` — without losing functionality, while cards using the visible names keep working untouched.
* **What changes are included?** Root resolution for the two folder families that lacked it.

Two already worked and are unchanged:

| folder | before this PR |
|---|---|
| Fonts | `/.fonts` **and** `/fonts` ✅ |
| English / StarDict dictionaries | `/.dictionaries` **and** `/dictionaries` ✅ |
| **Japanese dictionaries** | `/dictionaries/jp` only ❌ |
| **System state** | `/system` only ❌ |

**Japanese dictionaries.** `/dictionaries/jp` was ten hardcoded constants in `DictIndex`, so a card that hid its dictionaries **lost Japanese word lookup entirely while English kept working** — the asymmetry that prompted this. The root is now resolved once and the constants are rewritten under it. They stay full paths because `dev/dict_host_test/spx_verify.cpp` reads them directly. `releaseCaches()` clears the resolution along with the filename caches, so a dictionary uploaded mid-session (web file transfer) into the other root is picked up the next session rather than never — the reason that cache-clearing hook exists.

**System state.** `/system` held reading statistics, book stats, the clock stash, the translate hand-off and the Gemini API key across six constants. `sdsystem::dir()` resolves it the same way. It lives in **`lib/hal/`** because `HalClock` is one of the callers and cannot reach into `src/`.

**Existing cards are untouched.** Whichever spelling a card already has wins, so nothing is migrated or duplicated. `/.system` is created only when neither exists — previously `/system` was created unconditionally, so a hidden-layout card ended up with both.

## Scope Check

- [x] I have read SCOPE.md and ROADMAP.md.
- [x] This PR is **not** a new built-in theme.
- [x] This PR is **not** a new external network connector.
- [x] This PR is **not** an interactive app, writing tool, RSS/news/browser, media playback, or PDF feature.
- [x] The stock firmware does not handle this — hiding the dictionaries silently breaks Japanese lookup.
- [x] Touches `lib/hal/` by adding one file there, for the reason above; no change to existing HAL behaviour, and nothing in `freeink-sdk/`, the bootloader, OTA or recovery.

## Additional Context

**Memory / flash:** the resolution is one `exists()` probe per folder family, cached. Paths that were compile-time constants now build a short `std::string` per file operation; none of these are in a render or scan loop (statistics, clock stash, key file, dictionary open).

**Behaviour change worth noting:** `/system` used to be created unconditionally at clock-stash time. It is now created only if neither spelling exists, and as `/.system`.

**Areas to focus on:** that `jpRoot()` is not resolved before the card is mounted — it is called from lookup paths, well after mount — and the interning in `resolveIdxPath()`, which keeps the returned `const char*` valid for the caller's lifetime.

---

Did you use AI tools to help write this code? _**YES**_

body:
Stacked on #63 — **merge #63 first, then this one into `main`.** (Last time a stacked PR was merged into its own base after that base had already been squashed, and the content was silently stranded.)

## The fault

Slot 16 cold-booted, sampled **1702** while the sensor output was still rising to its ~1850 idle, and primed there. That 148-count gap latched `active_`, and the freeze then protected the very baseline that would have cleared it:

```
mask=00  raw=1899  base=1703 (frozen, unchanged across every sample)  delta=159  active=1
```

The hardware was already fixed at that point — `mask=00`, clean — and the cube still could not recover.

Worse, the bad value had **already reached NVS**. `shouldSavePresenceBaseline()` gates on `id_mask != 0 || active`, and in the instant it primed neither was set, so the gate was wide open. A power cycle restored 1702 and it relatched. Nothing short of new firmware could shift it.

## Two halves

**Prevention** — the reference now comes from the settled reading, not the first sample. A cold boot reaches the first `update()` before the sensor output has arrived; one sample is not something to commit to for the life of a board.

**Recovery** — `cube/device/<mac>/recalibrate` clears the RTC copy and the NVS copy and re-primes. Device-scoped like `auto_sleep`, since a board has a MAC before it has a slot and this is a bench action on hardware.

## Deliberately not done

Making the ID sensors authoritative over a latched activation would also have fixed slot 16, and I had it written. It breaks `test_presence_freezes_the_baseline_while_a_neighbour_is_present`, and that test is right: a neighbour whose ID magnets are not fitted would latch, adapt away, and drop presence after ~10s — **which is exactly the state slots 15 and 16 are in today.** The freeze semantics from #59 are unchanged here.

## Verified

```
MAC table OK: 21 rows, all MACs and octets unique and canonical, no compiled slots.
87 test cases: 87 succeeded
v1  v6  v6_with_hall  v6_with_hall_analog   all SUCCESS
```

Two new tests, and the important one is **proven to fail**: forcing the old prime-from-first-sample path reddens `test_priming_ignores_an_unsettled_first_sample` (`Expected TRUE Was FALSE` — it primes at 1702 instead of ~1850), and it passes again when restored.

Three existing tests changed, all of which asserted priming from the first sample — the behaviour this PR deliberately replaces. One is renamed from `..._adopts_the_first_reading` to `..._adopts_the_settled_reading`.

author: henrypinkard
body:
The focused-session section of the feed sits on a very faint tint of the accent: the whole region the chat's active session's cards live in, the head row and its columns together, reads as one region set apart from the rest of the feed. The user's ask of 2026-09-18 (paraphrased), through the manager; romp_feed owns the feed and is mid phase three, so the claim (feed.css, the `#feed-focus` rules and a token beside the wash) was mailed first and nothing else in the feed moves. Cut from main at 240782f0. Fix tier, unarmed.

**The change.** A new token beside `--accent-wash` in both of feed.css's theme blocks: `--accent-tint`, `rgba(156, 210, 255, 0.04)` in the dark block (a third of the wash's 0.12) and `rgba(194, 65, 12, 0.04)` in the light block (the light theme's accent is an orange, re-inked like the wash). `#feed-focus` takes `background: var(--accent-tint)`, an 8px radius and `padding: 6px 8px 2px`, so the tint has a margin around the cards; the divider, the head and the fold caret are unchanged. No literal colour anywhere; the theme-parity test's key parity holds (the light block re-declares the token). Tuned by eye in Chromium on the built page in both themes: the region reads as set apart, the cards keep their own grounds and hover wash, the light theme reads as a faint warm wash; the shots are in the drops folder as `romp_metrics-focus-tint-on-dark.png` and `-on-light.png` (the `-off-` pair shows the plain board). No clock input to any verdict.

**Tests.** The served focus lab, `tests/test_feed_focus_served.py`, which already renders the section over a hermetic kernel in both themes, reads the section's computed background against a plain board column's and a card's inside it: the section's ground is the theme's tint, the plain column carries none, the card keeps its own, the radius and left padding are 8px, in both themes. Red first at 240782f0 under `ROMP_SERVED_TESTS_REQUIRE=1` (a detached base, the module copied then restored): `AssertionError: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)' != 'rgba(156, 210, 255, 0.04)' : dark: the section's ground is the accent tint (the base had none)`, `1 failed`; `1 passed` at the head. `ui/webview/feed-focus-section.test.ts` pins the rule with the token, the token in both blocks, and no literal in the rule. The feed pins that read the sheet (the focus section, theme parity, the CSS vocabulary and census) `41 tests, 41 pass`. User-facing CSS, so the WHOLE extension suite ran before the push: (`node esbuild.js --tests`, then `node --test` over `out-tests/**`) `5039 tests, 5034 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped`, exit 0. Both test trees grepped for the changed rule's literal: only the re-pointed pin named it. The added lines carry the ruled-out word zero times and no em-dashes; no session names.

Review closed: no verifier or panel run by me.

Tier: fix

author: aaronontheweb
body:
## Summary

Adds dedicated, supported-platform (Linux + Windows) uninstallers and GitHub Actions smoke tests that validate them. macOS is out of scope for now.

## What's included

- **`scripts/uninstall.sh`** (Linux) — reverses `install.sh`: stops the process, removes pipx/`pip --user` install + `~/.local/bin/witticism` stub, desktop entry, autostart file, hicolor + pixmap icons, optional GNOME Shell extension, and NVIDIA sleep hook (sudo). `--purge` also deletes `~/.config/witticism` and `~/.local/share/witticism`.
- **`scripts/uninstall.ps1`** (Windows) — mirrors `install.ps1`'s `Get-Python312Path` so it targets the same interpreter that installed; removes pipx/`pip --user`, desktop shortcut, Startup auto-start files. `-Purge` also deletes `%APPDATA%\witticism` + `%LOCALAPPDATA%\witticism`.
- **`.github/workflows/uninstall-test.yml`** — 4 jobs (Linux, Linux `--purge`, Windows, Windows `pip --user` fallback) that install, simulate the headless-CI desktop footprint, run the uninstaller, and assert nothing is left behind (fails non-zero on leftovers). Pre-asserts the install fixture so absence checks can't pass vacuously.
- **README** — new "Uninstalling" section.

## Review

Two sub-agent adversarial reviews were applied (footprint completeness, headless-CI test validity, PowerShell 5.1 compat, README accuracy).

## Test plan

The Linux uninstaller was sandbox-run with an isolated `$HOME` to confirm it removes the full footprint while keeping config (and deleting it under `--purge`). The CI matrix runs the real install→uninstall flows on `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest`.

author: yshishenya
body:
## Кратко

Релизная проверка запуска собранного `GRAF.app` теперь требует появления главного окна. Раньше она довольствовалась маркером запуска, а его пишет начало обработчика — то есть приложение, которое запустилось и осталось жить, но окна не показало, гейт проходило.

## Feature identity

- Feature ID: `F232`
- Umbrella issue: `#7209`
- Spec task IDs: `T023`
- Branch/spec directory match: ветка `codex/232-launch-window-gate`, каталог `specs/232-macos-resource-bundle-hotfix/`

## Проблема

`app_launch_finished` пишется в самом начале `applicationDidFinishLaunching` — до `NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps:)` и до `presentMainWindow(reason: "launch")`. Сама по себе эта запись доказывает только вход в обработчик. Отказ 8 июня 2026 года выглядел ровно так: процесс живёт, окна нет. Гейт `validate-packaged-app-launch.sh` такое приложение пропускал.

## Что изменилось

| Файл | Изменение |
|---|---|
| `apps/macos/Scripts/validate-packaged-app-launch.sh` | добавлена проверка `event=app_main_window_presented`; сообщение прежней проверки уточнено до «launch marker» |
| `apps/macos/Installer/Scripts/test-packaged-app-launch.sh` | фикстура `living` пишет оба события; добавлена фикстура `no-window` — живой процесс без окна |
| `apps/macos/Installer/Scripts/test-release-signing-custody.sh` | страховка: валидатор обязан требовать событие появления окна |
| `specs/232-macos-resource-bundle-hotfix/contracts/packaged-startup.md` | описан признак готовности и границы проверки |
| `specs/232-macos-resource-bundle-hotfix/tasks.md` | задача `T023` |
| `changes/unreleased/F232.yaml` | фрагмент журнала |

Прежняя проверка маркера запуска сохранена намеренно: она отличает состоявшийся запуск от полного отсутствия журнала, и на неё опирается тест подписной цепочки.

## Как проверено

Доказательство того, что новая фикстура ловит именно старую дыру: если убрать проверку окна, тест падает с сообщением `packaged app launch test failed: candidate that never presented its main window was accepted`. С правкой тест проходит. Это подтверждает, что прежний гейт такое приложение действительно пропускал.

- `sh apps/macos/Installer/Scripts/test-packaged-app-launch.sh` — passed
- `sh apps/macos/Installer/Scripts/test-release-signing-custody.sh` — passed
- `python3 scripts/validate-changelog-fragments.py` — ok: `changelog-fragments: OK`
- `python3 scripts/check_spec_kit_governance.py` — ok: `spec-kit-governance: OK`

Дополнительно проверено на настоящей сборке. Запуск установленного Dev-приложения записал ровно те события, которых требует новая проверка:

```text
01:30:17 event=app_launch_finished detail=activationPolicy=regular
01:30:17 event=app_main_window_presented detail=reason=launch reused=false
01:30:18 event=app_window_visibility_checked detail=visibleWindowCount=2 mainWindowVisible=true key=true
```

Формат строки журнала сверен с исходником: `AppLog.writeRaw` (`apps/macos/RecApp/App/TwoBrainRecApp.swift`, строка 3687) пишет `event=<имя>`, поэтому поиск по `event=app_main_window_presented` корректен.

Гейт вызывается только из `apps/macos/Installer/Scripts/sign-graf-app-update-local.sh` и в CI не запускается, поэтому проверка не зависит от графической сессии на сборочном сервере. Аргументы командной строки не менялись — тест подписной цепочки, сверяющий строку вызова, остаётся валидным.

- GitHub `governance-fast`, `macos-pr`, `pr-metadata` на exact SHA и checked base: `governance-fast` — passed, `macos-pr` — passed, `pr-metadata` — после правки описания

body:
**Author:** policyforge-b5. **First review:** policyforge-1d (APPROVED fd4059b8f893922e85998fbe2bc11c3100541b6b). **Opened by:** policyforge-9b as release manager. I haven't changed this branch. Five commits. Last merge before the 1.3.0 release PR — our user asked for 1.3.0 with this feature in it.

Say why an empty crosswalk section is empty

Found by 9b reading the command's core, which is the part neither approver
had read closely and which they said so about rather than letting it be
assumed.

`satisfies` walks the crosswalk from the NIST requirements a document cites,
because the crosswalk is NIST-anchored. Nothing a user saw said so — not the
help, not the docstring. So a HIPAA-only document got an empty "Reached
through the crosswalk" section, and on this command an empty section reads as
*nothing satisfies this*: the exact misreading the report exists to prevent,
and a silent absence of the kind it was written to surface.

The report now says it where the section would have been, naming the cause
and that it is a property of the crosswalk rather than a finding about the
document. Stating the absence beats documenting the silence, which is why

**What it adds:** `policyforge satisfies` — what a published document can be shown against, from the citations in its text rather than from a topic's intentions. Requirement identifiers only, never a licensed catalog's prose. Published, reviewed and NOT REVIEWED crosswalk pairs stay visibly distinct, and superset/intersects render as "in part" rather than "satisfied".

**A finding I raised and b5 closed (c5):** crosswalk traversal starts only from NIST citations, and nothing a user saw said so — a HIPAA-only document got an empty section, which on this command reads as *nothing satisfies this*. b5 took the stronger option over the documented floor: the report now states the absence where the empty section would have been, ending "That is a property of the crosswalk, not a finding about the document." The traversal reads the same `nist_anchors` property the report explains, so the two cannot drift.

**Evidence:** 1d verified the four replayed commits two ways — cumulative byte-identical (5 files, 1727 lines) and per-commit patch-ids all identical — and gated c5 at 34 tests. I read the first commit's core (594 lines) independently: no licensed text reaches the renderer, provenance stays distinct, `[HIPAA AC-2]` is checked against the framework it names, and the notice is gated so it cannot fire on a document that cites nothing.

Fixes #437

## Summary

Implement incremental SG rental-flat ingestion using the `IncrementalConnector` protocol (watermark model from #454), mirroring the existing SG bankruptcy incremental connector (`bankruptcy_incremental.py`, #436). The connector uses cursor-based pagination and `updated_since` filtering against the scraper export endpoint, advancing the watermark only on full cursor drain.

## Changes

- **Wire models** (`services/ingestion/src/connectors/sggov/rental_flats_api_models.py`):
  - Add optional `updated_at: datetime | None = None` to `RentalFlatRow` (backward-compatible, falls back to `last_seen_at` when absent).
  - Add `RentalFlatCursorPage` wire model with `items: list[RentalFlatRow]` and `next_cursor: str | None`.
  - Existing offset-based `RentalFlatPage` left intact for backward compatibility with the legacy API connector.
- **Incremental connector** (`services/ingestion/src/connectors/sggov/rental_flats_incremental.py`):
  - New `SGGovernmentRentalFlatsIncrementalConnector` satisfying the `IncrementalConnector` protocol (`open_query`, `fetch_next_page`, `get_source_key`, `close`).
  - Calls `/integrations/hyperp/rental-flats` with `limit`, `cursor`, and `updated_since` parameters.
  - Reuses `build_rental_flat_envelope` and sanitization helpers from existing modules.
  - Normalizes timestamps to UTC and tracks max updated timestamp across items.
  - Detects cursor stalls (loops/duplicate cursors) and retries on transient errors (429, 5xx, transport) with exponential backoff.
- **Task registry** (`services/ingestion/src/tasks.py`):
  - Add factory `_create_sgrentalflats_incremental()` using existing `sgrentalflats_api_*` settings.
  - Register in `INCREMENTAL_CONNECTORS["sgrentalflats"]`.
- **Unit tests** (`services/ingestion/tests/test_sggov_rental_flats_incremental.py`):
  - 14 comprehensive unit and integration tests covering protocol compliance, bootstrap vs. delta pagination, `updated_at` fallback, empty page behavior, cursor stall detection, retry logic, auth error propagation, registry presence, UTC normalization, and watermark advancement on drain vs. preservation on safe yield.
- **Plan documentation** (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-incremental-sg-rental-flats.md`):

author: rhc52980
body:
Ten more touches for the Steampunk theme, most of them tied to what BAMF is doing.

## Tied to your network

- **Pressure gauge:** a brass dial sits in the header next to the next-scan tube. The needle shows devices online now against the most seen online this session, so it works whether your network is normally mostly up or mostly asleep. Below 70% it drops into the red zone and trembles. Hovering it gives the numbers, e.g. "Pressure: 6 devices online, of 16 at most this session".
- **Pneumatic tubes on the Map:** every 7 seconds a brass capsule shoots along one of your recorded cables, now copper pipes, with a puff of air where it lands.
- **Punch card for Identify:** while Identify runs, its entry in the results panel shows a punch card feeding through with holes being punched. The result replaces it when it comes back.
- **Orrery for port scans:** while a port scan runs, its entry spins a little orrery with a sun and two planets on their orbits.
- **Wind-up keys:** watched devices carry a small key beside their name that turns while they're online. When one goes offline, the key winds down and stops.
- **Brass clock:** the Last scan card gets a clock face keeping real time, with a ticking second hand. It chimes (♪) when a scan lands.

## Around the page

- **Brass lens:** pointing at a device's IP or MAC puts a brass-rimmed lens over it.
- **Telescope search:** the search box gets a telescope eyepiece, and the device rows glint as you type.
- **Oil lamps:** the corners flicker softly with warm lamp light. It's irregular and gentle, not a strobe.
- **Map unrolls** like a scroll of drafting paper when you open it.

As before, nothing runs in a background tab. With reduced motion switched on:
- the gauge and clock still show their readings, but nothing trembles, ticks, chimes or moves;
- there are no capsules, glints, lamp flicker or unrolling;
- the punch card and orrery hold still.

## Small changes outside the theme

- **Scan-panel entries** now carry `data-kind` (`identify` or `ports`), so a theme can style what's running.
- **The MAC cell** wraps its text in a `span.mac-text`, so the lens can grow just the text.

Neither changes anything visible in the other themes.

## Testing

On the demo DB, in Playwright's Chromium:
- **Gauge:** reads full on a healthy network. After simulating an outage it fell into the red and trembled, and the tooltip read 6 of 16.
- **Clock:** keeps real time and chimes on scan done.
- **Keys:** appeared on all 4 watched devices.
- **Punch card and orrery:** both show on busy Identify and port-scan entries.
- **Lens:** shows on hovering an IP.
- **Search glint:** fires on typing.
- **Map:** it unrolls on opening, and capsules fire along the pipes.
- **Switching to Dark** removes the gauge, the clock and the lamps, and stops every timer.
- There were no page errors, and the page script passes a syntax check.

author: lenaxia
body:
Fixes #1457, Fixes #1458

## What

Two legs of the routine-fire path lacked #1441/#1451's bounded transient-retry coverage:

- **#1458 (wiring tests)** — the WIP commit (24fca1c2) routed the `ScriptPath` pre-script leg through `executeWithRetry`; this PR pins it. A transient agentd transport 5xx on the pre-script leg is retried once and the fire **delivers** with **no consecutiveFailures burn**; a deterministic 4xx fails after exactly one attempt and burns exactly ONE failure.
- **#1457 (both ends)** — agentd's `createOpencodeSession` collapsed every failure mode (transport error, non-200, unparseable body) into `""`, reported by `execAgentNode` as HTTP-200 `errorCode: session_not_found` — a code `retryableAgentdFailure` never matches. A transient opencode 5xx during session create failed the fire and burned auto-disable budget one leg earlier than the class #1451 masked.
  - **agentd end**: `createOpencodeSession` returns `(sessionID, failCode, failDetail)`; every create failure surfaces `session_create_failed` with distinguishing detail following the file's existing conventions (`opencode returned NNN` — same as the message leg; `opencode session create: <err>` for transport; `cannot parse created session: <err>`). Wire shape unchanged: HTTP-200 `{errorCode, detail}`. Incidental pre-existing fix: the non-200 create path never closed the response body — now `defer`-closed on all paths.
  - **engine end**: `retryableAgentdFailure` retries `session_create_failed` **only** in its transient opencode 500/502/503 wrap shapes. A failed create sends no prompt, so retry cannot double-execute — unlike timeouts, which stay out of the class (each timeout attempt is a fresh session that may still complete in the background; unchanged #1451 r2 rationale).

## Semantics preserved

- `session_not_found` (message-leg 404: session existed at create, vanished before/during the turn) stays **non-retryable** — a genuinely missing session is permanent; retrying it would triple-burn the auto-disable budget. Pinned by `TestScheduler_RoutineFireSessionNotFoundNotRetried` and `TestWorkflowExecuteHandler_AgentNodeMessageLeg404StaysSessionNotFound`.
- `session_create_failed` transport-to-opencode detail (opencode down/crash-looping) is surfaced but **not retried** — consistent with the message leg, where opencode transport errors were never retried. Pinned by `TestExecuteWithRetry_SessionCreateFailedNonTransientNotRetried`.
- All timeout shapes (504 transport, `script_timeout`, opencode 504 wrap) remain excluded.

## TDD evidence

Red-first (witnessed failing on pre-fix code):
- agentd: `TestWorkflowExecuteHandler_AgentNodeSessionCreate5xx`, `TestWorkflowExecuteHandler_AgentNodeSessionCreateTransportError`
- engine: `TestExecuteWithRetry_SessionCreateFailedTransient5xxRecovers`, `TestScheduler_RoutineFireRetriesSessionCreate5xx`

Mutation-verified (each fix reverted → pin red → restored → green):
1. #1458 one-liner reverted (direct `AgentdClient.Execute` in the ScriptPath branch) → `TestScheduler_RoutineFireScriptLegRetriesTransient5xx` FAILS
2. `session_create_failed` arm removed from the classifier → both #1457 engine tests FAIL
3. agentd collapse restored at the call site (`session_not_found` again) → both create-leg handler tests FAIL

## Tests

- `go test -timeout 300s ./api/internal/workflows/` — ok
- `go test -timeout 600s -race ./api/internal/workflows/` — ok
- `go test -timeout 900s -race ./cmd/workspace-agentd/` — ok
- `go build ./...` — ok
- `make lint` — 0 issues (golangci-lint v2.13.2; was not installed in the dev pod, installed via `go install .../golangci-lint@latest` to a user bin)
- `bash -n local/issue-1417-templating-e2e.sh` — ok; T7's structural wiring-pin row now also asserts `TestScheduler_RoutineFireRetriesSessionCreate5xx` and `TestScheduler_RoutineFireScriptLegRetriesTransient5xx` exist in the tree

## Assumptions (README Rule 7)

- WIP one-liner landed — verified via `git show 24fca1c2`.
- Error codes surface as HTTP-200 `{errorCode, detail}` — verified in `writeWorkflowError` and asserted in handler tests.
- `createOpencodeSession` has exactly one production caller (`execAgentNode`) — verified by grep; signature change has no other call sites.
- `scriptedExecutor` results consume in call order across legs — verified by reading its implementation.

## Notes for reviewers

- `cmd/workspace-agentd` full-package runs are timing-flaky under this pod's load (one run died at ~340s in `TestManagedProcess_StopDuringCrashBackoffReturns`; passes standalone and on subsequent full runs, 269s plain / 317s race). Pre-existing managed-process subprocess tests, untouched by this diff.
- The nightly automation e2e rows are gated by #1456 (sibling lane); T7 here is the structural pin this branch can carry.

body:
## 概要

モーダルの文言を「判断に必要な情報だけを短く」の方針で見直す。長い説明文・revision番号・アセット件数・コンテンツルート名の繰り返しを削り、タイトル・本文・ボタンの役割を分ける。

## 変更

### 確認モーダル

- タイトルを名詞形に統一（「Nekote Blogへ反映」「このノートだけ反映」「コンテンツルートの変更」「反映内容の確認」「初めての反映」）
- 全体反映の確認: 反映先・「公開N件 / 下書きM件」・削除の注意書きの3行だけにする
- このノートだけ反映: 対象ノートと下書きの注記だけにし、ボタンを「反映する」にする
- 他端末の反映検出: revision番号を出さず、上書きされることだけを1文で示す
- 接続済みvaultの確認: 判断材料になる接続済みコンテンツルートを、折りたたみではなく本文に出す
- 別vaultで置き換え: 「全記事を削除して置き換える」の1文だけにする
- 走査の確認: 「ノートを読み取りますか？」の疑問形にし、件数と容量を1行で示す
- preflight: 初回接続と不明な理由コードの説明文を出さない。送信容量は大量送信のときだけ出す。件数行の「記事:」接頭辞を外し、全記事一覧の見出しを「反映する記事: …」にする

### 結果モーダル

- 失敗・中止の本文を「公開中の記事は変わっていません。」に統一し、「原因を直してもう一度」の指示を削る
- 反映待ちの本文を「送信は完了しました。結果は次に「Nekote Blogへ反映」を実行したときに表示されます。」にする

## 対象外（別途判断）

- 全体反映のローカル確認をサーバーのpreflight確認1回に統合する
- 「このノートだけ反映」の他端末検出モーダルを次の確認へ合流させる
- 別vault置き換え後のpreflightに出る「初めての反映」「別の記事ソースから切り替え」の言い換え

## 確認

- `typecheck` / `lint` / `test`（731件）が通ることを確認済み
- Obsidian実機での表示は未確認

## Intent

The captain believes our Firstmate fork has fallen behind and asked: "can you go ahead and get the latest firmate updates and fold it inot our fork?" Bring the latest upstream Firstmate changes into Mauryanx/firstmate while retaining the fork's own work. The captain added: "I don’t want to waste too many tokens on this. Make sure we are very targeted."

## What Changed

- Merged 75 upstream Firstmate commits into the fork (merge commit `005df64`), resolving twelve conflicted files side by side rather than taking either version wholesale. Upstream additions land in full - the Antigravity (`agy`) worker/scout adapter and `bin/fm-agy-trust.sh`, the `.claude/mods/firstmate-calm` Claude Code Calm module, opt-in typed dispatch resolution (`bin/fm-dispatch-resolve.sh`), read-only PR blocker/reviewer discovery (`bin/fm-pr-reviewers.sh`, `bin/fm-pr-state.sh`), `bin/fm-contributions.sh`, the herdr lab viewer, quiet AFK supervision, and the accompanying docs and suites - while the fork keeps its own axes: `codexHome` dispatch validation in `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh`, `--codex-home` spawn/relaunch/metadata behavior on upstream's restructured `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, voice-conversation intake, the line-anchored remote-sync parse, and the `fm_yaml_to_json` test helper.
- Extended the newly absorbed typed dispatch resolver with the fork's Codex account axis: `codexHome` is accepted and validated on use/default profiles (string, non-empty, `harness: codex` only) and participates in duplicate-profile detection; each distinct reachable account named by the matched rule - plus `default` only where the answer can fall through to it - is read once via `fm_quota_axi_read_codex_home`, all reads issued together under one 5s `fm-timeout-lib` bound, and candidates carrying a `codexHome` are bounded by that account's snapshot instead of the ambient one. Unvalidated homes become ineligible with the refusal reason; unreadable ones stay eligible but unranked. Output now carries `@<codexHome>` on candidate lines and `--codex-home <path>` on the emitted profile line.
- Updated the declared-field contract in `docs/configuration.md`, the dispatch boundary note in `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/verification/dispatch-resolve.md`; grew `tests/fm-dispatch-resolve.test.sh` with account-axis cases, and mapped `bin/fm-timeout-lib.sh` changes onto the resolver suite in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The fork's own new logic is small, fail-safe, and behaviorally tested, and the merge provably preserves both sides of all 12 conflicts with no deletions, but this branch absorbs ~31k lines of upstream commits that were reviewed here for integration correctness rather than line by line, so the test and CI phases are the real gate on the absorbed half.

No UI surface exists in this change, so evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots. Worktree left clean; the two files I touched to simulate a maintainer edit were restored.

body:
## 期間は「枠」であって「入れ物」ではない

仕事は期間があってもなくても存在しますし、ほとんどのワークスペースは期間を作りません。この前提を通しました。

## cadence が長さと名前を決める

quarter を選ぶとは「3か月」と言うことなので、終了日は導出します。**それ以外は何も導出しません。**

| cadence | 開始の制約 | 終了 | ラベル |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `quarter` | 1・4・7・10月の1日 | 末日 | `2026 Q4` |
| `month` | 月初 | 末日 | `2026-10` |
| `week` | 月曜 | 日曜 | `2026-W38`（ISO週） |
| `custom` | 任意 | **本人が指定** | **本人が指定** |

会計年度が暦年と違うワークスペースは `custom` を使います。暦年を前提に推測しません。名前のある cadence に違う終了日は指定できません（ラベルが嘘になるため）。

期間は重なりません。「今はどの期間か」に答えが2つある状態を製品が作らないためです。

## 引き継ぎは複製する

**元項目は変更しません。** すでにレビューを終えた期間が、いまも何が入っていたかを言い続けられるようにするためです。新しい項目は `fields.carried_from` で由来を残すので、「これは3回持ち越している」に答えられます。

**日付は引き継ぎません。** 前期間のために決めた日付が次期間の日付になるのは、決定の捏造です。

## 期間を使わないワークスペース

`GET /planning` は `cycles: []`, `current: null` を返します。エラーでも未完了のセットアップでもないので、画面も「期間を使っていません」と1行言うだけで、作れとは言いません。既存のワークスペースは何も変わりません。

## 経過時間は経過時間

バーは期間の経過率を出しますが、**仕事の進捗は出しません**。別の主張なので、混ぜると製品が静かに嘘をつきます。期間外では数字自体を出しません（`elapsedPercent` は `null`）。E2E で「進捗 N%」が表示されないことも固定しています。

## AI は期間を直接作れない

他の書き込みと同じで、`changesets/preview` に `POST .../cycles` を含めて提案し、本人が承認してから適用されます。差分には導出されたラベル（`2027 Q1`）が出るので、承認する側は何ができるか見えます。

## 実装

| ファイル | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `api/src/service.rs` | cycles CRUD、`GET /planning`、carry-over、export/import/snapshot、changeset許可パス |
| `src/shared/planningView.ts` / `PlanningBar.tsx` | Web・会話内共通のビューモデルと表示部品 |
| `src/PlanningScreen.tsx` | 期間の切り替え・作成・終了・引き継ぎ |
| `api/src/mcp.rs` | `pathbase_get_planning`（19ツール目） |

## テスト

| 追加 | 件数 |
| --- | --- |
| `api/tests/planning.rs` | 10（cadence導出、重複拒否、期間なしの互換、carry-overの複製性、終了、export/restore、AI提案→承認） |
| `tests/plan-view.test.mjs` | +6 |
| `tests/e2e/planning.spec.mjs` | 5 |

全て green: `cargo test` 24バイナリ（ローカル実TiDB込み）/ `playwright test` 52件 / `tsc` / `clippy` / node各suite / `npm run gate`。

author: darrenstasiakdev4you
body:
Refs #10
Tracking plan: .ai/runs/2026-09-19-command-api.md
Source doc: .ai/specs/2026-09-19-command-api.md
Status: complete

## 🎯 What changes
Before this PR, each business action was wired into the component that shows its button. The run header built its own mutations around `continueRun`, `cancelRun` and `archiveRun`, knew which 409 means "refetch", and picked cache keys itself. Extensions had a typed `context.commands`, but every call failed with "not available yet".

Now the cockpit has one **command registry** (`packages/web/src/commands/`). Three public core commands, `cezar.task.continue`, `cezar.task.stop` and `cezar.task.archive`, own the HTTP call and the cache rule. The run header runs them through `useCommand(token)`, and extensions reach the same registry as `context.commands`. Every failure rejects with a coded error that `isExtensionError` recognises. **Users should see no difference**: same requests, same toasts, same 409 refetch, same cancel confirmation.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  header["run-header (changed)"] -->|useCommand| reg["commands/registry (new)"]
  ext["extension (none built in yet)"] -->|context.commands| reg
  reg --> core["core task handlers (new)"] --> api["api/client (existing)"]
```

Components and extensions reach actions through one registry; only core handlers know the API client.

## 📋 Scope
- `packages/extension-api` (private, experimental): adds `Commands.has`, the codes `invalid-input`, `command-failed` and `command-timeout`, and the tokens `TaskContinue`, `TaskStop` and `TaskArchive`. The surface snapshot is updated on purpose.
- `packages/web`: the registry, the core handlers, `CommandsProvider` / `useCommand`, `cockpitServices`, the `main.tsx` boot order, a `cancelProjectRun` twin, and the run-header migration.
- Not included (spec follow-ups): the other copies of these actions (follow-up composer, review panel, `useContinueRun`, global Tasks archive), events, storage, components, the command palette.

## 💥 Compatibility
No route, state file, CLI or published package changes (`BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md` surfaces are untouched). `Commands.has` only affects code that implements `Commands`: the cockpit and the package's test fake, and both are updated here. Rollback is a revert; nothing is persisted.

## 🧪 Validation
All five gate commands (`typecheck`, `test:unit`, `npm test`, `build`, `test:package`) pass on `75b56d51` in a CI-equivalent Linux container (`node:24-bookworm`, non-root). `npm test` passes 7,531 of 7,531 tests. New tests cover:
- the registry's error pipeline, visibility and timeouts;
- each core command's request, input validation, 409 handling, cache keys, and when it resolves;
- an extension executing `TaskArchive` through the real host;
- the provider and hooks.

The existing run-header cases (Continue, the 409 refetch, Archive toggle, Cancel after confirmation) pass with only `CommandsProvider` added to their harnesses. [Automated review](https://github.com/DarrenStasiakDev4You/cezar-hackathon-ale-patryk-nazywa-go-brutusem/pull/11#pullrequestreview-5253369667): nothing blocking; its two minor findings and three nits are fixed in `6ff720cf`.

⚠️ On the WSL dev machine, `npm test` fails 8 **server** tests (`open-in-app`, `agent-profiles-api`, `route-parity`). A real `wslpath` is present, and `PATH` scans over `/mnt/c` hit the 5 s timeout. They fail the same way on `origin/main` on that machine, and this PR changes nothing in `packages/cezar`. GitHub Actions has not run in this repository, so no CI check covers this PR.

`needs-qa`: the run header's Continue, Cancel and Archive buttons need a manual pass before merge, and the PR needs a formal approval from someone other than its author.

## 📋 Progress
See the tracking plan.

body:
## Summary
- New `SchemaIntrospectionService` reflects on an entity class's `class-transformer` `@Expose`/`@Type` decorators (via `defaultMetadataStorage`) to produce a `{name, type, groups, nested?}[]` field tree — unbounded nesting depth, cycle-guarded via a visited-class set, arrays vs singular nested objects correctly distinguished (`type: 'array'` vs `'object'`).
- Also exposes `filterByScopes(entries, scopes)` to recursively filter that tree down to only fields whose `groups` intersect a given scope list.
- `class-transformer`/`reflect-metadata` are added as **peerDependencies** (+ devDependencies for this package's own build), not regular dependencies — see commit message for why (avoids a mismatched version range ever resolving to a second, disconnected `defaultMetadataStorage` instance).

Built for OPE-234 (auto-discoverable field schemas for shop MCP server tools) — consumed by a paired backend MR that adds `GET /<resource>/schema` routes across 5 services.

This supersedes an earlier attempt at putting this in `@openstrato/field-helper` — moved here since field-helper's actual job is filtering already-fetched data by a `fields` query param, not entity-class reflection; common_lib is already the home for scope-aware cross-cutting concerns (`scopesGuard`, `AudienceEnum`), which is a better fit.

author: thehashrocket
body:
## Summary

A pending transaction imported from a CSV file was never confirmed once the same transaction posted over the SimpleFIN feed — `syncSimpleFin`'s content-dedup pass had no promotion path (unlike CSV import's own `commitImport`, which already handles this), so the posted feed row was silently dropped as a plain duplicate and the pending row stayed stuck: excluded from the account balance forever, invisible to subscription detection, and permanently un-pairable by the transfer matcher.

This PR adds a **promotion** path: when a posted feed row's content matches an existing *pending* row, sync updates that row in place (memo, provenance, bank status) instead of dropping the feed row — routed through the same staging pipeline as an ordinary insert, so it gets identical race-condition coverage for free, with redirection from INSERT to UPDATE happening only at the literal write statement.

- `src/lib/contentCandidates.ts` (new) — shared pending/posted candidate-claiming logic, extracted from CSV import's `importBatch.ts` so sync can reuse it byte-for-byte.
- `sync_promotions` table (new, migration `0023`) — snapshots a promoted row's pre-promotion state (memo, merchant, payee, card last-four, hash, external id, feed provenance, bank transaction number, transfer pairing) so undo can restore it exactly rather than only ever deleting rows.
- `src/lib/simplefin/sync.ts` — staging loop tries `claimPendingCandidate` before falling to an ordinary insert; the write transaction re-reads the candidate fresh (rule 11) and either promotes it or falls through to insert if it's no longer available; a late fallback content check catches a concurrent CSV import claiming the same content in the staging→write window.
- `src/lib/simplefin/undoSync.ts` — `revertPromotion` restores a promoted row's exact prior state, including any transfer pairing that predates the promotion; `findLastSyncBatch`/`UndoResult` report `revertedCount` separately from deleted-row count.
- Also fixes a second, smaller race found while building this: a very narrow window between sync's content-dedup check and its write could let a genuine duplicate through if a second import landed in that instant. Sync now re-checks once more, right before writing.

Design went through 3 rounds of outside (Codex) review before implementation, each catching a real structural gap in the previous round (see `docs/plans/sync-pending-promotion.md` for the full history: batch/undo model → recheck-bypass → transfer-pairing breakage → transfer-pair-undo asymmetry/`pairsLinkedCount` → prior-pairing-state restore/`bankTransactionNumber` nulling).

## Pre-Landing Review

6 specialists + 3 red-team convergence rounds + cross-model adversarial review (Claude + Codex) ran against the implementation. Found and fixed **5 CRITICAL bugs**, each verified fail-without-fix / pass-with-fix:

1. `revertPromotion` could resurrect a one-sided transfer pair if the pre-existing pairing had been unlinked before undo.
2. The aggregate `SyncOutcome.insertedCount` wasn't adjusted for promoted rows even though per-account counts were — double-counting promotions as new money in the top-level summary.
3. `recheckContentDedup` could sacrifice a promotion-candidate row to an unrelated posted duplicate sharing its content signature during the staging→write race window.
4. `linkTransfersByBucket` was called with a pairing floor unrelated to a promoted row's own (possibly much older) date, so a pending row that sat unconfirmed while newer activity posted could be silently, permanently excluded from transfer pairing.
5. A concurrent CSV import could claim the same content a sync was about to promote, in the staging→write window — closed with a fresh fallback content check right before the write.

## Plan Completion

- [x] Promotion path routes through the same staging pipeline as ordinary inserts (governing design idea)
- [x] `sync_promotions` snapshot table + full-fidelity undo (`revertPromotion`)
- [x] Race re-verification inside the write transaction (rule 11) for the promotion candidate itself
- [x] Transfer-pairing correctness for a promoted row (pairing floor, one-sided-pair-restore)
- [x] Categorization is not re-run on a promoted row (it may already be categorized)
- [x] `bankTransactionNumber` correctly nulled/restored across promote/undo
- [x] Test coverage for every CRITICAL fix, plus core repro, deletion-race, concurrent-external-id race, unrelated-duplicate race, CSV-toUpdate race, undo variants (mixed insert+promote, one-sided-pair-restore, pre-existing-pairing-survives-undo, new-pairing-cleared-on-undo)
- [ ] PR2 (D8.1 cutover-boundary duplicate-id loss, TODOS.md) — explicitly out of scope, sketched only, tracked as follow-up

## Test Coverage

New `describe("syncSimpleFin — pending/posted content-dedup promotion", ...)` block in `src/lib/simplefin/sync.test.ts` (15+ tests) plus new tests in `undoSync.test.ts`, `syncRelinkGuard.test.ts`, `sync/actions.test.ts`, and `src/lib/test/db.test.ts` (migration table-list assertion). Full suite green.

## TODOS

- Fixed: TODOS.md's pending/posted content-dedup gap entry (line ~3465), marked `[x] FIXED`.
- New follow-ups recorded (all deliberately deferred, not silently dropped):
  - **P2** — a pre-existing (not introduced by this branch), unrelated dedup gap found while writing coverage tests: a posted row tagged with this feed's own provenance under a *different* external id than an incoming row for the same real-world transaction can produce a genuine duplicate. Candidate for bundling with PR2.
  - **P4** — accepted residual: `/sync`'s summary and `/import/success/[batchId]`'s count can show two different (individually correct) numbers for a batch containing a promotion. UX-only, no money-safety impact.
  - **P3** — accepted residual: undoing a promoted, later-rejected transfer pair leaves the `transfer_pair_rejections` row behind. Genuine product judgment call (what should "undo" mean for a rejection recorded after the fact), not a reflexive fix.

## Documentation

- **README.md** — bumped the top-of-file Status line from v1.6.2 to v1.6.3, describing the pending-row promotion fix in the existing per-version voice, and demoted the prior v1.6.2 text to a dated history line. Corrected the `/sync` "Undo this sync" bullet: it previously said undo unconditionally deletes the batch's rows, which is no longer true for a row this sync promoted from pending (that row is reverted to its prior state, not deleted, since it belongs to an earlier import batch).
- **docs/agent-notes/data-model-rules.md** — Rule 3 (dedup) gained a paragraph documenting that a posted feed row content-matching a pending existing row is now a promotion (`claimPendingCandidate`/`tryPromoteCandidate`), not a silently-dropped duplicate, closing a previously-documented gap. Rule 5 (snapshots/undo) gained a paragraph noting undo now reverts a promoted row via the new `sync_promotions` table instead of deleting it, with `revertedCount` reported separately from `deletedCount`.
- **docs/agent-notes/module-notes.md** — added an entry for the new shared `lib/contentCandidates.ts` module (`buildContentCandidates`/`claimPendingCandidate`), used by both CSV import and sync's staging loop.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test` — full suite green, including new promotion/undo/race regression tests
- [x] `pnpm build` — clean build
- [x] `pnpm lint` — clean
- [x] Fail-then-pass verified individually for each of the 5 CRITICAL fixes (temporarily reverted, confirmed the regression test failed, restored, confirmed it passed)

author: igorbabkin
body:
## What changed

**`@inject(fn)` / `injectProp(fn)` take exactly one argument — an `InjectFn`.**
`(options: ProviderOptions) => T` is the whole contract: it is called with the resolution context of the class being constructed (`scope`, runtime `args`) and whatever it returns is injected.

- The `Injectable` union on the decorator, the ten-overload mapper ladders on `inject` and `injectProp`, and `toMappedToken` are removed.
- Mapping is composition: `pipe(fn, ...mappers)` (already exported) returns an `InjectFn`, so `@inject(pipe(({ scope }) => scope.resolve<Config>('Config'), takeApiUrl(), requireHttps()))`.
- `resolveArgs(target)` stores those functions and calls each with the options it is given → its resolver is `(options: ProviderOptions) => unknown[]`.
- `arg` / `args` / `argsFn` lose their unused first parameter: `args = ({ args = [] }) => args`.

**The scope travels inside the options object, not beside it.**
`InjectOptions = { scope, args? }`, `ProviderOptions` adds `lazy?`. Every callback the library hands a context — `InjectFn`, `ArgsFn`, `ResolveDependency` — and every plumbing method — `IProvider.resolve(options)`, `IInjector.resolve(Target, options)`, `Injector.createInstance(Target, options)` — takes that one object and destructures what it uses.

The calls where the caller already addresses a scope keep it positional: `container.resolve(key, options)` and `token.resolve(scope, options)` take the new `ResolveOptions` (`ProviderOptions` minus `scope`; `ResolveOneOptions` adds `child`), so `container.resolve(key, { args })` never has to repeat the scope.

## Why

One decorator argument, one shape. The old decorator was a resolver, a token coercion and a mapping pipeline in one, and the coercion decided on the caller's behalf that a token parameter forwards the class's runtime args. Now that choice is written at the parameter — `({ scope, args }) => Token.resolve(scope, { args })` cascades, `({ scope }) => Token.resolve(scope)` does not — which is the library's explicit-injection stance applied to the decorator itself. The `(_, { args })` placeholders for an unused positional scope go away with it.

Recorded as [ADR 0019](adr/0019-inject-takes-one-function-scope-in-options.md).

## For reviewers

- **Breaking**, no shim — commit is `feat(ts-ioc-container)!:` for a major bump. Migration is in the commit body and ADR.
- All existing `@inject(Token)` / `@inject('key')` sites were translated **faithfully** to `({ scope, args }) => X.resolve(scope, { args })`, i.e. the runtime-args cascade from #164 is preserved 1:1. Sites where args are irrelevant could be shortened to `({ scope }) => …`; left as-is so the follow-up that adds a token-injection shorthand can decide the default.
- Specs updated (`injector-strategies`, `provider-behavior`, `token-based-injection`, `lifecycle-hooks`, `dependency-registration`) with two new acceptance scenarios in `injector-strategies.spec.ts`; README regenerated from `.readme.hbs.md`; CLAUDE.md updated.
- Verified: `pnpm run build`, `type-check`, `lint` (0 errors), `format:check`, `test` — 529/529 core, 14/14 react against the fresh build.

body:
The passing notice, the error in Settings, the strip inside a workspace and the turn history notice above the composer are now one Liquid Glass piece in three tones.

- `NoticeTone` (Core) decides the symbol, the colour and what VoiceOver hears. Information takes the system accent, stepping aside from `warning` and `negative`; warning and error keep their own colours (#32). Borders and shadows are gone; Reduce Transparency gives a solid surface.
- The passing notice keeps its reading time, hover hold and X; the draining bar is a thin line inside the glass along its bottom edge, in the tone's colour. Existing notices that report a failure are now errors, and those reporting something refused or not done are warnings.
- `NoticePlacement` (Core) is a new setting in Settings > Notifications: top centre under the toolbar (default), top right of the centre column, or at the bottom above the tallest composer, measured through an anchor preference on `ComposerDock`. The notice slides in from its side, or fades with Reduce Motion. A Show Test Notice button raises one notice of each tone in turn.
- Every piece is announced to VoiceOver when it appears, tone first.
- New `notices` design gallery, and `Tools/scenarios/glass-notices.json` for the preview.

Tests: `NoticeToneTests` (tone, symbol, ink, spoken text, test cycle, placement default and fallback, entrance, composer clearance), and the new scenario in `shippedScenariosRead`.

Also fixes #90, found in the preview and present on `main`: the settings strip, the error in Settings and the turn history notice fixed their text to its ideal height, which at the hosting view's zero proposal became the column's minimum and pushed the workspace off screen (the mechanism of #63). They now use layout priority; the strip's minimum went from 820 pt to 52 pt.

Also fixes #91: a preview scenario's agent lines were stored without `type`, so the transcript never drew them. They are now stored with `type` and `role` as the app stores its own, with a test that decodes an agent line back. Documents GitHub's stacked pull requests (public preview since 2026-07-30) in the `github-workflow` skill, so agents chain dependent PRs deliberately and register the chain instead of hand-managing base branches.

Covers: when a stack is the right shape (code then its docs; a retrospective then the todos it produced), the `gh api` calls for list/create/add/unstack while `gh` has no `stack` command, and three traps hit while using it on a live repo today:

- `gh api -f pull_requests[]=11` sends strings; the API rejects them as not integers. Pipe JSON through `--input -`.
- A merged PR cannot join a stack (422), so register the chain when you open it.
- GitHub may have created a stack already from PRs that target each other -- check `.stack` on the PR before creating one.

Unchanged: merge bottom-up, and each PR still has to stand on its own.

Verified with `node scripts/publicity-guard.mjs --all` and `node --test` (21 pass).

- **Tag inputs** (`InputTags`, `InputTagsOuter`): stable tag IDs kept in pure state via a new `tag-entries.ts` helper instead of refs mutated during render. 6 new unit tests.

`unknown` instead of `any`, empty interfaces → type aliases, `const`, removed dead assignments, described `@ts-expect-error`, `paceOf` moved into `das-data`, `WIZARD_STEPS` unexported, `_`-prefixed names treated as intentionally unused.
