author: anilcancakir
body:
Eight installer fixes plus the MCP registry manifest. Second of a seven-package batch, independent of wind.

## What ships

**The installer half is one defect and the three its fix exposed.** A pattern injection that matched nothing wrote nothing and returned normally, so `plugin:install` printed Success over a `lib/config/app.dart` it had never touched: the consumer app that found it registered no provider, booted no plugin, and was told the install worked. Making that a hard failure then widened the blast radius rather than narrowing it, which is what the rest closes:

- `fallbackPattern` keeps an empty `'providers': []` installable instead of failing an install that used to work.
- Both composite injections match from their list's own key forward, so `() => \w+,` before a `]` can no longer land the factory in some other list earlier in the file. The empty-list case was the same defect wearing a second face: the primary matched a later list's last entry, so the fallback that exists for it never ran.
- The providers key takes either quote, because anchoring on it made the quoting load-bearing for the first time.
- The append lookahead skips a trailing or own-line `//` comment, which is where a scaffold placeholder lives.
- The preflight runs before anything is staged, because helper-backed ops write through `dart:io` outside the `.tmp` rollback and the install record lands in phase 6, so a miss found mid-loop stranded an orphan import with nothing to reverse it.

Landed in #57.

**`server.json`** lists this package on the official MCP registry (#56). It is why the version stamp set went from five to six, and it is the least forgiving one: the registry refuses to rewrite a version it has already published, so a stale number fails the cut outright rather than shipping quietly. `test/server_json_version_test.dart` guards it against `pubspec.yaml`.

## Stamps

Six copies plus three doc pages: `pubspec.yaml`, `lib/src/mcp/mcp_server.dart`, `example/pubspec.yaml`, `example/packages/awesome_plugin/pubspec.yaml`, `server.json`, the `SKILL.md` stamp comment, and `doc/commands/install.md` / `doc/getting-started/installation.md` / `doc/plugins/authoring.md` where the constraint is quoted.

Four of the six are guarded (the MCP string, both example pins through version solving, and `server.json`); the `SKILL.md` stamp is the only one nothing checks, so it was grepped rather than trusted.

## Where this sits in the batch

Second, alongside wind and independent of it. `dusk` 0.0.14, `telescope` 0.0.6 and `magic` 0.0.14 all re-pin `fluttersdk_artisan: ^0.0.16`, so this has to be on pub.dev before any of them resolves.

## Gates

`dart analyze lib test bin` no issues. `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib/ test/ bin/` 193 files 0 changed. `dart test --timeout=60s` green at 1316. `dart pub publish --dry-run` clean once committed.

author: shand-j
body:
## Root cause

Photos attached during the quote-request flow are stored in **two different places**:

- `MediaAsset` rows — created by `POST /quote-requests/{id}/media` (staff) and `POST /customer/quote-requests/{id}/media` (customer app)
- `QuoteRequest.media_urls` (JSONB) — used by the public intake form `POST /businesses/{slug}/quote-requests` and staff `POST /quote-requests`

`POST /quotes/{id}/convert-to-job` only re-pointed `MediaAsset` rows to the new job (`job_id`). Photos that existed solely in `media_urls` — i.e. every photo submitted through the intake/portal quote-request form — never made it onto the job, so `JobRead.photos` (derived from `job.media` and rendered by the mobile job detail screen) came back empty. Closes #185.

## Fix

`convert_quote_to_job` (services/api/app/routers/quotes.py) now additionally promotes the linked quote request's `media_urls` entries into `MediaAsset` rows attached to the job:

- URLs already attached as `MediaAsset` rows (customer-app uploads) are skipped, so a photo present in both shapes is carried exactly once.
- The storage key is recovered from proxied download URLs (`/files/download?key=…`) into `file_key`; new rows are stamped `source="intake"` and keep their `quote_request_id` link.
- Because this runs at conversion time, it also heals quote requests created before this change.

No mobile change needed: the job detail screen already renders `job.photos` — the array was simply empty.

## Verification

- New test `test_convert_quote_to_job_carries_quote_request_photos` (services/api/tests/test_quotes_lifecycle.py) covers the carryover: `media_urls`-only photo, a `MediaAsset`-only photo, and one URL present in both (asserts no duplicate), plus persistence on a fresh `GET /jobs/{id}`. **Fails without the fix, passes with it.**
- `pytest tests/test_quotes_lifecycle.py tests/test_jobs_lifecycle.py tests/test_jobs_wave2.py tests/test_jobs_address_schedule.py tests/test_quote_requests.py tests/test_public_quote_requests.py tests/test_multi_day_scheduling.py tests/test_invoice_from_job.py -q` — 66 passed.
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` on touched files — clean.
- `mypy` on `app/routers/quotes.py` — clean for touched files; the one reported error (`app/rag/retrieval.py:263`) is pre-existing on `main` (confirmed by re-running on a stashed tree).

author: shanimosco47-pixel
body:
## The problem

`pullFromSupabase` read each table with a single `select('*')`. PostgREST caps one response at 1000 rows by default and gives no sign that it truncated. Since #87 the pull also reconciles: local rows the server no longer has are deleted. A truncated response therefore reads as "the server dropped everything past row 1000", and `mirrorTable` deletes those rows from the device.

Nothing is lost server-side, but the device shows a partial library until someone works out why. `photos` is the only table realistically near the cap, and multi-select upload (#89) shortens the road there.

## The fix

- `fetchAllPages(fetchPage)` reads a table page by page and stops on the row count the server reports, not on page size. A server configured with a cap below 1000 therefore still terminates correctly, and an unknown count falls back to stopping on an empty page so the loop cannot spin.
- The pull's ten table reads go through it, ordered by `id` so page boundaries stay stable across requests. `budget_settings` keeps its `maybeSingle()` read.
- An error on any page returns `{ data: null, error }`, preserving the existing behavior where a failed pull leaves the sync-error banner up rather than reconciling against a short list.

Out of scope, found in the same review and still open: `pendingIdsByTable()` is read after the SELECTs, so a row uploaded by a concurrent `flushSyncQueue` falls into neither set and is deleted locally.

## Verification

Five tests added around the paging loop: single page, past the cap, a server capping below the requested size, an unknown count, and an error page. `npm test` (243 tests), `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` all pass.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Spec #54: adds a third model-assisted selection tier that talks OpenAI-compatible chat completions to a server on the user's machine, so a 7–8B GGUF can rubric-score transcript windows fully offline. Heuristic ("local ranking") stays the zero-config default; OpenAI/Anthropic are unchanged.

New `Provider::Local` + `AiSettings.base_url` (default `http://localhost:11434/v1`, Ollama's endpoint). `connected()` for `local` requires only a model name — the base URL has a default. `select/local.rs` mirrors `openai.rs` but with a 600s request timeout (small models generate slowly on CPU) and **no bearer auth** — a stored cloud key must never leak into a user-entered base URL.

- `propose()`: `Local` arm runs the same windowed prompt/`parse_candidates`/`dedupe_similar` flow as the cloud providers, producing `selector: "local · <model>"`. On **any** endpoint failure (unreachable, non-2xx, malformed JSON from a small model), it returns heuristic candidates with `warning` set — `SelectionOutcome` gained a `warning: Option<String>` that `pipeline.rs` merges into `p.warning`, which renders in the existing warning banner. Selector is recorded as `"local ranking (local endpoint failed)"`.
- `test_connection()`: `GET {base}/models`; when the listing parses, the configured model must be in it, else the error names the served models and suggests `ollama pull`. Wired through both `/api/settings/ai` (save is test-gated as today) and `/api/settings/ai/test`.
- UI: provider option "Local endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio)", Base URL row + explainer note, key row hidden for `local`.
- README: one short "Local endpoint" section (`ollama pull`, default URL, LM Studio/llama.cpp ports).

No new dependencies; `reqwest`/`serde_json` are already in the tree.

## Tests

- `select::tests::local_endpoint_produces_candidates` — full `propose()` against a loopback stub returning a canned candidates payload
- `select::tests::local_endpoint_failure_falls_back_to_local_ranking` — closed port → heuristic candidates + warning, never an error

body:
## Purpose

Extract the synchronous presence-inspection and profile-cache chain into five narrowly scoped detection modules. The application keeps its existing entry signatures, MCP registration and model-snapshot scope. Cache hit/create/unsupported/failure paths preserve provider budgets, metadata, file format and partial-write evidence. Two focused commits form one independently deployable release.

## Risk
- [ ] Database schema or migration
- [ ] PLC protocol, address, lease, browser serial, or physical action
- [x] Authentication, permission, or configuration
- [x] Release, deployment, or production operation

Structural extraction only. No worker cutover, paid-model, prompt, retry, permission or PLC policy change. Source manifest v52 records all 131 actual sources for new fingerprints; stored snapshots and secret versions remain intact.

## Documentation impact
Updated architecture, configuration reference, production runbook, release management, PostgreSQL runtime and testing, plus current source-manifest references in text-inspection and worker documentation. The documentation contract includes both new smoke suites. Start with docs/agent-overview.md and docs/architecture.md.

## Verification evidence
- Original baselines: presence 20 and cache 21 groups passed on Windows/Linux.
- Expanded original bodies: presence 25 and cache 26 groups passed on Windows/Linux.
- Candidate/actual suites: presence 29 + cache 30; actual combined Windows 59 groups passed.
- Synthetic end-to-end cache hit/create/unsupported/failure paths retain budgets 3/2/3/2, call evidence, configuration identity and metadata.
- Independent component challenges: presence 129 and cache 106 valid mutations explicitly rejected, zero incidental errors. Seven complete function ASTs, signatures and literals preserved after explicit dependency substitution.
- Independent whole-domain first Go binds 703d50a76ab6bc6b822e2a08d5c6741812241f83 against 22a06bd0279d1c0081afc66e1ecd8cdf076f26ab. Actual Windows/Linux combined 59 pass with no candidate overlay; 17 dependency/HTTP/auth/model/docs/release gates and 46 Linux neighboring domain suites pass. All 1,078 other root functions, ordered top-level AST, six startup handlers and full MCP registry remain unchanged. All 353 original assertions retained (403 now). External independent review is documented in presence_provider_independent_first_review.json; this is not a formal GitHub approval. Independent remote second Go completed 2026-09-18 22:41:35 UTC on the same exact head/base: PR ready and mergeable; CI 35401862706 and all six jobs successful; current main unchanged; no unresolved review threads. Full independent record: pr144_independent_review.json, SHA256 0158AC1DF9142D9EE5F7D9DE5215A08D9248BF177FC3C248768A4F0A0F59500B. Reviewer /root/refactor_plan_challenge made no repository or GitHub edits. This external independent review is not a formal GitHub approval.
- No real PLC, paid inference or production database is used in acceptance tests.

## Review disposition
Accepted: missing first-failure/recovery windows, callee-before-argument ordering, dynamic dependency refresh, finite mock exhaustion and two incorrectly targeted subscription fixtures were corrected and retested.
Rejected: expanding mutation scope into an internal string encoding implementation; it is not a moved external dependency boundary.
Residual risk: original cache partial-file/record effects and original exception boundaries are intentionally preserved. Real production capacity and latency remain later-phase work.

## Rollback
Restore the previous complete immutable release and its matching runtime topology. Preserve task, model-secret and call evidence. Do not copy individual files, rewrite historical snapshots or reverse migrations.
